titleEn: AI and Open Source Are Building the Metaverse
contentEn:
**Metaverse and AI**

Many seem to believe the metaverse has failed, seeing Facebook, which changed its name to Meta, now focusing on AI instead of the metaverse. However, my feeling is a bit different. AI is a technology that can accelerate the metaverse. The metaverse's core lies in 3D and UX experiences, where all interactions occur through vision and movement, without keyboards or mice. Therefore, it must be able to recognize images from a camera in real-time and feed back my body's reactions to virtual objects. And AI handles all these technologies. Furthermore, one of the biggest problems with the metaverse was the high cost of content production. Rich experiences, conversely, demand more cost. For the metaverse, which always suffered from a lack of content, generative AI comes as a welcome rain.

**The Rise of Open Source**

However, many here seemed to think that AI was the exclusive domain of global corporations and large enterprises, but looking at the situation over the past year, while large-scale experiments by big companies are driving AI, it seems open source is ultimately what's making it explode. While ChatGPT itself certainly has the potential to become an OS by building a plugin ecosystem, I'm a bit skeptical about this. Of course, ChatGPT will become a giant platform like a second Facebook or Naver. But ChatGPT cannot replace the internet. When Midjourney came out, people were enthusiastic, and creators were worried. However, with the advent of Stable Diffusion, opportunities arose for individual creators and developers, and it's developing incredibly rapidly. The same goes for generative image AI. As Stable Diffusion's plugin integrated into the Krita open-source graphic editor, features like inpainting became surprisingly convenient. Similarly, smaller models capable of replacing ChatGPT have begun to emerge. Sensitive company information, or specialized information difficult for general services, will likely prefer these models over ChatGPT.

**Even if the Metaverse keyword fades, Mozilla Hubs continues.**

The metaverse is also the same. Believer is building a cloud platform based on Mozilla Hubs, a global open-source metaverse project. While there are many efforts to create a metaverse 3D ecosystem, the most popular Mozilla Hubs model on Sketchfab already has 4,300 downloads, 391 favorites, and 20,000 views. Which vertical metaverse's prosumer ecosystem has such an ecosystem?

{{IMG:1}}

Mozilla Hubs compatible assets sold on Sketchfab

Looking at YouTube, cases utilizing Mozilla Hubs have also increased significantly over the past year. And another fact I've recently learned and felt is that while Mozilla Hubs' web editor, Spoke, was powerful and good, it had limitations in graphics and production quality issues. After all, Spoke wasn't a professional 3D graphics editor. However, with the emergence of Blender's Hubs exporter, also open-source, the quality has significantly improved. [https://youtu.be/A51eHOkR0IY](https://youtu.be/A51eHOkR0IY)

This Hubs exporter is also open-source and can be further modified. The advantage of this is that the Hubs project is open-source, playing only standard 3D models and avatars, while the creation aspect is entirely entrusted to Blender, a professional graphics/animation tool, requiring only compatibility. WebXR and WebGPU performance in web browsers have already greatly improved. Mozilla Hubs' default map also shows a map created with Blender, not Spoke.

{{IMG:2}}

[https://hubs.mozilla.com/Pvg5MMt/hubs-demo](https://hubs.mozilla.com/Pvg5MMt/hubs-demo)

[**Hubs Demo | Hubs by Mozilla** Join others in VR at Hubs Demo, right in your browser. hubs.mozilla.com](https://hubs.mozilla.com/Pvg5MMt/hubs-demo)

I expect that AI rendering, currently under discussion, will eventually become a web browser standard. Attending MSF standards meetings and observing recent trends, one thing is clear: the technical standards and environment for the internet's transformation into the metaverse are increasingly moving towards open source. Observing these movements, I feel that the idea of the metaverse and AI being driven solely by big players might be a bit of an overconcern, and I'd like to suggest that metaverse projects attempting to build everything independently should reconsider their direction. In the graph below, green represents the metaverse search trend over the past 5 years, red is Mozilla Hubs, and blue is WebXR. WebXR and Mozilla Hubs have not had their scales changed. It's clear they are almost considered synonymous, and despite the decrease in metaverse search queries, they are actually on the rise.

{{IMG:3}}

The completion of the Chonnam National University metaverse project will likely extend until this month, so we haven't been able to speak actively about it yet, but we are thoroughly aiming to create a metaverse based on this future environment. We'll talk more about that once our product is released.

titleEn: Weathering with You Reminded Me of She and Her Cat
contentEn:
This image does not exist.

I watched "Weathering With You." These days, with Studio Ghibli gone, is Makoto Shinkai the only anime director left who suits my taste? It seems he's openly embracing his strengths: space, stars, and weather as themes. However, for me, his best works are still "Voices of a Distant Star" and "She and Her Cat." They've become too flashy, and there's too much to think about. Both his works and I, who watch them... [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_4Xwci4CUCs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_4Xwci4CUCs)

This was my favorite work during my university days. Nowadays, when you think of Makoto Shinkai, you might imagine vibrant skies and light, but this work, his debut, was created by him alone, using only light in black and white to craft beautiful images and tell his lyrical story. Yet, even then, he was already making "Sekai-kei" works. This first work, which calmly depicted how for the cat, "she" (the person he loved) was his entire world, is a theme consistently maintained throughout Makoto Shinkai's entire body of work.

{{IMG:1}}

Watching this work again, I find myself contemplating... my own self once more. I've aged, gained more networks, and acquired more skills, but am I truly continuing to tell my story honestly? Or am I trying to do more than my capabilities allow? What story did Director Makoto Shinkai, now undeniably a commercial artist, want to tell? My first assessment of him was that he was an "unwilling prodigy," a genius artist who boldly used computer graphics and could handle everything by himself. For "She and Her Cat," he did everything himself except for the female voice. But thinking about it, wasn't what was truly remarkable about him how well he expanded the scope of what he could control through technology? Despite that, I truly envy how consistently he has told his own stories. Am I telling my story well within the scope of what I can do? I feel like I haven't changed much, yet my surroundings and I myself have changed so much.

contentEn:
The original post was published on Belivvr's blog (Medium) on July 6, 2022.

I've given many metaverse lectures recently. This post aims to explain Belivvr's metaverse to internal and external audiences through three keywords: “Metaverse, New Analog, XR… medium.com

https://medium.com/belivvr/%EB%A9%94%ED%83%80%EB%B2%84%EC%8A%A4-%EB%89%B4%EC%95%84%EB%82%A0%EB%A1%9C%EA%B7%B8-xrweb-d91f03d5f6b9

Hello. I'm Luke Metaverse Woker (not Walker...), CEO of Belivvr. I've given many metaverse lectures recently. This post aims to explain Belivvr's metaverse to internal and external audiences through three keywords: “Metaverse, New Analog, XR Web.”

**1. Belivvr's First Keyword: “Metaverse”**
First, let's organize the common discourse around the metaverse. Everyone describes defining the metaverse as like the blind men touching an elephant. I think this is an apt description, as the metaverse is a much larger discourse than one might initially think.

{{IMG:1}}

I often describe it in a much broader sense, as shown below.

{{IMG:2}}

And to use an analogy, I'd like to express it differently than an unchanging elephant. If you piece together each drawing, you can understand the elephant. I would say it's like a small ant crawling on a butterfly that is in the process of metamorphosis.

{{IMG:3}}

**The metaverse is not static; it is ongoing.** Both the chrysalis before it transforms into a butterfly, and the wings that are just being unfurled and dried, are all 'butterflies.' What many people define as the metaverse is just a snapshot or a part of it. And what's important is not the 'butterfly' itself, but the difference between the 'chrysalis' and the 'adult butterfly.' If we are ants riding on this 'butterfly,' we shouldn't just be surprised by the change; we must understand that **this butterfly will soon “fly into the sky.”**

{{IMG:4}}

Therefore, the true meaning of the metaverse should not be about strictly defining it, but rather focusing on what value it will bring us. Let's move on to the second keyword, “New Analog.”

**2. The Value of the Metaverse: New Analog.**

**1) Analog for Digital, Gaining Renewed Attention**
To explain New Analog, I will compare and contrast digital and analog to clarify the 'analog' part of the term. Typically, digital is easily understood as 1s and 0s, while analog is a continuous signal. All naturally existing signals and information are analog, and digital signals can be thought of as encoded for computers.

{{IMG:5}}

However, strictly speaking, voltage, or the movement of electrons, does not jump suddenly like that graph. The movement of electrons actually rises in an analog fashion. In electrical engineering, it's more of a convention to consider the presence of voltage as a '1' signal. In computer science, logical operations and programming are built upon these agreed-upon signals. That's how the digital revolution occurred.

*However, in the metaverse, we need to pay attention to analog again.** This is because ****multi-sensory experiences are crucial in the metaverse, and the ability to record and transmit these experiences comes in the form of analog-like experiential data.******And we have defined this value as “New Analog.”***

**2) New Analog as a Value of the Metaverse**
To explain New Analog services more easily, let's take the example of popular map and restaurant review services on PC and mobile.

{{IMG:6}}

Typically, these services emphasize information like 'recommended order,' 'star rating order,' or 'latest order.' The value users seek from these services can be described as “summarized digital information” such as restaurant rankings or distance. But what happens when we move to metaverse services? The metaverse offers spatial experiences beyond the 2D screen page environment. Furthermore, it can provide a more direct experience of a space, making it feel as if you are actually there, rather than the indirect experience offered by images or videos on mobile/PC. The new service value of the metaverse is experience, and experience is analog-like information provided through a series of visual, auditory, and tactile data. Therefore, we defined this service value as “New Analog” and concluded that it is a service value that should be focused on in the metaverse. In fact, we already enjoy content that delivers new-analog-like experiences and feelings.

{{IMG:7}}

It's just that the smartphone environment wasn't suitable compared to immersive VR/AR devices. Images and videos, which are sweeping the mobile era, are also analog-like unstructured data. This is because more visual and auditory information can convey “feelings,” “vibes,” and “sensations,” and these demands from the MZ generation were also evident in the changes in webtoons and TikTok content. Finally, here's a summary in a table:

{{IMG:8}}

In the metaverse, digital signals carrying more information are directly delivered to our physical senses, providing new analog experiences. Furthermore, because it possesses digital properties, there are no physical limitations, and delivery costs are very low. **This is the value of the metaverse as we see it, in other words, New Analog.**

**3. Belivvr's Third Keyword: XR Web**
Next, to discuss XRWeb, **our third keyword that we are technologically focusing on**, let's briefly talk about mobile platforms.

**1) XR Web in the App vs. Web Platform War**
It's an old story now, but there used to be discussions like, 'Will web win on mobile, or will apps win?'

{{IMG:9}}

Actually, it's like the 'Do you like mom or dad better?' debate among programmers. When faced with a question that seems to cause decision paralysis, let's try changing our perspective for a moment. How about looking at it this way?

{{IMG:10}}

The mobile app rivalry was further divided into iOS and Android. While these two OSes provide the optimal smartphone experience, they impose many restrictions for the sake of their own ecosystem's exclusivity and competitiveness. Conversely, the web camp, based on W3C's global standard HTML5 technology, can be described as a world where freedom is enjoyed through various open-source tools. Now, let's divide the metaverse while maintaining the framework of this diagram.

{{IMG:11}}
                                
XRWeb vs. XRApp Ecosystem Rivalry in the Metaverse

No one can deny that Meta is at the forefront of the XR app ecosystem developed with game engines like Unity and Unreal. Meta is also building its own metaverse centered around Horizon. Although the Meta Quest Store has opened as App Lab, distribution and promotion are very difficult for general companies. Furthermore, given the nature of large corporations aiming for monopolies, they are unlikely to be very favorable to other metaverse platform ecosystems. Even the 47.5% commission fee has become a subject of controversy. **However, as a blue ocean company, we focused on XRWeb, which is based on W3C-led technologies like WebXR and WebRTC. That ship sailing into the wonderful sea is Belivvr.**

**2) The Expanded Technical Scope of XR Web Beyond Mobile Web**
Looking at the evolution of mobile web, initially, PC and mobile web were separate. However, current mobile web has virtually integrated all screens using responsive web technology and design. So, what about XR devices?

{{IMG:12}}

The responsive web technology that operates on XR devices is WebXR. A-frame is a framework that makes WebXR easier to use. Additionally, WebRTC is a technology used for real-time communication and interaction with other avatars. A prime example of an open-source metaverse using these technologies is Mozilla Hubs. Just as the mobile web became the mainstream of new web services with the advent of mobile devices, I believe XR web can become the mainstream of new web services with the advent of XR devices. And to create such XRWeb services, various technologies including WebXR are needed, and Belivvr is a company specialized in this, focusing its technological development around these technologies.

**3) XR Web as an Open Technology Including Web3**
We believe that Web is absolutely the most important technology and service for realizing the fully open metaverse we envision. It's clear that Meta is virtually monopolizing hardware, and a robust Meta-led app ecosystem will be built upon it. As an alternative, XRWeb can be a metaverse technology that is Meta-independent and driven by open-source and international standards. In fact, there is a W3C group that has begun discussions on metaverse interoperability.

[**https://www.w3.org/community/metaverse-interop/**](https://www.w3.org/community/metaverse-interop/)

**Metaverse Interoperability Community Group** Our mission is to bridge virtual worlds by designing and promoting protocols for identity, social graphs, inventory, and more. www.w3.org

https://www.w3.org/community/metaverse-interop/

Considering the closed nature of metaverse platforms aiming for monopolies, it's hard to imagine any technology other than web technology having the potential to open portals, much like America Chavez in the multiverse.

{{IMG:13}}
                                
                            America Chavez traveling through the Multiverse (Marvel Comics)

In that sense, even current mobile apps operate based on web technology for connectivity, and it's no exaggeration to say that B2B-based services are more than 90% web technology. (That's why we are focusing on B2B.) While the web might fall slightly short in terms of user experience, it is an overwhelmingly superior technology compared to apps in terms of scalability, maintainability, and operability. Furthermore, if we consider a democratic web metaverse utilizing fully decentralized technology, Web3 can be included. Therefore, XRWeb can be referred to as a new web service that corresponds to a metaverse in an XR environment, composed of a collection of technologies such as WebXR, WebRTC, and Web3.

**3) XRWeb, True Metaverse Democratization Possible Even on Low-Performance Devices**
Of course, because the web is developed based on standards, it's difficult for it to adopt the latest technologies as quickly as apps, and since it must support even low-end hardware, it's challenging to provide as polished an experience as apps. Therefore, it clearly has a weakness in "experience," one of the core aspects of the New Analog mentioned earlier. However, conversely, it operates on very low-performance devices and anyone can easily access it with just a URL.

{{IMG:14}}
                                
                            Believer's web-based metaverse platform (Mozilla Hubs) running on Whalebook/Chromebooks

And device performance improvements are a matter of time. On mobile, there are already web services that provide app-level experiences. (The web can also utilize GPU accelerators, and assembly code is becoming possible.) Of course, the web was not developed to replace apps. The two technologies have different purposes. However, when compared to game engines in the metaverse, while game engines, which were originally 3D and had metaverse-like development experience with MMORPGs, face minor changes, the web, which was fundamentally an asynchronous 2D environment, faces greater technological challenges and opportunities in its transformation into a synchronized 3D metaverse.

And we would appreciate it if you remember Believer. We hope this has been somewhat helpful in understanding Believer and the metaverse.
#Believer #Metaverse #NewAnalog #XRWeb #WebXR

titleEn: Reviewing the 20th Presidential Election: Why
contentEn:
First, before starting this post, I want to state that I supported Candidate #1. I even have party membership. However, I don't believe that the country will collapse just because the person I supported didn't win. The reason is not that Candidate #1 or #2 is as flawless and clean as their respective supporters wish, but rather that the Korean system is not that weak, and the many experiences the Korean system has gone through over time are expected to prevent what is feared. Nevertheless, new problems may still arise, but the government is not foolish enough to repeat past mistakes, and if concerns do materialize, the public is not weak either. A nation that endured guns and swords has no reason not to endure the prosecution. Therefore, I respect each person's choice and the outcome. Nevertheless, I couldn't concentrate on work yesterday. However, I also think the good thing is that it became an opportunity to understand what Korea's problems are and what the public sentiment is, based on the results. Since I haven't had time to analyze it meticulously, I might be wrong, but I'd like to briefly talk about why Candidate #2 won. Many people will remember the battle between Candidate #1 and #2 as the battle of Daejang-dong vs. Kim Keon-hee. But how many people were swayed by those issues? And if you ask if that influenced the overall election, I would say no. The battle of Daejang-dong and Kim Keon-hee was a fight to give each other a big 'screw you'.

https://www.sisain.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=46923
                                [**[굽시니스트의 본격 시사만화] AHK - 시사IN** www.sisain.co.kr](https://www.sisain.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=46923)

<A current affairs cartoon by Gupbonjwa that explains the situation in Korea so well>
Ultimately, it was content that created and consumed the identity of each side's supporters. Because of this, supporters would send ridiculous KakaoTalk messages to each other, despise each other, and were convinced that their candidate would win. However, the result was a close race, and a simple look at the data reveals a few changes from before. There appear to be two major changes: one is the conservative shift of men in their 20s, and the other is the defection of Seoul. Some may talk about votes from Jeolla-do and Gyeongbuk, but those regions already have a distinct political color, and only the proportions change slightly, so they are not good indicators for identification. And as mentioned earlier, the votes from Seoul, or Gyeonggi, are ultimately from regions with a sufficiently large population and a weaker sense of historical debt, making them good to view as a median value. To conclude, the "regime change" frame was more effective than Lee Jae-myung/Democratic Party's argument about an incompetent candidate. If so, we need to reconsider why the "regime change" frame worked. First, I won't broadly generalize it as a simple economic failure. "Economy" is a collective term that encompasses too many topics, such as currency, scientific and technological development, real estate, exports, and domestic demand. While they influence each other, policies are separate and should be viewed individually. I believe that discussing it in terms of policy-making entities will allow for a more specific analysis of the causes.

If I were to recall the biggest events of the Moon Jae-in administration, they would be COVID-19, Kim Jong-un, and the Cho Kuk scandal. This order is actually somewhat arranged from less to more fault on the part of the Moon Jae-in administration. First, COVID-19 strengthened the argument for regime change. However, it's regrettable that even though Korea did quite well while other countries were burning, the blame still fell on the administration, and as a supporter of the Democratic Party, it's annoying. And it's surprising how the Moon Jae-in government carried the responsibility for the situation where hundreds of thousands of cases were emerging daily, even though it was clear that the COVID-19 era would soon end with Omicron. They might have hoped that the next administration would be the Democratic Party, but in any case, the Moon Jae-in administration carried COVID-19 to the very end.

And the biggest mistake of this administration caused by COVID-19, I believe, was "real estate." And that sparked the judgment argument in this election. The liquidity supply to solve COVID-19 and inappropriate real estate regulations truly caused the real estate market to explode. I believe that treating real estate as an investment asset and controlling its flow at an appropriate level is correct, but approaching transactions and investments in real estate as evil already showed amateurism. How could it work when half the nation, or even those without homes, recognized it as an investment asset, and the administration alone went against the current and tried to establish a new order? It seems like the biggest blunder. However, conversely, if one voted for Yoon Suk-yeol expecting an overall rise in real estate, it would be a mistake, but if it was for the purpose of capital gains, wouldn't it have been a good choice? I don't think the capital gains market will drive up real estate prices. Inflation, high interest rates, a flood of supply, and active transactions do not, in my opinion, mean rising house prices. Ultimately, public sentiment turned, starting from the regions most affected by this pain. That is Seoul. It can be interpreted that it wasn't homeowners who voted for Yoon Suk-yeol, but rather those who suffered the most from soaring house prices. What remains for the Yoon Suk-yeol government now is terrifying inflation. I hope they resolve it well.

Next is the defection of men in their 20s from progressive politics due to the Cho Kuk scandal, which led to gender conflict among those in their 20s. I won't use the term "conservative shift." It is perfectly natural for people in their 20s, as they enter the labor market, to have progressive tendencies. How could a new employee be expected to understand the CEO's mindset? They've never been a CEO. The Cho Kuk scandal was approached by progressives through the frame of prosecutorial reform, but it ultimately ended in a conflict over fair competition and gender among those in their 20s. I think it's very bad and frustrating that it ended in division, and I'm a bit angry at the People Power Party who benefited from this, but if I understand their position in fighting a war, I'd like to discuss who the problem is. First, the biggest contributor to creating that frame was the media, but I'll pick radical feminism as the second biggest contributor. And the third is the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family (MOGEF), which became controversial for its potential abolition. Those not interested in online communities may not know, but the rise of feminism due to the #MeToo movement led to the growth of radical feminism. Personally, I always feel that the two extremes are somewhat akin to a disease... you can think of them as the feminist equivalent of the Taegeukgi Corps. The biggest problem with these individuals is that they spread gender conflict in online communities. Starting with "mirroring," which was about copying trash to respond with trash, I believe their influence affected some policies. Their biggest problem is that men are seen as targets of struggle. One cannot compromise with a target of struggle; they are subjects to be enlightened. Therefore, despite being unable to engage in politics, they tried to influence politics and policies. They imposed gender issues on every current issue that needed to be resolved and tried to interfere. One of the worst habits of progressives is regulation and interference. This characteristic makes both progressives and conservatives seem like "꼰대" (old-fashioned, preachy elders) to those in their 20s, and among them, progressives are described as "선비" (a classical scholar, often implying dogmatism). As a result, without proper policy research, claims and policies emerged that were nonsensical under the guise of "awareness improvement" or tried to impose frames without analysis of each domain. And the ministry that proactively carried this out, or rather, had no choice but to carry it out, was likely MOGEF.

I believe that MOGEF's role, instead of promoting women's rights, should be to solve women's discrimination issues and improve structural problems. However, for administrative convenience, it kept talking about quotas and regulations. Conversely, to men in their 20s, who are sensitive to fair competition and have a strong sense of victimhood due to military service, it could only be seen as unfair regulation. Furthermore, since MOGEF regulated games, a major consumer product for men, the backlash was inevitably greater. Conversely, in the case of webtoons, a major consumer product for women, the female adult market grew explosively within the framework of self-regulation, but in this atmosphere, the male adult market was demonized, leading to increased resentment. It is highly likely that even the progressive circles, far removed from the internet and those in their 20s, were not properly aware of these points, and perhaps conservatives quickly noticed and utilized them. Therefore, MOGEF might have thought it was doing its job well, but it is difficult to avoid criticism for having exacerbated gender conflict through its regulatory omnipotence. Despite having much to do with actual structural problems such as the proportion of high-ranking public officials or the issue of women experiencing career breaks, these areas received little attention, and by advocating for gender equality, MOGEF found it difficult to avoid suspicion of being radical feminism. What the next government, which discussed the abolition of MOGEF, should consider is not a regulation-centric approach but other ways to protect women and utilize female talent. The utilization of women as human resources at the national level is a very important issue. We must prevent capable women from being overlooked simply because they are women. Then, such problems must be identified and solved one by one, and policies must have details and evidence. However, this was not done; scientific evidence and research were ignored, and justification and struggle were emphasized.

Finally, Kim Jong-un. I understand that the Moon Jae-in administration put a lot of effort into peace negotiations. If there hadn't been the COVID-19 crisis, it might have even been realized. And as a result of that achievement, the Democratic Party might have smoothly taken this administration. However, COVID-19 occurred, diverting resources, and with the recent economic war between the US and China and the Ukraine crisis, we are entering a new Cold War era, making the timing very difficult. It is a time when the possibility of a proxy war on the Korean Peninsula is increasing once again. If North and South Korea fight, both North and South Korea will be screwed. That is clear. It's truly bitter that the bad guys who start wars are easily remembered, but the countless righteous heroes who prevent them are not. Perhaps that's why Marvel movies exist.

ps1. President Yoon Suk-yeol, please stop using social media... and make sure to get your posts reviewed by an aide before uploading them. If they were already reviewed by an aide, I hope you replace them. And if you are planning political retaliation, please refrain. Remember that you were not elected by a large margin. Please take care of the enormous issues currently at hand. Although the Moon Jae-in government largely carried the near-fatal COVID-19 problem, you will have to deal with enormous after-effects.

ps2. Huh Kyung-young in 4th place... Isn't this further evidence of the dark side of Korean politics? I wonder if it's a good thing that politicians who lack basic qualifications get high votes and minority opinions disappear.

final ps. This article is my personal opinion, so I will disable comments. If you find it insightful, please refer to it; if not, I apologize for not being able to dedicate much time to analysis, so I might be wrong, please just move on. I will now focus on my work.

ComicsV: A Fresh Start for 2020
contentEn:
ComicsV, which became everything to me after I started my first business in 2017. I knew that if a startup item didn't prove itself within three years, its value would dilute, but we've already passed the full three-year mark. Perhaps due to my shortcomings, these three years, long if you consider them long and short if you consider them short, have truly flown by in an instant. When I first started the business, many people questioned why "comics" needed to be viewed in VR. Those who spoke of interaction and sparkle have now largely disappeared. I believe this is less because we did well, and more because the VR market has progressed slower than expected, and even games haven't found a clear answer for it. Ultimately, it seems everyone is realizing that the market is more important than the service concept itself.

However, seeing Oculus, invested in by Facebook, slowly but surely advancing, building up its technology, and the market gradually expanding, makes me reconsider what a VR company should aim for. Was ComicsV's core content, or technology? And what has accumulated within the company? Many team members have come and gone, and I'm grateful to the friends who ultimately believed in us and stayed. Unlike the first year, when we just blindly tried everything, I believe that from the third year onwards, we need to show a more evolved appearance. This year, ComicsV aims to establish fundamental technology and quality systems that can find the right market, marking our first year of turning into a technology company, and we will ensure that both people and technology accumulate within the company. Until now, it seems we were just scrambling to create and survive. Considering that even the main features of the service planned at the time of our initial startup haven't been launched after three years, we still have a long way to go. We ask for your continued interest and support for ComicsV in 2020.

**A comics/art company operating based on changes in technology platforms such as VR/AI/Blockchain.**
We build and expand an ecosystem where creators and readers can enjoy comics/art together, and conduct profit-generating businesses based on this. We continuously research and realize the scope of technology-based comics/art and the correct ecosystem. Each organization and its members continuously contemplate the above mission and mutually assist each other to become experts in their respective fields.

We will definitely create a global VR webtoon market where anyone can participate.

titleEn: VR Webtoon Platform ComicsV Officially Enters Chinese Market!
ComicsV VR Webtoon: 20
contentEn:
Although it's been a year and a half since the service launched, due to my own capabilities and corporate operational issues, only now has ComixV's main page redesign incorporated the vision I had for a webtoon platform. (Even though it's my first time starting a business, I truly feel my lack of skill. ㅜㅜ) When I learned about planning, I was taught that the first page represents the service's direction. What defines a service is not technology, but user experience.

{{IMG:1}} The revamped face of ComixV

**1. ComixV aims to have a small promotion area, focusing on discovering buried content and matching it with users.**
ComixV's main page features a main banner, which is its promotion area, that is overwhelmingly smaller compared to other services. In particular, the main list is randomized and uses a familiar card-type UX. The goal is for this to evolve into personalized recommendations in the future. Currently, simply pushing the latest content doesn't guarantee suitable recommendations for individuals or new users. This was the minimum effort we could make to prevent good content from getting buried due to age.

**2. We aim for a platform where anyone can upload and share content across various channels.**
The upload systems of other webtoon platforms are vertically structured compared to webtoons, forming a pyramid (Webtoon > Best Challenge > Challenge), with less attention paid to personal spaces. (Pixiv is an exception.) This hinders the easy accessibility that is a strength of comics, and conversely, it creates a situation where amateurs only gather among themselves. (Even though I was an editor...) The editor-driven upgrade system also presents a problem where the market is driven by editors' tastes and abilities. ComixV has brought this to the forefront, like YouTube, and wants to activate it to strengthen the recommendation system and advance it with technology. If we had enough money, we would strengthen promotions, but since active participation isn't even happening yet, and we're currently approaching it through education, that's still a distant goal. In the future, the goal is to move towards a model based on distribution fees and cloud usage. Someday, I want to provide an open API so that various platforms can be built on top of it. Currently, we are directly integrating into various channels, making us a hub-type platform, unlike other webtoon platforms. I believe there isn't yet a proper, concrete webtoon platform that incorporates these efforts, including scrolling. I think this is because there haven't been many cases where the webtoon industry has been properly approached under the name 'platform'. In that sense, if you ask if Netflix is a 'platform'?? I think it's only half a platform compared to YouTube.

**3. ComixV's platform still lacks features and content compared to expectations.**
Since the first day of the new year, reviews like the following have been posted. One pointed out the lack of system features, and the other, the lack of content. These two reviews very clearly showed us the path we need to take. However, the fact that both reviews were underpinned by expectations for us made us feel a sense of responsibility and duty. These kinds of reviews are the most terrifying. The greater the expectation, the greater the disappointment, and disappointed users do not return.

{{IMG:2}}
{{IMG:3}}

Let's do better in 2019! As if every day is our last! (The situation for a startup really feels like it's always the last day haha)

Learning About Corporations
contentEn:
IT Story

Learning about Corporations.

Luke ・ August 14, 2018. 8:43 AM

Copy URL Add as Neighbor

More Post Options

Starting a business seems like a process of learning about corporations. In *Sapiens*, it was said that humanity (Homo) triumphed because of its power to believe in fiction, which created religions, armies, and corporations. And what maximized this was writing.

A corporation is composed of people, but in reality, it exists as text. A corporation's existence is recognized and it exercises power based on higher laws, which are essentially text. It defines each role within the corporation and enters into contracts and operates for the corporation's benefit or for any common purpose written in its articles of incorporation. The moment that small piece of paper is written, it comes alive like a child, eats, and sometimes even hits its friends. Parents can also leave instructions for disciplining the child or guiding its behavior in writing, and these must be based on higher laws such as the Commercial Act or various national statutes.

One must not misunderstand corporations. A corporation is text, and text must be controlled. While the coming and going of talent might be a human issue, what ultimately drives a company is text, and even the CEO is not free from that text. If a child makes a mistake, the parents must take responsibility, and by that text, the child itself can even change its parents. Some people say they get paid for consulting on articles of incorporation, but it seems as pointless as outsourcing software development. If you don't agonize over it intensely, it has no meaning.

What I always heard at the Software Policy Research Institute was that all policy formulation and implementation must align with the legislative intent. The legislative intent for corporations seems to be a mix of dispute resolution based on capital and equity, labor-management dispute resolution, and profit realization. Since one cannot expect romance from such laws, they must be examined more carefully. A corporation is ultimately software. The saying, often spoken as a joke, that software is never soft, now sounds like a dagger.

When my child asks, "Is ComicsV yours, Dad?", I always say, "No, it's not Dad's. ComicsV belongs to ComicsV." Ultimately, that refers to a few pieces of paper based on laws and tax ledgers, and based on these, it refers to the people, money, and intellectual assets gathered.

To be able to purchase such a standalone virtual reality device for just 238,000 won, including shipping!!!

This is the story of the Oculus Go, an ambitious virtual reality HMD created by Facebook in collaboration with Xiaomi.

Delivery is via DHL, so you can receive it incredibly quickly, almost unbelievably fast for an international shipment.

Oculus Go | Oculus

Introducing Oculus Go, an all-in-one virtual reality headset. Move freely in virtual reality without a phone or PC. Experience true standalone VR now.

www.oculus.com

Moreover, while Gear VR only worked with Samsung phones, the Oculus Go can be used with any phone that has Bluetooth. It also comes with a controller that feels more comfortable and secure than those of Gear VR or Daydream.

It fits snugly, and since it uses AA batteries, there's no need to worry about charging like with Daydream.

Even I, who am in the VR business, bought this Oculus Go and started trying out various things. I was curious not only about the hardware but also how the software and content had changed. One of the biggest changes is that once you connect it to your phone for the first time, you can use it completely standalone without needing the phone afterward. Another change is that downloaded content can be played even when the network is disconnected.

As for content, the store seems to be paying more attention to operations, with events and various promotions, unlike in the past. (Can't you give us some attention too?) However, one difference is that, much like the early smartphone market, many worthwhile games are paid. Free games or apps are generally low in quality or just demos. Beyond that, there are various types of videos to enjoy, but 360-degree videos on a 2k display still feel somewhat frustrating. Even the famous Jurassic Park... The wider 360-degree view is good, but the seemingly poor image quality is a bit disappointing. I do think that those new to VR will still be impressed by it. Of course, LG and Google recently created a 1443ppi display, but the Oculus Go hasn't reached that level. Also, there are some decent-looking options in education and other fields, but they're in English.... Especially for something like Epic Roller Coasters, which is now an app solely dedicated to themed roller coasters, the ones that had high satisfaction were Night Sky and Tomb Raider.

Ultimately, there's also a lack of information on what content is truly good. It's about three times more expensive than mobile games but three times cheaper than console or PC games, making it difficult to purchase easily. Videos all seem fun, but often the running time is shorter than expected, which is a pity, or the more active they are, the more dizzying they become, making it hard to play for long. Achieving a balance between these two aspects truly determines the quality of VR content.

So, overall, it's still common to feel dizziness and discomfort after enjoying videos and games for about 20 minutes. The device itself lasts about 2-3 hours... but overheating, especially when focusing on games, means you still have to let the device rest after about 30 minutes, which remains a drawback.

BUT! Plot twist: there's content that's immersive and enjoyable for extended periods.

It's a self-promotion, but it's the VR webtoon ComixV. To be honest, I've mostly viewed ComixV on web and mobile rather than VR, as it supports both. However, I was surprised by how comfortable and immersive our content felt when I enjoyed it on the Oculus Go this time.

It's story-based, and I thought I'd only watched for about 10 minutes, but when my wife told me it was late and to go to bed, I took off the headset and 20 minutes had flown by... I was surprised to experience the "content time machine" feeling I used to get from Civilization, but in VR. I even got scolded for playing Civilization too long...

I didn't realize how much fun it would be to sit in my comfortable swivel chair at home and lightly tap the controller to flip through pages.

Webtoons tend to cause "turtle neck" syndrome from constantly scrolling on a small screen... This service was made for VR, and I was surprised myself when I watched it in VR after a long time.

Seriously, if you've bought an Oculus Go, you absolutely must download and try it. It's almost the only VR content that updates with new content every week, and the artists' production skills are continuously improving. (We love our artists who are serializing on our humble platform.)

Due to an issue with the Oculus Store not properly handling Korean at the initial launch, we received a penalty and didn't appear in recent updates, but looking at the metrics, even with a small number of users, those who try it once continue to use it consistently. You could say the loyalty is even higher than for web/mobile. If you've bought an Oculus Go, immerse yourself in the charm of VR webtoons. It's a service that truly utilizes the Oculus Go for long play sessions. If you come in and watch everything, you can easily spend over an hour.

ComixV is a startup that needs more people to support us so we can introduce new works.

Currently, all content created directly by famous webtoon artists is FREE! You can find it by searching for webtoon, comic, or comix in the Oculus Store. We ask for your continued love and support.

ComixV - VR Comic / VR Webtoon

Webtoons come to life, VR webtoons are ComixV

www.oculus.com

P.S. For additional information, to factory reset the device, long-press the power + volume down buttons. Once an Oculus account is assigned to a device, it must be reset for another person to use it. It's also possible to connect multiple Oculus Go devices to a single smartphone. Oculus Go can be purchased from the localized Oculus Go website and requires payment by credit card.

titleEn: (ComicsV) The Resin Crisis' Innovative Solution: Blockchain
contentEn:
Miscellaneous Thoughts on IT

(ComicsV) The Lezhin Incident: An Innovative Solution, Blockchain

Luke ・ Jan 30, 2018. 0:31

Copy URL Add Neighbor

More options for this article

1. The Troubled Webtoon Ecosystem

If we talk about the hot issues in the webtoon ecosystem recently, the Lezhin Comics incident and other issues related to a fair ecosystem would be at the top of the list. Today, they even sued another artist. Just how far is this situation going to go...?

Despite being a new startup, ComicsV is still developing its monetization features, so we've been hesitant to speak about a fair webtoon ecosystem as a player within it. However, seeing the current situation, I thought it would be better to speak up first, so I'd like to share some of my thoughts.

As ComicsV aims to be a comic technology company, we are constantly contemplating if there are "technological" solutions for almost every issue. Therefore, we've been studying "blockchain" technology, which has recently stirred up South Korea, believing it could fundamentally solve this problem. Although our study is still somewhat insufficient, I wanted to be the first to speak about our future direction and the market's development, and to revitalize the webtoon ecosystem, so I've outlined a few proposals I've considered.

2. Problems with Centralized Webtoon Platforms

First, the problems can be diagnosed as follows:

Problems of Centralized Webtoon Platforms

Although I wrote "Lezhin Comics," centralized platforms, including ours, cannot fundamentally solve the above problems either technologically or politically. The best way to fundamentally solve these issues is to transition centralized platforms to a more decentralized system. And for this method, the core technology can be "blockchain."

3. Reorganizing the Webtoon Ecosystem Using Blockchain and Decentralized Technology

Here's a summary of each point:

Solutions for the Webtoon Content Ecosystem Using Blockchain (Source: ComicsV)

First, Step 1 is to register the contract details between the artist and the platform on the blockchain. This allows artists to verify contract terms, and profit sharing can automatically occur through smart contracts directly from the payment itself, without separate settlements. Another advantage is that fees can be set very low on a global scale.

Smart contract - Wikipedia

Contents  [ hide ]  1 History 2 Implementations 3 Replicated titles and contract execution 4 Security issues 5 In popular culture 6 See also 7 References History [ edit ] The phrase "smart contracts" was coined by computer scientist Nick Szabo in 1996, and reworked over several years. Szabo's first ...

en.wikipedia.org

Step 2 is to build a reward system similar to Steemit. This allows authors, reviewers, and even celebrities to share in the platform's growth. Although, if you look closely, a significant portion of it is said to go to miners...

http://steemit.com

Step 3 is to enable individual content (comics), rather than the platform, to conduct crowdfunding. While typical comic crowdfunding is often reward-based, it could also be bond-type crowdfunding, similar to movies or animations. A similar approach is being attempted by Musicoin.

Musicoin

Share the value of music on Musicoin, a platform where creators are respected and patrons are satisfied.

www.musicoin.co

Step 4 is to move physical content to distributed servers via IPFS (InterPlanetary File System), which often accompanies blockchain technology. Although there are projects to database webtoon content, if it's only thumbnails and titles, this method would ensure no content loss even if a webtoon platform fails or disappears.

Concept of Decentralized Web (Source: ipfs.io)

The reason for disclosing the above proposals is that we hope many webtoon platforms, not just ComicsV, will consider these methods. However, the technical investment and implementation will not be easy. While ICOs are frequent recently, many companies are evaluated as technically unsound when looking at the details.

4. Technical Risks in Blockchain

The technical considerations and risks are greater than one might think. Especially in systems where existing legacy systems are running, bearing this burden is not easy, so it's likely to be operated in a hybrid manner or used only for marketing purposes. Developers are already scarce in the market, and extensive study is needed on the technical risks and pros and cons of each blockchain. If you're building it from scratch, it's impossible to know what risks lie ahead. It's also necessary to consider whether each blockchain technology has the appropriate functions, performance, and a sufficiently large network for its purpose.

One particular concern nowadays is the treatment of ICOs as a panacea for fundraising. I believe it's crucial to consider whether the company possesses sufficient technical capabilities and whether blockchain is truly the best way to solve the problem it aims to address.

We also briefly considered an ICO, but decided to focus more on the essence of the problem and its solution rather than an ICO in the coin market, which already requires economies of scale. ComicsV (I) will need to study for about another month and analyze whitepapers to find the appropriate method. Although resources are scarce in many ways, expansion is not easy if the architecture for future expansion is not designed in advance and discussed with the development team. Whether these considerations are made or not means that even if they look the same on the surface, they are not the same software. Having these concerns at a stage where billing is implemented and the business model is not yet settled might actually be an opportunity for us.

5. Evolving Blockchain Technology is Suitable for Startups

Blockchain technology is clearly a new opportunity for content companies and will be a wonderful technology that can build a new ecosystem. Perhaps it could shake up the ecosystem and solve many existing problems. However, blockchain technology is not yet a complete technology; it is evolving. Therefore, I believe startups like us have more to do in terms of building, implementing, and studying it, rather than large companies where even small system changes can have a big impact.

Furthermore, many content companies claim to be technology companies like Netflix, but due to the nature of content companies, their understanding of technology doesn't seem very high. Therefore, I believe there is widespread excessive expectation or excessive disparagement of technology. As a content player with a background as a software engineer, I intend to leverage this aspect to the fullest. Based on this, I think one approach is for a content company to transform into a technology company, and from an ecosystem perspective, into a financial company.

While exchanges are important for blockchain technology, "Gajua~" (Let's go!) isn't everything. I hope people carefully examine the opportunities and risks behind it, and I expect this technology to become a core technology that can reshape content ecosystems like webtoons.

titleEn: [Suggestion] What We Should Do More Than 5G for the 4th Industrial Revolution
contentEn:
Musings on IT

[Proposal] What needs to be done for the 4th Industrial Revolution, more than 5G

Luke ・ 2017. 11. 23. 1:19

Copy URL  Add Neighbor

Main text other functions

No matter how busy I am, I can't just leave this blog abandoned... so I'm finally going to write a post I've been meaning to. The keyword "4th Industrial Revolution" has become a hot topic for the government, and among government-led IT technologies, telecommunications always comes up. So, it seems telecom companies are subtly inserting 5G into the 4th Industrial Revolution narrative, equating the 5G era with the 4th Industrial Revolution. However, I'd like to briefly share my thoughts on the 4th Industrial Revolution as I perceive it.

What I've most keenly felt since diving into the startup scene is the customer on the ground. Because of this, I started seeing things differently than when I only read about them or was surrounded by IT experts. First, while TV and the government talk about future technologies like VR/AR, AI, and the 4th Industrial Revolution as policy agendas, I felt that for many people, these stories are too distant, and might even evoke fear or a sense of alienation. Since I brought up 5G earlier, let me tell you about the telecommunications situation I've experienced in the field: for general customers, especially young students, ajummas, and mothers, data is still not something to be used freely and lavishly. They were still searching for Wi-Fi, and begging for data was the reality. Although unlimited data plans have become cheaper, not everyone can afford them. The point I want to make first is that it's not a matter of speed like 4G or 5G, but that the communication infrastructure is not yet popularized for all customers. For them, a well-functioning Wi-Fi, even if not super fast, is more important than 5G, and being able to use 3G unlimitedly is more crucial. Why is that important for the 4th Industrial Revolution?

1. Everyone must be connected to the network.

This is because the 4th Industrial Revolution is not about network speed, but about changes in daily life, as follows:

I knew China was a country where even beggars used QR codes for donations, and when I visited recently, the network wasn't exactly smooth. But the important thing was that everyone installed apps and used them in their daily lives without hesitation. What's important is not the network, but the apps – in short, the change to a smart lifestyle. This doesn't require 5G or 4G speeds. Recognizing a QR code doesn't need a massive network. Rather than 5G, expanding the supply of unlimited 3G plans and stabilizing Wi-Fi can achieve network democratization.

As long as there are supermarket owners who bought a Galaxy S8 and get angry when you don't pay cash, we are in a worse situation than China.

2. Storage space for new apps

Nowadays, with many budget smartphones available, it's an era where everyone uses a smartphone. However, after personally helping many people install apps, I was surprised to find that many couldn't install them due to smartphone storage limitations. While sometimes this was due to photos, many people using low-capacity smartphones found that after installing a few essential apps for daily life, they couldn't install any more. Despite this, numerous pre-installed apps were occupying smartphone storage. (Pre-installed apps on budget phones are a bit much!!!)

If you use a Chinese phone, even a low-capacity one, the storage space is quite generous.

Problems and Responses to Pre-installed Smartphone Apps

The world is in the era of smartphones, and it has reached its most mature peak. Global smartphone subscribers are projected to exceed 4.5 billion by 2020, and apps, often called the "flowers" of smartphones, already have over 2 million registered in app stores. In terms of revenue, Apple has already announced that it has helped developers earn over $40 billion, boasting about its contribution. However, Apple and Google's smart mobile...

slownews.kr

Currently, new app installations are not happening smoothly, forcing startups to spend more marketing costs than in the past, and even compelling users to delete other apps or photos. Existing top apps are expanding their functionalities like an octopus, and their sizes are growing too.

To overcome this situation, users first need an environment where they can install apps, meaning securing storage space. The pre-loaded apps installed by telecom companies might need regulation, even for the sake of startups. Or, how about regulating a minimum amount of storage space to be secured?

Startups are trying to guide the public to the threshold of the 4th Industrial Revolution, but people can't even install apps. Unbelievable!

3. Need for learning about the value of paid content, services, and software

What I've noticed about paid services is that there's a huge difference between experiencing only free services initially and experiencing paid ones. However, in the software and content usage patterns of students, there's virtually no experience with paid services. In schools, it's taken for granted that educational software is distributed for free, and educational content is given away for free. Of course, schools might purchase them on their behalf.

But how would it feel if software and content used for free during school became paid after graduation? Also, for many small businesses, students, or even startups... what percentage use genuine software? When looking at government support items and projects, this aspect is hardly considered. In a way, the core companies of the 4th Industrial Revolution era are those that sell these things, yet support is directed elsewhere. Subsidies for vulnerable groups, educational institutions, and businesses for purchasing paid content, services, and software should extend to the purchasing experience. Don't just buy it for them. I also run a webtoon startup, and I feel that public awareness of content and copyright is truly at rock bottom. It seems many still believe the myth that internet businesses make money from ads if users view many pages. (That era ended long ago.)

K-Webtoons Expanding Globally… Hindered by Illegal Uploads

The 4th Industrial Revolution era is a time to pay proper money for intangible values like content, services, and software. To achieve this, the value of copyright must be protected, and the industry must grow for new innovations to emerge from it. We must remember how the Korean B2C packaged software industry and the single-volume comic book market were destroyed. You're not just shouting "born global" while abandoning Korea, are you?

4. Paperless Office

The reason I advocate for a paperless office in South Korea is not for "environmental" reasons, but for "health." This thing is going to give me cancer. This is actually about a certain word processor and ActiveX. There's a certain standard document format for government agencies, and if you don't use it, you practically can't do any government-related work. Of course, sometimes docx files are uploaded, and there are compatible office suites. I tried a compatible office app to save some money and try something new. This office app is one that government agencies can now choose to use (software).

But there was a critical problem. Sometimes documents created here would crash when opened in the office app used by government agencies, which was a fatal flaw. But the bigger problem was that the page-unit layout would break when printing, and the issue is that government agencies demand page-unit printouts.

However, fundamentally, page-unit layouts are practically difficult to match with block-unit document standards like web documents. And the issuing agency wouldn't look kindly on pages overflowing or similar issues. In the end, I've given up and am considering purchasing the existing word processor.

The biggest problem here, which I initially thought was just an issue with linking to the approval system, turned out to affect all print-based administrative processes. Simply put, print-based administrative processing itself must disappear, and documents viewed page by page must disappear.

Electronic standard documents, like web documents, only have a logical document structure with a table of contents, but no physical document structure. Blog posts look slightly different on different machines, screen sizes, or browser sizes, but there's no problem viewing the content.

In particular, public institutions are often the ones that demand word-unit line breaks... but ultimately, this problem also arises because of printing. I believe that eliminating printers is the shortcut for public institutions, or all institutions, to transform into software organizations suitable for the 4th Industrial Revolution era. Half of the ActiveX problems also stem from printing. If we do this, the entire nation's cancer will improve, and health insurance expenditures will decrease. I expect an effect greater than Moon Jae-in Care.

ps. The 4th Industrial Revolution doesn't originate from grand technologies like VR/AR/AI/5G. Ultimately, these technologies are just ingredients, and the reality is industrial change arising from meeting people and connections. (Of course, it can't happen without ingredients either.) To achieve this, fundamental changes at the societal level are needed; if only the front leads, there's a high possibility that the public will view it as someone else's problem. The 4th Industrial Revolution that can be felt truly starts with "the basics."

Lately, most of my posts seem to be about ComixV, the VR webtoon I'm working on. I recently posted about Daydream View on my blog, and perhaps because there aren't many apps for Daydream, the ComixV app has been consistently popular, almost rising to the ranks of a representative VR comic app on Google VR (Daydream).

However, in the case of Samsung Gear VR, despite being installed on far more devices, it seems to be losing momentum over time, so I'm posting about it on my blog. In fact, for a month after its initial launch, there was an unfortunate incident where it wasn't exposed in the "latest" category. After protesting to Oculus multiple times, it finally got exposure, but it seems some time has already passed...

Currently, ComixV's VR webtoons, which are on permanent display at the Bucheon Manhwa Museum, are being exhibited using Samsung Gear VR. While exhibiting, I sometimes hear people say, "I have one at home!" and often encounter situations where they ask back, "This is possible?" It seems surprisingly many people have bought a Gear VR, either as a free gift from Samsung Electronics or just for fun, and then left it gathering dust.

Perhaps the reason is that most of the games are paid, but there wasn't much to enjoy as expected, or it was just used for watching interesting videos. Therefore, I'd like to introduce the ComixV app, where you can experience familiar Korean webtoons on your Gear VR.

VR webtoons, ComixV experience video, anywhere on VR, PC, or app

1. Download

You can search for "comixv" or "코믹스브이" in the Oculus Store and download it.

The URL for the store is below.

ComixV - VR Comic / VR Webtoon

Experience webtoons vividly, VR webtoons are ComixV

www.oculus.com

2. How to Operate

The operation method is very simple. If you're a Gear VR user, you probably know that tapping selects, and swiping the touchpad forward goes to the next page, while swiping backward goes to the previous page or cancels. Easy, right? Plus, it supports the remote control for the new Gear VR, so you can view it even more conveniently.

3. Current Works

As of October 5, 2017, 6 works, totaling 15 episodes, are currently in service.

Representative works include "Wara! Convenience Store VR," a familiar title from animation and webtoons, allowing you to enjoy the experience of stepping right into a convenience store. Go Il-kwon's "Jeongamjin" lets you experience being in the middle of a battlefield during the Imjin War. Professor Choi Ho-cheol's "Strolling Through Alleys" allows you to enter the scene of the Candlelight Revolution in Gwanghwamun, and Hwanjaengi's "On the Mars" lets you encounter mysterious incidents of a Mars exploration team.

Additionally, if you view Genyu's beautiful illustrations in 360 degrees, famous characters you already know will unfold right before your eyes.

Works are continuously being updated.

4. What if you don't have Gear VR?

While it's a bit less immersive than viewing in VR, you can also watch directly on the web below.

The price of Gear VR has also dropped recently to less than 100,000 won (under 50,000 won for overseas direct purchase).

### AR as Seen by Apple and Google, Kakao's Opportunity

https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
[Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
* ・ *
2017. 6. 21. 22:52

[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=221034655416&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[** Add Neighbor**](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=221034655416&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=221034655416&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
[Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=221034655416&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

##### 1. The Meaning of VR/AR as Seen by Apple and Google

For a change, instead of talking about ComicsV, my company that deals with VR webtoons, I'd like to discuss IT, which is what I primarily used to do. As you may have already heard, Apple and Google are getting into AR. As I argued in my VR/AR report, VR and AR are essentially almost the same technology from a software technical perspective, rather than a hardware one.
And recently, I've been thinking about what VR and AR, as pursued by Apple and Google, or MR, as pursued by Microsoft, truly mean. And, though it might seem a bit out of the blue, I'd like to offer some suggestions for Kakao.

https://www.youtube.com/embed/-o7qr1NpeNI?wmode=transparent
ARKit iPhone Demo

When people think of VR and AR, most imagine wearing an HMD, but as the video above shows, they use a camera app, much like Pokémon GO. If you look closely at what Google, Apple, or MS are pursuing recently, you'll notice they are aiming for service scenarios or software platforms that scan real-world information and add virtual information to it. Ultimately, it doesn't matter if it's something you wear, a Samsung device, or an LG Electronics pad. Ah, of course, in Apple's case, they use their own hardware.
Here, "scanning real-world information" means, from an MR perspective, contemplating how to best overlay virtual information. That far, yes. However, if we think a bit further, consider AR/VR technology combined with rapidly growing AI technologies, namely image recognition, speech recognition, or various data pattern recognition technologies. What we call AR can actually include not only information from human senses but also certain real-world information that only computers can perceive. In other words, the most critical point of AR and MR is that computers can have eyes and ears, or even more senses, to analyze context, understand its meaning, and provide situation-appropriate services.
If that's a fixed ear, it's SKT's AI speaker "Aria"; if it's an eye, it's Google Photos service. And AR, MR will have these eyes and ears in real-time. Do you understand why global companies are staking their lives on this? Do you think AR/VR is just a passing technology? Before, I only spoke from the perspective of media and computing platforms, but now, even from the perspective of global service providers, I am convinced that AR/VR is not a passing trend but a business where they must stake everything and plant their flag.

##### 2. So Who in Korea? Suggestions for Kakao
What if we combine chatbots and AR in KakaoTalk? Kakao Eye

However, since I originally specialized in portal and platform planning, in my experience, this technology can be best utilized in search. While search generally brings to mind services for finding answers to questions, in the mobile era, providing relevant information at the right time or pushing predicted necessary information also falls within the scope of search. And these services are very closely related to artificial intelligence. In fact, it's safe to say that the backend of search services is entirely AI technology. While previously it was about analyzing patterns and correlations between texts, now, with AI speakers or AR/MR services equipped with "eyes," we've reached a point where we need to analyze patterns in unstructured data like images and sounds.
Kakao and Naver should not approach AR technology merely as a service for taking pretty selfies or creating games like Pokémon GO. Previously, when I lectured on the success factors of Pokémon GO, I discussed how the failure factors of older AR services included the inconvenience of launching camera apps and the hurdle of app installation due to low smartphone penetration. However, camera app launch is now so fast that it's barely noticeable, camera performance has significantly improved, and everyone has one app installed.
In Korea, that's KakaoTalk. What kind of impact would there be if an AR service activated when something was pointed at with KakaoTalk? China is already a QR code world. QR codes are, in fact, merely information expressed in an image. Kakao image search integrated into KakaoTalk? Or should we call it Kakao Eye?
First, regarding Kakao's inherent functional value, friend requests could be filtered based on facial recognition and location information, and users could add friends by taking a picture of their face using similarity comparison technology.
Furthermore, Kakao is likely to gain an effective point of contact between offline and online, which it has been pursuing with O2O.
"Try typing *** in Naver's search bar" could now be replaced by some Kakao tag. It could be included in newspaper ads, flyers, and even signboards. It could even be used for payments, and perhaps linked with Alipay in China. And the terrible UX of fast-food kiosks could be transformed, allowing orders to be placed through a conversation with a 3D chatbot, simply by scanning a Kakao tag.

{{IMG:1}}
A grid UX where all thumbnails look the same, making you feel like you have decision paralysis just by looking at them.

{{IMG:2}}
How great would it be if this came out in AR and took orders... (Is it just me who thinks so?)

The possibility that cameras, which have been used for taking selfies or pretty pictures, can be platformized is being shown by AR. It's not the time for Kakao to just use AR technology for Kakao Cheese.

{{IMG:3}}

Move like a platform, and the core competency of a platform is technology. I hope Kakao can demonstrate technological leadership.
As I'm a content platform, I focus on VR, but for general services, there's a reason to put effort into AR. AR services like these won't just stop at displaying objects; a complete AR service with a flow that recognizes objects and connects them to services will be even more crucial.

* If I were still at Naver, I would have mass-produced VR/AR service patents... If any Kakao officials see this... public ideas can also be filed within 6 months.
Now, I'm going back to prepare a new idea-based proposal for expanding our service. I have many ideas, but unlike when I was at a large company, even a provisional application is quite a burden.

### This is what the people truly wanted.

                        
                        
	                
	            
	        
        
        
        
        

    
        https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
        [Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
        
            * ・ *
            2017. 5. 19. 8:51
        
    

	[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=221009187967&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

        [Other Post Functions](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=221009187967&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
               [Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=221009187967&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
                [Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=221009187967&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
	
    

        
        
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        The talk that President Moon Jae-in would not be able to achieve unity was wrong. Winning hearts begins with empathy for anyone. Which candidate could have empathized more with the people than this?
                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                [Interview] Sign language interpreter who wiped away tears during broadcast, "At that time..." Today, during the live broadcast of the 37th anniversary of the May 18th Democratic Uprising, the sight of a sign language interpreter constantly wiping away tears was broadcast live, becoming a hot topic. We directly heard the story of Kim Hong-nam, a sign language interpreter with 18 years of experience. Reporter Ryu Ran (nany@kbs.co.kr) v.media.daum.net

http://v.media.daum.net/v/20170518194028002

                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                         I think I finally understand what the people truly wanted. It wasn't about grand promises or satiety. Just as users and planners often don't know what users truly want, I wonder if I, too, had been arrogantly misunderstanding.

 We chose a good president. He is not Roh Moo-hyun's shadow. Moon Jae-in is Moon Jae-in.  

I wanted to be a helper and a watchdog, not a fan, but if you keep doing this, it's a foul. No matter what I do, even if it's a difficult path, I must be this sincere. Is there a greater lesson than this for the people and for children?
I am a pro-government blogger.
