contentEn:
[Miscellaneous Thoughts on IT](https://blog.naver.com/PostList.naver?blogId=fstory97&categoryNo=41&from=postList)

### Qualities of Presidential Candidates Examined Through the Lens of the 4th Industrial Revolution

https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
[Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
* ・ *
2017. 4. 18. 12:00

[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220986016706&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[** Add Neighbor**](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220986016706&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[Other Post Functions](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220986016706&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220986016706&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
[Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220986016706&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

A very unique aspect of this presidential election seems to be that IT technologies have come to the forefront as the "4th Industrial Revolution." Consequently, there's talk of reviving the Ministry of Information and Communication, and with a candidate from an IT background, it seems they're trying to draw more support to their side. As I've already stated on my Facebook timeline, I left the SW Policy Research Institute, where I was directly involved in government IT policies like the 4th Industrial Revolution, to actually start a startup. Therefore, perhaps for me now, it's real-world experience, and these policies might resonate more deeply.

##### 1. The Top Policymaker Doesn't Need to Know Technical Details.

However, watching the 3D printer controversy, a thought occurred to me: does it really help for the top policymaker to know the technical details? If we were to name the biggest achievement of the Park Geun-hye administration, which faced the worst outcomes, it would be the establishment of a system for startup support and the creation of an atmosphere preparing for what is now called the 4th Industrial Revolution, thanks to mandatory software education. These days, you can easily find books on coding and software at bookstores, and some children I've met possess truly astonishing—no, frightening—software skills. I am a computer academy kid from the late 80s. Lee Going of Life Coding also created presentation materials on this, but I believe that generation of kids has actually grown into quite capable individuals in this field. I've also heard that the so-called 1st and 2nd generation venture entrepreneurs were influenced by the era when computers were introduced at KAIST and considerable freedom was given. If this current trend continues, I look forward to what the next 10 years will bring. Looking at it that way, did President Park Geun-hye really understand IT well for this situation to arise? Or could it be said that it happened precisely because she didn't? The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism being thoroughly investigated due to its ties with Choi Soon-sil might be attributed to the Yukyoung Foundation's expertise in cultural arts. Conversely, the Ministry of Future Planning felt relatively less involved given its size, which might be because it didn't fully understand IT technology. If they had understood it well and deeply intervened in startups and R&D, what would the situation be like now? The thought alone is terrifying. Anyway... despite all that, it can be said that some results were ultimately achieved. And I believe there was a lot of hidden effort from many experts and public officials. Let me ask again. Would a president who truly knows the technical details of IT do well in IT? Would a president who can technically distinguish between Active X and .exe be a good president? I won't separately explain what happens when a company CEO gets involved in coding. What's important is recognizing the direction. How well one understands the potential and direction of a technology is the ability of a manager.

##### 2. The Reality of the 4th Industrial Revolution as I See It
- Paradigm Shift in the Information Industry

So, let's talk about how well one recognizes the direction referred to as the 4th Industrial Revolution. First, what exactly is the 4th Industrial Revolution? Hmm... honestly, I still don't quite know. If you ask me to differentiate it from a software-centric society, I'd be even more clueless. In fact, a software-centric society seems like a broader concept. You're probably familiar with the 1st Industrial Revolution (agricultural) and the 2nd (industrial). If you look at Wikipedia's entry for the 3rd Industrial Revolution, it talks about manufacturing evolution, virtual goods, content, the internet, distributed power networks, and even 3D printers. Blockchain, smart grid, IoT, 3D printers... these are no different from the keywords of the 4th Industrial Revolution. The only thing missing is perhaps the AI keyword... and if that's the case, I think the Ministry of Future Planning's 'Intelligent Information Society' is more accurate. Therefore, among experts, there's a question of whether the 4th Industrial Revolution even exists. Even in Germany, said to be the origin of the 4th Industrial Revolution keyword, rumors suggest it's just 'so-so,' and in the US, the birthplace of startups and innovation, it's heard like an unknown term.

Third Industrial Revolution - Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Third Industrial Revolution Jump to: navigation, search The Third Industrial Revolution is a vision of future society foreseen by economist Jeremy Rifkin and others. Jeremy Rifkin (1945~) is a world-renowned American economist and literary critic. His works include "Entropy," "The End of Work," "The Hydrogen Economy," and "The Third Industrial Revolution," which warn against modern civilization based on a mechanical worldview and energy waste. Nationality: American # Field of activity: Economics # Place of birth: Denver, Colorado # Major works: "Entropy," "Biosphere Politics," "The End of Work," "The Biotech Century," "The Age of Access" "Water ko.wikipedia.org

https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EC%A0%9C3%EC%B0%A8_%EC%82%B0%EC%97%85_%ED%98%81%EB%AA%85

So, is there no 4th Industrial Revolution? Personally, I don't see it that way. Maybe a 3.5? Or perhaps it's more appropriate to call it the Second Information Revolution. The major paradigm hasn't changed from the 3rd Industrial Revolution. However, with the decline in network infrastructure and computing technology prices, coupled with artificial intelligence, intelligent software has truly begun to activate the 3rd Industrial Revolution. That's my personal opinion. (Compared to the 1st and 2nd, it hasn't actually been that long since we started discussing the 3rd Industrial Revolution.)
Anyway, the question is whether we're properly recognizing that direction. In my opinion, the Information Revolution can be divided into a 1st and 2nd phase.
This is one of the slides I made a while ago.

{{IMG:1}}

https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220986016706&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

This story is about how not everyone who talks about IT is talking about the same IT.
One of the reasons I bring this up is whether those who talk about IT are referring to the former or the latter.
Those who talk about the former mainly advocate for protecting the small and medium-sized enterprise software industry, especially focusing on SI and packaged software, and are resistant to the emergence of global software companies. They view MS and Google as targets for defense. Yet, they take subcontracting for software development for granted. I was genuinely surprised when I saw a certain candidate's proposal to designate the security industry as a small and medium-sized enterprise sector for the expulsion of AX. This is exactly that point.

** "Designating the security industry as a small and medium-sized enterprise sector for AX expulsion" : A certain candidate's official response regarding AX expulsion**
** (If this happens, won't Windows 10 Defender also be unusable in Korea? They said they'd lift regulations, but they're creating more.)**

They also think of developers as mere numbers and believe anyone can easily transition into a developer regardless of their work. While I respect President Kim Dae-jung, one thing I consider his worst achievement is mass-producing low-quality SW developers in academies. Professional software developers are not churned out that easily.

** "****There will be a shortage of specialized personnel in 4th Industrial Revolution fields such as AI, IoT, big data, and 3D printing. We will train 100,000 experts by educating youth and middle-aged individuals." : A certain candidate's 4th Industrial Revolution pledge**

What's more important is that the core of the 4th Industrial Revolution (3.5 Information Revolution) is innovating one's domain by learning software within existing work. If the idea is to churn out 100,000 people from academies and get them re-employed, then it means treating Korean SW developers as mere components once again.
**This is a policy that has regressed compared to the Park Geun-hye administration, which advocated for nationwide SW education and dissemination.**

I won't name any candidate, but I wrote this out of sheer frustration that someone who was supposedly in this field would put forward such pledges. That's why some company's stock price seems to have doubled in a few months. Is this the return of MB...?

{{IMG:2}}

https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220986016706&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

##### 3. Power to the People, Participation and Decentralization

Times have changed. Power has been decentralized, and it's an era of collaboration, co-development, where expertise in various fields is leveraged to create integrated outcomes. Software is no longer specialized knowledge; it's a part of life. 3D printers will likely become the same. Who even looks at you these days if you say you have a Word certificate? But being good at creating digital documents is a different story. That is the future position of software.
I was actually surprised by how excellent a certain website was, run by the person who mentioned 3D printers. I even imagined how great it would be if such a site could be linked to an actual government policy platform.

[Moon Jae-in 1st Street, Korea's First Policy Shopping Mall www.moon1st.com](http://www.moon1st.com/)

The term '4th Industrial Revolution' isn't what's important. What's important is value. When planning services, I used to hear it constantly: "Find customer value, not what you want to do." That's what I want to say to all presidential candidates.

By the way... I like Yoo Seong-min's startup policies the most. I hope good policies are continuously benchmarked by all.

contentEn:

### Virtual Reality Technology to Understand Humans and Bring Light to People with Disabilities

	                
	            
	        
        
        
        
        

    
        https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
        [Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
        
            * ・ *
            2017. 1. 2. 16:51
        
    

	[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220900786345&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

            [** Add Neighbor**](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220900786345&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
	
        [Other Body Functions](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220900786345&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
               [Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220900786345&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
                [Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220900786345&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
	
    

        
        
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        **This column was **[**written at the request of Smart Choice**](http://www.smartchoice.or.kr/smc/smartreport/smarttalkview.do?sm_Seq=6586&searchType=tc&searchKeyword=&pg=1)**. The original can be found at the link below.**

Recently, interest in virtual reality and augmented reality has been hotter than ever. At first glance, virtual reality and augmented reality devices might seem like simple gadgets that you put on your head, track your gaze, and project two images. However, if you actually try to create a service, you'll encounter numerous problems.
 
Those who have experienced virtual reality will easily recall the dizziness caused by device performance issues. However, this problem is likely to be resolved over time, so it's not as big a concern as you might think.
 
Instead, the recent focus in virtual reality seems to be on identifying human physical and cognitive characteristics to determine how VR can approach people more effectively and without resistance, and what kind of user experience services or content should provide in a 3D spatial computing environment.
 
And the characteristics of these technologies show a tendency to understand humans better.
 
Virtual reality displays are not pursuing higher resolution or higher image quality, which TVs and monitors have traditionally aimed for, but rather are grappling with how to effectively convey focus and distance to people. Flat-panel displays like TVs and monitors have ultimately been products of two-dimensional painting. However, virtual reality demands three-dimensional objects, like sculptures. This is why virtual reality technologies have begun to fundamentally examine the understanding of light and the human eye.
 
For example, eye-tracking technology, predicted to be integrated into VR HMDs, aims to improve perceived performance by increasing the resolution where the user is looking and lowering the resolution in the remaining areas. This is an application of the fact that human vision is similar to video processing and has uneven resolution.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
	        
	            
	            
	                
							

https://www.youtube.com/embed/VHXx7XTPULE?wmode=transparent

	                
	                
	                    	FOVE VR Headset : Eye Play the Piano Video
	                
	            
	        
	    
    
	

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Identifying these cognitive limitations of humans is collectively referred to as human factors, and technologies based on human factors demand a deeper understanding of the human body.
 
While technologies like medical devices were previously used solely for the purpose of treating the human body, human factors technologies, gaining attention due to the virtual reality market, are new technologies that liberate humans or augment their abilities.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

		
			
				
					
						{{IMG:1}}
							
								
									 Magic Leap possesses 'Photonics Light Field' technology, which naturally renders virtual images. A small projector embedded in the device shines light onto a transparent lens, adjusting the direction of light reaching the retina to make virtual objects appear like real-world objects.
								
							
					
				
			
		

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Furthermore, it is expected that these technologies will eventually pave the way to bring light to people with physical disabilities. Magic Leap, which garnered significant investment from Google and became a hot topic, is said to possess technology that projects light directly into the eye to display 3D objects. This light essentially transforms virtual information into perceivable data, beginning to quantify human-perceived information three-dimensionally. If this technology further develops to analyze not just the front of the eye but also the processing methods of the nerves at the back, creating artificial eyes will become entirely possible, bringing good news to those who have lost their sight.
 
Robot technology has already evolved into technologies that augment human strength, and it is expected that virtual reality's five-senses technology will also develop into technologies that understand and assist the missing senses of people with disabilities.
 
Humanity's greatest value lies not in the body, but in thought. This is what allowed Homo sapiens to conquer the Earth. However, we still primitively see physical deficiencies leading to social discrimination. While we cannot see as well as a hawk, hear as well as a dog, or run as fast as a cheetah, those among us who cannot see, hear, or run as well as the average person face economic and social discrimination. And this has been evidence that the evolutionary mechanism of animals is still valid for us.
 
However, just as IT technologies have done in the past, virtual reality technology is expected not only to expand our senses and strength but also to be a technology that will liberate many who have been discriminated against.

### [Sseoljeon MB Version Mir Youth Startup Foundation] The Truth Needs More Caution

	                
	            
	        
        
        
        
        

    
        https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
        [Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
        
            * ・ *
            2016. 10. 28. 13:32
        
    

	[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

            [** Add Neighbor**](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
	
        [Other Body Functions](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
               [Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
                [Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
	
    

        
        
        
    

    
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        These days, the whole country is in an uproar because of a shaman. As a political progressive, I was drinking beer, waiting for 8 o'clock, and looking forward to Sseoljeon this week. However, I was a bit disappointed that the Choi Soon-sil case was postponed to next week. Instead, the first topic was the Youth Startup Foundation, which was pointed out as another Mir. I wondered if it was a warning from JTBC towards the non-Park faction. 
                    
                
            
        
    

    

		
			
				
					
						{{IMG:1}}
					
				
			
		

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        
**However, although I also like Sseoljeon, after seeing a post on Facebook today, I am writing this to share the correct facts. That Youth Startup Foundation, where is it? It was D.CAMP, the oasis for startups.**
****
                    
                
            
        
    

    

	
		
			
				
					 	
						{{IMG:2}}
					

https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

				
			
		
	

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        ******That's not that kind of place...**

It's the place run by Director Kim Kwang-hyun, well-known as Blogger Sphere and "Gwangpari" in IT. I've been there a few times. If it's that place, 5 billion won in operating expenses is understandable. 

                    
                
            
        
    

    

		
			
				
					
						{{IMG:3}}
					
				
			
		

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        But, Lawyer Jeon Won-chaek. The D.CAMP I know **does a lot of things. ㅜㅜ**

                    
                
            
        
    

    

	
		
			
				
					 	
						{{IMG:4}}
					

https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

				
			
		
	

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Searching for D.CAMP on Naver News yields 2,990 articles.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

		
			
				
					
						{{IMG:5}}
					
				
			
		

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        If you look at the D.CAMP tag on VentureSquare, a total of 99 activities have been uploaded since April 1, 2013.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                [D.CAMP Tag - VentureSquare This is the article list page for the D.CAMP tag on VentureSquare. www.venturesquare.net](http://www.venturesquare.net/tag/%eb%94%94%ec%ba%a0%ed%94%84)
                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Moreover, D.CAMP is located in the middle of expensive Gangnam, as most IT startups use Gangnam as their forward base. It's impossible for it not to incur costs. However, startups are inherently short on every penny, so all events held where they gather are conducted without pomp and circumstance. I've seen them doing so and people supporting such events late into the night. Startup spaces never turn off their lights, operating 24 hours a day.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

	
		
			
				
					{{IMG:6}}
				[View Map](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#bSize){{IMG:7}}{{IMG:8}}{{IMG:9}}{{IMG:10}}{{IMG:11}}{{IMG:12}}{{IMG:13}}{{IMG:14}}{{IMG:15}}{{IMG:16}}{{IMG:17}}{{IMG:18}}{{IMG:19}}{{IMG:20}}{{IMG:21}}{{IMG:22}}{{IMG:23}}{{IMG:24}}{{IMG:25}}{{IMG:26}}{{IMG:27}}3km{{IMG:28}}{{IMG:29}}{{IMG:30}}© NAVER Corp.[More](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)[/OpenStreetMap](http://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright)

##### Map Data

[x](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)© NAVER Corp.[/OpenStreetMap](http://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright)
				
					
						
							D.CAMP
						
							551 Seolleung-ro, Gangnam-gu, Seoul
					
					
						[Phone](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
					
					[View Details](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220847624854&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#end)
				
				
			
		
	

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Looking at [DCamp's 2015 performance](https://www.google.co.kr/url?sa=t&rct=j&q=&esrc=s&source=web&cd=2&cad=rja&uact=8&ved=0ahUKEwj-lu7w1PzPAhUQh7wKHU9wCUoQFgglMAE&url=http%3A%2F%2Fdcamp.kr%2Fevent%2Fget_ev_source%3Fev%3D33%26file%3D2015%25EB%2585%2584%2520%25EC%259E%25AC%25EB%258B%25A8%25EC%2582%25AC%25EC%2597%2585%25EC%258B%25A4%25EC%25A0%2581.pdf%26db%3D1&usg=AFQjCNFP9tMMEKDD1N1lKf9EErfUceRIcA&sig2=U9vN_O0aOg6f92MvjArfQA&bvm=bv.136811127,d.dGc),

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                [www.google.co.kr](https://www.google.co.kr/url?sa=t&rct=j&q=&esrc=s&source=web&cd=2&cad=rja&uact=8&ved=0ahUKEwj-lu7w1PzPAhUQh7wKHU9wCUoQFgglMAE&url=http%3A%2F%2Fdcamp.kr%2Fevent%2Fget_ev_source%3Fev%3D33%26file%3D2015%25EB%2585%2584%2520%25EC%259E%25AC%25EB%258B%25A8%25EC%2582%25AC%25EC%2597%2585%25EC%258B%25A4%25EC%25A0%2581.pdf%26db%3D1&usg=AFQjCNFP9tMMEKDD1N1lKf9EErfUceRIcA&sig2=U9vN_O0aOg6f92MvjArfQA&bvm=bv.136811127,d.dGc)
                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Out of a cumulative investment of 130.6 billion won, 75 billion won was invested, and the number of invested companies reached 531. In addition, they hold a demo day once a month, providing office space to 11 companies and investing in 8 companies out of 15 startups. It would be strange if it didn't cost that much.

 This information is all available with a single internet search. It's an organization known in the startup industry for working hard... Moreover, Center Director Kim Kwang-hyun is somewhat (?) left-leaning, even participating in anti-Wall Street financial protests. 

 In the startup industry, the general consensus after watching yesterday's Sseoljeon (a talk show) is that the stray bullet hit the wrong target.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

		
			
				
					
						{{IMG:31}}
					
				
			
		

    

		
			
				
					
						{{IMG:32}}
					
				
			
		

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Although the creative economy has become an object of ridicule due to this incident, there are companies, startups, and individuals who have benefited, grown, and achieved their dreams thanks to policies implemented by the previous government, and who have wholeheartedly supported these efforts.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

		
			
				
					
						{{IMG:33}}
					
				
			
		

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        The kind of work described below simply cannot be managed with a small number of staff and a single professional advisory board. How broad is the startup field, and how many things are needed? Can it be done with a small number of staff and one advisory board? Startups are small in terms of personnel, but they can move quickly at scale by using the shared resources of these startup camps.

If you want to know more about their activities, the article below summarizes it well.
                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                [[Visit to a Startup Support Space] A Startup Workshop Where Youth Gather, ② D.CAMP | IT DongA it.donga.com](http://it.donga.com/22182/)
                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                [Kwangpari says 'Go for it' at D.CAMP Pizza Day. This is Kwangpari's blog, which easily delivers global technology (IT) news. kwang82.hankyung.com](http://kwang82.hankyung.com/2015/05/blog-post_21.html)
                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Although the creative economy was a franchise of the Park Geun-hye administration, regardless of its name, the meaningful efforts of many people have contributed significantly to the startup ecosystem. It's regrettable that even that is becoming an object of ridicule all at once. I ask JTBC to be more careful and handle this part cleanly. It's truly unfortunate that such a mistake was made at such a critical time.

### [Electric Vehicles and Solar Power] Is Energy Independence Possible?

https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
[Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
* ・ *
2016. 10. 11. 10:35

[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220833241645&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220833241645&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

I am actually an IT specialist, not an expert in electric vehicles and solar power. However, by combining a few facts I've recently heard, I believe these two technologies will significantly change the way we live, which is why I'm writing these posts. Many people have been negative about electric vehicles, saying that the era of internal combustion engine cars still has a long way to go. This was attributed to the cartel of oil companies, the resistance of the internal combustion engine ecosystem, and the still-insufficient technology of electric vehicles.

##### 1. The whole world is moving towards electric vehicles.

But... a shocking piece of news recently emerged: Germany, the birthplace of BMW and Mercedes-Benz, declared it would no longer produce internal combustion engine cars.

[Germany plans to ban internal combustion engine vehicles from 2030. Germany's Federal Council passed a resolution to ban diesel and gasoline internal combustion engine vehicles after 2030, Spiegel reported on the 8th. The resolution passed by the German Federal Council www.huffingtonpost.kr](http://www.huffingtonpost.kr/2016/10/10/story_n_12423264.html)

And Germany's will soon becomes Europe's will. As I mentioned in a previous post, I've talked about how China, the world's largest market, is strongly driving electric vehicles.

Tesla-beating Chinese EV 'BYD': 10 facts. It's not a lingerie brand. This company is a Chinese electric car manufacturer. And it sold the most electric cars last year. Why not Tesla Motors? Indeed. While Tesla dominated all global media, a Chinese company called BYD was quietly increasing its market share in the EV market. Let's uncover all of BYD's secrets today. - BYD website 1. BYD surpasses Tesla and Nissan [2015 EV Sales Ranking - Green Car Report] In 2015, the company that sold the most pure electric vehicles was not Tesla, which constantly makes headlines, but thegear.co.kr

http://thegear.co.kr/12259

While Tesla is often considered the be-all and end-all of electric vehicles, it was actually a kind of trigger, and it's clear that the global automotive market is moving towards electric vehicles. Hyundai's Ioniq Electric, launched in June 2016, has already surpassed 1,000 cumulative sales in Korea alone, a result incomparable to the 650 hydrogen cars sold in 17 countries so far.

##### 2. The world is more strongly driving eco-friendly carbon policies.

Behind this lies the climate change crisis and the desire of urban dwellers for a cleaner life due to increased income. There was news recently that the concentration of carbon dioxide had exceeded the critical threshold of 400ppm, possibly reaching an irreversible level, and the strong typhoons and hurricanes that have plagued the world recently are widely believed to be due to climate change. It is already a proven fact that tropical cyclones become stronger as the Earth gets hotter, and this year's controversy over progressive electricity rates and powerful typhoons all indicate that this year was record-breakingly hot.
Global warming is being blamed as the main culprit for the heat that the Korea Meteorological Administration couldn't even predict. As seen in the recent controversy over luxury apartments in Busan, many coastal areas are home to the world's wealthy neighborhoods. I once saw a documentary that even discussed an enormous plan to block the Strait of Gibraltar to prevent the submersion of Mediterranean coastal cities.
Thus, the warming of the Earth is a given, and carbon dioxide emissions from coal and thermal power are pointed to as the main culprits. Industrial emissions currently rank first, followed by internal combustion engine vehicles like cars. Furthermore, diesel cars, also implicated in the emission of toxic substances like NOX, received a critical hit from the Volkswagen Gate scandal and were identified as the main cause of fine dust, which threatens health in the closest proximity, rising hundreds of times near roads. (These days, I strictly forbid my children from opening car windows on urban roads.)
It is clear as day that eco-friendly carbon policies and green trade barriers based on them will solidify globally, especially among powerful developed nations. For export-oriented South Korea, green is one of the mountains to overcome.
And, in fact, it is somewhat known that the US government's support played a role in Tesla's growth.

##### 3. Solar-centric Electrical Infrastructure Policy with Electric Vehicles

Many who oppose electric vehicles point to the progressive tax due to increased electricity consumption and the need for expanding nuclear power generation. However, Tesla is also pushing solar energy projects, proposing a distributed generation system and a method of charging electric vehicles at night with electricity generated during the day, unlike the centralized generation system of the past. In Korea, solar power facilities used with ESS (Energy Storage System) battery packs are said to be given quite high incentives, and for detached houses, installing solar facilities allows for air conditioning use without worrying about progressive taxes, and simultaneously enjoying electric vehicle charging with incomparable economic benefits.
Of course, such energy policies are not yet widely adopted in Korea, so only those running pilot projects are largely benefiting.
However, I wonder if KEPCO (Korea Electric Power Corporation) has the capacity to respond if these policies spread, and whether the current system is adequate. This is because KEPCO's profits from household electricity could rapidly worsen, and from the perspective of a privatized KEPCO, investing in solar power to worsen profits would be a strange situation. Therefore, rather than hoping for KEPCO's own change, I believe a stronger policy-driven initiative is needed.
Those who say 'solar power is impossible' have decreased significantly these days...
It's not impossible, but rather requires sequential application. The same goes for electric vehicles. We cannot suddenly replace all cars with electric vehicles. No matter how popular they are, we cannot produce that many. Cars and power infrastructure are not cell phones.
Germany has strongly promoted solar and wind power, to the point where electricity is surplus in summer, sometimes even leading to temporary negative charges. The statement 'Korea can't do it' loses its persuasiveness when looking at Germany's case, and Germany's strong energy policy seems to be the reason behind the announcement of ending internal combustion engines by 2030.
I hope that the government and KEPCO will not just focus on meeting current increasing demand, but will more strongly consider eco-friendly power policies from a long-term perspective of Korea's future economic infrastructure. This is not about overturning everything with a revolution right now; it's about realistic discussions.

##### 4. Is Energy Independence Possible?

Looking further ahead, is energy independence truly possible? Replacing the energy used in industry with solar power will likely not be easy. However, considering that energy has been a reason for human wars, I see solar power as an energy of peace and the sole starting point for having infinite energy for the first time. That's why, although it's currently a dream, extreme sci-fi imaginings like the Dyson Sphere, a structure surrounding the sun, have also emerged.

[다이슨 스피어 namu.wiki](https://namu.wiki/w/%EB%8B%A4%EC%9D%B4%EC%8A%A8%20%EC%8A%A4%ED%94%BC%EC%96%B4)

A prime success story of solar power is Mars' Oppy (Opportunity). This rover, built 13 years ago when feature phones with less than 1000mAh batteries were common, can hardly be called cutting-edge technology. It was planned to operate for 90 days, but it's still moving after 13 years! (The ultimate in solar efficiency!) This is an incredible solar power system showing nearly 5,000% ROI.

{{IMG:1}}

https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220833241645&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

We all remember those famous first words spoken by an astronaut on the surface of Mars: one small step fo- HOLY SHIT LOOK OUT I GOT SOME KIND OF DRILL! Get back to the ... [unintelligible] ... [signal lost] 

..Translation (A comic suggesting Opportunity didn't just perform miracles but evolved into something else??)..

2010: Six years later, Spirit stopped, but Opportunity is still working. / What an amazing rover!
2015: It's been 11 years, wow. / Wasn't it only supposed to work for 90 days? / This is getting weird.
2025: Its battery is completely disconnected, so how is it working? / Considering what Opportunity did to the Mars 2020 rover, we might never know why.
2450: All places touched by light are our domain. / What about that dark place? / That's Opportunity's land. We must not go there. [5]
Comment: We all remember those famous first words spoken by an astronaut who landed on Mars: "This is a small step for me- SHIT watch out! That thing has a drill! Get back quickly... [unintelligible]... [connection lost]"

Recently, NASA has been seriously considering warp drive, and Elon Musk is planning to colonize Mars, so I wonder if the day will come when these are no longer dreams but reality. With infinite energy and intelligent machines superior to humans, what challenges will a future society, where a warming Earth is the biggest problem, pose to us? This is no longer imagination but the reality for our children, and it seems the time has come for policymakers to also consider these issues.

### Start of the Kim Young-ran Act and Hyundai Motor's Recall Concealment

	                
	            
	        
        
        
        
        

    
        https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
        [Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
        
            * ・ *
            2016. 9. 28. 10:09
        
    

	[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220822737117&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

##### 1. First Day of Kim Young-ran Act Implementation

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                         Today is the first day the Kim Young-ran Act comes into effect. I also received in-house training yesterday regarding the Kim Young-ran Act. As it happens, I am in a position where I am subject to the Kim Young-ran Act... Since this year, I've been occasionally asked to give external lectures, and there was one lecture that would have exceeded the standards of the Kim Young-ran Act, which was enacted today. (Since it was in the past, it's not illegal.) 
For reference, bloggers are not considered media under media law, so they are not subject to the Kim Young-ran Act. From the outset, a blogger's fees are not at a level that would violate the Kim Young-ran Act, and expenses and gifts for official promotional events do not fall under the Kim Young-ran Act. I learned this yesterday during training. Currently, those most concerned seem to be star lecturers or company representatives who also hold professorships, finding themselves in an ambiguous position. Some people around me are considering stepping down from their adjunct professor roles, and it makes me wonder if this is the right path for the professionalization of the education sector.

The Kim Young-ran Act seems to minimize unconscious public power abuse and provides a legal way to refuse the bad behavior of some media outlets. While there might be a quantitative reduction in the restaurant industry as some claim, I believe it's a good direction because I don't think general, commoner-friendly restaurants under 30,000 won have much to worry about. The entertainment culture prevalent in Korea has obscured many public affairs and created indebted relationships, leading to significant communication costs. In that regard, I support the Kim Young-ran Act for its potential to revolutionize this. The Kim Young-ran Act, also known as the 'Dutch Pay Law,' is, in my opinion, correct in its aim for social transparency and the right path.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        

##### 2. [Hyundai Motor Gate] Whistleblower Confession of Recall Concealment

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        However, today, a post related to Hyundai Motor's recall caught my eye on my timeline.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Hello. 
I want to inform many people about the 'Hyundai-Kia Motors Recall Concealment.' My respected father made the difficult choice of becoming a 'public whistleblower.' No, he had no other choice. My father has been working as an engine expert at Hyundai-Kia Motors for the past 25 years. While working in the Quality Strategy Team, he became aware of safety-related manufacturing defects and raised concerns internally, but the only response he received was coercion into illegal practices.
You might be able to temporarily deceive customers by 'pulling the wool over their eyes.' However, if we continue to hush up and overlook these issues, despite many problems directly related to life already occurring, it will only lead to bigger problems. Even at this moment, countless Hyundai-Kia vehicles are driving on the roads. No one knows who on the road – myself, my parents, siblings, friends – might become a victim of this problem. 
Although related content has been reported through various media outlets such as Kyunghyang Shinmun (2016.09.23), MBC (2016.09.25), and Yonhap News (2016.09.27), due to powerful media lobbying, despite numerous page views and comments, it is being removed from main news sections on Naver, Daum, etc., and even articles are being deleted.
From a family's perspective, it's true that we have many worries, but our family trusts and supports my father's great decision for the well-being of all citizens. As a Hyundai man's family, my sister and I were able to study in a good environment thanks to the company my father diligently worked for. Therefore, we hope that Hyundai-Kia Motors can seize this last opportunity to regain the trust of its loyal customers, minimize recall costs, and promote long-term company development.
I hope my respected father's courage shines brightly. I also sincerely thank the many people who have supported us through comments and posts. Please help spread the word to more people by sharing widely! 

MinJee Kim (2016-09-27) Facebook Timeline
                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                [MinJee Kim - Hello. I want to inform many people about the 'Hyundai-Kia Motors Recall Concealment'... | Facebook www.facebook.com](https://www.facebook.com/mimmimjee/posts/1200031633371296)
                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        This is actually as shocking as Volkswagen's Dieselgate. Moreover, considering the number of cars sold domestically, the scope is even larger. Furthermore, if it's a safety issue rather than an environmental one, it's even more serious. Hyundai and Kia Motors are already losing the trust of the public, and the steady rise in the proportion of foreign cars likely contributed to this.
One article wrote that Hyundai might be caught by Kia, calling it a crisis, but the real crisis is that imported cars have grown by over 150% since 2010.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                {{IMG:1}}
                
                    
                        http://auto.daum.net/review/read.daum?articleid=225011&bbsid=27

Amidst all this, far from restoring trust, with events like the absurd i30 drift demonstration and even whistleblowers coming forward, Hyundai Motor's credibility seems to be falling endlessly. When buying an expensive car, people no longer buy it based solely on advertisements. While I know that large corporations like Samsung Electronics and Hyundai Motor wield immense power through advertising spending in the media, if they are indeed controlling the media as current suspicions suggest (a common theme in dramas), it seems they are only worsening the situation.
The implementation of the Kim Young-ran Act is also a warning from the public to the media. It is hoped that the media will become more transparent and fulfill its inherent role. I sincerely hope that fair articles will be published. As a consumer who drives a Hyundai car, and given the blog's position as an alternative media, I thought it would be good to inform more people, which is why I am making this post.
And I hope Hyundai Motor will also provide a forthright explanation.
Although I have written several critical posts about Hyundai Motor, I do not doubt Hyundai Motor's technological prowess or its production capabilities. The IONIQ electric car, which recently began production and sales, also seems like a very good car, and I have been watching it closely.
Amidst this, the eruption of such a "gate" marks a time when Hyundai Motor is being put to the test by the public.
Currently, Hyundai Motor is indeed in a "crisis." It is time to re-evaluate its ranks, both internally and externally. Looking at recent global situations, even the largest companies can collapse in an instant. I, too, had a somewhat critical view of Nokia, but I never expected it to fall so completely.

Additionally, I am leaving links to related media articles. Just because something has been done as a custom doesn't make it okay. I believe it's time to think that if we don't move forward now, we will perish.

[2. Hyundai Motor, Mysterious Engine Recently, a Hyundai Motor employee reported to 2580. There is a defect in cars equipped with Hyundai Motor's so-called ‘Theta engine’. It starts with metallic noise, and in severe cases, a hole in the engine wall... news.naver.com](http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=214&aid=0000675196&sid1=001)

They refuted the whistleblower's claims point by point for each specific issue. With both sides' arguments clashing, the truth battle is expected to continue. ■YF Sonata Theta 2 media.daum.net

### The Respected and Feared Chairman Jack Ma and Chinese Companies

	                
	            
	        
        
        
        
        

    
        https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
        [Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
        
            * ・ *
            2016. 9. 5. 15:35
        
    

	[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220805310466&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

            [** Add Neighbor**](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220805310466&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
	
        [Other Post Functions](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220805310466&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
               [Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220805310466&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
                [Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220805310466&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
	
    

        
        
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                         When we talk about IT success stories, we often dream of a 20-something genius leading the world with groundbreaking items and technology. Representative examples include Bill Gates, Steve Jobs, and Zuckerberg. However, the success stories in Asia's IT sector seem somewhat different.
 Asian stories seem to have more patience embedded in them. This is true for the life story of SoftBank's Chairman Masayoshi Son and Alibaba's Chairman Jack Ma. Similarly, most domestic IT success stories have gone through periods of patience, growing by refining existing or foreign ideas and adapting and expanding them to local conditions, rather than relying on exceptionally brilliant new ideas.
 While there are geniuses in Asian success stories, there are also teams and organizations. This leads me to wonder if Asia is a different society from the individualistic West.
 Amidst this, news came that Chairman Jack Ma was stepping down from his company. Alibaba, so successful, and it hasn't been long since its IPO – why would its chairman resign? It's truly puzzling.
                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                [[Super Rich] This person quit as president before turning 50. For the company [Herald Economy = Super Rich Team Reporter Yoon Hyun-jong] On May 10, 2013, a 'special performance' was held in Hangzhou, China, where Alibaba's headquarters is located. It was for founder Jack Ma's ... news.naver.com](http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=016&aid=0001112106&sid1=001)
                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        Alibaba reportedly has its own "executive retirement system." It states that executives can apply for retirement if their current age combined with their tenure at the company exceeds 60 years. In some ways, this seems to align with the "labor reform" advocated by the government, but what's most different is that it overturns the notion that executives and CEOs were excluded from the labor reforms we've discussed so far.
 Furthermore, this rule is said to prevent the company from falling into the hands of unqualified successors. This is starkly different from the situation in domestic conglomerates, where rumors of management succession openly sway stock prices. What's more surprising is that not only Alibaba but also companies like Haier, Tencent, and Huawei are preparing or implementing similar systems. 
 Among the executive retirements at Alibaba, a notable case was that of Zhang Ying, one of Alibaba's 12 founding members and Jack Ma's wife, who resigned in 2008. The reason for her resignation was reportedly that employees viewed her as the chairman's wife rather than by her official position.
 This seems to clearly show how Jack Ma and his wife view Alibaba. For them, Alibaba was not "my company" but an organization they built together that needed to develop. In contrast, many Korean founders often seem to place individuals above the organization and tend to view it as one person's property.  Although the very reason for the existence of joint-stock companies was to separate the company as an independent entity, not personal property, thereby creating today's economic system, many Korean companies still hold pre-modern ideas. I wonder if this is why they fail to fully leverage the advantages of a joint-stock company.
 As a Korean myself, I find such actions surprising and remarkable. It might be a very natural measure if one prioritizes the organization even as a representative. And, on the other hand, it makes me feel a bit scared.
 I once heard that China should not be viewed as an Eastern country. From Korea's perspective, China should be seen as equivalent to a Western country, not a Confucian one. Chinese people, it was said, think much more Western than Koreans.
 I'm not sure if having this country, with its large market, power, and capabilities, next to Korea is a blessing or a threat. But what's clear is that they exist, and just as Korea practiced "sadaejuui" (serving the great) towards China in the past, their strengths are worth learning from.
 Looking at the recent crises in the shipbuilding and shipping industries, it seems that even large corporations are not safe. In this situation, I believe Korea's competitiveness should be sought elsewhere, not in the large corporations that modern Korean economy has built.

titleEn: It's not Megalia that's important
contentEn:
**This post will not have comments or discussions. Discussions about Megal will proceed below. Please refer to the related link within the post below for the reason.**[**http://fstory97.blog.me/2207823071**](http://fstory97.blog.me/2207823071)

http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/2207823071
                                [**The Future of Korean Internet, Not the Punishment of Megal** I'd like to re-organize the Megalia issue on my blog. The operating principles announced on my blog on August 3, 2016... blog.naver.com](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/2207823071)

It seems I have something to add after writer Lee Seon-wook's article, so I'm writing again.

http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=006&aid=0000082001&sid1=001
                                [**Megalian Firing Controversy? This is Not a Problem of Misogyny** [Contribution] Selective justice and the value of progress... Extremists should not represent our beliefs [Lee Seon-ok, Writer for Media Today] (From the community site Megalia4... news.naver.com](http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=006&aid=0000082001&sid1=001)

1. The post I previously wrote as a 'Megal Support Declaration' was actually about the desires within me.

Regarding the meaning of the post where I previously declared support for Megal, I actually don't know Megal well. I wasn't a member there, nor do I agree with the 'trashy' posts they talk about. (I've already written about this in the relevant content.) However, there's another reason why I wrote such a provocative title at the time. **It is a confession that Megal and Ilbe exist within me.** This is to talk about the instincts and desires that everyone possesses, and I say this with the hope that netizens' anger will be discussed in a more constructive direction.

First, let's talk about R-rated content. I don't know much about women, but for men, there are porn videos they've probably seen at least once... These contents often contain misogynistic elements. Conversely, though I don't particularly like it, BL (Boys' Love) content, which women enjoy, often contains misandristic elements. This is essentially about having some sexual objectification and violent fantasies towards the other. While it's possible to express this well literarily, I agree that such adult content is not good for teenagers. So, what I want to say is that desires, like Ilbe and Megal, are inherent in everyone. And I believe there needs to be a space to resolve or at least properly enjoy them. Provided, of course, with adult verification. I think this is necessary for both women and men.

2. But Spaces Where Desires Are Expressed in a Distorted Way

However, **the problem is that spaces like Megal and Ilbe are where desires are expressed and consumed in a distorted way.** Furthermore, a more serious problem is that children can join and view them. Expressing one's desires is actually never a pleasant thing. It's easy to despise each other, and often the target is not a real person but content. It is a clear error to think that enjoying porn will turn someone into a rapist. Just as enjoying BL content doesn't lead to kidnapping middle school students. (Oh, of course, I'm not suggesting it should be allowed for teenagers. This is about adults for now.)

In fact, I believe Lezhin Comics has grown into a content consumption site that plays such a role to some extent. The same goes for subcultures like light novels that are consumed recently.

But... what's surprising is that such content has been expressed unfiltered through communities, fueling each other's emotions, and it even feels like we've reached a point where people can't distinguish between content and reality. If that applies to the administrators, it's even more serious.

Here, I want to talk about DC (DC Inside), not Megal. As I mentioned, my online life started with PC communication, and a certain bulletin board from PC communication became DC, and I heard that it later moved towards sites like Utdae and Ilbe. Considering that era, several assumptions can be made. In the early days, it was a platform teeming with adult men. Surprisingly, it was mainly composed of highly educated individuals. Therefore, they maintained a certain line regarding subculture or their lewd jokes. However, recently, women have emerged as a significant force on the internet, and even children and seniors have joined in, making it no longer a network enjoyed only by university students but by the entire nation.

Therefore, this means that these communities are more likely to cross that line. Moreover, it seems that communities have begun to openly display social conflicts, which is their inherent nature. Once again, I am not talking about Megal or Ilbe.

3. Will Burying Megal Be Okay? I Think Megal Might Just Be the Beginning

More importantly, how can we control the monsters lurking within us or on the internet, Megal and Ilbe?

In this situation, let me ask again. **Will burying Megal end it? Will destroying Lezhin Comics end it? I don't think so. Rather, I see this situation as an opportunity. Is Megal not okay, but DC galleries or Ilbe are? No. Is there any guarantee that Utdae won't be corrupted?**

Who monitors large communities, and who regulates them? The National Intelligence Service? Or who regulates the level of your comments? Should we bring in Chinese personnel for pre-screening? It's not such a simple issue, but a very important one.

I think it's better that Megal has become a social issue without much trouble now. If left as is, someday people might discuss bombing the Blue House on DC, or plot gang rape and human trafficking incidents on Ilbe.

There's no law saying that Korea won't become like Europe. If firearms were allowed in Korea, I actually think it would have already happened. The important thing is that current community structures deepen conflicts, strengthen confirmation bias, and make people think there's nothing to fear when acting as a group. It even makes me think of Japan's Kamikaze.

Therefore, a higher level of discussion is needed now. To prevent the birth of second and third Megals, mirroring, and various 'bugs.' I want to talk about that situation now.

As I mentioned, I don't know much about Megal. It's hard to know the background of a community with such a long history unless you've been actively involved for a long time. In fact, I'm not very interested. **The important thing is that Megalian created the currently enraged people, but in reality, all of this seems to be a phenomenon created by the Korean internet. Was DC the culprit from the start? To say so, there are too many new people who have entered the network.**

I feel that the confirmation bias created by social networks and communities, the diversification of user demographics, and the deepening of social conflicts in Korean society are appearing more easily online. I do want to bring up the topic of regulation, but I'd rather put it aside for now, as my thoughts are still shallow at this point. It seems more thought is needed.

**Attachment. I hadn't written this because it seemed like a shallow and clumsy alternative, but since some people were curious about my thoughts, I'm adding what was on my mind. (If I've thrown a stone, I should offer an alternative. However, if I put too much effort into this, I'll neglect my main work...)**

I believe that communities, like webtoons or app stores, also need a framework of self-regulation. As platforms, they should have operating principles revised based on standard operating principles set by the government, and they must fulfill their duty in regulatory activities. In this process, they might be positioned as adult-only communities, in which case adult verification must be mandatory.

If, from an external perspective, a platform is deemed to have failed in its duties under self-regulation, a complaint can be filed with a central regulatory body, and this will then be resolved through consultation between the regulatory body and the platform.

Of course, given the nature of communities, it's not right to prevent small communities from forming and disappearing. Therefore, I believe that regulation should be mandatory for communities with a certain number of members or more, considering their social influence. And this includes not only Megal, Ilbe, Utdae, Ruliweb, and Miznet, but also Naver and Daum cafes.

(Especially in the case of cafes, they have the nature of local communities, so their impact on offline life is considerable.)

Oh... and I'm not a writer. Why do people keep calling me a writer...?

### The Internet, So Different Compared to PC Communication, Is This Okay?

https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
[Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
* ・ *
2016. 7. 26. 22:47

[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220772403267&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[** Add Neighbor**](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220772403267&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[Other Body Functions](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220772403267&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220772403267&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
[Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220772403267&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

I remember first stepping into the network market during my middle school years. At the time when Ketel was just transitioning to Hitel, the number of PC communication users was probably comparable to today's Megalian or Ilbe. The pen name "Forest Story" (숲속얘기) for this blog started when I moved from Hitel to Nownuri. Even then, there were famous issue-makers, and the news sometimes called us "PC communication tribe." There were also several online comic communities, and it was like a small internet world by today's standards.
Back then, when an issue arose, it was relatively easy to grasp. The world of PC communication was small, and IDs were always familiar faces. However, communities centered around DC Inside, mini-hompies centered around Cyworld, and the blogs we have now created a search-based internet, and now it's a world dominated by social networks like Facebook and Twitter. The influence of social influencers has grown enormous, and the user base, called netizens, has become very diverse. In particular, the spread of smartphones began to include voices from people in their 40s to 60s in the internet, which was previously dominated by those under 30. And with the explosion of e-commerce, women's purchasing power began to concentrate on the internet. It's also true that, apart from webtoons which are mainly shonen manga-focused on news and portals, women's influence is absolute today.
The current path of internet public opinion is vastly different from the bulletin board-centric PC communication era. Portal main pages and search engines empowered internet pages as individual units. The context before and after a page is created is completely lost. This phenomenon is even more severe on Twitter. Twitter involves more omissions, making it difficult for users who access a page via search to understand the situation.
Online communities are somewhat better off because they have many regulars, but when you look at how pages from different communities cross over via social networks, it's a structure easily prone to misrepresentation or manipulation. Social networks are powerful tools that reinforce confirmation bias.
The active comment system in Korea further fuels this. While trackback usage has already died out on Korean blogs, comments are actually closer to the nature of SNS like Twitter and have a strong conversational character.
What about wikis? When searching for information, I always end up cross-referencing with English wikis, as domestic wikipedians are too limited. While Namuwiki certainly has a lot of interesting content, there's a tendency to fabricate information about things they don't know well, and sometimes it turns into a battleground, much like comments.
Someone once said SNS is a waste of life, and I somewhat agree. Before that, in the case of South Korea, a significant portion of comment wars are a waste of life.
I've always enjoyed discussions, from the PC communication era's debate rooms to comments, but the moment it escalates into an emotional battle, I deeply regret it later. This is because 99% of the time, it reaffirms that it was ultimately a waste of time.
However, as mentioned earlier, there are times when so-called "aggro" or "issue-mongering" is necessary. This is due to the nature of internet platforms, where information is easily buried due to its sheer volume, and the public doesn't react unless it's provocative.
I realized this while working on internet services and blogging. Of course, if taken too far, one eventually loses their value. This refers to distinguishing between the "zapping" stage and the content delivery stage. As I mentioned in my first post, Megal was obsessed only with zapping and failed to solidify its core, ultimately collapsing by consuming its zapping. One must not lose sight of the essence.
Also, from the perspective of someone who has worked in internet services, it is correct to remove emotion from conversations with customers as a service provider. Looking at the customer service case below, one might call it "refreshing," but

https://www.youtube.com/embed/fRYK0EZ72kU?wmode=transparent
The Gutsy Gyeongsang-do Designated Driver Counselor

From the perspective of a company providing services, it is not the right course of action. It would be fortunate if that thug were unemployed, but if they were truly an influential person, everyone could be screwed. Service providers should be humble, but internally, it's right to take care of employees separately and comfort each other. It's better to say "We love our customers" and then curse them out after hanging up, and that is the correct professional conduct.
Anyway, looking at the current situation, people are clashing emotionally in a very complex situation, and they are precariously trying to cross each other's lines. If a certain webtoon artist's cursing raised doubts about their professionalism as an artist, readers are now expanding the scope to demand restrictions on creative freedom itself.
Furthermore, the Megal issue is being expanded into a gender issue, or there's a witch hunt atmosphere targeting even those who agree with Megal's members or all of its policies and slogans. Ultimately, I am very concerned about creating an "either you're with us or against us" structure, which is why I wrote about the first issue being very complex, using a title that could draw attention.
Anyway, I know this long post won't be read much this time either.
The issue of regulating internet communities, which I brought up jokingly, also seems to have genuinely necessary aspects, and in any case, I feel the matter is more complex than I thought. In such a situation, allowing it to escalate into a purely emotional confrontation and completely eliminating one side is, I believe, detrimental to the development of Korea's internet and democracy.
Anyway, the current situation doesn't seem very constructive. Even if the webtoon artist or Megal initially created the unconstructive situation, I believe it was a problem that could have erupted at any time on the Korean internet. I hope we can now think about what comes next, and I hope that "what comes next" doesn't turn into trivial matters like stifling creative freedom, like "Yes Cut," or burying a few artists, just when we thought we might gain some cultural diversity.
If a problem involving such a small minority can shake the whole system, it seems that Korea's internet and webtoon industry are still fragile or have structural issues. I at least hope this space doesn't become a battleground for TV idols or "aggro" provocateurs.
This doesn't seem like a problem that can be resolved in a short time; rather, it feels like a genuine research topic. And for a proper conclusion to emerge, a wider range of opinions from more people is needed.

This post is a failure. I had many thoughts, but I wrote it in a way that's difficult for anyone to read.
Please just read it thinking, "Oh, this is one way to think about it."

**ps. I will no longer talk about this matter. **
** This matter consumes a lot of energy, so please don't be upset if I don't reply to every comment.**********
** As I also need to tell the next stories... **
****
** I stepped forward, knowing I might be criticized, simply to provide an opportunity for thought.**
**It seems someone needs to play this role. Right now, everyone seems to be quietly waiting for the storm to pass, or else lurking to destroy the opponent. If it ends this way, I don't think anything will be gained.**
**I stepped forward hoping for constructive discussions to emerge. **
********
****Thanks to this, many people who know me worried about me. Thank you.****
**Also, I apologize for some expressions that may have been irritating.**
****
