titleEn: Pokémon GO AR? VR? Why Can't Korea Make It?
contentEn:
Pokemon seems to be a truly amazing game. Content that can excite the whole world like this is probably countable on one hand. This isn't the first time Pokemon has become a social issue in Korea. In the early 1990s, Pokemon bread, which included Pokemon stickers, became a social issue in Korea. And now that those children have grown into adults, Pokemon is once again creating social buzz even before its official arrival in Korea. As I mentioned Pokemon on Facebook, I received several questions, so I'd like to answer those first.

{{IMG:1}}

1. Is Pokemon an AR game? Is AR rising instead of VR?

**- Strictly speaking, Pokemon is not AR, but MR, a descendant of AR and VR.** Augmented Reality refers to showing additional information in the real world. Strictly speaking, Pokemon Go is not AR but VR. It has a worldview close to a parallel world of the real world. There is only a virtual world that resembles Sokcho, but there is no additional information about Sokcho. However, from a technological perspective, it falls under MR, a descendant of AR.

http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220743460716
[**Definition and Classification of VR, and 360-degree video** VR is quite hot, but it still feels like VR isn't well-defined. The Software Policy Research Institute's V... blog.naver.com](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220743460716)

Mixed Reality refers to a form that overlays Virtual Reality or Virtual Objects onto the Real World. It's a bit ambiguous to call MR a technology. As I mentioned when explaining AR/MR/VR before, it might be easier to just call it VR. Games are originally meant for playing in a virtual world, not for better understanding the real world. Of course, the technology is closer to AR technology because it recognizes surrounding information and objects. And the VR market will not change because of Pokemon Go. It's just that a well-made mobile game has been released. VR hasn't even started yet. Saying that AR is unfolding instead of VR is close to overreacting. **- And it's a location-based mobile online game.** In fact, there's one more important thing: it's a location-based mobile online game. While AR provided a new experience, it's not actually the core element of the Pokemon Go game. The core element of the Pokemon Go game is that it's an online game using smartphones based on the user's location. In fact, Pokemon Go can be played with the camera off, using only GPS.

2. So, will mobile AR rise again?

Perhaps because of VR, people keep asking if mobile AR will rise again. My answer to this question is "no" on one hand, and "yes" on the other.

1) "No." Pokemon Go's success wasn't largely due to AR. Other factors were too strong.

First, the "no" answer is that I believe the core success factor of Pokemon Go was not AR, but rather the influence of the location-based mobile online game, as mentioned earlier. Ultimately, whether a game is well-made or not will be determined not by whether it used AR technology, but by how well the location-based mobile online game was made. Currently, people's reactions are not bad. The success of an online game depends on whether its users create their own culture, and it seems they are already doing so. Therefore, if Pokemon Go is managed properly, its popularity is unlikely to be temporary. Of course, proper management of an online game is not easy, but with a year of know-how from Ingress, I believe they will do well. On the other hand, some might argue that the novelty of AR attracted many initial users. However, I believe the number of initial users due to AR is minuscule compared to the power of the Pokemon IP. The power of the Pokemon IP is practically a cheat code.

1) However, "Yes." There are already successful AR cases.

However, on the other hand, I can say "yes." There have already been cases where mobile AR technology has shined. Until now, mobile AR technologies have mainly been used briefly in marketing and have not seen actual success. There were several games before Pokemon Go, but they failed because taking out the camera was very burdensome. However, an app that solved this already exists: "Snow" and "MSQRD." This technology is AR, and strictly speaking, it's also MR. It uses image recognition technology to create new virtual photos and makes it fun like a game, essentially performing its original duty as a photo app. Since taking out the camera was burdensome, it approached it as a selfie camera from the start. Furthermore, photo-sharing SNS like Facebook and Instagram increased the desire to use such apps. I can simply say that mobile AR is ultimately about photos. In fact, many Korean users encountering Pokemon Go share AR photos via Facebook. Pokemon Go users, whose Pokemon locations change as they move, try to find suitable locations to share on Facebook. In Pokemon Go, the role of AR is ultimately photography. In the Pokemon Go teaser video, Pokemon trainers appear to be looking at the real space and throwing a ball without looking at their smartphones, but in reality, that's not the case. Trainers end up looking only at the smartphone screen, which becomes similar to the composition of taking a photo of a Pokemon. And those photos are spread through Facebook and Instagram, gathering people... It's sufficiently serving as a customer acquisition tool. That's as far as I see mobile AR technology going. The hurdles to create further value are too high.

3. So, will location-based online games succeed?

Location-based online games are not new either. The weakness of location-based online games is the restriction of time and place. This is far from the convenience of mobile games. For a typical game, I'm somewhat pessimistic about this. Online games require network effects and economies of scale. Can a network effect of this magnitude be created in such a short time with an IP other than Pokemon? Even Niantic's previous work, which created Pokemon Go, did not perform particularly well in terms of revenue compared to other mobile online games. If a good IP is attached and the game is well-made, the story might change, but an easy entry like Pokemon Go won't be as simple as it seems. The only applicable IP that comes to mind is Minecraft, acquired by MS. However, I believe it has sufficiently demonstrated the effect of small-scale location-based events, rather than global success. Sokcho City really hit the jackpot. Therefore, the desire to create location-based games for regional promotion seems likely to increase. But if you're thinking of making big money, the answer is still no. Unless it's a location-based online "dating" game... Ultimately, it's about targeting a customer base with the ability to pay. The very nature of a location-based game reduces the customer base, so you need to capture a customer base that can spend a lot of money. Oh, of course, Pokemon, which already has hundreds of millions of users, is an exception.

4. Why can't Korea make Pokemon Go?

1) The difference between Pokemon IP as a video game and an online game

Honestly, I think this question is as foolish as it gets. In the case of Pokemon Go, it was able to grow so large so quickly through the global IP of Pokemon, which is almost unique in the world. Even the US doesn't have it. Have you seen Disney make online games? Isn't it strange to ask why we don't have something like this? And Nintendo's video games played the biggest role in creating this global IP. In contrast, Korea grew centered around online games. Video games, or home console games, are characterized by playing alone for extended periods. Therefore, they often have extensive storylines and worldviews. On the other hand, online games developed in Korea are played by many people sitting in PC bangs (internet cafes). Few people in PC bangs study worldviews. Even with so much StarCraft played, how many Korean users know the StarCraft scenario? It was more urgent to set the speed to maximum and block drone rushes to play one more game. In the Korean game market, which grew centered on such fast-paced, competitive games, it was virtually impossible for stories and worldviews to survive. Even the first online game, "The Kingdom of the Winds," which started with a wonderful story by author Shin Il-sook, eventually went on almost unrelated to its story, didn't it? Therefore, such world-building IPs cannot remain in Korea. So, is the original sin with the Korean game industry? For reference, buying a video game console in Korea was like buying a drug-making machine for a child, and game software was naturally copied in the market. From the beginning, game software survived as online games as a self-preservation measure in such barren land. Ultimately, if we trace the cause, the preference for popular game forms, despite being a gaming powerhouse, could not create global IPs, and more fundamentally, it was a structure where making other types of games would lead to failure, with little chance of improvement. Making video game software in Korea is madness. After that, mobile games became popular again. In mobile, which pursues lightness to an even greater degree, even combat is automated, so stories... naturally don't exist. Don't look for a story in Anipang. It's better to read the webtoon if the game is based on one. The game itself was not an environment where it could create its own IP.

2) If we must pinpoint a cause, it's the environment of South Korea, which has weak cultural diversity.

그리고, 포켓몬스터는 전세계 거의 유일무이한 ip다. 아무나 만들고 싶다고 퍽퍽 찍어 만들 수 있는 ip가 아니란 말이다. 그리고 재밌는 것은 포켓몬스터는 지속적으로 재창조되었다. 게임 뿐만 아니라 다양한 형태의 산업에 OSMU로 활용되었고, 일본에는 거대한 2차 저작물 시장인 동인지 시장도 활성화 되있다. 소위 말하는 오덕문화는 이러한 ip가 자라나는데 큰 거름이 된다. 그리고, 이러한 동인지 시장에 금기는 없다. 얼마전 한국에서 시끄러운 "후레자식"은 일본 동인시장에 내놓으면 소프트물이다. 결국 매우 다양하고 거대한 서브컬쳐를 바탕으로 튼튼한 메이저컬쳐가 형성되어있으며, 이러한 문화창작물에 기꺼이 돈을 지불한다. 전세계에서 가장 콘텐츠를 잘 사주는 나라가 일본이다. 그에 반해 한국은 중국하고 앞서거니 뒤서거니... 그러면서 위해하니, 마약이니 온갖 난리는 다 친다. 사주고나 욕 얻어먹으면 덜 억울 할텐데.. 그러니 결국 핑계같지만, 돈되는 성인물이나, 사행성에만 오히려 손을 대는 것 같다. 오버워치를 못만드는 이유가 한국의 게임에 대한 인식 때문이라더니, 한다는 소리가 규제완화로 결제한도 완화를 주장하는 판국을 보면 가슴이 답답하다. 오버워치같은 새로운 경험을 제공하는 잘만든 게임을 만들려면 망할지도 모르는 신선한 게임들에 대한 투자들이 지속적으로 이루어져야 한다. 이로서 기업의 논리보다는 창작자들의 창작욕구를 지속적으로 강화하고 다양한 경험과 실험을 통해 문화적 다양성을 확보해야 한다. 앞서서 내가 위치기반 AR온라인 게임은 기존에도 있었고, 망할 가능성이 높다라고 꼰대같은 소리만 해뎄지만, "난 더 재밌게 만들 수 있어요." 라는 창작자가 있다면 기회를 줘야 한다. 그것이 문화적 다양성이다. 포켓몬go의 주목을 보면서 우리도 저런 기술있는데 부러워하기 이전에.. 기술의 문제가 아니다. SKT에서 정부과제로 게임만든다는 이야기를 듣고... 한숨이 나왔다. SKT가 기술을 안가진게 아니다. 그냥 게임을 만들줄 모를 뿐. 기술이 중한게 아니라 뭘 만들려고 하는지를 고민하는게 낫다. AR이던 VR이던 게임을 만든다면, 결국 게임성이 가장 중요하고, 영상을 만든다면 영상미와 스토리가 중요하다. 기술이 암만 좋아봐야 콘텐츠의 기본가치가 안된다면, 그냥 기술 demo일 뿐이다.

### 3) 그리고 냅두면 한국에서는 시들해질거다.

사실 난 한국에서 이 이슈가 그리 오래 가지 않을거라고 본다. 지금은 그저 글로벌 이슈와 속초라는 지역적 제한으로 인해 희귀성으로 인해 더 주목 받는것 같다. 여기에 지자체의 힘까지 보태지고, AR포토의 바이럴 효과까지 겹쳐지고, 무엇보다도 하지말라니까 더 하고 싶은 심리가 겹쳐져, 한국에서는 다 해야 할 것처럼 느끼는것 같다. 하지만 이는 지속성이 있는 이슈들이 아니다. 장기적으로는, 한국은 성인이 게임하는걸 그다지 좋게 보지 않는데다가 위치기반 게임하기에는 너무 바쁘다. 키덜드가 주목 받지만, 여전히 마누라 몰래 하는게 게임이고, 국내 키덜트 시장 규모는 초라하다. 포켓몬 키즈 인구는 제한되어있으며, 한국의 아이들은 터닝메카드에 열광한다. 클래시오브클랜과 같은 출퇴근기간에 할 수 있는 게임은 여전히 인기가 있을 것이다. 물론 그렇다고 흔적도 없이 사라진다는건 아니다. 메니아층으로 인해 상위랭킹은 유지할 가능성이 높다. 물론, 여기에 한가지 예외 변수가 있는데, 포켓몬go의 캐릭터나 아이템이 현금거래가 가능해질 때 이다. 그럼 이제 게임이 아니라 리니지처럼 부업이 된다. 그리고 온라인 커뮤니티성이 강화되어 온라인게임으로서의 성격이 강해진다면, 한국에서도 유효하다고 본다. 한국은 아시다시피 자의인지 타의인지 온라인게임 강국이다. 그러나, 한국을 위해 게임의 성격을 바꿀까? 차라리 닌텐도에서 만들 모바일 포켓몬이라면 모르지만, 외향성이 강한 서양출신인 나인엔틱은 게임 성격을 바꿀 것 같지는 않다.

### 5. go, go 결국 디지털 콘텐츠의 문화적 다양성 확대가 답이다.

자. 그래서 한국은 뭘해야 하냐고? 알파고의 하사비스가 어릴때 뭘했는지 기억하나? 롤러코스터 게임개발했다. 포켓몬go는 뭐라고? 게임이다. 그리고 게임은 문화콘텐츠다. 문화의 가장 중요한점은 그리고 다양성이다. 지금 당장 돈 벌어들이는게 아니고, 돼지처럼 잘 먹기 위한게 아니라 웃고 울고 그리고 우리가 사는 사회와 주변사람을 돌아보게 하기 위한 것이 콘텐츠다. 콘텐츠산업에서 콘텐츠를 떼버리고 산업만 남겨서는 안된다. 언제까지 우리는 애니메이션에서는 작화만 할 것인가.. 스마트폰에서는 하드웨어만 생산할것인가.. 와 같다. 중요한 것은 소프트웨어고, 보이지 않는 문화 경쟁력이다. 이는 돈으로만 측정되는게 아니다.

titleEn: [Bastard Lawsuit] Does the Web
contentEn:
I hope this post will be the last one about the "Bastard" lawsuit. Through this incident, I learned about the public's perception of webtoons, and conversely, how ignorant our society is about children's culture. If we don't understand, we can't diagnose or help them.

{{IMG:1}}

South Park

1. What is a Webtoon?

First, I realized that many people, including the webtoon plaintiff, are ignorant about webtoons. While 8 million webtoon users are mentioned, the majority of them are in their 20s and 30s. And many of them consume webtoons lightly, like slice-of-life comics shared on social media. They might be called webtoon consumers, but they don't know everything about webtoons, nor are they what you'd call "hardcore fans." For them, webtoons might be nothing more than billboards.

1) Webtoons are Cultural Content

To be considered a demographic that properly understands webtoons, one should at least have webtoons they regularly follow every week. One of the biggest differences between webtoons and print comics is their serialized nature. They are closer to dramas than movies. While webtoons are an extension of comics, their production costs are lower and their reliance on the artist is higher compared to traditional comic books. This allows for an incomparably diverse range of subjects and themes compared to other media that are highly dependent on capital. This is precisely why the broadcasting and film industries, which demand only verified content, are paying close attention to webtoons. Their dilemma is that while broadcasting and film require significant capital investment, they must minimize risk, which often runs counter to the novelty of subject matter and themes. To bridge this gap, they began to look at webtoons. It's no coincidence that many popular dramas and films recently are based on webtoons. The plaintiff, in their complaint, mentioned Pororo and Dooly as examples of proper comics, but they clearly haven't seen the original work by Kim Soo-jung. The episode depicting the Iraq War is one of the most memorable works of my life. Dooly's origin itself was changed to an animal because the author was afraid of being arrested for drawing social commentary... **-- Episode 95, March 1991, Gulf War II --** 『Dooly』 is by no means unrelated to current events, and this episode, in particular, seems to be remembered as shocking by many readers. Dooly's gang divides into teams, shaking hands with Iraqi soldiers and multinational coalition soldiers, confronting each other. Up to the middle, it proceeds in a comedic tone, with Iraqi and American soldiers even reconciling. However, on the 10th page, the atmosphere dramatically shifts as the two soldiers step on landmines and are blown up. Afterward, scenes of devastation follow: a destroyed city, a girl left alone after her parents died, and people eating a dead sheep because there's nothing else to eat. After Dooly's gang gives up collecting bombs and leaves, it's revealed that the girl's older brother was the Iraqi soldier who was blown up by a landmine right in front of her, intensifying the tragedy, and the episode ends there. Overall, the anti-war message is clear.

http://egloos.zum.com/shaw/v/3693971

[*The Patriot missile, which was a hot topic during the Gulf War, also appears in the work.*](http://egloos.zum.com/shaw/v/3693971)[*http://egloos.zum.com/shaw/v/3693971*](http://egloos.zum.com/shaw/v/3693971)

**All Episodes of Baby Dinosaur Dooly (3) August 1988 ~ July 1991** 『Dooly』 was first published in the April 1983 issue of the comic magazine 『Bomulsom』 and was serialized in the same magazine for 10 years. 『Dooly』 has since been published in several collected editions, but some episodes were omitted and the order was sometimes changed. The problem is severe from the very idea of webtoons being only for the Pororo age group. You should be using Juniver, you've chosen the wrong service. The role of webtoons lies in their diversity, breathing with the public. While there are charts that mock the predictable stories of Korean morning dramas, such charts cannot be created for webtoons. It's safe to say that most predictable stories are cut, and there are almost no webtoons where you can predict the conclusion from the beginning. The plaintiff's "Bastard" is no exception. It's difficult to judge a work based on just a few expressions.

2) Regulation of Webtoon Copyrights

Since webtoons are free content based on an internet advertising model, some people seem to think they are public performances that anyone can view and use. Webtoons are clearly the author's copyrighted work. Furthermore, the right to choose that work belongs to the reader. It is the platform's competitiveness to present this work to the appropriate audience. However, only works defined as 19+ under the Youth Protection Act require age verification. The scope where subjectivity cannot intervene in the 19+ debate is limited to direct expressions. Things like actual stabbing scenes, or nudity beyond a woman's toplessness. "Bastard" avoids all such expressions. However, the scope of sexual imagination or violent expression is actually more attributable to direction and story than to such direct scenes. Therefore, it is usually controlled at an appropriate level by censorship bodies, and often regulated more broadly than the law. And, in the case of webtoons, due to the nature of comics, they also have the effect of being viewed with less repulsion. Expressiveness weakens from live-action to drawings, and from drawings to text only. Therefore, it is natural to see webtoons having a broader range of expression than live-action, or video content. However, on the other hand, imagination has the effect of filling that void more strongly than live-action, so rather than cutting it with a knife, it is right for those with professional knowledge or within the relevant cultural industry to appropriately self-regulate.

3) Webtoons are Cultural Content

Amidst all this, the controversy over central pre-censorship of a thriller webtoon ("Bastard") is a critical issue that could infringe on creative freedom and lead to a contraction of the entire Korean cultural industry. The plaintiff probably didn't understand this well, but it's close to a challenge to the cultural sector that has worked for decades to establish self-regulation. In fact, I was surprised that many people didn't even understand the meaning of self-regulation. Self-regulation doesn't mean central regulation has disappeared. The plaintiff should have filed a complaint with the central regulatory body, not a lawsuit. This negates the current self-regulatory system and advocates a return to the past dictatorial era.

2. Do Violent Webtoons Really Make Children Violent?

The most common argument I heard when discussing the "Bastard" lawsuit was that "violent scenes" are harmful to children. And the conclusion is that they can make children violent. I agree with some of it, but I disagree with some (actually most) of it.

1) Where Does Children's Violence Come From?

Let's talk a bit about violence. Will children, clean as paper, not use violence? We could go into the debate of human nature being good or evil, but any parent who has raised a child knows the answer: "No." Children are inherently purely violent. To be precise, it's more accurate to say they are instinctive. They generally lack proper control over the intensity of violence. This is because they haven't learned about pain or developed empathy for others. However, a repulsion to blood does exist. This doesn't seem to be learned. It's probably closer to a fundamental instinct to protect oneself from threats to safety during a long evolutionary process. People who lack or have a weak version of this (it's difficult to call it a disease) can be called psychopaths. In fact, there's a scene where the protagonist of "Bastard" recalls childhood memories, and this could be that part. (In the webtoon, he sealed away that memory himself. And it's one of the biggest twists in the theme.) This is likely one of the biggest factors that puts a brake on children's violence. And I agree with the psychiatrist who, in a previous post, referred to "children from normal families" as those who have gone through a less externally stimulated upbringing, suggesting this effect would be significant for them. Furthermore, sensitivity to violence isn't limited to children. Adults also exist who are sensitive to horror, disaster, and thriller genres. Honestly, I myself have vivid memories of the gunshot wounds in Robocop 1, which I saw as a child, and it scared me for a long time. Since this can be traumatic, I also recommend that children use media and computers under parental supervision. This cannot be definitively stated as it varies depending on the child's condition. But can only a sensory aversion to violence truly prevent violence? I don't think so. Violence isn't just physical; it also exists in social or indirect forms, and there are many webtoons that use this as their subject matter.

2) Does Insensitivity to Violence Reinforce Violence?

Moreover, sensitivity to violence weakens through various stimuli as one grows up. I admit that this has the effect of making one insensitive to violence. The professions most insensitive to blood are soldiers, firefighters, police officers, and doctors. They continuously see blood, suppressing this instinct, and learn that it is unrelated to their own safety. This is unrelated to the reinforcement of their own violence. Children feel scared when they see an injection, but they become okay with it as they grow older. When they are children, getting hit by their mom feels so scary, but when they go to the military and get hit with a bat, they might just say, "Oh, shit." This is the result of such learning. In conclusion, this growth is very normal, and insensitivity to violence is unavoidable as one grows up. Ultimately, the degree of sensitivity to violence is not a direct control mechanism for committing violence.

3) Suppressing Violence During Growth is Understanding the Absurdity of Violence

그러면 폭력의 기재를 억누를 수 있는 가장 큰 원인은 무엇일까? 바로 공감과 사회성이다. 피해자로서 느끼는 1차적인 아픔이 아니라, 바로 폭력의 부조리함에 대한 학습이다. 폭력으로 인한 것이 어떠한 영향을 미치는지를 사회적으로 아는 것이다. 이것에 대한 학습이전에 법으로 막아두고는 있지만, 법으로만 폭력이 나쁘다는 것을 아는 것은 앞서말한 싸이코패스와 가깝다고 할 수 있다. 이 분들이 기준이 될수는 없으니 그냥 보통 사람들 이야기를 해보자. 때문에 방송통신윤리 위원회의 공감능력이 존재하는 보통사람을 위한 폭력에 대한 규제는 “폭력을 찬양”하는지에 대해 중점을 두고 있다. “폭력에 대한 표현”이 아니다. 후레자식은 단연코 폭력을 찬양하지 않는다. 오히려 앞서말한 폭력의 부조리함을 이해하는데 도움이 된다.

4) 웹툰 미디어의 10대와 대중 공감의 우수성

앞서 말한 웹툰의 특성은 10대에게 폭력의 부조리함을 이해시키는데 효과적인 미디어다. 제작 비용이 싸서 진입장벽이 낮으며, 심지어는 직접 생산이 가능한 구조는 젊은 창작자들에게 높은 자유도와 낮은 진입장벽을 선사했다. 결과적으로 매우 어린작가들의 등단이 가능한 구조며(실제 고등학생 작가도 있다.) 10대에 대한 이해도가 높다. 그들이 말하는 것, 행동하는 것을 이해한다. 또한 다양한 사상과 생각, 상상력을 버무리고, 경쟁을 통해 문학적, 대중적 요소가 높은 것들이 상위로 올라오는 구조이다. 때문에 폭력에 대한 굉장히 실증적이고 다양한 해석들을 해준다. 난 오히려 사전검열을 강하게 거치는 깨끗한 방송에서 정말 십대들을 위한 솔직한 이야기를 한 적이 있는가? 라고 묻고 싶다. 학생사회의 1진에 대해 성인들은 얼마나 알고 있는가? 그저 학교폭력을 당하면 신고해라. 가 다 이지 않나? 선생님들의 교권이나 땅에 떨어진 상황이나 아이들의 학업에 대한 고민, 그리고 그들의 꿈에 대해 어떤 미디어가 이야기를 해주고 있나. 웹툰에서 1진물의 위해성은 여전히 논란의 거리이긴 하다. 웹툰에서 상상하는 멋진 1진은 사실 “나라면 다르겠지”라고 느끼는 피해자들이 그린 상상속의 1진의 모습이기 떄문이기도 하다. 그러나, 이러한 상상력은 성인들의 내가 재벌총수가 되면.. 과 다를바가 없다. 성장기 아이들 사회에서 폭력도 하나의 계급이기 때문이고, 이를 완전히 제거하기는 어려울것이다. 그렇다면 이 아이들에게 필요한 것은 앞서 말한 폭력의 사회적 부조리함을 더욱 가르쳐야 한다. 적어도 웹툰의 1진물들은 “폭력 찬양”은 19금에 걸리기 때문에, 작가의 실력에 따라 차이는 나지만, 폭력을 찬양하는 작품은 없다. 오히려 성인이 된 1진이 학창시절에 무심코 했던 폭력이 어떤 끔찍한 결과를 가져오는지에 대한 소재도 정면으로 그린 작품들도 존재한다. 간단히 말해 방송에서 외면한 학교 폭력에 대한 진짜 심각한 논의는 웹툰에서 다루어지고 있고, 어른들의 미디어에서는 아이들을 어떻게 벌줄지와 격리할지만 고민하고 있다. 어쩌면 당연한지도 모르겠다. 생산,소비자가 모두 10대가 아니니.. 요즘에는 그 범위를 넓혀 최근에는 가족간의 폭력까지 소재의 범위를 넓혔다. 그런 웹툰을 보고 펑펑 울었다는 댓글이 달리는 요즘이다. 과연 우리의 미디어가 가야할 길이 어디일까? 이런 웹툰을 다시 중앙 규제로 회귀하자는 말인가?

3. 사회를 비추고 사회를 치유하는 웹툰

그제 영화 곡성을 보았다. 이 영화도 15금이 아닌 부모의 지도하라면 15세 이하도 시청가능한 15가다. 솔직히 말해 후레자식보다 훨씬 잔인했고, 후레자식보다 혼란스럽게 떡밥을 늘어놓았다. 이 영화도 19금 논란이 좀 있는 듯하지만, 그럼에도 불구하고 엄청난 인기를 끌고 있으며 이러한 문제가 수면 위로 올라오고 있지 않다. 이는 꽤 수준 높은 작품이기 때문일 것이고, 영화를 보는 사람들은 중간에 그만둘 수 없기 때문일 것이다. 후레자식처럼 고소자처럼 몇편만보고 이거 19금걸어야 되. 이러지는 않는다는것이다. 잔인한 표현이 많았지만, 끝나고 나면 피에 대한 기억보다는 스토리와 떡밥만 떠올랐다. 이것이 연출과 스토리의 힘일것이다. 사실, 몇개의 웹툰이 떠오르는 스토리를 가지고 있었는데, 고비용의 영화에서 저정도의 감독의 자유로운 이야기가 펼쳐졌다는 점은 그만큼 우리의 문화계가 성숙한 증거일것 같다. 오늘날의 웹툰은 사회를 비추고, 사회를 치유하고 문화를 풍요롭게 한다. 어릴적 불량만화방에 대한 기억만 있는 분들이 웹툰에 대해 심각한 오해가 있는듯하다. 일본의 Anime나 망가와 달리 한국의 웹툰은 사회적으로 성장해가고 있다. 일본의 영화계가 한국의 영화계를 부러워하는 일이 만화에서도 일어나고 있다. 물론 모든 웹툰이 좋다는건 아니다. 포털의 연재물이 아닌 자유기고가 가능한 커뮤니티의 웹툰들은 아이들의 욕망만을 여과없이 뱉어내는경우도 존재한다. 하지만, 이러한 위험을 스스로 걸러내지 못할만큼 우리의 문화계와 사용자들과 독자들이 무식쟁이들은 아니라고 본다. 이를 역행하지는 말자.

titleEn: Parents Who Don't Understand Their Bratty Kids Are More Concerning.
contentEn:
타임라인에 올라온, 전체 이용가의 웹툰, 후레자식을 보고 아이들이 볼까봐 걱정스럽다는 글을 봤습니다. 저도 한 아이를 키우지만, 어릴때 많은 미디어를 접하고 부모님과 좀 다투었던 기억이 있기 때문에, 이 글을 보고 든 느낌은 "꼰대" 그것이었습니다.

[**평범한 아빠의 네이버 고소 이유? 웹툰의 전체이용가 진실 – Daum 아고라** m.bbs3.agora.media.daum.net](http://m.bbs3.agora.media.daum.net/gaia/do/mobile/petition/read?bbsId=P001&objCate1=1&articleId=187769&pageIndex=1)

내용인 즉슨 전체적인 줄거리와 표현만 놓고, 위해하니 보지 말랍니다. 초등학생과 중학생 아이를 두었다고 하네요. 저도 아이를 키웁니다.  만약 새봄이에게 이 웹툰을 보여주었다면, 일단은 새봄이가 재미없어할겁니다. 초교 이하가 보기에는 글이 너무 많습니다. 그리고 자극적이어서 무섭다는 이야기를 할지도 모르겠습니다. 그러나 크고 작은 자극은 어디에나 있습니다. 아이들의 책을 읽어주다보면 그 표현의 범위가 문제지 부모의 죽음을 다루거나 한 내용들도 있고, 아이가 슬프다고 합니다.

[**후레자식** '내 집안에 살인마가 산다.' 본격 세대갈등 잔혹 스릴러 comic.naver.com](http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/list.nhn?titleId=628997)

​ 이는 아이들이 살인이나 무엇을 죽이는 행위를 몰라서 라기보다는 자기 인지범위에 들어와 있지 않기 때문입니다. 인지범위에 들어오는 순간 무섭거나, 혼란스러울 수 있죠. ** 제목의 후레자식 보고, 아 나도 살인해봐야겠네. 하는 아이들은 없습니다. ****있다면 잘 못 키우신겁니다. 아이를 로봇으로 만드신겁니다.**게임 하면 바깥에서 총쏴델거라고 생각하는 것과 마찬가지죠. 오히려 외부의 자극을 차단 해놓을 수록, 작은 자극에도 견디지 못하거나 과잉 행동을 합니다. 초콜릿이나 게임의 경우에도 이러한 현상이 발생합니다. 후레자식웹툰은 처음부터 끝까지 읽어보았는지나 궁금합니다. **본문의 캡춰된 내용만 가지고 19금 떼리자는것은 레슬링 캡춰장면이 야하니 19금 떼리자는것과 같습니다. (무려 동성애물!)****살인마 아버지와의 대결과 삐뚤어진 애증이지, 아빠가 살인마니 아이도 후레자식이라는 내용이 아닙니다. 스포일러가 될 수 있으니 자세한 줄거리는 말씀못드리지만 한번 읽어보십쇼.** 아이를 말리고 싶으면 먼저 자세히 보고 해보십쇼. 생각할거리가 많은 웹툰입니다. **떠먹여주는 교육물 보다 어쩌면 이런 생각할거리를 주는 미디어가 더 교육적일 수 있다고 생각합니다. 실제로 저같은 경우, 생각의 능력을 교과서보다는 이런 미디어들을 통해 길렀습니다.****적어도, 게임은 플레이를 해보고, 웹툰은 읽어보고 판단을 내리십쇼.****그리고, 먼저 할일은 고소가 아니라 아이와의 대화입니다.  아이는 무엇을 느끼고 무엇을 배웠는지를 확인하십쇼. 그게 문제가 있다면 정말 작품의 문제가 있는걸 수 있습니다. (단, 유도심문은 하지 마시고요.)****그걸 안하고 저런 행동을 하셨다면 100% 꼰대질 하신겁니다. 아이들에게 신뢰 -10 을 얻으셨습니다.**

                            TIG OneSound, Gamer Child Verification Method

titleEn: [VR Health] Is VR Okay for Kids?
contentEn:
1. Concerns about people's health exist, and there are quite a few concerns about VR. In particular, there are many questions about whether young children can use it, and Oculus warns against use by users under 13, following concerns that it might be dangerous for children whose senses are less developed.

**Is VR too dangerous for kids? We asked the experts** We’ve investigated the age ratings of VR headsets and talked to optometrists and vision experts to find out if VR is safe for children. These are the potential risks of using VR for kids. www.digitaltrends.com

http://www.digitaltrends.com/virtual-reality/is-vr-safe-for-kids-we-asked-the-experts/

However, as seen in the case of Google Expeditions, there are attempts to apply VR in various fields such as education, raising the question of whether it is right to unconditionally prevent young children from using VR.

**Google Expeditions** Imagine exploring coral reefs or the surface of Mars in an afternoon. With Expeditions, teachers can take students on immersive, virtual journeys. www.google.com

https://www.google.com/edu/expeditions/

Furthermore, this issue is very significant as it determines the size of the market, making it a crucial problem.

2. Medical evidence is still lacking, and more time will be needed.

However, no medical 'smoking gun' has yet been found anywhere to prove that VR technology itself is harmful. Even TV... self-illuminating displays have not been around for even a few hundred years in the tens of millions of years of human history. The side effects of this convenience of civilization, which has come to us in a very short time, have not been verified. It takes a considerable amount of time and large-scale statistical tracking to medically determine if something is harmful, but there are no mass-produced products, only a small number of people use it, and the wearing period is limited, so there is a lack of data to accept this as a fact. Further research on this is needed. However, what has been confirmed is that it can cause eye fatigue and photosensitive syndrome, which can also be caused by fluorescent lights and lightning, but this varies greatly from person to person.

{{IMG:1}}

KBS Crisis Escape No. 1 (2011. 08.01)

And there is no medical evidence that the dizziness or discomfort we feel is harmful. Just as no evidence has been found that car sickness or seasickness is harmful to people.

3. Problems will arise when moving between the VR World and the Real World.

You might find it a bit strange that the discussion in this post seems to go back and forth, but long-term VR use could make daily life uncomfortable. Human senses and bodies are highly adaptable, so if they are continuously exposed to abnormal sensory situations like VR, they adapt to them. Later, when returning to normal, there can be a sense of rejection, similar to land sickness or astronauts experiencing 'Earth sickness.' If one is deeply immersed in VR for a long time, it could interfere with daily life. However, this is not significantly different from saying that long periods of living in space or at sea can interfere with life on Earth, and it is questionable whether this is a harm inherent to VR itself. Similar themes have already been depicted in animation, such as the portrayal of prosthetic bodies in Ghost in the Shell, showing the sense of discomfort and sensory confusion when changing bodies, or the child born on the Moon in Planetes who cannot return to Earth.

{{IMG:2}}

From Planetes, Nono at 12 years old

She had the body of an adult to anyone who saw her, but her actual age was 12. As one of the few 'Lunarians' born and raised on the Moon, where gravity is weak, she grew quickly but had weak bone density. She has a congenital low-gravity disorder that prevents her from living in places with strong gravity, so the hospital is her home. - Source: Namu Wiki -

The adaptability of humans and living things is astonishing! Perhaps if we become deeply engrossed in the value that VR offers, we might even evolve with VR. Some might call it degeneration, but then again. (In fact, 'degeneration' and 'evolution' are the same word. Degeneration specifically implies a direction, while evolution should be seen as a higher concept that originally has no direction. Of course, if you argue that the Chinese characters say otherwise, I have nothing to say.)

4. What's more important is the value that the VR World provides.

The reason astronauts go into space, even enduring space sickness and loss of bone and muscle, is because there is value in it. The same applies to VR. No matter how similar VR is made to the Real World, Virtual is Virtual. If it becomes exactly like Real, then Virtual has no value. Therefore, problems, big or small, can arise when returning to the Real World. What is important is the value that Virtual provides. Just as the time we spend on smartphones and PCs increases, and we experience conditions like Turner syndrome or 'turtle neck' syndrome, we use smartphones and PCs because we gain some value from them. Similarly, if we consider VR as an extension, what we should be careful about with VR is using the Virtual World only to the extent that it does not interfere with the Real World. Just as it is healthy not to sit foolishly at a desktop until you can't get up, or not to look at a smartphone until your neck hurts. Additionally, more thorough research should be conducted to ensure that the side effects and fears surrounding VR use are not exaggerated. It seems that efforts are already underway overseas. However, I am concerned that regulations might emerge before the industry even has a chance to grow. **ps. If you have any good additional resources on VR health, please feel free to share links.**

“Manufacturers could build in vision tests and allow people to see that they might have a problem and should consult an eye specialist,” suggests Prof. Banks.

If things go wrong, we might end up buying VR at an optician's...

titleEn: Ideas for Transitioning to a Hangul-Centric Public Document Environment
contentEn:
1. Purpose of Disclosure

South Korea uses two word processors. One is Hancom Office, used in public institutions and schools, and the other is Microsoft Word, used by the private sector. Recently, Google Docs has also been used, not prioritizing format, and in response, Naver released Naver Word using Synapsoft technology, but it doesn't seem to be gaining traction. Amidst this, the following news article was published, and the reaction from educators I know was, in a word, unenthusiastic. Teachers I know are doing excellent work with Google Docs, collaborating online, and some teachers wonder why the use of specific software is being forced. The advantage and disadvantage of software is that the switching cost is relatively low. Therefore, companies try various methods of lock-in and stake their lives on the quality of their services.

http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=018&aid=0003574358&sid1=001
**Hancom 'Office NEO' Selected as Integrated SW for Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education** [E-Daily Reporter Jeong Byeong-muk] Hancom (030520) announced on the 28th that 'Hancom Office NEO' has been selected as the integrated office software (SW) for the Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education. The Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education... news.naver.com

http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=018&aid=0003574358&sid1=001

However, the actions of the first-generation ventures, whom I deeply respected, are now met with all sorts of criticism. At some point, even though they are in the same software industry, they are almost being called a "software mafia," making me wonder if they have forgotten the fundamental spirit of software – the customer – in their fervent pursuit of their own survival. This corporate survival strategy tends to focus on sales rather than technology, which is poison in the long run. I do not recommend public institution SI projects to capable startups or companies with ample resources. The money the government provides to foster industries is our tax money, meant for companies to grow enough to compete globally, not to cling to these projects. Moreover, the interference is so severe that it doesn't even allow for focusing on the core. A helicopter parent's child lacks competitiveness. How long will they be carried? I particularly do not recommend the use of Hangeul (Hancom Office) for elementary and middle school students. I recommend using Google Docs, even if its features are a bit clunky. The key competencies for future children are collaboration, digital literacy, and global perspective. I feel that Hancom's collaboration support is limited and unstable, and it's not as digitally native as Google Docs. Furthermore, it is detached from global standards. It's difficult to understand why we would hinder the essential competencies children need just to save one company, Hancom. The Ministry of Education should set the most appropriate technology for education and empower the teachers who teach the children. I am now disclosing an idea I had prepared for a proposal some time ago. If things continue this way, the competitiveness of Korean public documents will be nonexistent, and it will be the biggest factor in losing public productivity competitiveness, along with ActiveX. I had written this down purely as an idea to develop the current paradigm and achieve international competitiveness. While it may not be perfect, if implemented with determination by experts, I believe it could bring some competitiveness to this closed environment.

2. Ideas for Improving the Public Electronic Document Environment (First Draft: April 7, 2015)

Existing public document collaboration systems and policies have focused solely on digitizing paper documents. However, in an era centered on software, by developing a collaboration system based on documents that are digital from the creation stage and corresponding policies, we can achieve the values of Government 3.0: sharing, communication, and collaboration.

**□ Current Status and Problems of Public Electronic Documents**

ㅇ **(Closed Technology)** Public documents centered on HWP Hangeul files
- De facto standard use of a specific company's file format (HWP)
- ODF, an international standard, has been selected as a Korean industrial standard, but its use is not mandatory for public institutions.
- Concerns about forcing private companies that collaborate to use a specific company's product (Hangeul word processor).
- Concerns that a specific company's file format (HWP) has low international usage, leading to international isolation.
- ODF, supported by Hangeul and various other word processors, has limitations in actual use due to issues of reproducibility and system integration.

ㅇ **(Web Environment)** Low accessibility and difficulty in searching and sharing
- Public documents are uploaded as files and shared as attachments to specific web posts.
- Attached files are more difficult to search than web documents.
- Due to government security guidelines, the URL of web posts is not disclosed beyond the domain, making it difficult to share and disseminate on SNS sites that typically rely on fixed URLs (Permalinks) for sharing and communication.

ㅇ **(Underutilization)** Limited to use as a substitute for paper documents
- High cost and effort across all stages: creation, distribution, use, circulation, storage, and disposal.
- Advantages such as collaboration and version control are not utilized.
- Failure to achieve a paperless environment.
- Inability to guarantee access due to document changes or deletions.
- In mobile environments, the frequency of using separate document viewers is low, and the small screen size reduces the usability of existing digital documents.

**□ Research Topics for Solutions**

ㅇ **(Open Technology)** Defining and disseminating public document formats
- Defining and disseminating public document file formats considering market impact, global standards, implementability, and usability.
- Establishing a practical technical system through public-private cooperation.

ㅇ **(Web Environment Optimization)** Improving web accessibility and usability of public electronic documents
- Developing SEO strategies optimized for the domestic portal environment.
- Developing web environment improvement strategies for sharing and dissemination (e.g., Permalink).
- Improving accessibility for document changes and deletions.
- Developing mobile response strategies.

ㅇ **(Improving and Disseminating Utilization Environment)** Researching and promoting utilization systems suitable for electronic documents
- Reviewing utilization systems across all stages.
- Developing systems and methods to utilize advantages such as collaboration and version control.
- Analyzing and overcoming obstacles to achieving a paperless environment.

Diagnosis of current status and problems was conducted by dividing into two divisions: citizens and public institutions, to develop integrated improvement plans, which were then pursued as an integrated topic until completion. Irregular individual in-depth interviews were continuously conducted.

ㅇ **(Public Service)** Joint development by two groups: Open Technology and Web Environment Optimization
- **(Open Technology)** Hangeul and Computer, Microsoft, Infraware, Handysoft, Unidocs, Synapsoft, Open Source (OpenOffice) development group
- **(Web Environment Optimization)** Naver, Daum Kakao, Google, Synapsoft, Social Network Expert Group, etc.

ㅇ **(Public Institution Utilization)** Joint dissemination by groups: Open Technology and Utilization Environment Improvement & Dissemination
- **(Open Technology)** Hangeul and Computer, Microsoft, Infraware, Handysoft, Unidocs, Synapsoft, Open Source (OpenOffice) development group
- **(Utilization Environment Improvement & Dissemination)** Korea Electronic Document Industry Association, Web Document Experts, Korea Electronic Document Society, Public Officials, etc.

**□ Expected Effects**

ㅇ **(Establishment of Fair Market Order)** By establishing a document environment compliant with international standards, international compatibility and a fair market order in the document market can be achieved, leading to improved quality through competition in the public document market.
ㅇ **(Improved Job Satisfaction and Productivity)** Maximizing the advantages of digital documents to create a paperless environment will increase job satisfaction within public institutions and enhance productivity.
ㅇ **(Improved Public Satisfaction and Trust)** Creating a digital document environment that enables sharing, communication, and collaboration will improve public satisfaction with digital public documents and enhance trust in the government as a transparent entity.

titleEn: Modular Phone Google Ara Is Different From G5
contentEn:
1. Modular Phones as the New Trend in Smartphones?

Looking at articles about modular phones in Korea, it feels like modular phones are being treated as the new trend in smartphones. It feels like modular phones are simply seen as expandable phones where users can choose their preferences. However, I was quite shocked when I saw Google Ara's project. This might be the first signal of Google shedding its long-standing image as a software company. Whatever the architecture of the Android phone Google created as a reference, it was essentially a lightweight Linux desktop machine with some phone functionalities added. In terms of computer architecture, not much has fundamentally changed. The PC's power supply was replaced by a battery, the monitor by IPS or AMOLED, and the keyboard and mouse by capacitive touch. Honestly, it's a machine no different from a computer. In contrast, Apple's image as a hardware powerhouse didn't originate with smartphones. Apple's hardware prowess, which dates back to early Apple, involves technologies found in computer science textbooks.

2. But the Ara Concept is Post-Smartphone, Not Just New

But Ara is different. Google isn't just talking about a slightly different, smaller desktop-like smartphone; it's talking about a modular hardware computing environment.

{{IMG:1}}
                                
                            http://www.modularphonesforum.com/news/project-ara-15-questions-and-answers-2214/

It's like applying today's distributed software technology to hardware. Indeed, the best insights seem to come from developers, not news articles. I'm just puzzled why reporters don't grasp how significant this is.

[**- YouTube** YouTube에서 마음에 드는 동영상과 음악을 감상하고, 직접 만든 콘텐츠를 업로드하여 친구, 가족뿐 아니라 전 세계 사람들과 콘텐츠를 공유할 수 있습니다. youtu.be](http://www.youtube.com/embed/F3S6Kjb3m0g)

" all slots are generic and support and any functionality moudles are assinged to work with variety of form factors. future frames can be larger, they can be smaller or somtthing completely different than a smaprtphone. " " All modules can generally support any function, allowing for various operations across different form factors. Future frames can be larger, or smaller. It will be a device completely different from a smartphone. " A technical look reveals that it supports variable power supply, a very fast low-power data bus (UniPro network), an application-independent software stack, and Graybus, among others. Its speed allows for real-time 4K video transmission between modules, using only about 1/3 of the power of USB. The features immediately noticeable to users are multiple slots and the ability to expand functionality without rebooting. Currently, there are 6 slots... but theoretically, it's possible to do something like the 108-robot combination shown below. Surely some idle developer might create this with Ara... The Ara platform would definitely be useful for building a 108-combination robot. (Ara was soliciting ideas, should I submit one?)

3. The G5 is Expandable, Not Modular.

So, what about the G5? Let's look at the nostalgic Space Three Musketeers. (Couldn't find the Korean version)

The Space Three Musketeers don't combine or fuse. Of course, there are terrifying cartoons where living beings combine, but... what's even more regrettable is that the G5 has only one module, and a look at the AppsPortTM 1.0 spec reveals it's USB 2.0. There are clear limitations in speed and power. Moreover, it requires a reboot, which means it has the disadvantage of not being attackable during its transformation time.

**Clien > Everyone's Park > Ah... I have to reboot every time I swap G5 modules.....** http://pocketnow.com/2016/02/21/lg-g5-friends-hands-on-lg-cam-plus-lg-hi-fi-plus Pocketnow's hands-on says it reboots when you swap modules.................. They should have at least put a small 300~400mAh battery inside....................... www.clien.net

http://www.clien.net/cs2/bbs/board.php?bo_table=park&wr_id=44547115

It's the rule of transformation shows... let's understand it. If you attack during transformation... it's a big problem. Fearing a post-blind situation, I'll just provide the link. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lQzVHj5EYIU](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lQzVHj5EYIU)

4. Google's Ara is a Distributed Hardware Module Form Factor.

I'm certain that Ara is not a phone meant for immediate sale. Let's stop comparing it to the G5. They are completely different devices. While it might look like garbage commercially right now, technologically, it's a phone beyond comparison. It's closer to a device created by a research organization aiming to capture future computing technology, rather than a phone made by marketing and product planning departments like LG's. The difference between the G5 and Ara is as vast technologically as the gap between a smartphone and a feature phone. Comparing the two is absurd in itself. And the technology used to create Ara is quite useful. I believe it could become a pretty good platform for IoT in the future.

titleEn: Will Adult Content Save VR?
contentEn:
1. VR. Of course, porn will be a thing.

When talking about the VR market, there's always a joke that comes up: "Wouldn't the adult content market be easy?" And recently, I heard news that an adult VR content event in Japan was a great success.

http://m.wikitree.co.kr/main/news_view.php?id=263154&fb=1
                                **Wikitree │'Huge Crowd' Japan's First Adult VR Festival** Japan's first adult content VR (virtual reality) experience event was held. Japanese subculture news 'Nico Nico News' reported on the 12th. 【アダルトVRフェスタ】主催者「リアルはコスパ悪い」 超満員で入場不可の\ m.wikitree.co.kr

http://m.wikitree.co.kr/main/news_view.php?id=263154&fb=1

Upon hearing this news, many Koreans' opinions were often derogatory remarks like "land of perverts" or "perverted nation."

2. As expected, the land of perverts, while we pretend to be scholars. We don't go for the easy stuff.

However, I find these reactions uncomfortable. It gives the impression that "adult content" is a fruit we could easily pick, but we are too noble to do so, and it makes Japanese people seem like primal perverts. But I confess, I've encountered quite a bit of Japanese adult content. Even at a relatively young age, I knew content from companies like Elf and Illusion, which have recently gone bankrupt one after another. And I've also come across doujin games and doujinshi created by Japanese amateurs.

{{IMG:1}}

Does making something like this really look easy?

It feels like just yesterday we were disparaging Japan for being obsessed with school uniforms, but these days, it's not uncommon to see Korean idols wearing clothes reminiscent of school uniforms and performing sexy dances.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6hRntxJCgR0
                                **New girl group in school uniforms…'Uniform voyeurism' is a concern** New girl group in school uniforms…'Uniform voyeurism' is a concern [Anchor] With over thirty girl groups debuting last year, the music scene is overflowing with new girl groups, regardless of their fame. Many of these groups attempt a 'schoolgirl in uniform' concept. Why is that? Reporter Park Hyo-jung investigates. [Reporter] Long hair... www.youtube.com

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6hRntxJCgR0

I also heard that for VR filming of female singers, low angles are insisted upon. Simply put, this means that the commodification of sex is happening in Korea just as much as in Japan. The consumption rate of adult content in Korea is already self-evident, and everyone knows the existence of a sex market, even if it's not legally recognized. Even someone like me, who has never been to such places, knows where they are.

3. Not to point out the commodification of sex, but to look at it properly.

I'm not trying to say that I'm against the commodification of sex. The commodification of sex, as feminists argue, is not just about packaging female sexuality. Countless sexual codes are processed and sold to both women and men. Almost everything we know contains sexual codes, directly or indirectly. Sexual codes are not as simple as the general public thinks.

http://www.slideshare.net/yonghakim900/ndc-2014
                                **[NDC 2014] Moe Theory** In the East Asian subculture scene, 'Moe (萌え)' is a representative concept referring to attractive characters. What is 'Moe'? What kind of character can be considered 'Moe'? How can one create a 'Moe' character? This slide presents new perspectives on 'Moe' through various examples. www.slideshare.net

http://www.slideshare.net/yonghakim900/ndc-2014

In fact, the bigger problem in my view is that Korea is ignorant and has a low understanding of sexual culture and expression, to the extent that the idea that men are weak to visual information is used in school sex education materials.

{{IMG:2}}

It seems those who created this learned about sex from pornography and made their materials.

Because of this, there's a feeling that expectations for adult content in Korea are either excessively high or excessively disparaged. Adult content is still content. Content has diverse codes, changes, and is consumed. The belief that unconditional strong stimulation will be effective is on the level of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family's view of games as addictive substances, and actual content creators know very well that unconditional stimulation is not effective.

4. The reason I envy Japan is the cultural diversity that comes from lifting taboos and bringing things into the open.

The reason I envy Japan's adult content market is that there are so many diverse codes and layers, and the consumer base is visible, allowing for discourse on the topic.

{{IMG:3}}

The simplest example of a heroine... In fact, adult content is more diverse.

Therefore, Japanese sexuality is rich and can exist freely in other content as well. In old Korean movies, showing a beach as a metaphorical expression, when you think about it differently, how comical is that? A flash doujinshi I encountered in college had subtle ambient sounds with each page turn. The splashing of water in a swimming pool, the sound of the wind... The very effects you can feel in Naver webtoons today were being used in Japanese doujinshi when I was in college. Of course, there were H-scenes, but the direction was so fresh that it was shocking to me, and it was sufficient as a preliminary direction to beautifully depict the H-scenes. Thinking back, it had a bit of a Makoto Shinkai vibe, perhaps? And the advantage of Japan is that such an adult doujinshi market, as a paid market, greatly helps creators in their free creation. While Lezhin Comics occupies a position in adult content, and there are indeed some somewhat precarious contents, the scope of expression has expanded beyond just being sexually explicit adult material to various other fields. In some Middle Eastern countries, holding hands can be a sexual code, while in some tropical countries, exposing one's chest might not be a sexual code at all. In fact, the degree of stimulation and the code are determined by the consumer group and the direction. Something can be not explicit at all in its depiction but appear sexual through direction, and something can be explicit in its depiction but evoke no arousal and different emotions due to the direction. Simply put, many women are uncomfortable with explicit content watched by men, but in fact, female-oriented content can also be uncomfortable for men to watch. So, I'm not saying we should eliminate and despise both for each other's sake. The important thing is to recognize that appropriate content can be consumed by the appropriate audience, and that it might be uncomfortable for other groups, and to accept this diversity. I believe this is a good way to preserve cultural diversity. Of course, crime is another matter. In other words, we don't need to disparage Japanese adult content, and it's not as easy a market as one might think, as adult content is still content. Rather, I believe that because Korea consumes adult content covertly, disregarding copyright, situations arise where content and reality cannot be distinguished, and proper adult content is not valued.

5. Adult content is not easy, and VR is no different.

My opinion is the same for VR. While immersion is important in adult content, the elements that actually create that immersion are not whether it's 2D or 3D. If that were important, people wouldn't react to comics or graphics. The strength of comics and graphics lies in imagination. Immersion comes from imagination, not realism. Imagination is maximized through story and direction, not from UHD video where you can see every blemish on an actress. The same applies to VR. VR adult content is likely to be more limited in storytelling than in display. Just as VR games are experimental, VR adult content also requires much experimentation. Of course, VR adult content, being advantageous for curiosity, might be good for user acquisition. However, I'm still not sure if it will save VR. How many people would buy a million-won device just to watch porn realistically? It might be a means to attract curiosity, but I'm not sure if it will save VR. I believe something more than sexual curiosity is needed to make VR continuously essential.

6. Let's view VR as a technology that comforts humans.

Virtual sex is, in fact, a connection with lonely people, and VR embodies the value of virtual space. Expanding on this a bit, not just erotic sex but also platonic love is suitable for VR, and VR games and many other contents will try to explore these elements. Unlike AR, you can't see the person next to you in VR. And you also can't see that you're alone... I hope that VR technology can connect many lonely people to the world and bring them comfort. Here's an anime worth watching. For some reason, the full episode is on YouTube (it's not explicit).

titleEn: Interested in Investing in a Promising O2O Startup
contentEn:
1. Korea's Representative O2O Startup, Wyper

Following Cyworld, Wyper is the second company to attract investment interest on Wadiz, and I'd like to share its story. I've previously shared a link introducing Wyper, but this time it's introduced via a broadcast video, making it easy to understand.

http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220408564204
                                [**[Delivery Car Wash Wyper] Don't worry about hand car washes when you're too busy to die** 1. Why O2O? Now there's no business unrelated to software. Until recently, all startups were social net... blog.naver.com](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220408564204)

In '[[Infographic] Everything about Korea's O2O](http://www.mobiinside.com/kr/index.php/2016/05/13/korea-o2o-1/)' published by Mobiinside, Wyper is listed as a representative O2O company in the car wash sector in Korea.

{{IMG:1}}
                                
                            Car Wash O2O Company Wyper, featured in '[Infographic] Everything about Korea's O2O'

2. Korea's Representative O2O Startup is Up for Sale.

I've used a somewhat provocative title for the second section, but I'm introducing this opportunity because shares of such a famous startup are available for purchase. Of course, if you buy 1 share, the allocation is 0.0008%, and the maximum number of shares to be issued is 1.0985%. If you invest the maximum amount, you can secure about 1% ownership for approximately 50 million won. Of course, this doesn't mean you can buy it outright, as it won't exceed 50%. However, at this point, it's closer to angel investment or VC funding than crowdfunding. In any case, there are virtually no ways for non-professional investors to purchase startup shares, and even professional investors require significant coordination with the company itself. However, this type of crowdfunding allows the public to easily participate in small-scale investments, aiming for a high-risk, high-return effect, while the company itself can secure funding and achieve marketing effects.

https://www.wadiz.kr/web/wprogram/detail/336
                                [**Wyper, who goes to the hand car wash for me** Please crowdfund Wadiz www.wadiz.kr](https://www.wadiz.kr/web/wprogram/detail/336)

If it were to be acquired by a large corporation like Kakao, or if the lifestyle of the entire nation shifted from visiting car washes directly to using O2O platforms, causing the market size to grow rapidly, the company's value could grow just as quickly. That's precisely the advantage of internet service companies.

3. Disappointments with Wadiz Crowdfunding: Complex Procedures

The advantage of crowdfunding is light investment. Treating it like pocket money, or investing a small amount in a good company doing great things, might even be a much higher-probability lottery. However, what I felt when encountering this service was its inconvenience. Even during the Cyworld investment, there were difficulties like creating a securities account, but this time, even if you have a securities account, the registration process requires scanned copies of paper documents, making it seem not easy to start. It seems to demand the same level of effort as opening a bank account. I just want to spend my own money... ㅜㅜ

{{IMG:2}}

I don't understand why they separately require proof of identity like a driver's license or resident registration card scan when there are online authentication methods like mobile carrier authentication or universal digital certificates. For an online system, making it feel so 'offline' like this feels like a very significant hurdle. If this is due to regulations, I think they should be boldly removed.

4. Despite the Difficulty of Purchase, It's Selling Like Hotcakes

I was worried that many wouldn't invest due to these inconveniences, but only 6 days have passed out of a total subscription period of 47 days, and 31% has already been achieved. At this rate, 100% will be easily reached. This means that many people see its high potential. My only regret is that if Wadiz's investment process were much simpler, companies might have received more benefits from such crowdfunding. People abandon shopping carts if they're inconvenient; these steps before investing might be a way to make people give up on investing altogether. For the sake of discovering promising companies, I hope these aspects are improved quickly.

titleEn: Same Market, Different Strategies: Why Xiaomi Is a Real Threat to Samsung Electronics
contentEn:
The article was written in August 2015, when the Xiaomi craze was in full swing. I couldn't publish it on time, but I still believe it's meaningful, so I'm releasing it now, albeit late.

1. Same Market, Different Strategies: Xiaomi Enters the Smartphone Arena

Many compare Samsung and Apple, but recently, it's not just Apple that's giving Samsung Electronics a hard time. In the second quarter of 2015, as Apple's performance rose, China's market share plummeted significantly, while Chinese companies Xiaomi and Huawei saw their global performance increase.

{{IMG:1}}

2015 Q2 Global Smartphone Market Share

This trend is particularly pronounced in the Chinese domestic market, which is a standalone market comparable to the global market, signaling a red light for Samsung Electronics' smartphone business.

{{IMG:2}}

Until now, Samsung has tirelessly strived to produce high-quality smartphones to compete with global giant Apple, and has fought by collaborating with Google in the relatively weaker software sector. However, are new competitors like Xiaomi and Huawei threatening Samsung merely with what we commonly call "Made in China" or "price-to-performance ratio"? If so, it wouldn't be a huge threat. In fact, competing on quality-to-price ratio is something South Korea and Samsung have excelled at, and it's not significantly different from Samsung Electronics' strategy. Therefore, they would know how to respond, and I don't think it would be a major threat. If the problem were simply the quality-to-price ratio, it could be solved by moving Samsung's factories to China or Africa. Among these, I want to talk about Xiaomi, which is acquiring the image of an innovative Chinese company. For Samsung, Xiaomi is a much tougher opponent than Apple. This is because it employs a different strategy in the smartphone market than Samsung, directly targeting Samsung's weakness: software.

2. Why Xiaomi is an Overt Software Company

Why is a company that makes smartphones a software company? In fact, Samsung Electronics also develops software. Many people are involved in software development, and they are brilliant individuals who achieved top grades at the best universities in Korea. If you look at Samsung Electronics as a whole, its reliance on software is likely growing, as is the case with most companies worldwide. The problem, however, lies in Samsung Electronics' still hardware-centric culture and organizational structure. In contrast, Xiaomi possesses the following differentiators:

1) A Company Built by Software-Oriented Personnel

As is widely known, Xiaomi's founder and co-founders all come from software backgrounds. They are also very proactive in recruiting software talent, such as bringing in former Google executives. In IT, especially software, knowledge and process capabilities dictate corporate culture, so these human factors significantly determine whether a company is hardware-friendly or software-friendly. This means there is very little room for hardware-centric talent to interfere in a company that started as a software company.

2) Software Distribution and Update Culture

For a hardware-focused company, all revenue is earned at the time of hardware sales, so software updates represent additional cost expenditure. Therefore, it's crucial to accurately grasp user needs early on to minimize additional costs, and a hugely successful product can even hinder sales of the next product. Fortunately, smartphones show signs of aging, such as rapid battery drain, after about two years, but hardware faces a new challenge with each new model. This is why the Galaxy S6 is inevitably compared to the S5, and the company's fortunes fluctuate with the results of each new model launch. This characteristic means that the distribution of software included in products aligns with product sales, and typically, only quick patches to fix issues are performed immediately after product launch. Then, the highly capable veteran team moves on to develop new models, and a relatively less experienced team or new hires take over maintenance. However, what if the company is software-centric? Sales are merely the stage for creating customer touchpoints, and actual revenue is generated through business models *after* sales. A prime example is the Amazon Kindle, which adopted this model, and it's widely known that Xiaomi benchmarked it. For such companies, customers who purchase the product *are* the market. Therefore, to avoid losing the market, they must continuously understand market needs, and services—that is, software—are continuously improved based on data generated from customer touchpoints created through sales. This process is strictly data-driven, applying some features to a subset of users to gather feedback and assess the potential of new features. This approach is characterized by small, fast, and very frequent deployments. Xiaomi embodies these characteristics of a software company, releasing weekly updates. Although there's talk of Samsung adopting Agile recently, articles suggest that they are focusing only on speed as an advantage of Agile.

http://www.kbench.com/?q=node/153926
[**Samsung 'Galaxy S7' to adopt Agile development method... Development period shortened by 1-2 months | KBench** www.kbench.com](http://www.kbench.com/?q=node/153926)

In fact, the advantage of Agile is not speed, but rather the optimization of user needs through rapid changes. Agile without user consideration is like a corpse.

3. The Extreme Differences in Strategy: Mi Band vs. Gear S2

These differences between the two companies are even more pronounced in wearable devices worn on the wrist than in smartphones.

1) Lightweight Hardware vs. Eye-Catching Hardware

Xiaomi's Mi Band offers a light price (under 20,000 won) and a light product. It provides healthcare and alarm functions, which can be considered killer apps for wrist-worn wearables, and features a lightweight, long-lasting battery. It even sacrifices the watch function for this lightness. While it might not seem like a direct competitor to Samsung Gear, from the perspective of a service aiming to occupy a user's wrist, it is clearly a rival. For a software company making smartwatches, almost all wrist-worn devices should be seen as a threat. In contrast, the Galaxy S2 pursues the look of a luxurious watch with a circular display, focusing more on ostentation and fashion than practicality. This is the same strategy as Apple's iWatch, and Samsung's preoccupation with Apple seems a bit excessive. Of course, this has brought more profit than loss. However, unlike the Mi Band mentioned earlier, it doesn't provide a clear answer as to why one *needs* to wear a smartwatch. A watch that needs to be replaced after a year is unlikely to achieve luxury status. Unless, of course, the target market is oil tycoons who can replace multi-million won watches every two years. Ultimately, this has been proven by the lower-than-expected sales of the iWatch, and the Gear S2 appears to be following this failed strategy.

2) The Hardware is Light, but the Software is Anything But.

So, what is the aim of this cheap and seemingly flimsy Mi Band? As of June 10, 2015, the Mi Band had surpassed 6 million units in sales. In April, it was announced at 4 million units, meaning an increase of 2 million units in two months, which feels like watching the subscriber growth of a software company. Considering various IoT devices like the Mi Fit scale in addition to the Mi Band, it means Xiaomi's customer touchpoints, especially the number of app users, are exploding. Even when using a Samsung Galaxy smartphone, Samsung Electronics' grip on software services is minimal. Compared to Xiaomi, Samsung doesn't actively promote its own software, which seems to be due to Samsung Electronics' cooperative relationship with Google. In contrast, Xiaomi, which independently modifies Google's Android to create its smartphones, actively draws users into its own service platform. The app market preloaded in MIUI, which operates independently, had already reached 1 billion cumulative downloads in 2013 and is said to have reached 20 billion in 2015, comparable to Google Play, which launched in October 2008 and surpassed 1 billion cumulative downloads in July 2010. Furthermore, the 6 million sales of the Mi Band mean that 6 million people's biometric information is being collected. Moreover, the long-lasting battery and the non-intrusive nature of the device allow users to wear it even while sleeping. If the purpose is to collect users' biometric information, wouldn't a luxury watch worn only on special occasions be somewhat contradictory? If information is the goal, the device should aim to stay on the customer's body, whether they're in water or asleep. If this is important, even a watch that insists on having a constantly lit display should not be the target feature. Software companies value customer information more than product sales revenue because customer information is value itself, a value that can be converted into money in business. This consideration has led to the creation of extremely different products.

4. Xiaomi's Stance on IoT

**- Hardware margins are unnecessary; I'm only interested in services and data.** Moreover, the Mi Band is just the beginning. What about the IoT market that is about to unfold, or has already begun?

1) The core of IoT is not hardware, but user services and data.

Even without the absurd claim that sensor or network technology is key to IoT, many people still talk about the importance of technology platforms in the IoT era. This argument can extend to the claim that we must benchmark Android on smartphones and dominate the IoT platform through Tizen. However, looking at the current trend of explosive growth in hardware startups, it seems unlikely that an OS platform like Android will dominate IoT, apart from communication infrastructure like Bluetooth. The fragmentation of devices and the widely varying requirements make it difficult for such a general-purpose OS to dominate. Even if an agreement is reached in this environment, it is highly likely to become a loose standard, much like W3C's web standards. IoT has low dependence on technology; instead, it has high dependence on services connected to people's real-life activities. O2O is also one of the terms that always accompanies IoT; most IoT devices exist as touchpoints for O2O services, and the core here is the service provided via the internet. Therefore, IoT devices, though invisible like air, must leverage essential services as their weapon, with user data collection and processing as the core foundation of these services. Of course, this is clearly also software technology, like an OS, and thus requires software capabilities. However, it's closer to internet software than embedded software like an OS, making it much more flexible or much more software-technology intensive.

2) Maximizing the Value of Data is Connection

And the value of such data skyrockets when interconnected data is secured. For example, in healthcare, important information like exercise volume (e.g., step count) combined with user weight information significantly increases its value. In this regard, the value of Xiaomi's Mi Fit smart scale goes beyond that of a cheap and pretty scale. Therefore, sales revenue from simply selling scales becomes meaningless.

5. Can Samsung Innovate to Become a Company Like Xiaomi?

Which domestic companies could pursue such a business? First, there are LG and Samsung, which produce a variety of hardware. The problem is that they would have to start a self-destructive game, innovating the way they played, which relied on Google for software, and competing with Naver and Kakao domestically. Ultimately, success cannot be guaranteed as it requires innovation that abandons existing business models, and the price to pay is risking everything. In fact, the probability is low. The second option is for hardware startups to emerge and enable various interconnected data. In Korea, the overly strict and arguably ineffective Personal Information Protection Act might act as a regulation hindering such industrial development. Third, the most realistic approach I envision is for mobile service-based companies like Kakao to aggressively acquire companies through M&A, thereby capturing the user lifecycle. Kakao's aggressive acquisition of O2O companies is part of this context. While the iPhone in the past represented a vertical integration of technology, this approach can be described as more "Naver-like" in Korea, and Chinese companies like Tencent, Alibaba, and Xiaomi also follow this model. This strategy is a much tougher opponent for Samsung Electronics than Apple, which differentiated itself through innovative product sales and locked in users through vertical technological integration. This is because they are opponents who have changed the very rules of the game in the smartphone market where Samsung Electronics and Apple competed. While Apple, which tortures aliens to make high margins, still leaves some opportunities, a service company that drives hardware margins to zero is tantamount to a death sentence for Samsung Electronics.

6. Xiaomi's Challenge to South Korea

Furthermore, a factor in Xiaomi's success is China's environment, with vibrant hardware startups in places like Shenzhen, which serves as the world's factory and where anything can be prototyped. Even without significant technological prowess, excellent devices can be created with just brilliant ideas and software, and China has an environment where a second or third Xiaomi can emerge at any time. In contrast, Cheonggyecheon, once said to be capable of making nuclear weapons, is a story of the past; Korea's Yongsan Electronics Market barely sustained itself with computer parts but has recently almost collapsed. Domestic hardware startups knock on Chinese factories, and if they succeed, they then have to consider competing with large corporations like Samsung Electronics or LG Electronics in Korea. Therefore, it is by no means an easy environment for a company like Xiaomi to emerge. If this environment were limited to Korea, I believe it wouldn't have been much different even for a large company like Pantech. From this perspective, I reflect on whether we are placing excessively high expectations on Samsung Electronics, whether we criticize or praise it. Isn't an environment where various startups unleash big and small innovations far more realistic and beneficial for the nation than dreaming of innovation from a single heroic company like Apple? In a world of increasing uncertainty, there is a need to re-examine an economic system that focuses solely on large corporations as a single powerful solution. Xiaomi's challenge to Samsung is akin to a challenge to South Korea's economic system. What we should see in Xiaomi is not another manufacturing-centric conglomerate like Samsung Electronics, but China's robust startup environment and software capabilities.

titleEn: [Which is Lighter?] Surface Pro 4 vs Miix 700 vs TabPro S vs Teclast X98+
contentEn:
I prioritize portability most when purchasing laptops and tablets. I can tolerate slow performance to some extent, but since I travel a lot and use devices outdoors for extended periods, battery life and weight are crucial factors. However, when comparing these products, I noticed that they often don't clearly state the weight including the adapter or keyboard. This made it difficult to know the true weight when I put the keyboard and adapter in my bag for work. So, I decided to research it myself and share the findings. This is not based on actual measurements, but a combination of internet search results.

1. All-in on Portability: Teclast X98 Pro+ (800g)

First, the devices that score best in portability are naturally Atom-based tablets like Cherry Trail. These tablets are under 10 inches, making them excellent for portability. They are also inexpensive, but a bit lacking for everyday work. However, the price is truly attractive. The fact that the keyboard and stand must be purchased separately is both an advantage and a disadvantage. Thanks to this, it's possible to maximize portability under 800g.

http://teclast.co.kr/product/detail.html?product_no=57
                                [**Teclast Korea - Welcome to Teclast Korea. - Welcome to a delightful online shopping space!** teclast.co.kr](http://teclast.co.kr/product/detail.html?product_no=57)

Total weight is approximately 800g = Main unit (517g) + Bluetooth mini keyboard (180g) + Phone charger (30g)
Performance is a disappointing 1715 points based on Passmark X5-Z8500. The lower version, X5-ZX8300, scores 1193 points, quite a difference.

2. The Windows Standard: Surface Pro 4 i5 (1.36kg)

It looks light, but when you add the charger and keyboard, it's as heavy as a typical laptop. I didn't realize the pen was so heavy.

http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?nv_mid=9050071561
                                [**Naver Shopping** Microsoft Surface PRO 4 i5 RAM 4GB SSD 128GB shopping.naver.com](http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?nv_mid=9050071561)

Total weight is 1,357g = Main unit (786g) + Keyboard (310g) + Charger (154g) + Pen (107g)
Performance is 4305 points based on Passmark i5-6300U.

3. Surface for the Budget-Conscious: Surface Pro 4 M3 (1.31kg)

The Surface Pro 4 M3, widely adopted by students through aggressive promotions, is slightly lighter. Not only the main unit but also the charger is lighter.

http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?nv_mid=9050071008
                                [**Naver Shopping** Microsoft Surface PRO 4 M3 RAM 4GB SSD 128GB shopping.naver.com](http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?nv_mid=9050071008)

Total weight is 1,307g = [Main unit + Keyboard] (1,066g) + Charger (134g) + Pen (107g)
Performance is 3056 points based on Passmark m3-6y30.

4. Surface Pro's Chinese Rival: Miix 700 (1.33kg)

The Miix 700 closely resembles the Surface, and can even be equipped with a CoreM7 instead of a CoreM3. If you find the CoreM3's performance lacking, this is an excellent choice. RAM and SSD can also be upgraded to 8GB and 256GB.

[**Gmarket - miix 700 M7／8G／256G (Dedicated Folio Keyboard Included)** item2.gmarket.co.kr](http://item2.gmarket.co.kr/Item/detailview/Item.aspx?goodscode=767030746&GoodsSale=Y&jaehuid=200001169&NaPm=ct%3Dioc8zy40%7Cci%3D72d9aa033788e93190d4ba27e996928884ca6029%7Ctr%3Dslsl%7Csn%3D24%7Chk%3D84c0c167a707deac62c0158266dda958eb8295f4)

Total weight is 1,333g = Main unit (780g) + Keyboard (330g) + Charger (197g) + Pen (25g)
Performance is 3674 points based on Passmark m3-6y30.

5. TabPro S with USB-C Type Charger (1.10kg)

I had high hopes for the sleek and light main unit resembling a tablet, but the keyboard weight was an unexpected challenge. However, the TabPro S, which regains portability with its USB-C type charger, is here. The keyboard is a bit inconvenient, but it seems optimal for a compromise between performance and weight. I chose this one.
