titleEn: Legend of Dragonia Part 1 Episode 11
contentEn:
The gleaming blade rose above his head, and Aaron squeezed his eyes shut. Now, everything was over. Aaron had thought he was living solely for revenge against Anania, but with death staring him in the face, he recalled not Anania's face, but the events of his life. There had been countless hardships, but amidst them, the thoughts that arose were "I want to live" and fear. He had thought he could die at any time for revenge, but now he realized he had underestimated death. Just then, someone's voice boomed through the palace.

"Stop for a moment!" And then, silence fell. Aaron cautiously opened his eyes, confirming he was still alive, and looked towards the source of the voice. Aaron's body was still trembling with the fear of death. It was another merman, dressed in splendid attire. A sword hung at his waist, and he wore a magnificent coat and cloak. On his head was an elaborate ornament adorned with coral. At a glance, he seemed to be of a different social standing than other merfolk. All the merfolk, including the one who had raised the sword to kill Aaron, suddenly bowed their heads. "Your Highness! You mustn't do this!"

At that moment, an elderly merman stepped forward and pleaded earnestly. The merman prince then drew the sword from his waist and shouted in a voice full of rage.

"Stand back! Who dares to block me when I wish to see my mother?!"

The elderly merman retreated in terror. The merman prince stood before the mermaid queen and

I don't think so."
This time, Aaron asked, surprised, "Huh? Marry the prince?"
"We were in love, but it was impossible because of the class system. I even thought about running away with him..."
"To think of eloping with a prince of a nation... I don't know whether to call it amazing or naive. You're cute." Aaron hadn't disliked Elissa from the start, but as he talked with her, he genuinely found her cute. Then, this time, Elissa said with a slightly annoyed expression, "Hey... Is this kid making fun of his noona? Want to taste another knuckle-rap?"
"Oh, I'll decline. I've had enough of that taste already. You're a weather mage, but your mood is as unpredictable as the weather, noona."
Before they knew it, Aaron and Elissa had completely untangled their complicated feelings, to the point where they were exchanging jokes. "But there's something I wanted to ask." Aaron suddenly said in a serious voice. "You have something you're curious about? Ask anything. Except for things like my body measurements." "I'm not joking. What is the Dragon race you referred to as 'teacher'?"
At Aaron's question, Elissa asked back, surprised. "What? You didn't know that the person you're following is of the Dragon race? The Dragon race is the one that rules us mermaids. There's even a story that the Dragon race created the ancestors of our mermaid race. In reality, they are also very powerful... From the mermaids' perspective, perhaps they're like the divine race that humans talk about in myths? Well, from the perspective of those being ruled, there are many who don't think highly of the Dragon race, including those in the royal palace, but there are even factions divided into pro-Dragon and independence groups. Anyway, this whole situation worked out well for me. But you didn't know that person was of the Dragon race?" "Yes. Not at all... Weren't dragons just big lizards with wings?"
"Well, sometimes they are. But we don't know if their human form is their true form, or if that form is their true form. No, both are probably their true forms. For details, ask them directly. I'm too scared to even speak to them, but you're really traveling with an amazing person. Anyway, thank you so much. And, this is..." Elissa kissed Aaron on the cheek. "It's a gift in return." Aaron's ears turned red, and he couldn't say a word. "Hehe. Well then, I'm leaving. I have to go see my darling. Goodbye, cute little brother~ Go carefully." Saying that, she swam off into the blue water and disappeared. Aaron gazed at Elissa swimming away until she was completely out of sight, then slowly began to walk back to Elleasal.
"The mermaid race was surprising enough, but for Teacher to be of the Dragon race..."
Aaron instinctively sensed that his destiny had somehow become twisted.

titleEn: Legend of Dragonia Part 1 Episode
contentEn:
The sun was setting in the forest. The red glow of the sky dyed even the trees crimson, and the scenery was enough to evoke emotion in anyone who saw it. The crimson sunset, like a maiden's blush, found its way to the forest camp. For some reason, many people were gathered in the plaza at the camp. In front of the people was a wooden platform, and Aniam stood upon it, shouting to the crowd.

“Everyone, I thank you for your hard work. It is all thanks to you that we were able to safely conclude the battle with the monsters. And there is one more important thing I especially want to tell you today. Um... what it is, is...”

Aniam, who always seemed full of confidence, hesitated uncharacteristically before opening his mouth again, his face slightly flushed. Fortunately, no one noticed his face was red, thanks to the crimson sunset.

"This evening, I have decided to tie the knot with Danna. Please give us your abundant congratulations."

At the same time, whistles and applause echoed through the forest.

"Congratulations, Aniam. We were wondering when that news would come out."

At someone's shout, people burst into laughter. Smiles bloomed on people's faces for the first time in a long while, and everyone offered their blessings.

Soon, the sun set, and darkness arrived. People lit bonfires and reveled in the evening's joy, oblivious to the darkness. For this one day, sighs and groans did not echo in the night for them. There was one man standing far off, watching them with what seemed like envy. He held a hot teacup in his hand and watched their joyful scene, looking entirely like an outside observer. To him, Danna approached, holding Duma's hand. In the flickering bonfire light in the distance, her figure, dressed as a bride, was a blend of shadow and light, exuding a mature beauty different from that of a newlywed maiden.

"Ellasar, why are you standing here? Come join the fun."

"Huh? Me... Still, you haven't changed. That masculine way of speaking..."

"Tch. What's wrong with my way of speaking?"

Danna pouted.

"Since when were you two so close? Suddenly today..."

"Well... I should have known from the moment that old man kept saving me, but it turns out he had ulterior motives, didn't he?"

"Still, it seems like you're happy."

"Yes. I'm so happy."

A sense of contentment, as if felt for the first time in a long while, emanated from her face. However, she soon changed her expression and spoke with an anxious tone.

"But this kind of happiness makes me uneasy. Happiness always quickly slips away from me. I'm afraid of when this happiness will disappear."

"You have the right to be happy. Duma too, Duma must be happy. Having a father."

Duma hid behind Danna, like a chick nestling in its mother's embrace. Duma, who was always fierce towards others, strangely feared only Ellasar. Furthermore, Ellasar was the only person besides Danna who could look Duma directly in the eye.

Was it because Ellasar knew Duma's secret? Ellasar already knew that Duma was the child he was looking for, but he couldn't bring himself to tell Danna. Because that would mean the separation of Danna and Duma.

"Um... about Duma."

Just as Ellasar was about to speak cautiously, the camp's music suddenly stopped, and the joyful sounds of people turned into a murmur of commotion. As Danna focused on where the people were gathered, she could see them stirring.

"What's going on?"

Danna, along with Duma and Ellasar, went to where the people were gathered. A man was bleeding from an arrow wound in his shoulder and was being supported by others. Aniam, dressed as a groom, rushed to him.

"What happened?"

"The people in the watchtower were attacked."

"Monsters again? Even with that many troops, it wasn't enough?"

Aniam shouted in a panic.

"No. It wasn't monsters, it was the regular army of the Ceres Kingdom. A large force, at that. Everyone was either killed or captured, and I barely escaped after being captured myself."

Hearing that it was the regular army, Aniam sensed something serious and urgently asked again.

"Why the Ceres Kingdom?"

"From what I heard when I was captured, it seems there was a monster attack on Lasaea. They seem to be pinning it on us."

“What? You escaped? How?”

Aniam's face turned pale at his words as he asked.

"Well, my hands were just tied, and there were no guards, so I escaped."

The man answered, unaware of why Aniam was so surprised. At the man's answer, Aniam's suspicion turned into certainty, and he shouted.

"Those bastards don't take prisoners! Damn it! We're in big trouble! Our location has been discovered!"

"Gather everyone! Tell everyone to assemble in the plaza! Not a single person missing!"

The emergency bell in the camp watchtower rang loudly, and everyone quickly gathered in the plaza. The wedding celebration and the laughter of the people thus came to an end.

"Men who can fight are to remain here, and the rest of you, as soon as you are ready, flee to the northern forest. You must go as quickly as possible. It's a dark night, but there's no other way. The soldiers of the Ceres Kingdom will soon be upon us to kill us. Pack only a few necessities and travel as light as possible. Now, please prepare quickly."

As Aniam's concise and brief instructions ended, people went about their respective tasks. The men took up their bows and spears, as well as bamboo lances and hoes, their own weapons, while the women were busy packing their belongings. Only the children, unaware of what was happening, hopped around excitedly as if they were moving. Danna approached Aniam with a very worried look in her eyes. Aniam stared intently at Danna.

Then, he let out a small laugh and said,

"Danna, you look truly beautiful today."

"You..."

Danna's voice trailed off at the end of her address to Aniam.

"It's okay. I'm just listening to that shriveled old woman who babbled about Yin-Yang and the Five Elements... and we just happened to pick today's date... It'll be over quickly. I'll be fine, so take good care of Duma."

"I'll stay too."

"Don't talk nonsense! This is my first command as your husband! Please listen to me!"

Then, Danna retorted, as if unwilling to back down.

"I haven't even shared a bed with you yet. You have no right to tell me what to do!"

"Don't talk foolishly, I have enough headaches with the current situation. Stop acting childish. It's not like we won't meet again... Don't you trust me? I'm Aniam!"

Aniam shouted with a voice full of confidence.

"Still..."

"Please..."

At Aniam's plea, Danna finally nodded a few times in understanding and turned away. Aniam immediately went to Ellasar, who was sitting on a rock, tending to his blade. Aniam grabbed Ellasar's shoulder.

"That's a good sword..."

"It's a cherished sword."

"You don't have to stay."

"Huh?"

"I don't want to trouble you too. You're our guest, after all."

"But I could be helpful."

"I know your skill, but this battle seems difficult. I spoke lightly to Danna, but it seems..."

"Surely not..."

"Take care of Danna and Duma. At least until I return..."

Ellasar couldn't refuse his earnest request and reluctantly agreed. Many people were busily preparing to leave, but those who were ready began to depart one by one. The people's torches formed a long, continuous line. Those fleeing through the dark forest, avoiding soldiers, were enveloped in a somber atmosphere. Muttering conversations, the occasional cry of a child, a mother's anxious voice trying to soothe, someone's sobbing—it was an atmosphere entirely different from when the news of Aniam and Danna'

"Huh?" "I know! So! So! I have to go!" she cried in a voice like grinding metal. When Elleasal grabbed her arm and wouldn't let go, Danna chanted a spell instead of answering. "Aswat!" Instantly, Elleasal lost his sight. When his vision returned, Danna was gone. In front of Elleasal stood a child holding a long sword. It was Duma. The child's eyes were still cold, and a long sword was in their hand, while lights from magic and fire from the camp flickered like monsters, casting shadows.

"Let's go." Duma spoke to Elleasal for the first time. "You can save Mom," Duma pleaded. Elleasal had never dreamed such words would come from the child's mouth. As Elleasal stood bewildered, Duma cried out, "Then I'll go alone!" Duma ran towards the camp as if flying. Only then did Elleasal snap out of it and chase after him. "Duma! Wait!" Duma didn't answer and kept running towards the camp.

Just as he was about to enter the camp, he encountered a soldier. Duma saw the dark figure and, with a cold gaze, drew his sword. Duma had been secretly training quite diligently every dawn. The soldier screamed and attacked. Duma rolled to dodge, then struck the soldier's sword with Halhas's blade. Perhaps lacking experience, the sword that clashed with Duma's easily spun several times in the air and embedded itself in the ground. At that, the soldier, who had lightly dismissed Duma as a child, clearly showed signs of panic. Furthermore, the soldier, exposed defenselessly to Duma's long sword, was in an overwhelmingly disadvantageous situation.

The soldier screamed, drew a small dagger from his waist, and charged desperately. Even Duma, with his cold eyes, couldn't help but be flustered. The child had never killed anyone before. Duma's cold gaze was merely a facade, a way to defend himself by appearing cold to others. Inside, he was still just a child. What flustered Duma even more was the soldier's eyes, contorted with fear. The thought that if he didn't kill the enemy in front of him, he would die... Seeing his eyes, Duma was afraid. The soldier's skill was definitely inferior to Duma's... but defending with a cold gaze and killing someone were entirely different matters. The soldier wildly swung his dagger, but his fear was felt by Duma throughout his body.

'I can kill him... but should I kill this person who is only afraid of me? This person might also have someone waiting for them...' As these thoughts reached him, Duma began to waver. Moreover, against a soldier using a dagger, a long sword could only be used for offense, not defense. Duma was dodging his attacks here and there, but he couldn't keep dodging forever. Suddenly, with a chilling sensation, his clothes were torn. Only then did Duma realize his predicament. The death situation the soldier feared could at any moment become his own.

'In this situation, I must kill that person to survive.'

The soldier, his face contorted with fear, raised his dagger and charged. In Duma's now focused eyes, the random attacks of the soldier revealed huge openings. He couldn't keep retreating like this. More than anything, if he didn't get to Danna as quickly as possible, Danna might die. Finally, he plunged his long sword into the soldier's belly. At the same time, a terrible sensation of tearing flesh was transmitted from the tip of his sword. When Duma pulled out the sword, the soldier collapsed to the ground. The soldier groaned, "Ugh!" and tried to say something while looking at the blood gushing from his stomach, but blood surged from his mouth, perhaps having injured his digestive organs. Then he looked at Duma. His eyes were a mix of fear of death and resentment. That expression was more terrifying than a ghost. The soldier writhed, spilling an enormous amount of blood from his abdomen.

Duma's heart pounded wildly after killing the soldier, and the sight of the dying man was so horrific that he stepped back a pace or two. He continued to spill red blood onto the ground, convulsed a few more times, and then finally slumped, his eyes still open. Duma noticed an ornament tied next to the soldier's dog tag string around his neck. The ornament, tied with a red thread, was a token given by women or daughters to their loved ones going to war, asking for their safety. Seeing that token, Duma's legs gave out.

'What have I done? I've cut down someone who had someone waiting for them.' Young Duma felt like screaming. But before Duma could scream, a tremendous roar erupted nearby, and the soil that shot into the sky stung Duma's ears. It seemed magic power had fallen nearby. Duma's ears rang with a "whoosh..." And just as his hearing seemed to return, he heard groans and screams from people. It seemed the people directly hit by the magic power nearby hadn't died. Hearing that sound, Duma suddenly realized that the person hit by the magic power was surely one of the people who had once laughed and enjoyed themselves in the camp. Duma suddenly felt a chill and goosebumps from the threat to his life, and thanks to that tension, he was able to escape the shock of having killed someone. Now was not the time to worry about the soldier's life or the guilt of murder. Danna was dying. With that thought, Duma frantically wiped the blood from his hands onto his clothes and ran back towards the camp.

'I killed someone... but I had no choice. But I had no choice. Now I have to save Danna.' After running for a while, he arrived at the camp entrance. It was scorched and burning in many places, having been subjected to several magic bombardments. It was no longer a war, but a one-sided massacre. Some resisting youths died with wide, terrified, and enraged eyes, and the screams of people and the explosions of magic filled the forest everywhere. What was being trampled and rolled around were corpses. Amidst them, various items used in the camp lay scattered. Even children and women who hadn't managed to join the evacuation line fell to the swords of soldiers filled with murderous intent. To find even those hiding, soldiers searched thoroughly, mercilessly thrusting spears and swords into any place where someone might be concealed. Their eyes gleamed with madness, and the blood on their swords and uniforms made them look like devils.

A soldier heard the cry of a newborn baby coming from a bush and searched it. Behind the bush, a mother was covering her child's mouth. The mother looked at the soldier with eyes full of pleading and resentment. The soldier's cold gaze swept over them, and the child's crying stopped. Duma stood there, staring blankly at the unbelievable scenes. Duma slowly walked into the chaotic scene and suddenly noticed something at his feet. It was a crudely made puppet. It must have been played with by a child from the camp. There was blood on the doll.

'What happened to the child...?'

However, there was no time for deep thought. Several soldiers spotted Duma, raised their weapons, and charged. Duma quickly blocked with his sword. Duma remembered the terrible sensation from before, but he had no choice. The moment his sword roared, several soldiers fell, and an unpleasant sensation was transmitted from the sword's tip. Although they were said to be regular soldiers, they were troops from the rear, conscripted from nearby. Nevertheless, Duma, who had wielded a sword alone without any master, had his limits. There were some front-line soldiers who had been rotated to the rear, and they spotted Duma and pressed him hard. Before long, Duma was cornered, having sustained various injuries, and was about to take a fatal blow. Duma thought, 'Am I going to die just like the soldiers I killed?' and squeezed his eyes shut.

Just then, with a "thud," the soldiers' swords flew into the air. "Hold your sword longer!" Elleasal stood there, sword in hand. He skillfully cut down several soldiers. Duma looked at Elleasal. His appearance was different from what Duma had known before. His eyes seemed terrifyingly cold. Eyes he had seen somewhere before, Duma suddenly recalled Halhas's gaze. 'What were they thinking when they killed people? Then what about me? What should I be thinking? Why!' Duma felt even the unpleasant sensation transmitted to his fingertips becoming increasingly familiar. He felt both fear and doubt about himself.

Elleasal was single-handedly dealing with multiple soldiers while also giving Duma sword-fighting instructions. It was an overwhelming display of composure. Duma vaguely knew Elleasal was strong, but he hadn't imagined him to be *this* strong. Duma, Elleasal, and the soldiers fought entangled for survival. Their initial purpose was forgotten. For the soldiers who suddenly faced strong enemies, it was a fight for survival

Duma watched the demonic scene as if in slow motion. The flesh of the soldiers and the ground before him burned.

"Happy birthday! Happy birthday!" Duma had a chaotic day. Suddenly, Danna told him it was his birthday today, then took his hand and led him to a boisterous gathering of people. Food and good times... Duma wasn't used to such things. No, he thought he shouldn't get used to them. His father and mother, who died before his eyes... that scene never left his mind. He shouldn't be happy with them gone. He had to grieve forever and prepare for revenge. To do that, he had to become strong, and to be strong, he believed he had to abandon trivial affections. For that, he trained his body every dawn and practiced sword fighting, even without a master. Such a gathering could only bewilder him. But everyone rejoiced. At his birthday... Then Aniam said to Duma, "You can smile today, little one. Many people here have had so much sadness that they are starved for joy. So they celebrate each other's small occasions." 'Are they really happy for me?' Anyway, Duma spent the day like that. He even received a kiss on the cheek from a little girl his age... which made him blush from head to toe. Others laughed a lot, but as people were so boisterous, Duma found the sight pleasing and smiled without realizing it. It was a smile he hadn't shown in a very long time. So the day passed.

As it was almost time for bed, Duma gazed at the lake reflecting the moonlight. Duma drew his father's sword from its sheath. *Srrung...* The sword slid out very smoothly, making a cold, chilling sound. The sword glittered in the moonlight, and Duma stared intently at the sword, as if his parents' faces might appear on it. 'Dad. Mom... What should I do?' The joyful events of today overlapped with the happy times of his father and mother in the past. Going hunting with his father... causing trouble by setting fire to a barn in the village. The old stories his mother used to tell... Somehow, Duma's cold heart seemed to melt. A single tear flowed from his eye, then it seemed unstoppable. *Hoo-hoo-hoo...* He missed them so much it felt like he would go mad. In the heart of twelve-year-old Duma, his mother held such a significant place. His mother's warm embrace made the current cold night wind feel even more piercing. Duma sat, hugging himself tightly with both arms, his shoulders trembling.

Then... "Mom?" Someone's warm embrace held him from behind. It felt just like his mother's scent. "Duma. Did you just call me Mom?" But the voice from behind was different. "...N-no. You... misheard me!" Duma quickly wiped away his tears and replied curtly. But his voice was still choked with emotion, leaving him speechless. ".....Yes... It's okay... For now... let's just stay like this...." Danna just held Duma tightly. Duma felt Danna was truly like a mother. A warm embrace... He realized anew how much he had missed it.

Then, Danna continued. "I also lost my parents when I was young. But I had a younger sibling. Just about your age... But they died... But I decided not to grieve anymore. Because that wouldn't be what my sibling wanted... If I keep grieving, it feels like my sibling will remain dead forever. Their soul must have already flown freely. No, maybe I was afraid of being forgotten by that child. But you can't hold onto them forever, can you? It might be selfish for me to say this to you... but could you think of me as your mother? You don't have to call me Mom right now. But let's just stay like this... I'll take care of you, and you'll rely on me... No, let's rely on each other... because I also have so many hurts..." As those words sank into Duma's heart, he began to think differently about his parents. 'I said I would seek revenge... but for whom? Perhaps I was the one who kept my parents dead for my own sake... Perhaps I was afraid of being forgotten by my parents in heaven...' "Let's just stay like this..." Danna whispered gently into Duma's ear once more. Hearing those words, tears began to flow from Duma's eyes again. And his still small lips tried to say something. "Uh... Mom..." "Yes..." Danna, holding Duma from behind, sang a song she had once sung to her younger siblings. It was a beautiful and melancholic lullaby. "Oh... Mom! Mom!" Duma burst into a twelve-year-old's cry and hugged Danna back. His once-sealed lips called out the name he had so longed to say, without restraint. And silent tears flowed from Danna's eyes too, and in the sky, the moon smiled like Danna's sibling... like Duma's parents. A great light faded away. All those happy memories, just within reach yet disappearing, faded away for both Danna and Duma.

When Duma opened his eyes, only Elrasal and Duma stood on the ashes. The camp was completely burned down. In the distance, the sound of magic clashing with *pavabak* echoed, and the forest across glowed in various colors, accompanied by screams. It was clearly the direction of the refugee column. But those sounds quickly faded away. The frenzy of the battlefield also vanished. Only ashes remained where the camp had been. A pale moon quietly illuminated the ashes, which looked like a dark, demonic maw in the middle of the forest. Human corpses were rotting, unrecognizable, scattered around. The clamor of the battlefield had disappeared, leaving only the silence of the night, Duma, and Elrasal. There was no camp left, and no one alive. The night wind carried the metallic scent of blood, along with the sound of mountain birds, like sobbing cries, echoing from somewhere.

"Hezekiah is a technique only Anania's magic army can use... To use such magic even with allies present... Humans are utterly cruel." Elrasal spoke quietly to himself. But he received no expected answer from Duma. Duma, with his wounded body and mind, merely rummaged through the corpses under the faint moonlight. Soon, he found two bodies and carried them with his small frame. It was Aniam and Danna. They had managed to remain relatively intact, covered by other bodies. They were embracing each other tightly, as if confirming their love, dressed like a bride and groom. Fortunately, Danna's face was smiling, as if she had forgotten all worries. Now, she had truly returned to her family. Elrasal thought of Danna. For her, the world and war must have been a source of worry. Born of a different race, living a different life than his own... Then, he wished her happiness. Duma carried the bodies into the forest and cremated them. Elrasal sat on a wide rock in the forest. And he gazed at the moon. Duma had, in a way, returned to how he was before meeting Danna. Duma's animalistic, grotesque laughter and cries shook the forest. Elrasal quietly sat on the rock, looking at the moon, and sang an unknown song. It was hard to tell if it was a song or a spell... It seemed to soothe the sorrow of those who had died unjustly, and also sounded like the cries of many in pain. And so, the moonlight and the forest enveloped it all.

titleEn: Legend of Dragonia: World Settings
contentEn:
**1. What is the Magic of the Legend of Dragonia?**
Magic includes fire, ice, destruction, healing, escape, defense, psychological, natural force, and practical magic, and the types and power that can be used vary depending on the mage's ability. It is generally known that human magic originates from the power of the 'god' that humans believe in. Among races other than humans that use magic, dragons use magic composed of their own language, which humans cannot use. Furthermore, each magic has a magic circle symbolizing power, and these magic circles gather power to multiply its force. Magic does not consume mana, but rather stamina. The stamina consumed varies depending on the mage's aptitude. If a warrior with good stamina casts a spell, even the same spell might consume more stamina than when cast by a mage with an aptitude for magic.

**2. Types of Magic:**
This list is based on the current serialized content and may be subject to change in the future.

1) Fire Magic -
- Ul (Beginner): The easiest magic, used as practical magic rather than offensive magic when fire is needed.
- Ur (Beginner): Flames extend in a consistent attack direction. Despite being a beginner-level spell, its attack power is strong. Destructive power is doubled when used with a sword. (For swordplay)
- Sysmae (Intermediate): Fire gathers into a ball shape and is thrown. Intense flames explode around the impact point.
- Uriel (Advanced): Turns the area ahead into a sea of fire.
- Cereba - Undecided

2) Destruction Magic -
- Iwa (Intermediate): The attack direction is consistent. Everything is pulverized.
- Amasha (Advanced): The attack area is larger than Iwa, and its destructive power is also greater.
- Hezekiah (Advanced): Usually cast by several advanced mages combining their power. Its destructive power is immense, capable of obliterating an area with a radius of about 50M and creating a massive fireball. However, it consumes a lot of magic and usually cannot be cast alone, though legendary powerful figures seem to have used it solo.
- Vera (Advanced): The attack direction is consistent, and its destructive power is double that of Iwa.

3) Healing Magic: Healing magic is not omnipotent. It is only effective immediately after an injury occurs. Healing magic is less effective on injuries that have already begun to heal naturally.
- Irbuel (Intermediate): Can treat burns and external injuries.
- Yohah (Advanced): Heals a person's wounds for a certain period, as long as they are not dead.
- Yason (Intermediate): Increases consumed stamina and magical power for a certain period.
- Ezekiel (Advanced): Consumes a lot of the mage's stamina, but in critical cases, it draws energy from the surrounding earth to sustain the patient's life while healing all wounds.

4) Escape Magic -
- Eliezer (Advanced): A type of teleportation that allows short-distance instantaneous movement, but consumes a lot of stamina.
- Aswat (Beginner): Bursts light instantly to obscure vision and escape.
- Zephaniah (Intermediate): A hiding spell that makes the caster invisible for a short time.
- Age (Advanced): Can teleport allies. Consumes a lot of stamina.

5) Defense Magic -
- Shiryon (Beginner): Magical power explodes in one direction simultaneously with an incoming attack, neutralizing the attacking magic and largely defending against physical attacks. It can also be classified as destruction magic.
- Blegon (Intermediate): Defends by creating a circle of flames around the caster instantly. It can sometimes be applied for offensive purposes. Depending on the classification, it can also be considered fire magic.
- Yasera (Advanced): Envelops the body with a magical shield. It's similar to thinking of a steel spell like 'Astron'. However, the body itself does not transform, and it cannot be used for extended periods.
- Geba (Advanced): Defends a wide area at once. Consumes a lot of stamina, and cannot defend against strong attacks.

6) Ice Magic -
- Gorah (Intermediate): The attack range is radial, and the affected area freezes upon impact.
- Beret (Advanced): Cast above the target, magical power explodes in the sky and pours down around it. Magical power pours down like hail, and each individual strike has the same effect as Gorah.

7) Psychological Magic: Magic that causes fear, confusion, hypnosis, etc.
- Harada (Intermediate): Induces fear.
- Esdon (Intermediate): Calms the confusion, fear, and other psychological states of others.
- Birsha (Advanced): Draws out the evil intentions of an enemy. (Varies depending on the enemy's level of wickedness.)
- Beres (Intermediate): Induces doubt.
- Baana (Advanced): Makes the target feel as if they are in great pain.
- Maaga (Advanced): Induces a state of helplessness.
- Naaman (Intermediate): Boosts morale.

8) Natural Force Magic: Magic that controls natural elements such as wind, rivers, hail, rain, and animals.
- Yoreh (Intermediate): Summons rain. (The extent to which it can be summoned varies depending on the region's humidity.)
- Anan (Intermediate): Summons clouds.
- Sihon (Advanced): Summons a storm.
- Siha (Advanced): Drives away rain and summons drought.
- Buwa (Intermediate): Creates wind.
- Belek (Advanced): Causes an earthquake.
- Barua (Intermediate): Makes plants sprout or grow.
- Ghelada (Beginner): Summons animals.
- Abiyam (Advanced): Calms waves.
- Abia (Beginner): Creates a gentle breeze.
- Benebrak (Advanced): Summons lightning.

9) Practical Magic (Magic used in daily life, such as binding, opening, attaching, etc.) -
- Julio (Beginner): Binding magic, can tie ropes, etc., to desired places.
- Beor (Beginner): Opening magic, opens locked things.
- Dela (Beginner): Detaches. Used to separate things that are stuck together.
- Genan (Beginner): Attaches. Acts like an adhesive.
- Nel (Beginner): Emits light, acts as a torch.
- Emmaus (Beginner): Can warm objects.
- Hadit (Intermediate): Sharpens objects like knives.
- Ham (Intermediate): Can heat objects.
- Hiddekel (Beginner): Amplifies sound. For transmitting to people far away.
- Dilon (Advanced): Moves objects.

10) Light Magic (Magic of the lost ancient civilization of light) -
- Ebes (Beginner): Shines light in a straight line.
- Seretsahal (Intermediate): The area illuminated by the light energy beam shatters into pieces.
- Neriah (Advanced): When used with a sword, it requires less power and takes the form of a sword aura, with considerable force. It can be used as a light sword that extends for tens of meters, cutting through everything. When cast by a regular mage, it manifests as lumps of power.

===================== Currency Units ===================
1. Currency Units of the Legend of Dragonia
-1 Shekel (copper coin)
-1 Denarion (silver coin: 1000 Shekels)
-1 Talent (gold coin: 100 Denarions / 100,000 Shekels)
-Average monthly wage for a laborer: 1000 Shekels (1 Denarion)
-Aaron's monthly income: 3 Denarions (approx. 3000 Shekels)
Essential expenses: Food, accommodation (approx. 2800 Shekels - little to no savings, as a traveler, income is irregular)

2. Currency Units Used in Part 1
- Accommodation (50~100 Shekels)
- Meal (30 Shekels)
- Winter clothing (300 Shekels)
- Lysia's Brooch (10 Denarions)
- Lysia's Staff (1 Talent)
- Aaron's Dragon Fang / Sargon's Fang (50 Denarions)
- Lysia's Imitation Ring (100 Shekels)

titleEn: The Core of Chromecast is the Cloud App Platform
contentEn:
I wrote a post about Chromecast last time, and I'd like to share some additional thoughts. This is a prediction about Google Chromecast's strategy and how it might evolve.

**1. HTML5 Platform Already in Full Swing**
The source code below is for Chromecast, as introduced on Google's developer page.
<html>

<script src="https://www.gstatic.com/cast/js/receiver/1.0/cast_receiver.js">
</script>
<script type="text/javascript">

 var receiver = new cast.receiver.Receiver(
     'App ID', [cast.receiver.RemoteMedia.NAMESPACE],
     "",
     5);
 var remoteMedia = new cast.receiver.RemoteMedia();
 remoteMedia.addChannelFactory(
     receiver.createChannelFactory(cast.receiver.RemoteMedia.NAMESPACE));

 receiver.start();

 window.addEventListener('load', function() {
   var elem = document.getElementById('vid');
   remoteMedia.setMediaElement(elem);
 });

</script>

<body>
  <video id="vid" style="position:absolute;top:0;left:0;height:100%;width:100%" />
</body>

</html>
If you're a developer, this code will be very familiar. The code is very simple. It reads JavaScript and renders video. Also, let me show you an interesting article.

{{IMG:1}}
KT Media Hub, First Commercialization of HTML5-based IPTV…Also Kicking Off Platform Exports [http://www.etnews.com/news/telecom/telecom/2802778_1435.html](http://www.etnews.com/news/telecom/telecom/2802778_1435.html)
Another point is that everyone probably knows Tizen is already an HTML5-based platform. Even Windows 8 can be developed with HTML5. Perhaps Google's Chromecast could be considered one of them, an HTML5-based platform identical to Tizen and KT IPTV's web middleware.

**2. However, the Powerful Differences of Chromecast (Chrome Platform)**
**1) Chrome Browser Capable of Cross-Platform**
Tizen is a platform only available on Samsung phones, and KT's IPTV is only available on KT's IPTV. While there is technical compatibility with HTML5, if the browser is different, web applications will inevitably encounter compatibility issues. Even IE and Chrome show quite significant differences. Although HTML5 is said to be all-powerful, the reality is that development must be done "per browser" to achieve practical compatibility. Chrome is already the most stable browser across all platforms.

**2) Provides a Complete Environment for Cloud App Services.**
First, in the case of Tizen or Windows 8, only HTML5 is used as the language, but the actual operation seems to be binary after compilation. Rather than running on a web server, programs are downloaded and executed. In the case of KT's IPTV, it is structured to run on a server, but after a registration request to KT, it is verified and then distributed, which doesn't seem to differ much from previous DnP IPTV.
However, Google's significant difference is that it operates based on Google's cloud. This is similar to development environments like Google Apps. While it offers convenience to developers and users, it also provides a closed environment. Apple's iTunes was closed, but it didn't interfere with apps once downloaded from iTunes. Google's cloud apps, however, are closer to a structure where the app itself and its data reside on the web, meaning Google's platform must always be used.
While convenient, it entails strong control, prevents other platform providers from intervening, and carries the fundamental fear of the cloud: all data is controlled by Google, posing the risk of becoming a Big Brother.
On the one hand, it's daunting, but the powerful appeal of a global cloud platform provider is hard to shake off. Especially for CPs (Content Providers) who create apps, the Google platform will inevitably be a land of opportunity.

**3. Google Holding the Future of the Web, and its Ambition to Spread the Web's Platform Power**
While people say the web is the platform of the future, no one can deny Google's influence. The powerful strength of the Chrome browser, the establishment of HTML5 standards, and the strong influence of the W3C.
Chromecast is, in fact, another name for Chrome OS and the browser. And, with the ability to develop even Socket-based apps, the web is acquiring the performance and environment to run most games, excluding FPS and action games that require real-time capabilities.
Chromecast dedicates most of its explanation to video streaming apps, but this is merely describing it as an immediate killer application due to the characteristics of TV as a device. Most of Google's receiver app source code is written in JavaScript, and the resource links on the developer site also introduce core HTML5 app links, including Canvas.
The web is a platform that can be used universally, regardless of whether it's a large screen like a TV or a small screen like a watch. And any platform with a browser can run web applications, and Chromecast is what creates the possibility and APIs for Chrome to be ported to all screens. Chromecast can be applied not only to TVs but also to watches.
And all these screens, regardless of which platform Google Chrome is ported to, will be organically controlled by logging in with a Google account to a web app that supports Chromecast. This will even be possible on Safari on iPhones or IE.
Chromecast will be the simplest and cheapest device to draw all displays into Google's web platform.

titleEn: How Should Christians View Homosexuality?
contentEn:
Recently, due to some circumstances, I looked into information about homosexuality. In fact, I am a Christian. In Christianity, the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah is attributed to sexual depravity, with "homosexuality" being cited as one of its forms, and homosexuality is perceived as a sin. This is why, nowadays, the acceptance of LGBTQ+ individuals, including "homosexuality," is often linked to sexual depravity, portraying it as a sinful world. Traditional Christianity, in fact, taboos sexual matters, and this is observed not only in Christianity but also in Buddhism and Catholicism. So, how should ordinary Christians, not clergy, establish their sexual values today?

**1. The Christian Definition of Sin Was Defined a Thousand Years Ago**
Strictly speaking, the Christian concept of "sin," or evil, is fundamentally different from what the world calls "sin," or evil. Christian sin means anything that is not God. It differs from the concepts of good and evil in secular law or humanism. However, it is generally believed that God's good encompasses humanism and the world, so God's good must be higher than the world's good and must not be wrong. However, despite the fact that modern views on homosexuality and sexual minorities have changed significantly from the past, a problem arises because the biblical texts were written at least a thousand years ago. In the past, there was an impression that they were dirty, impure, committed sins, and spread diseases, and this was universally accepted. This view was maintained in many religions, not just Christianity.

**2. The Link Between Homosexuality and AIDS?**
In fact, it was only after researching the relationship between AIDS and homosexuality for this occasion that I understood their causal link. While homosexuality and AIDS have a high statistical correlation, I also learned for the first time that homosexuality is not the cause of AIDS. AIDS is a viral infection, and the probability of contracting it through anal sex is said to be high. Since gay individuals have a higher rate of anal sex, it merely appears relatively higher. In other words, if you look at the ratio of traffic accidents by gender, men appear to have a higher rate, but this is not because men are inherently more prone to accidents, but rather a probability issue because male drivers tend to drive more. While it's a bit awkward to write this on a blog for all ages, this means that a heterosexual person who engages in anal sex without a condom has a higher risk of contracting the disease than a homosexual person who engages in anal sex with a condom. Furthermore, female homosexuals who do not ejaculate are said to have a lower incidence of AIDS than heterosexuals.

**3. Leprosy: A Changed Perspective, Now It's AIDS' Turn**
It's a bit embarrassing to talk about sexual matters on a blog. Historically, AIDS is not the only condition that has been viewed this way. Leprosy, also known as Hansen's disease, recorded in the Bible, was also perceived as a punishment for "sin" in biblical times. And today, when we hear stories of pastors working in leper colonies, we consider the pastors great, not the lepers as sinners. This is also because the clear cause of leprosy has been revealed by modern science.

**4. Sexual Minorities and Rape Are Separate Issues**
Some strongly object to discussions about sexual minorities, a broader category than homosexuals, by asking if this means pedophiles would also be accepted. Indeed, when one thinks of pedophilia, child rape often comes to mind, making it difficult to accept. However, there is a misunderstanding here. It's not pedophilia itself that is abhorrent, but child rape. According to a certain manga (though its reliability isn't high as it's based on a manga), "lolicon" is said to be one of the most common sexual fantasies, affecting tens of percent of men. Not all of them become child rapists. This is, in fact, obvious. Just as not all heterosexuals become rapists. The problem is that while heterosexuals can easily find suitable partners, for pedophiles, finding a suitable partner can be illegal or criminal. Therefore, I oppose the marriage of pedophiles with minors who have not yet established their values.

**- Do Not Covet Your Neighbor's Wife**
Having materialistic desires does not mean one is punished as a thief. According to the Bible, coveting your neighbor's wife is akin to committing adultery with her, demanding extreme suppression of desires. Here, one could focus on "coveting," but also on "neighbor's wife." Coveting "my own wife" is an expression of the same desire, but it can also mean cherishing my wife. The criticism of homosexuality is similar. Homosexuals do not rape someone else's wife, or rather, someone of the same sex. Just as not all heterosexuals rape people of the opposite sex. The so-called "dropping the soap" joke is a common humor, but it's not an issue of homosexuality, but of rape, which is a crime.

**5. Sexual Depravity Needs to Be Redefined**
Did Sodom and Gomorrah really perish because of homosexuality? Between homosexuality that cherishes and respects each other, and heterosexuality that perpetrates violence against each other, which do you think is more criminal and depraved? Sexual depravity does not simply refer to a specific act or position. (It is said that in North Korea, anything other than the missionary position is considered embarrassing.) Now that I think about it, perhaps the meaning of 'sexual depravity' that I learned in Sunday school needs to be re-examined.

ps. For the record, writing such an article might make me seem like a promiscuous person, but I have only ever had one woman in my life. And I do not believe that the fundamental values of the Bible are compromised solely by the interpretation of homosexuality. This is because it has been humanity's role to interpret and apply God's word. The same word can be taught differently across different eras. Historically, religion and society have influenced each other and evolved.

**1. A brief introduction to NFC technology before introducing the case**
This time, I'd like to introduce an interesting idea smartphone case released for the Galaxy S4. (I guess you have to buy the latest phone to use the latest case... OTL) But before introducing the case, let's briefly explain NFC technology. The concept most similar to NFC for the general public is the bus card. This technology, which transmits data by mere contact within a distance of 10cm or less, is mainly used for payments and small-scale data transfers. Since it's often used as a tag substitute like QR codes rather than for large-capacity data transfer like Wi-Fi, it's more accurate to view it as a successor to electronic barcodes or RFID rather than for device-to-device data transfer. This technology gained particular attention due to rumors that Apple would introduce NFC technology to iPhones to dominate offline payments and ticketing platforms, and Google's Android adopted this technology first, leading to its widespread use. However, although NFC is already built into most smartphones, a killer app for NFC has yet to emerge as much as expected. But, surprisingly, a domestic company used the features of this technology to create an innovative smartphone case.

 **[ Cat Struck by Lightning ]**
When the phone rings, a part of the case lights up. It's presumed to contain low-power LEDs. Surprisingly, this case does not contain a battery. Nor does it use solar power or any other charging method. In a past advertisement, the superiority of AMOLED was emphasized by stating it doesn't require a backlight, describing it as "self-illuminating." This product, like the AMOLED ad slogan, is a magical product that glows on its own. However, it's not magic; it's an innovative product that utilizes the NFC technology explained just above.

**3. A power-free glowing case that also receives power via NFC**
One of the technical characteristics of NFC is that an NFC chipset operating in passive mode receives power from a counterpart NFC device operating in active mode, allowing it to function without its own power source. If you think of a bus card, the bus card reader operates in active mode, and the bus card operates in passive mode. And, utilizing this technical characteristic means that LEDs can be turned on in passive mode without a battery.

Thus, a domestic company created a sparkling smartphone case using these technical characteristics. The price is around 25,000 won, which is not particularly burdensome. What's important is that unlike cases that usually emphasize uniqueness solely through design, this one highlights its uniqueness by sparkling when a call or text message arrives. Given that a patent has been secured for this idea, it truly is an "idea product," and its novelty can be highly praised.

**4. How to use it?**
This case can be made to sparkle in the following situations and ways:
{{IMG:1}}
It goes without saying, but NFC must be activated. For calls and SMS, you need to use go Locker or Magic Locker. It seems these Lockers are designed to do something different with NFC during calls or SMS. Since using additional Lockers often means you can't use the OS's built-in lock screen function, I wonder if creating a separate app wouldn't have been a better approach. And through app customization, it could be made to sparkle even more beautifully.

When new technologies emerge, interesting idea products often appear that were not intended during the technology's development. And sometimes, these change technology to a new stage or provide solutions in completely unexpected fields. I think this product might be one such case.

**5. Design where technology and concept harmonize well**
Of course, the design element, which is the essence of a case, cannot be left out. Themes like 'lightning' or 'window' based on sparkling also seem to be good examples where concept and design are well-harmonized.

titleEn: Opposing Tax Waste, Daedong River Water
contentEn:
**1. I express my opposition to S# Mail.** Following yesterday, I'd like to talk about S# Mail again today. I had hoped this government would show pro-IT tendencies, such as creating the Ministry of Science, ICT and Future Planning, but I don't understand why the projects they're undertaking are so displeasing to me.

### Government to apply S# Mail to all public institutions… Activation plan to be announced as early as July (2013-06-19)

[http://me2.do/G68JLDRe](http://me2.do/G68JLDRe)
{{IMG:1}} First, the technology called S# Mail is not bad. I won't deny that it's superior to existing email in terms of security. This is because it's very easy to spoof the sender of an email just by changing header values. However, **I clearly express my opposition to this absurd legislation that mandates the use of S# Mail across all government agencies and makes S# Mail the *only* email with legal effect, such as certified mail.**

**2. Only secure S# Mail has meaningful legal effect?** If only S# Mail has meaningful legal effect, it means that all internet service terms of agreement processes, operational notices via email, and guidance via SMS would have no legal effect. It leads to the absurd conclusion that because something can be spoofed, it has no effect at all. If this happens, no internet business can operate in South Korea. If this logic is applied, does mail also have no legal effect if someone impersonates a postman to send registered mail, or if mail can be forged in transit?

What's clear is that both email and postal mail have legal effect. Therefore, it is clearly wrong to say that only S# Mail has legal effect, and that other forms have no legal effect simply because they can be technically forged or altered. This is because even such vulnerable mail or email, in the event of a dispute or legal issue, there are clearly circumstantial evidences or technical data that can be found if actual manipulation occurred. Furthermore, although it's an anomalous characteristic of South Korea, with many users on portal sites, it's not easy to forge or alter these either. When sending an email from Naver Mail to Naver Mail, even if it uses the mail protocol, it's essentially just internal network movement. And Naver is unlikely to step forward to forge it.

**3. They're not creating a message standard that only the government uses, at a high cost, are they?** One more thing, I don't understand why it's a high-security email designed for use only among internal civil servants. The security flaw of email is that it's sent between unrelated servers, so third-party verification is needed. Why is third-party verification needed when sending mail from one government entity to another?

**4. If storage is the goal, there are better and free options.** Furthermore, if storage is the goal, many email-based companies store, search, and utilize emails for work. And many of those solutions are free. Are they worried about it being hacked or forged?

**5. Whether sharpening a pencil or catching a chicken, use a cow-slaughtering knife. And all companies that deal with us...** I would understand if this were applied only to highly confidential documents with very high security needs, such as military or National Intelligence Service documents, but forcing it on the entire government and all companies that communicate with the government is applying an unnecessary level of security. Do they want to put expensive electronic locks even on dog doors at home?

The more communication, the higher its value. And email is a means of communication. Therefore, lowering the hurdles is very important. The first government's internet project in the 21st century is raising the government's threshold, and they're asking us to pay to cross that threshold. I'm speechless.

**6. Who is this repeatedly for? When the government's fairness is already questionable... what kind of fair market is this?** This seems no different from making private companies engage in stamp duty business. Who exactly is the owner of the private company that is extracting money from the nation, which is the people's enterprise, and earning such absurd net profits? Indeed, who are these projects repeatedly being done for? Instead of external companies, shouldn't the Fair Trade Commission first investigate government agencies?

**The act of legally protecting specific technologies and companies should be fundamentally prohibited. This destroys a fair market economy and is discriminatory legislation. This is a socialist-type "communist" project that conservatives so vehemently criticize.**

**P.S. For those who pointed it out, there is no law that explicitly mandates S# Mail. However:** The [Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions](http://www.law.go.kr/lsEfInfoP.do?lsiSeq=125865#0000) sets out some standard technologies, and S# Mail falls under this. International standard technologies do not satisfy this. It's similar to the public certificate case. It means "de facto" government standards are being enforced. Circumstantially, it's a de facto standard. I have no intention of playing word games with this. I'm thinking of writing another post about additional alternatives to prevent S# Mail from becoming a de facto standard, if I have time.

titleEn: Why Innovation Disappeared from iPhone 5 and
contentEn:
The sales rate of the Galaxy S4 seems to be much lower than expected. When the iPhone 5 was released, the market's reaction was that it was "just a longer iPhone," and the S4 also received reactions like "I don't know what's changed." However, looking at Quadrant scores, the S3 and S4 clearly show a twofold performance difference. Numerically speaking, the innovation, or rather, the advancement from S3 to S4 is as significant as the advancement from S2 to S3. So why has everyone grown tired of the S4 and iPhone 5?

**1. Standardized smartphones, having reached a high level, desire reliability over innovation.**
This also means that recent smartphones have become quite usable. What do you look at when choosing a car? Do you look at how much the horsepower and top speed have changed between the 2012 and 2013 models? Or do you look at whether it's a Hyundai or a BMW? You'd probably choose the latter. The commonality between Hyundai and BMW is that they are both now usable cars. This means we are now at a point where the focus is shifting from innovation to brand reliability. In that regard, the weapon of trust that Samsung and Apple have gained in the smartphone market now seems difficult for other smartphone developers to challenge with minor innovations.

**2. Can there be innovation in smartphone apps?**
Perhaps, as I've often written in past posts, the new innovation that hardware manufacturers can create is software. However, even this now seems difficult. This is because an enormous number of software companies have emerged in the smartphone market, experimenting with countless ideas, and leading software companies have already secured top positions in each sector. It has already become an established fact that it is difficult to capture this market with pre-installed apps alone. There isn't much that manufacturers do better than other software companies. Also, for this reason, users no longer actively seek new apps. Whatever app they need, there is usually an app for it, and they look for the most reliable, representative app.

**3. This signifies the ossification of the smartphone market.**
This means that the smartphone platform has already become quite solidified. Therefore, if we are to talk about innovation in smartphones, it will now happen *outside* the smartphone itself. Whether it's a watch, a tablet, or a new software service linked to offline activities, I expect comet-like companies to emerge from *outside* the platform, rather than new comet-like companies appearing within the already established structure.

**4. Still remaining emerging markets, smartphone growth is still ongoing, but not for flagships.**
Of course, not everything is over. Many countries where smartphone penetration is still low remain blue oceans. Therefore, the smartphone SW and HW markets are expected to continue growing, centered around these emerging markets. A characteristic of these countries is the strong demand for usable and affordably priced devices rather than flagships like the iPhone 5 or Galaxy S4. For this reason, I believe the smartphone war is already shifting towards budget models.

titleEn: [Patent] Naver Green Window: Method, System
contentEn:
This was once a feature in the Naver app. It seems to have been removed due to low user satisfaction compared to its technical difficulty. This is a currently registered patent, and I am releasing the draft.
METHOD, SYSTEM AND COMPUTER READABLE RECORDING MEDIUM FOR RECOGNIZING MULTIPLE INFORMATION USING MOBILE CAMERA AND SEARCHING USING THE SAME

Application Number: 1020100043089 (2010.05.07) - Registration Number: 1011934850000
Applicant: NHN Corp. / NHN Business Platform Corp. Inventor: Yang Byung-seok, Kim Hyung-tae
**1. Title: Search Window Recognition and Application Technology Using Mobile Camera**
2. Introduction: In the case of domestic portals, promotions using search windows are active. Phrases like "Try typing *** into the Naver search window," which are frequently seen online and offline, have been utilizing the CI, such as the "Green Window" of each portal, for several years. This search window offers superior user recognition compared to 2D barcodes or QR codes and even has an advertising effect. We will configure a search technology utilizing this.
**3. Technical Applicability** - The Green Window has a very simple feature, being in the form of black text on a white background with a green rectangular border. - It is also a very easy form to recognize, especially with black Gothic text on a white background.{{IMG:1}}
**4. Basic Configuration Diagram**
1) Mobile Client: Search Window Recognition
   - The application searches for the existence of a search window using a real-time camera app.
   - There is also a method to increase the recognition rate by overlapping the Green Window's guidelines in terms of UI. (Optional)
2) Query Extraction
   - The search window transmitted to the server extracts the query through preprocessing and OCR technology.
3) Mobile Search Result Generation
   - Extracts the URL of the corresponding mobile page or mobile search results from the recognized query.
4) Transmits the generated mobile search results to the client.
5) Renders the received results on the mobile device.
**5. Usage Examples**
 - If there is a Green Window at a bus stop containing the bus stop number, taking a picture of it immediately searches for bus stop information.
 - When photographing the Green Window on a florist's sign, it shows search results for "florist."
 - When photographing the business card address in a Green Window on a business card, it downloads the online business card.{{IMG:2}}
**6. Application Technology**
1) Insertion of additional information defining the attributes of the search query
 - The query within the search window can represent not only information for integrated search but also image search, online business cards, blog addresses, etc. For this, formal additional information can be inserted in advance.
   ex) If [Blog - fstory97] is searched within the Green Window, it immediately navigates to m.blog.naver.com/fstory97.{{IMG:3}}
   This additional information can be a Symbol rather than text.
   If it's [☞ Namdaemun], it is recognized as a search query for Naver Map service.{{IMG:4}}
2) Selective search by defining the attributes of search results in a mobile app
 - Place multiple search buttons next to the Green Window guideline on the LCD.
 - Integrated search, image search, Knowledge-in search buttons. When aligning with the Green Window and pressing each button, different search results are shown.
 - Alternatively, it is also good to determine the recognized query first and then allow the user to select which search result to navigate to.
**7. Revenue Model**
- Keyword bidding on mobile web
- Mobile business card service for businesses and retailers

titleEn: Google Project Glass's True Intentions
contentEn:
Expectations for Project Glass at Google I/O were high, but nothing came out that made us say "wow~" like when the iPhone was first released. Will Google really release something as cool as Apple's iPhone? Here's a video that I'd like to share, which I think clearly shows the current state of Google Project Glass.
{{IMG:1}}

http://techcrunch.com/2013/05/10/through-the-looking-glass-what-youll-see-through-googles-lens-tctv/

[http://techcrunch.com/2013/05/10/through-the-looking-glass-what-youll-see-through-googles-lens-tctv/](http://techcrunch.com/2013/05/10/through-the-looking-glass-what-youll-see-through-googles-lens-tctv/) It's actually questionable how many users would pay $1500 for such a device. Therefore, the commercial success of the product itself seems uncertain in reality.
However, there's one thing that's been overlooked: Google is not Apple or Samsung. Google is a software company. Would the product success of Project Glass truly be meaningful to them? So, what is Google really aiming for? Here are the scenarios I'm thinking of:

**1. Future User UX Collection and Experimentation**
Whether computers are embedded in lenses or prosthetic bodies are used like in Ghost in the Shell, it's clear that future users will be connected to computers in their daily lives. Even today's smartphones seem to be always with us, but they are not used while driving, during meetings, or during certain actions. During those times, connectivity is interrupted, leading to a disconnected experience, and they are primarily content consumption devices.
However, Project Glass is the first always-connected device. It can provide the necessary computing environment even while driving, in meetings, or studying.
At the last PAG discussion, I heard that the Project Glass planner first experimented with it at MIT because looking down to take notes while listening to a professor's lecture was a disconnected experience, and they wanted to overcome that. They wanted to create a device that could perform both actions – listening to a lecture and taking notes – simultaneously.
Project Glass is an experimental work for this. One of those actions was voice and touch, and perhaps in the future, it will involve gestures or separate sensors worn on fingers or wrists. Perhaps if Google Watch and MYO, which uses muscle nerve sensing, are combined, they could become new input devices for Project Glass. This means Project Glass might not be a complete service product on its own.
And all these attempts by users and developers will be recorded and analyzed by Google. Personally, if Google aims for this, I think they should release it to developers and schools at a particularly lower price.

**2. Future Search and Information Acquisition Experimentation**
Ultimately, it is judged to be a stepping stone for search, Google's main revenue source. It's clear that future search won't be done sitting in front of a PC. While mobile search is emerging, I believe it falls within the framework of 'mobile search'. This means it's a subset of the search that can be done with Project Glass. Therefore, it can be said that Project Glass offers the most hints for Google's future.
The reason maps and natural language search were introduced at Google I/O 2013 is also a scenario leading to Project Glass.

**3. Patent and Technology Acquisition**
To turn these intellectual experiences into assets, output will ultimately be needed. I think Google can patent these. The method of projecting onto the retina using a prism, which is Project Glass's approach, is quite groundbreaking in terms of display technology. It's also the most realistic miniaturization method before digital lenses emerge. Furthermore, the user data already discussed above becomes a valuable asset for Google. Through the insights gained from this, new technologies can be invented and patented.
The company Nuance, which created the technology for Apple's SIRI, has a very long history. Starting in 1974, this company can be said to be the history of recognition technology, with over 1000 voice recognition patents. SIRI is not perfect. However, without using Nuance's technology, it's difficult to create anything similar to voice recognition. And the patents acquired through Project Glass could become an unavoidable minefield in the future era of lens computing or ocular computing.

**4. Pre-emption of the Cloud Infrastructure Market for Wearable Computing**
When simply thinking of wearable computers, I used to imagine computers using sensors, but Project Glass is making a more Google-like attempt. This Google wearable computer allows apps to be created using Google's APIs and has large-scale servers to mediate them. This structure can be applied not only to Google Project Glass but also to other wearable computers. It can be called a Google-like attempt, as an internet platform company. If Samsung or Apple had made it, I wonder if they would have made such an attempt. And what's clear is that any future device will need this kind of software infrastructure. The fact that Android OS is now found not only in smartphones but also in TVs, game consoles, and even refrigerators and washing machines is a form of this software power. And the seamless Project Glass is strengthening its ownership by turning this into an API. Currently, it's no exaggeration to say that there are almost no companies that can compete with Google in this regard. And someday, this market will open.

**5. The best way to predict the uncertain future is to create it.**
I don't remember where I heard this before. "The best way to predict the uncertain future is to create it." Google is trying to realize this. This is possible partly because they have already amassed enormous capital. However, our reality is that we only chase trends like 'Web 2.0, social, mobile, big data,' and it's difficult for tech companies to survive. Isn't that too different from us, who are only focused on immediate concerns and survival? I wonder if we are truly ready to face such a future.

titleEn: The Era of the Creative Economy: How Should We View Namyang Dairy?
contentEn:
**1. Creative Economy and Namyang Dairy**
The Namyang Dairy incident is becoming a hot topic. Furthermore, this incident is significant because it goes beyond a simple "갑(gap)-을(eul)" (principal-agent) relationship and is deeply connected to "co-prosperity," a core pillar of the creative economy currently under discussion. I am a service developer and planner, not well-versed in management or finance. However, I am very interested in the new business models emerging in the IT industry, as they are said to be created by new economic values. Whatever the case, the core axis of the creative economy, as discussed by the Park Geun-hye administration, aims for a more diverse and organic economic model, rather than a leadership economy centered on large corporations. Those who believe that large corporations are the epitome of capital consider this to be leftist and even communist.

**2. Anti-large corporation economic slogans do not mean socialism.**
It is completely different from socialism. Socialism is, in fact, the ultimate leadership economic model. The government is virtually a single enterprise, and state-owned enterprises are seen as mere departmental roles within that enterprise. In other words, if a socialist country were considered a company, it would be a single company with a seniority-based pay system, whereas a capitalist country could be seen as a company with annual salaries and incentives. In truth, it's hard to say which has more advantages or disadvantages, so today's economy is neither perfectly capitalist nor perfectly socialist. This is called modified capitalism. And for your information, the opposite of the political term "democracy" is not the economic terms "socialism" or "communism." The opposite of the political term "democracy" is "totalitarianism." It is correct to call North Korea a totalitarian state.

**3. Collusion and Monopolies/Oligopolies that Distort Equal Transactions, the Flower of Capitalism**
I think the explanation that it's not communism is sufficient here. Large corporations and small and medium-sized enterprises, principals and agents (갑 and 을), employers and employees – these are all essentially the same relationship. And the core of capitalism is not capital itself, but the measurement of capital's value and the exchange of various forms of capital. All of these exchange labor and products based on currency. And this relationship is one of equal "transactions," not a hierarchical one. However, there are cases where these equal transactions become unequal. According to the tenets of capitalism, if the law of supply and demand functions properly, the price of a transaction may decrease, but the relationship should remain equal. But this equal relationship breaks down when external factors cause the law of supply and demand to malfunction. These are monopolies/oligopolies and collusion. And a country where this reaches its extreme is not a capitalist country, but rather a socialist country that permits monopolies/oligopolies. Therefore, a healthy capitalist country should strive to minimize monopolies/oligopolies and collusion. Looking at the Namyang Dairy incident, is this simply a problem between Namyang Dairy and its distributors? Why can't distributors easily switch to other milk products despite experiencing this inequality? And why has such a situation been left unaddressed for so long, as if it were natural?

**4. The Second Party Responsible for This Incident is the Government**
Here's the core point I want to make. Namyang Dairy bears the greatest fault in the Namyang Dairy incident. So, who's next? I can't pinpoint a specific government, but all South Korean governments since liberation, which became a capitalist nation, bear responsibility for what has happened. Of course, a long time ago, they might not have even known this was their responsibility, and their understanding of these principles might have been low. Therefore, this incident is not merely a problem of a certain large corporation failing to achieve co-prosperity; it is the government's job to consider why such practices have been prevalent and considered natural for so long, and to devise ways to prevent them. Many companies that have benefited from monopolies/oligopolies and collusion, likely mostly large corporations, might find this sudden, but they must recognize that the time has come to change the economic paradigm.

**5. Is Namyang, Unfazed by a 10-Year Business Suspension, a Good Company?**
Another interesting point about this incident is the perception that Namyang Dairy is a blue-chip stock and will remain unaffected no matter how widely this issue spreads. And the perception that it will eventually return to normal. Behind this is the talk of its massive cash reserves, which are supposedly enough to disregard consumer boycotts. Some even say it could survive without operating for 10 years. While such cash reserves do play a significant role in increasing a company's value, from the perspective of the nation and the market, is this truly a good company? A company that can survive for 10 years without earning a single penny – why should such a company exist in a capitalist society? Or, why did this company possess such massive, unnecessary cash reserves in the first place? Ultimately, this only causes monetary expansion and inflation, doing nothing to help the national economy. Would a company like Namyang Dairy, which is not even human, be happy having accumulated retirement funds to live off for 10 years? I don't understand why such a company would make its sales staff work. Couldn't it just enjoy the best welfare for 10 years and live happily? South Korea has achieved much growth through monetary expansion during its rapid development. However, this can no longer continue. Instead, we must focus more on making stagnant money flow. In the past, accumulating money was considered meaningful. The rich were thought to be individuals and companies with more cash. But in reality, capital only has meaning when it is exchanged. In a healthy capitalist system, households provide labor and consume, while companies pay wages and produce. Therefore, money (capital) stagnating on one side essentially means depletion on the other. And this creates a vicious cycle. The government's responsibility, as the operator and manager of this platform, is to ensure that money flows well and doesn't stagnate. **From the perspective of the market or the government, isn't a company that can remain unfazed for 10 years not a good company, but rather a bad company that has effectively postponed several years' worth of investment or employment?**

**6. For South Korea to Survive, Good Companies Must Survive.**
For South Korea to survive, good companies must survive. This doesn't simply mean companies that perform good deeds. It means companies that compete fairly and properly must survive. Companies based on illicit practices and power, having not learned how to compete fairly, could collapse helplessly in the global market where such practices and power do not work. Protecting good companies and either improving bad companies or making them lose competitiveness – this is our homework. ps. As this post was written with limited knowledge, there may be leaps in logic or inaccuracies. I am indeed becoming increasingly skeptical about capitalism in many ways. Things I absolutely believed in collapsed at the end of the 20th and into the 21st century. I've seen countries and banks fail, and realized the illusion of reserve currencies. I even wonder if the dollar or won, which we firmly believe in, are no different from in-game currency. In such a world, what kind of economic perspective should we establish? How can we live without worshipping money, without being dominated by it, and while preserving human dignity? I believe this is the challenge of the 21st century.
