titleEn: My Thoughts on ChatGPT-4o'
contentEn:
I officially took over the project and got back into development work after a long time. In particular, the things I posted on my Facebook timeline about how shocking ChatGPT-4o was, received good reactions, so I'm sharing them on the blog as well.

ChatGPT-4o really came out at the right time. Without it, my understanding of the code I inherited wouldn't have been complete, and I would have spent a whole day re-studying grammar, fixing things, and going through trial and error. It was done in just 1 hour. All that's left is for the batch to run through all projects, completing all data migration due to the termination of hubs... With this, XRCLOUD has become completely independent from the Hubs project, even with its data. I should write a post. In fact, after a month or two, I wonder if working alone will lead to faster development because I won't have to explain the work... AI seems to extremely boost the capabilities of seniors.
May 17, 2024 (https://www.facebook.com/fstory97)

The reason why juniors' productivity improvement is slow even when they adopt AI is that they can't visualize the architecture, making it difficult to formulate questions. When a problem occurs, GPT explains it, but they can't understand the explanation and are forced to copy and paste. The danger of copy-pasting is that if executed incorrectly, it can break the code or architecture. They need to be instructed to properly break it down and create modules, and when reflecting it in a live service, they must consider the risks to the live service. However, it's difficult for juniors to do this. In the past, we needed juniors who learned by creating relatively simple code, but now ChatGPT seems to completely take over that role and steal their learning opportunities. It doesn't seem like this only happens with AI art. Ultimately, what schools should teach are fundamental things like computer architecture and the knack for learning by building projects with AI.
May 17, 2024 (https://www.facebook.com/fstory97)

#ChatGPT-4o #AIdevelopment

titleEn: Nuclear vs. Solar: Which is the more economical energy
contentEn:
I saw a post criticizing exaggerated data about solar power. It claimed that China's solar capacity exceeded 500GW, surpassing nuclear power... which is, of course, a lie. While solar power is growing rapidly, it has not yet surpassed the energy output of nuclear power. This is because, purely in terms of electricity generation, nuclear power is quite an effective energy source. If you only look at generation volume, that is. But what if we include land costs, construction costs, and disposal costs? It's naturally expected that these costs would be difficult to estimate. Most comparisons of energy production costs use maintenance costs as the standard, positioning nuclear power as the cheapest energy source. Hmm... but I wondered if that was really true, so I asked ChatGPT4. Its conclusion was solar power. This answer is significant because ChatGPT4 has collected numerous data points up to 2023 and is aware of many academic papers. While I can't exactly say it 'understands,' due to the nature of LLMs, more frequently mentioned data or papers will be weighted more heavily, and by leveraging the relationships between tokens, more accurate answers can be elicited depending on how the question is posed. When I asked for representative recent data arguing for nuclear power's economic advantage over solar, several technologies already known in Korea came up. However, these technologies are all under development and are not existing technologies, meaning they haven't been proven in practice. So, when asked which is more economical if one had to choose now, it answered: solar power. I don't believe any political judgment was involved here. Finally, when asked 'How should Korea formulate its policies?', the answer was somewhat textbook-like. However, whether Korea is actually following that textbook approach, I'll leave to individual judgment. Starting with ChatGPT4, hallucinations have significantly decreased, and it provides sources, allowing for cross-checking. Especially in STEM fields like science, which are generally built upon textbook knowledge, it seems to provide very accurate answers. I feel that the trends in learning and searching have completely changed.

**Question:** Between nuclear and solar power, which is more economical when including land costs and construction costs? Please also compare them, even if not precisely, including the disposal costs of their power generation facilities.

**ChatGPT:** When comparing the economic viability of nuclear and solar power generation, the main cost factors to consider are as follows:
- **Land Costs**: Solar power generation requires a relatively larger area of land compared to nuclear power. This varies depending on the location and region of the power plant, and land prices also significantly impact the cost.
- **Construction Costs**: The construction cost of nuclear power plants is generally higher than that of solar power plants. Nuclear power plants require high levels of safety and complex technology, leading to significant initial investment costs.
- **Operation and Maintenance Costs**: Nuclear power plants have relatively low fuel costs and can provide a stable energy supply. In contrast, solar power plants have almost no maintenance costs, but their power generation can fluctuate depending on the availability of solar energy.
- **Decommissioning and Disposal Costs**: The decommissioning and disposal costs for nuclear power plants are very high, requiring the safe handling of radioactive waste. While the recycling and disposal costs for solar panels are relatively lower, environmental impacts still need to be considered.
To compare overall economic viability, various factors beyond these costs must be comprehensively considered, including generation efficiency, technological advancements, government policies and subsidies, environmental impact, and social acceptance. For an accurate comparison, the latest data should be referenced. However, my knowledge is based on information up to April 2023, so it is advisable to check the most recent economic analyses or research findings. Based on current trends and available data, the cost of solar power generation is continuously decreasing, and its long-term economic viability is expected to increase due to improvements in technological efficiency. On the other hand, nuclear power requires more complex considerations regarding economic viability due to high initial investment costs and concerns about waste disposal. To find the latest comparative analyses or research results, it is recommended to consult recent research reports or analyses by energy economics experts in the field.

**Question:** Are there any representative reports or papers related to this? And what conclusions do these reports and papers draw?

**ChatGPT:** Several important conclusions have been drawn in representative reports and papers regarding the economic comparison of nuclear and solar power generation. Lazard's 2023 Levelized Cost of Energy+ report provides a detailed analysis of the levelized cost of energy for various generation technologies, energy storage technologies, and hydrogen production methods. This report emphasizes that large-scale companies can leverage supply chains and other economies of scale, and companies with these advantages will continue to lead the development of new renewable assets.

According to an analysis by EnergySage, one of the biggest differences between solar and nuclear power generation is the cost and time required to construct each facility. Nuclear power plants cost significantly more and take a longer time to come online. For example, a single nuclear power plant recently constructed in the U.S. took over 30 years to complete, and ongoing projects are experiencing budget overruns and delays. In contrast, multiple solar projects have been completed within the same period, built with significantly less cost and time than nuclear power plants. According to Lazard's latest Levelized Cost of Energy analysis, the cost of large-scale solar is less than $1,000 per kilowatt, whereas nuclear power ranges from $6,500 to $12,250 per kilowatt, making it almost 10 times higher than the cost of building a solar power plant.

These differences in cost and construction time suggest that solar power generation has an advantage over nuclear power in terms of initial investment and speed of deployment. Furthermore, solar power can quickly produce energy even during construction, offering the potential to generate a greater amount of carbon-free electricity within the same timeframe.

This information provides important considerations when comparing the economic viability of solar and nuclear power generation. With the continuous decrease in solar power costs and anticipated improvements in efficiency due to technological advancements, solar power could become a more attractive investment option in the long term. Conversely, nuclear power remains a more complex option due to high initial investment costs and concerns about waste disposal.

**Question:** Please also explain recent papers or reports that have reached the opposite conclusion.

**ChatGPT:** Recent reports and analyses provide a nuanced view supporting the potential advantages of nuclear power over solar in certain contexts, especially in the pursuit of decarbonizing the energy sector. Here are the insights from these sources:
- **The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine** highlight the future of nuclear power in a low-carbon world, suggesting that advanced nuclear technologies could offer significant benefits. These include smaller, safer, and less expensive to build reactors that are better integrated with modern grid systems​.
- ​.
- **McKinsey & Company** acknowledges the challenges associated with scaling nuclear power, such as the complexity of construction and regulatory hurdles. Despite these challenges, McKinsey notes that the next generation of reactors, including Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and advanced Gen-IV reactors, are designed to overcome these obstacles with benefits such as lower costs, faster build times, increased safety, and the potential for deployment in remote areas or for specific applications like microgrids​.
- ​.
- **The World Nuclear Association's World Nuclear Performance Report 2023** offers an up-to-date overview of the nuclear power sector, including the operational and under-construction reactors. This report provides a global perspective on nuclear energy's role in electricity generation, showcasing ongoing developments and the deployment of new technologies in the nuclear energy sector​.
- ​.
These reports and analyses collectively suggest that while nuclear power faces challenges, such as high initial costs and complex construction processes, it also presents significant opportunities for providing stable, low-carbon

네, 지금까지의 논의를 바탕으로 원자력과 태양광의 경제성을 비교하는 일러스트 한 장을 구상해 보았습니다. 아래는 그 일러스트에 포함될 주요 요소와 구성에 대한 설명입니다.

---

**일러스트 제목:** **에너지 경제성 비교: 원자력 vs. 태양광**

**전체적인 구성:**
일러스트는 중앙에 수직선을 기준으로 왼쪽은 '태양광', 오른쪽은 '원자력' 섹션으로 나뉘며, 각 섹션 하단에는 '결론 및 고려사항'이 배치됩니다.

---

**왼쪽 섹션: 태양광 발전 (Solar Power)**

*   **상단 아이콘:** 밝게 빛나는 태양과 여러 개의 태양광 패널
*   **주요 특징 (긍정적 측면 강조):**
    *   **비용 하락 추세:** 아래를 향하는 화살표와 함께 "지속적인 비용 감소" 텍스트. (예: 2010년 vs. 현재 발전 단가 그래프)
    *   **빠른 건설 및 설치:** 작은 건설 크레인과 빠르게 조립되는 패널 이미지, "단기간 건설" 텍스트.
    *   **낮은 초기 투자:** 작은 돈 가방 아이콘과 "상대적으로 낮은 초기 비용" 텍스트.
    *   **낮은 유지보수:** 간단한 청소 도구 아이콘과 "운영 및 유지보수 용이" 텍스트.
*   **주요 특징 (고려할 점):**
    *   **간헐성:** 해가 뜨고 지는 모습, 구름 낀 하늘 아이콘과 함께 "날씨 및 시간에 따른 변동성" 텍스트.
    *   **넓은 부지 필요:** 넓게 펼쳐진 태양광 단지 이미지.

---

**오른쪽 섹션: 원자력 발전 (Nuclear Power)**

*   **상단 아이콘:** 원자력 발전소 굴뚝에서 수증기가 나오는 모습과 원자력 심볼
*   **주요 특징 (긍정적 측면 강조):**
    *   **안정적인 전력 공급:** 24시간 시계 아이콘과 함께 "24/7 안정적인 기저부하 전력" 텍스트.
    *   **고밀도 에너지:** 작은 연료봉에서 엄청난 에너지가 나오는 모습, "고밀도 에너지원" 텍스트.
    *   **낮은 탄소 배출:** 녹색 잎사귀 아이콘과 "운영 중 탄소 배출 없음" 텍스트.
*   **주요 특징 (고려할 점):**
    *   **높은 초기 건설 비용:** 거대한 돈 가방 아이콘과 "막대한 초기 건설 비용" 텍스트.
    *   **긴 건설 기간:** 공사 중인 발전소와 긴 달력 아이콘, "장기간의 건설 기간" 텍스트.
    *   **복잡한 규제 및 안전:** 수많은 서류와 안전모 아이콘, "엄격한 안전 및 규제" 텍스트.
    *   **폐기물 처리 및 해체 비용:** 방사능 폐기물 드럼통과 해체 작업 이미지, "폐기물 처리 및 해체 비용" 텍스트.
    *   **미래 기술 (SMRs/Gen-IV):** 작은 원자로 모형과 물음표, "SMRs/Gen-IV: 잠재적 경제성 개선 (아직 실증 초기)" 텍스트.

---

**하단 섹션: 결론 및 고려사항 (Overall Conclusion & Considerations)**

*   **중앙에 저울:** 한쪽에는 태양광 패널, 다른 한쪽에는 원자로가 놓여 있으며, 저울은 약간 태양광 쪽으로 기울어져 있지만, 완전히 한쪽으로 치우치지 않음.
*   **핵심 메시지:**
    *   "**현재 시점:** 태양광은 낮은 비용과 빠른 구축으로 경제적 우위."
    *   "**원자력의 역할:** 안정적인 전력 공급과 에너지 안보에 필수적."
    *   "**미래 에너지 믹스:** 두 기술 모두 상호 보완적으로 중요."
    *   "**종합적 고려:** 단순 비용 외에 에너지 안보, 환경 영향, 그리드 안정성, 기술 발전 속도 등 다각적 관점 필요."

---

이 일러스트는 시각적으로 각 에너지원의 경제적 장단점을 명확히 보여주면서도, 복잡한 에너지 시스템에서 두 기술 모두의 중요성을 강조하는 균형 잡힌 메시지를 전달할 것입니다.

{{IMG:1}}
                                
                            Economic Comparison of Nuclear Power and Solar Power by ChatGPT4

**Question**: Additionally, considering evolving technology, security, and global carbon regulations, how do you think South Korea's energy policy should approach solar and nuclear power? Based on your knowledge of South Korea's current situation, please explain how each factor should be approached.

**ChatGPT**: Overall, South Korea's energy policy should be designed to consider a balance of various energy sources, including solar and nuclear power. This balance must respond to technological advancements, security, and global carbon regulations, and be tailored to South Korea's current situation and goals:
- **Support for Technological Development and Innovation**:
  - Solar Power: Promote the development of cost-effective solar technology and its integration with smart grids and energy storage systems.
  - Nuclear Power: Strengthen research and development into new nuclear technologies like SMRs and Gen-IV to enhance safety and economic viability, and improve waste management technologies.
- **Strengthening Energy Security**:
  - Reduce reliance on energy imports and diversify domestic energy production to enhance energy security.
- **Responding to Climate Change and Achieving Carbon Reduction Targets**:
  - Accelerate the transition to renewable energy sources to support carbon neutrality goals, and increase the proportion of low-carbon energy sources, including solar and nuclear power.
- **Social Acceptability and Education**:
  - Promote public participation in energy policy decision-making processes, and strengthen information provision and education on solar and nuclear energy to gain public understanding and support.
- **Environmental Protection and Sustainable Development**:
  - It is crucial to minimize the environmental impact of energy projects and take measures to protect ecosystems.
- **Consideration of Economic Viability and Long-term Stability**:
  - Investment decisions for solar and nuclear projects should be made through long-term energy demand forecasting and economic analysis.
Through this approach, South Korea can establish a stable, sustainable, and environmentally responsible energy mix. This will strengthen the nation's energy security, support climate change response and economic development, and simultaneously improve the quality of life for its citizens.

titleEn: Tips for Porting Your Minecraft Space to XRCLOUD
contentEn:
When it comes to the origin of the metaverse, there's one game everyone thinks of. That's Minecraft. It's a sandbox-style indie game created by Mojang Studios in 2009, with its square voxel 3D design as its trademark. Minecraft's map size totals 4,096,000,000 km², an enormous scale boasting eight times the size of Earth.

Image does not exist.
                
            
                            Minecraft's Open World Size

And the structures built in that world are often as grand and beautiful as the architectural wonders of the world.

Since older versions of Minecraft have been released as open source and the map data format is also public, it can be utilized in various ways if you have programming skills. The web metaverse PaaS service offered by Believer is based on Mozilla Hubs, which has no restrictions on map design. So, we wondered, "Could we use Minecraft's map data in our service, Mozilla Hubs?" So, we tried it. To cut to the chase, it works well. First, I'll show you a video of the map we created, and then explain how to make it.

Concept Explanation

- To explain the concept first, to import Minecraft data into Spoke, Mozilla Hubs' map editor, you need to convert it to glTF, the standard 3D file format, then import it to create and deploy the map. I will provide the necessary file download paths along with the explanation, but if you have trouble finding them, please refer to the Google Drive link below where all files are shared.

**Minecraft_map_building - Google Drive** You are using an unsupported browser. If you see some unexpected behavior, you may want to use a supported browser instead. Learn more Name Owner Last modified File size More sorting options minecraft-home-Alpha.png Owner hidden 10:53 AM 14 KB Download minecraft-home-RGB.png Owner hidden 10:53 AM 37... drive.google.com

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1o6GBY3F4gMaP9qw_Bi3OywcaMJPOh0rN?usp=sharing

1. Download Minecraft Data

Download a suitable map from [https://www.minecraftmaps.com/](https://www.minecraftmaps.com/). I downloaded the first map, 'a-modern-house 13', from the House Maps section under the Best Map menu. [https://www.minecraftmaps.com/house-maps/a-modern-house-13](https://www.minecraftmaps.com/house-maps/a-modern-house-13)

[**A Modern House #13** A Modern House with indoor decoration. www.minecraftmaps.com](https://www.minecraftmaps.com/house-maps/a-modern-house-13)

Download and unzip it.

2. OBJ File Conversion, MineWays, JMCobj Download and Installation

To convert to an OBJ file, install Mineways for Windows or JMC2OBJ for Mac.
For Windows: [https://www.realtimerendering.com/erich/minecraft/public/mineways/](https://www.realtimerendering.com/erich/minecraft/public/mineways/)
For Mac: [https://www.jmc2obj.net/](https://www.jmc2obj.net/)
I will explain using Mineways. In the menu, go to File > Open and browse to the unzipped file from above; you'll see a 'level.dat' file. This is the Minecraft data file. Opening it will open the map. Then, as shown in the image below, drag and select the desired area with the right mouse button. For Mozilla Hubs, if the map data is too large, smooth operation might be difficult, so cut it to an appropriate size. Set the import height and depth for the selected area using 'Height' and 'Depth'. Unnecessarily deep settings will increase file size.

{{IMG:1}}

Then, select the 'Export for Rendering' menu and save; options will appear as shown below. You must check the settings below to include textures and exclude unnecessary blocks.

{{IMG:2}}

This will save the OBJ file. However, since Spoke, the editor, cannot load OBJ files, you now need to convert the OBJ file to a glTF file.

3. Import OBJ file into Blender and Export as glTF

Blender can be downloaded from the URL below: [https://www.blender.org/](https://www.blender.org/)
When you run it, a single box will appear as shown below. Select and delete any unnecessary boxes...

{{IMG:3}}
                                
                            Blender Initial Screen

Insert the File > import > wavefront(obj) file into the Blender project.

{{IMG:4}}
                                
                            Importing OBJ file

When first loaded, it appears gray as shown below.

{{IMG:5}}
                                
                            Blender Import View of Minecraft Map Data

Changing the shader to Material Preview allows you to see it in color, but since it's not for editing purposes, simply select File > Export > glTF 2.0 and save the file.

{{IMG:6}}

​

4. Import glTF file into Spoke

Now, add a project in XRCLOUD (Mozilla Hubs) and click the '+' (Add) button in the Scene menu to open the Spoke editor. [https://xrcloud.app/ko/scenes](https://xrcloud.app/ko/scenes)

{{IMG:7}}

The initial screen looks like this; delete the default glb terrain.

{{IMG:8}}

In the Asset area at the bottom, add the glTF file you just created to My Assets, then select it again to add it to the project. Since I didn't set the depth separately, it was buried under the 3D file as shown in the image below.

{{IMG:9}}

Adjusting the height value makes it look decent now. However, a warning is visible. This is because the Minecraft map has more polygons than recommended by Mozilla. You can largely ignore this.

{{IMG:10}}

5. Editing the Map in Spoke

Afterward, I performed a few tasks.
- I selected an appropriate spawn point so the house is clearly visible.
- The door was blocked when climbing the stairs, so I used Link Asset and Waypoint Asset at that location to allow passing through the door with a click. This was the [method used when creating a 360-image gallery in a previous post](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97?Redirect=Log&logNo=223174026927&from=postView).
- The space felt empty, so I added water to create waves and added an Equirectangular sky image to the image assets to create a sky.
​​

6. Experience it Yourself.

To actually experience the metaverse space created with a Minecraft map using XRCLOUD (Mozilla Hubs), click the link below. It's compatible with mobile, PC, and VR. [https://room.xrcloud.app:4000/XjmrSyP/yummy-precious-plane](https://room.xrcloud.app:4000/XjmrSyP/yummy-precious-plane)​

7. Web Metaverse Platform Development is XRCLOUD!

And if you need professional web metaverse platform development using the Mozilla Hubs engine, look for XRCLOUD. [https://xrcloud.app](https://xrcloud.app/)

XRCLOUD Developer Center Low cost, fast access, powerful features Experience 3D space web and metaverse. Create your own metaverse in 15 minutes without any separate installation programs. You can create a web metaverse easily and quickly, just like building a website, and at a low cost. We add additional features needed for development and operation to the global metaverse open-source Mozilla Hubs and even provide secure G-Cloud for public institutions. Prepare your web services for the XR space computing era with XRCLOUD. Have you been at a loss as to where and how to start creating a metaverse space? All this time, complex... xrcloud.app

https://xrcloud.app/

titleEn: Building a Metaverse with Data Sovereignty in Mind:
contentEn:
In this post, I'd like to explain XRCLOUD's philosophy by demonstrating how to build a metaverse platform using XRCLOUD through a practical exercise. To explain our philosophy, an understanding of Web APIs is necessary. Simply put, it's best understood as an open technology that organically creates services through agreed-upon protocols between web services. If that's still unclear, just understand it as 'exchanging information via website URLs.'

**1. Why build a metaverse platform with APIs?**

You might wonder why we make you build a metaverse platform with complex APIs when website URLs already look quite complicated. We have the following reasons for this:

**1.1. Business Logic-Independent Metaverse Technology**
Many companies looking to adopt the metaverse may not want to conduct business in a way dictated by a metaverse platform. Most metaverse platforms offer specialized features for each industry sector, while also imposing their business methods on tenant companies. A metaverse focused on education might include an LMS, and when trading paintings or 3D objects, NFT fees and trading methods are locked into the metaverse. Therefore, the way business is conducted in such metaverses is very rigid. Companies that have been operating in their respective industries with their own methods cannot utilize their existing business practices and systems.

However, our XRCLOUD is different. This is because we provide a web editor for creating metaverse spaces, and APIs for managing metaverse editor projects and deployed spaces. Through APIs, developers can create new sites that include space editor functions for creation, modification, deletion, and updates, allowing them to build entirely separate metaverse services and conduct business in their own way.

Due to these requirements, various organizations often request customized independent software from metaverse companies. In such cases, building an independent metaverse involves modifying and distributing the source code through customization, making it difficult to receive continuous updates for the original source, and incurring very high development and maintenance costs. However, XRCLOUD is a service designed from the outset to create independent metaverses, so its cost is very low, comparable to that of developing a web service. The reason for this is simple: XRCLOUD's metaverse is inherently a web service, and it embodies the philosophy of developing and providing spatial web services as SaaS APIs.

**1.2. Metaverse Technology That Does Not Store Personal or Customer Information**
Furthermore, since we do not provide avatars, we do not store personal or customer information on our servers. 'No avatars in a metaverse service? What does that mean?' You might be puzzled, but we approached it with this concept from the beginning because we utilize standard technologies for avatars, and we participate directly in the standardization process to improve them. The most similar example is VR Chat, famous as the platform where virtual idols operate. VRChat avatars are created and traded in stores other than VRChat, and can also be used for VR streaming broadcasts via VRoid. This is because VRChat's VRCA avatar files provide conversion methods to the open standard VRM file. In other words, if avatar files use a standard format, the metaverse platform doesn't necessarily need to hold avatar information; users can simply enter with their avatar files. The Mozilla Hubs avatar, which is the underlying engine of our metaverse, can be obtained via [open source](https://mozilla.github.io/hackweek-avatar-maker/) or developers can create their own editors using the open source. Ready Player Me also supports Hubs avatars because it uses the international standard glTF avatar.

The full-body avatar for XRCLOUD, which we are currently working on, is also being developed with its editor released as open source, completely eliminating dependency on XRCLOUD. Not only avatars, but also user names and all information are processed in this manner; when entering a space, expressive information such as the user's avatar is brought in from the client's platform to the space in our cloud via API. In other words, we function purely as a client player. The advantage of this technical structure is that it fundamentally prevents the metaverse platform from storing valuable customer information. Roblox, Zepeto, ZEP – all metaverses require registration. However, we do not require such a demand; since the client's customers can enter with their customer information, we do not store customer information.

**1.3. Metaverse Technology Focused Solely on Space**
In other words, unlike other metaverses, we have focused on creating web spaces and securely managing entry, exit, and permissions within those spaces. To help you understand, let's consider an educational metaverse. Developing an educational metaverse often involves a simultaneous demand for LMS development, and the metaverse boasts built-in LMS features. But wouldn't it be strange if, while building a school building (metaverse platform), you were asked to also build an academic system into the building's functions? And wouldn't it be odd if all of a student's personal information had to be present in the classroom (metaverse platform) when they enter? A student (3rd Party user information) should simply be assigned to a class through the school organization (3rd Party platform) and enter the corresponding room. Of course, a teaching assistant should be able to unlock (authenticate) the door.

We are solely focused on innovating 2D web spaces into 3D web spaces, concentrating only on the space itself. We abstract and generalize the software logic for this, helping each business area excel at what it does best. Therefore, our greatest values are not beautiful avatars and beautiful spaces, but rather easy integration, linkage, and expansion. Beautiful avatars and beautiful spaces can be handled by individual developers, and their quality and performance will continuously evolve based on web technologies like WebGPU. The advantage of XRCLOUD's design identity is its absence, which allows for diverse experimentation.

{{IMG:1}}

Various avatars from Mozilla Hubs used in the research paper 'Toward Facilitating Team Formation and Communication Through Avatar Based Interaction in Desktop-Based Immersive Virtual Environments'

**2. XRCLOUD API Structure Explanation**

Above, I only discussed the values, but now I will explain the actual API structure by looking at it. Please refer to the links below for documentation and services.

**API Documentation URL:** [**https://api.xrcloud.app/docs/ko**](https://api.xrcloud.app/docs/ko)
**Service URL:** [**https://xrcloud.app/ko**](https://xrcloud.app/ko)

**2.1. The Essential Key for Calling APIs: Authentication Key**
Developing through an API means you can think of the developer's role as the administrator of the platform they intend to create. As an administrator, you would naturally need a key to do anything, right? If you have registered for XRCLOUD, you can obtain a Key from your Mypage. If the Key is leaked to a hacker, they can freely manipulate the platform's data, which is extremely dangerous. Therefore, please use it with caution. If it is leaked, please click 'Generate api key' to create a new one.

{{IMG:2}}

API Key for calling APIs in XRCLOUD

This Key is used when making API calls. I will explain its actual usage by demonstrating an example of calling a Project API using Postman, a widely used tool for API testing.

**2.2. Relationship and API Structure of Project, Scene, and Room**
Understand a Project as a service unit created by a developer or company. For example, if a developer named 'Anyone' created Google and Facebook, then Google and Facebook would be projects. Underneath this project, there is a Scene, which corresponds to a space blueprint, and a Room, which corresponds to an actual building created from that space blueprint. This forms a hierarchical structure, and the API also follows the same hierarchical structure. The parts indicated by {} are IDs that can be obtained from the parent object API or the XRCLOUD site.

`/api/projects/{project_id}/scenes/{scene_id}/rooms/{room_id}`

For example, if we assume project_id is P1, scene_id is S1, and room_id is R1, then the API to call information for Room R1 would be `/api/projects/**P1**/scenes/**S1**/rooms**/R1**. You can think of it like a school class and number: '3rd grade, 1st class, student number 12, [name]'.

**2.3. Get Projects: Let's retrieve project information using Postman.**
First, let's look at the API documentation for 'get Projects', which retrieves project information.

{{IMG:3}}

get project API documentation

**2.3.1. API URL and Call Information**
Looking at the description, on the left, you can copy how to actually call the API. Pay close attention to whether it's a Get or Post request. Values enclosed in {} must be entered into the URL. The `get project` API requires a project ID to know which project to retrieve. You can find the Project ID on the XRCLOUD project page, so copy and paste it.

{{IMG:4}}
                                
                            Project ID Location

**2.3.2. API Authentication and Parameter Description**
At the top of each API description, you'll find the authentication information and required input values for API calls. This explains that the key from your My Page is required.

**2.3.3.) API Result Value Description**
At the bottom of each API description, the values returned upon calling the API are explained. Do you see `sceneCreateUrl`? Calling this URL means you can launch the Scene editor, which corresponds to the blueprint of a space. Through this, administrators can create as many Scenes as they want under a project.

**2.4) You can test API calls with Postman as follows.**

{{IMG:5}}

**2.4.1. API Input and Settings**
As explained in [2.3.1], I entered the API URL including the project ID and set it to GET.

**2.4.2. API Authentication Information Input**
As explained in [2.3.2], in the Authorization tab, the Type was set to Bearer token, and the Key from XRCloud's My Page was entered. Then, click Send to execute.

**2.4.3. Confirming Values After API Call**
As in [2.3.3], you can check the actual return values. If you put the `SceneCreationURL` into your browser's URL bar, a web editor for creating space blueprints will appear. Of course, you can also load and overwrite existing space blueprint (Spoke) files.

{{IMG:6}}

**2.4. What can you do with this getProject API?**
By using the `GetProject` API above, you can integrate an editor into your user platform. In fact, the information needed to implement `Create Scene` is passed through `getProject`. For example, you can assign the URL returned above to a [Create Space] button. Below is XRCLOUD's Scene management tool, which you can consider implemented through similar internal APIs. The '+' button here is for adding a scene. You can implement the same functionality on your platform using the API above.

{{IMG:7}}

**2.5. How to view and modify a created Scene?**
You might then wonder, "How do I modify a Scene after creating it?" The API for this is `get Scenes`.

{{IMG:8}}

Authentication is the same as above; just add `scenes` after `project_id`. This will display a list of information for all created scenes. For pagination, `skip` and `take` information are received as query parameters. For example, if you want to display the 4th page of a project with `project_id` P1 and retrieve 10 items, you would use `api/projects/P1/scenes?skip=30&take=10`. This will fetch items from the 31st to the 41st, allowing you to compose the 4th page.
Individual scene item information is as follows.

{{IMG:9}}

And if you look closely at the URL above, you'll see **sceaneModificationUrl**. Calling this URL allows you to modify the Scene you created. You can see that XRCLOUD's Scene list is also composed of the API return information above.

{{IMG:10}}

**2.6. How to create and enter a Room?**
Just as a blueprint doesn't immediately erect a building, you need to build the structure from the blueprint. The actual spaces built are called Rooms in XRCLOUD/Hubs, and we provide `create room`, `get rooms`, and `get room` APIs. As I explained above on how to use the API documentation, when you create a room and read its information, the room details are exposed as shown below. You'll see `roomUrl`, right? If you look closely at this `roomUrl`, you'll notice a `token` parameter appended to it.

```json
{
  "id": "f24ee5ba-8f1f-4f7a-86ed-738f95ea1f8b",
  "name": "example room name",
  "size": 10,
  "sceneId": "c322b49b-6e12-47d9-b293-b5ab3727459c",
  "createdAt": "2023-07-12T09:27:41.600Z",
  "updatedAt": "2023-07-12T09:27:41.600Z",
  "roomUrl": "https://xrcloud.app:4000/7UizZDL/example-room-name?token=WRlNDAtNWQ0OC00NjZjLWFlYTUtOTNkZDA1Yj...",
  "thumbnailUrl": "https://api.xrcloud.app/files/852a6f47-3978-4201-a637-9699d7845266.jpg"
}
```

You can add additional query parameters to the access URL to pass extra permissions for entry, avatars, etc. **This part will be further organized and published in the API documentation with examples.**

**2.7. How to manage my platform's user information and user-created spaces?**
However, you might have this question. If this is the case, users on my platform should be able to create spaces and only see the spaces they created. But the provided API doesn't have a way to identify users? Believer also had many discussions about this development approach. The final conclusion we reached was that this management should be handled on the platform of the third-party developer, who is a user of XRCLOUD. As you can see from the content above, **XRCLOUD allows you to query all information about scenes and rooms.** In other words, this means that when building your platform using this information, you don't need to call the API every time; you only call it during creation or modification, and you can store a copy of the information in your DB to manage it further in conjunction with necessary additional user information. You can manage scene and room information in your user platform's DB and allow platform users to freely select and query it as developed by you. Between providing convenient features to third-party developers or offering more freedom and higher security, we chose to give more authority to third-party developers. **Helping to build a metaverse without business or user information seems to be the philosophy that best describes our platform, XRCLOUD.** To this end, for enterprise cloud infrastructure, we are using g-cloud certified by the government, aiming for GS certification within the year, and considering on-premise server-based business models. Currently, many public institutions have built metaverses, but systems that consider certification in data security are rare. Recently, with the advancement of AI technology, the issue of data sovereignty has emerged as a very important topic. Metaverses that originated from global game services have not considered this, and foreign metaverses also lack such considerations. Mozilla Hubs, which we use, also runs services based on foreign Amazon cloud, and the Amazon service for Mozilla Foundation's open source that we use does not support Korean regional servers.

http://www.itdaily.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=209676
**[CSAP in the Fog ④] Government's Cloud Direction Must Focus on Data Sovereignty - IT Daily** [IT Daily] As interest in public cloud grows, the 'Cloud Service Security Certification Program (CSAP)', necessary for supplying cloud services to government and public institutions, is becoming an issue. The reorganization of the CSAP system... www.itdaily.kr

http://www.itdaily.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=209676

The fact that we pondered these unseen aspects and internalized the technology is why our technology development was more difficult and slower than other metaverses. However, as the importance of the metaverse grows, if it's a metaverse for actual use rather than just display, safety and security inevitably become the most crucial topics. Therefore, please show great interest in XRCLOUD, a scalable platform that upholds these values, and make good use of our strengths. We will focus XRCLOUD as a framework for creating and managing spatial web. Thank you. We appreciate your interest. The pricing policy has been decided as shown below. Personal version monetization is expected in August, and the Pro version is targeted within the year. Business version inquiries are welcome at any time.

titleEn: Team BEIAI Reveals How to Create AI
contentEn:
Hello. I am Yang Byung-seok, CEO of Believer, and I also oversee Team BEIAI, which produces AI webtoons for [LOOOL](https://loool.io/). Team BEIAI is an AI webtoon content production team that directly creates and edits webtoons using Stable Diffusion, rather than focusing on AI technology development like software development. Unlike me, who majored in software development and had experience as a webtoon PD, the reason our team, composed entirely of webtoon majors, is creating AI webtoons is not because they can't draw.

**Team Member Introduction**
Please don't mind the CEO and share your thoughts and a brief introduction while working on the project.
- Sun: This was my first time working with Stable Diffusion for this project. I found the work fascinating, experiencing various things like 'Oh, AI can do this!' and 'Wait, it can't do that?' I mainly focused on character implementation and post-processing.
- Wonny: It was my first time working with AI, and it was easier yet harder than I expected... It feels like a special experience. AI isn't as smart as I thought it would be...^^ I mainly focused on storyboarding, character extraction, and typesetting.
- Goofy: It was quite challenging because the character's poses and expressions didn't turn out as I imagined. I mainly focused on storyboarding, character extraction, and retouching.

**Production Environment**
We use a custom-built PC from Yongsan, costing around 3 million won, equipped with an RTX 4090, and a Wacom One. The RTX 4090 graphics card used by our artists is expensive and accounts for most of the PC's cost. We wanted to provide Cintiqs, but since Believer has many Wacom Ones purchased for webtoon education, we are using those devices. We'll earn money and buy you big Cintiqs.
In addition to these devices, Believer has several small PCs with RTX 3090s in the server room, which are used for Believer's AI education platform and also for generating AI images.
Video memory is crucial for AI webtoon production, so we recommend RTX 3090 and RTX 4090. Those who need to generate high-resolution images or train their own models should definitely keep this in mind.

**Production Method**
We plan to disclose more details in the future, but here's a brief introduction to our webtoon production process. There's already a lot of scattered information in communities, and YouTube has excellent usage methods that even we haven't fully mastered. However, not all of this information is optimized for webtoon production. We hope that more people can easily approach AI webtoon production by referring to our method, so we're briefly sharing the methods we've organized so far, hoping more people will try AI webtoon creation.
First, our production process assumes the existence of a visual storyboard for the webtoon. Currently, we are working with a writer for the text storyboard, and internally, we are proceeding with visual storyboard creation and subsequent tasks.

**Creating a Base Model Suitable for the Webtoon's Intended Atmosphere**
The biggest advantage of Stable Diffusion is that various models are publicly available. [https://civitai.com/](https://civitai.com/) is a representative AI model sharing site, where you can select models most similar to the webtoon you plan to create. You can choose one or select multiple and blend them. In our case, we wanted to create a unique model, so we blended several models. The model created at this stage serves as the base model for generating backgrounds and characters, thus determining the overall atmosphere of the work.

**Character Concept Creation via Prompts**
We create prompts based on the character features discussed within the team to define the character's appearance. It's especially important to capture the work's atmosphere and clearly represent the character's features.
ex) Prompt for Berry, a character from <If I Drink This, I'm Going to Space>

{{IMG:1}}

prompt : Purple Hair, girl, 1girl, Solo, Cute, Simple Background, White background, Beautiful eyes, Purple eyes, Beautiful skin, Clean skin, High Quality, Masterpiece, (Bobbed Hair:1.2), Natural Hair, Beautiful delicate eyes, old, K-pop style, Korean Webtoon Style, full bangs , long eyes to nose, Mature, Long face shape, Adult, Straight Hair, Short hair, Focus on face, Left tear dot, Dot under the left eye, Apron
negative : easynegative , ng_deepnegative_v1_75t, Long Hair, young, Curly Hair, Low Quality

**Character DreamBooth Model Creation**
Once prompts that achieve the desired atmosphere are finalized, we create character faces from various angles, then crop and upscale each character's face into 512x512 images to create training images for DreamBooth.

{{IMG:2}}
                                
Normalized images used for creating the character Berry model

After inputting the 512x512 normalized images and defining the character's keywords, we generate the DreamBooth model. Detailed DreamBooth training methods can be found by searching on YouTube. When generating the DreamBooth model, the base model created in the previous step is used to maintain consistency. The created model is tested with various keywords. At this point, if the DreamBooth model feels standalone or overfitted when creating DreamBooth character images, we blend in more of the base model to stabilize the character model. Since this model will be used continuously, it's important to create it well.

**Character and Background Production using ControlNet based on Storyboards, Photos, and 3D Models**
Currently, we work based on hand-drawn storyboards and do not generate characters and backgrounds simultaneously. Although it involves the inconvenience of post-processing, it facilitates division of labor and aligns with the traditional webtoon production process. We primarily use OpenPose, either by taking photos to create poses or by using 3D characters to select poses and compositions, and then generating characters based on these. For backgrounds, we establish the composition using SketchUp and then create backgrounds with img2img. The Stable Diffusion feature used here is ControlNet, which you can also find good tutorials for by searching on YouTube. The utility of ControlNet is continuously growing, so it's good to master it.

**Panel and Speech Bubble Placement and Post-processing**
Panel and speech bubble placement is identical to the general webtoon production process. We add shadows to the composited images. Although we didn't work on the background and characters simultaneously, AI images have very high density, so proper application of shadows and light is essential for the background and characters to blend naturally without awkwardness. Specifically, we correct oddly extracted parts, or relatively emphasize important areas by applying Gaussian blur or reducing saturation to less important parts.

{{IMG:3}}

A characteristic of AI webtoons is that everything comes out with high density, so it's crucial to use post-processing to 'remove' less important details. This is the biggest difference from AI illustrations.

**Fixing Clothing**
While clothing can be somewhat fixed through LoRa training, LoRa requires a relatively large amount of training data, so we haven't created LoRa models yet. Currently, we've gone as far as fixing clothing color output using the Cutoff plugin. We plan to review the technology to see if it would be convenient to collect the generated uniforms from serialized episodes and then create a LoRa model from them.

**Our Biggest Current Concerns**

- **Establishing a system to increase the probability of desired image output** - Currently, we generate a large number of images to extract suitable characters and backgrounds. To increase this probability, quality control of our self-generated models and prompt management by the artists seem crucial. Especially for team projects, sharing prompts is important, so managing them is necessary, and establishing a system to manage and reuse well-generated panels and data seems vital.
- **Advancing the character and background production process** - Currently, since we generate characters and backgrounds separately and then combine them, there's a lot of post-processing work, and the high quality and naturalness, which are advantages of AI, seem to be diminished. Therefore, we plan to further consider ways to switch to a method that generates characters and backgrounds simultaneously.

**Conclusion**
We cannot claim that our method is the best for AI webtoon production. However, there is currently no method to easily produce AI webtoons of a sellable quality with just a single prompt. Above all, we wanted to show that AI webtoons can be created this way, and we hope this helps those who wish to utilize AI in webtoon production. We will continue to share good methods as we discover them.

Check out AI webtoons on [LOOOL](https://loool.io/).

titleEn: Unearthing an IR Document from a 7-Year-Old Startup
contentEn: As a startup founded in 2017, now in its 7th year (having completed 6 full years), I've started working on IR documents again after a long time. The last time I properly created IR documents was in 2020, so it's been almost 3 years. As a lot has happened since then, I initially laid everything out, adopting a 'I didn't know what you'd like, so I prepared everything' approach, and then restructured it with the most appealing stories and content. Everything is factual, but it's a bit regrettable that the stories of many other things we've done seem to be discarded. Among them, we've also hidden proud technologies that, while not attractive enough to present upfront and not fitting our survival or this scenario, are still something we're proud of. Now, too much time has passed to be called a startup, but in the success stories of each company, the hidden stories seem to be much more complex and difficult than the pretty ones that are shown. I cheer on all startup CEOs worldwide.

titleEn: What is the Real Metaverse?
Metaverse is the Internet of the Future
contentEn:
I was going to write this post for the company blog, but I got a bit unnecessarily excited, and it felt like it would be a more personal piece, so I'm writing on my Naver blog for the first time in a while. I watched Facebook's video along with the news that their company name changed to Meta.

Honestly, for me, working in VR, the company that best embodied innovation was Facebook. Apple and Samsung felt old. From an engineer's perspective, there were no new challenges whatsoever. The mobile ecosystem had become stagnant; whether displays folded or cameras improved 100,000-fold, a smartphone was still just a smartphone. Those who hoped the market would grow as large as smartphones initially paid attention when Oculus was acquired for a huge sum, but then turned away when it didn't immediately generate profit or live up to expectations. Perhaps the fantasy shown in Ready Player One was too grand. However, Oculus, nurtured by Facebook, consistently showed significant technological advancements with every iteration: Gear VR, Oculus Go, Oculus Quest, and Oculus Quest 2. The excitement I felt as a child seeing a green-screen computer, the excitement in college seeing a PDA (the precursor to smartphones), and the third biggest excitement was seeing Cardboard while at the research lab. This was because I saw the possibilities of the computing world and the direction of technology it held. Besides the excitement I felt seeing hardware, there was also excitement I felt seeing software. The excitement I saw in PDAs was the ability to put software on mobile phones. I even specifically pursued training as a second-term student for WIPI (Korea's early wireless internet platform) on the 2.5G network because I envisioned the future I saw in PDAs. However, that future only truly exploded after the 3G network and iPhone emerged, networks were established, and a considerable amount of time passed, becoming almost mainstream by the time 4G arrived.

Watching the video, I thought, 'Facebook is indeed envisioning the future I imagined,' but at the same time, I was a bit worried. This was because Facebook, which is leading such a wonderful future, has recently been under suspicion of being a 'Big Brother.' Also, from the perspective of having launched an app on the Oculus Store, my experience with Oculus felt very close to a Big Brother. It was difficult for new app developers to market their products, only so-called 'chosen' apps had an advantageous position, and for service-oriented companies like ours (not games), it was an extremely difficult structure to achieve anything. Even the AppLab launch, which was supposed to have no review process, took over a month. Furthermore, for us, being service-centric (like webtoons or educational platforms) rather than games, the frame-by-frame Unity development method was far removed from event- or request/response-based app/web development, leading to many disadvantages. On top of that, Unity's backward compatibility version issues were a headache.

{{IMG:1}}

From Yumi's Cells Episode 4, a Unity bug that popped up

The devices we've developed for and launched on include Oculus Go, Daydream, HTC Vive, FOVE, DPVR, Windows MR, and PICO. It was almost unbelievable how many there were. Because of this, we even considered whether we should put a porting layer within Unity, like in the old days of mobile phone development, and we looked into UniRX, an event-based development method, for a long time. However, as we were busy just keeping the company afloat by doing both web and client development, we didn't have the luxury to invest in refining Unity's development approach. So, as if in defiance, we were building WebXR-based technologies and services. This was because it allowed us to avoid dependence on the Oculus Store. But still, there was no way to expose users to the Oculus Store's home screen, and logging in was inconvenient, so we explored various workarounds, such as ClassV using a PIN code method in conjunction with its own login system. Seeing that video in such a situation made me sigh deeply. It's a wonderful future, but could it be a future of dictatorship? Although they said they would open the SDK, it seemed they would only provide very closed, game-engine-dependent features rather than those based on open standards. I wanted to ask Mark Zuckerberg, "What do you think of Tim Berners-Lee? Are you trying to monopolize the future of the internet?" However, today, after discovering this video and revisiting the Facebook Developer Center, my mind changed. When Facebook employees were recently asked about Mark Zuckerberg, the short answer was, "He's not evil," and I could feel that Facebook is seriously contemplating the future of the internet. I could see how they are approaching 2D apps. 2D apps refer to applications that can provide various existing information services, not just 3D games. Specifically, they interpreted this as an 'Infinite Screen,' simply an extension of the browser, and finally paved the way for creating WebApps. In essence, it means Oculus has begun to embrace the open internet of the future. This video resolved many of our concerns. It finally opened the way for web and Oculus to be organically connected and for web-based apps to be developed. To overcome the limitations of WebXR, Facebook officially provided PWA and WebView, which we had thought we would have to develop ourselves because Facebook hadn't opened them up yet. [https://fb.watch/8Y-PL-KnYp/](https://fb.watch/8Y-PL-KnYp/)

**Facebook Reality Labs - Bringing 2D Apps to VR's Infinite Screen | Facebook** Learn about the new 2D apps and Progressive Web App (PWA) platform for Quest that enable developers to build tools for a more enjoyable and productive... fb.watch

https://fb.watch/8Y-PL-KnYp/

If things continue this way, Facebook seems poised to become a company that combines Google and Apple – a company with Apple's hardware and Google's openness. To briefly summarize the video above, it's as follows: Facebook is serious about building the internet of the future, especially if they are indeed building out all these architectures. I felt the same excitement I experienced with Android Cupcake (1.0) once again. I see the future of technology not in videos, but in developer centers. You can sense much more in advance than from a well-produced video. What felt frustrating when I first saw the iPhone was precisely what Android's developer documentation cleared up. And the result is the market we have today. But now, Facebook has taken both the excitement of the iPhone and the excitement of Android. What I thought was right. We will show good progress. Soon, we will create WebXR results and immediately apply PWA. I was wondering how to implement Korean localization for the Infinity Office keyboard at the JavaScript level, but it seems this approach will solve it quickly. We just need to trust Facebook's sincerity and focus. **Believer is an internet company of the metaverse, and as Zuckerberg said, the metaverse is not a 3D gaming environment, but the internet of the future itself. The meaning of 'meta' implies more software architecture, like metadata, not just what appears in 3D. 'Meta' is originally invisible.**
---I'm adding my summary of the video above. --
**1. Supports all input devices: controllers, hands, and keyboard/mouse.** -> The most important part seems to be the support for video-through Infinity Office.
**2. Authentication**
- Shares login status between apps. -> I need to look into what this means.
- Supports Facebook login. -> This is what we've been waiting for.
- Can save passwords. -> This is a basic browser feature, but they're finally doing it.
**3. Push**
- Android push support planned -> This will effectively be Oculus's FCM.
**4. Very simple PWA creation process**
1) Create a manifest in a simple JSON file -> Generate APK -> Sideload and test -> Upload to Developer Center (Done)
**5. WebView**
1) Self, blank browsers appear as tabs, multi-tab support,
- Multi-tab options available. File controller support
2) Includes hardware-accelerated video player
- Supports normal, 360 (180-degree not mentioned)
4) Communication - Microphone and WebRTC support
- Supports 6DOF, Timewarp layers(?), controllers, hand tracking, and hybrid 2D+3D PWAs
6. Additional features: Multitasking, PWA, WebXR
7. Developer Center Introduction: [https://developer.oculus.com/pwa](https://developer.oculus.com/pwa)

titleEn: (ComicsV) What I'm Learning as a Startup CEO These Days
contentEn:
When I founded ComicsV, I was quite confident because I believed I had selected a good item, had some clumsy experience as a PM, understood well how to build services with various people, had a network, and came from a development background, which meant I could even back up the implementation if needed. I thought I knew most of what there was to know. I figured all that was left was learning how to establish and operate a company.

However, as I passed the two-year mark, I've come to a new realization. An angel investor from the initial founding period once said, "I've watched him for several years, and I'm investing because he's not a strange person." And recently, I heard a similar response: "We're collaborating because we've seen that he's not a strange person." At first, I didn't understand why "not a strange person" rather than "competent" should be a condition for collaboration, but I've only recently grasped its meaning. It's because there are quite a few truly "strange" people among the employees we hire and the many companies we collaborate with. This was a point I couldn't perceive from my past position as the "client" or "superior." And I believe student founders might also find it difficult to grasp this meaning. I now realize the importance of discerning these "not strange people," or rather, "trustworthy people," and that I've never truly learned this skill. I've come to understand that not every encounter is valuable, and not everyone has pure intentions. Relationships with such individuals or companies can be quite exhausting and can harm the company's valuable opportunities. Therefore, I need to cherish encounters more and be more cautious.

The second point is how to maintain "relationships." I feel like I'm just starting to learn this, but once you've discerned "not strange people or organizations," the next step is to build "lasting relationships." This aspect, too, isn't solely determined by the skill of discovering and implementing good items. When I was at a large company, I didn't put effort into maintaining those relationships. That's because many organizations/people who wanted to establish relationships did that work for me. Therefore, it's difficult to learn this skill. It seems a similar reason explains why more successful companies often have weaker sales organizations.

I've learned that while "items" and "technology" are important for a startup, ultimately, "people and relationships" are what truly matter. Since not all members can be perfect, I also feel the need to leverage their strengths and provide mutual backup. In any case, I was fortunate to start with people who believed in me, and with team members who still believe in me, I persevere, learn, and grow.

And sometimes, when I discover even very young founders who already understand and manage these aspects well, I feel a sense of respect. Even if one has more experience, knowledge, or brilliant ideas, a startup is a company before it's an item; it's a place where employees and people live. These areas cannot be expressed by team members with impressive IR careers. I've also had the experience of passing public recruitment exams for quite good companies, but I am confident that our employees, who have been filtered and gone through tough times with us, are friends who would perform above average even among the successful candidates of those good companies. However, due to lower paper qualifications, an inability to present themselves well, or perhaps a bit of bad luck, they couldn't get into those places, and we are unable to provide them with the same level of compensation.

Anyway, I started with luck, and I'm continuing with luck. Even if the company doesn't work out, I'll probably be able to say that this experience was incredibly fortunate in my life. The best outcome, of course, would be for this luck to lead to the luck of success.

I write this from the perspective of someone who's gone just a little ahead for those who dream of a startup... or those who dream of entrepreneurship with only a great item or great technology. And I express my respect to senior entrepreneurs who have already learned these things and are ahead. I hope and expect to learn more in the future and to work with even better people.

titleEn: What Happens If We Provide VR Subsid
contentEn:
Miscellaneous Thoughts on IT

(VR's Opportunity to Propel Korea Forward) What would happen if VR subsidies were provided?

Luke ・ 2018. 10. 24. 22:46

Copy URL Add Neighbor

Body Other Functions

1.  **VR's Unfavorable Atmosphere**

Honestly, the atmosphere in the VR market doesn't seem very good these days. As I wrote in a previous report, VR, due to excessively high expectations in its early stages, hasn't yielded quick results, leading to deep disappointment. The situation reported from overseas isn't great either, and looking at the latest VR-related apps and news, there's a distinct feeling that interest and updates have significantly decreased. This situation is not good for VR, which is already said to lack content. And probably, the first to die off in the struggling VR market will be the B2C market, including games, which requires a certain market scale.

2.  **The "Large" AR Market is Actually Just the Mobile Market, Nothing New**

Although there's talk that AR is much larger, the two markets are fundamentally different in nature, and it's still a long way from bringing about a new paradigm shift like the mobile revolution. The irony is that mobile AR is an immediately applicable field, so formally, the AR market might feel large. However, strictly speaking, rather than a new AR market unfolding, a smaller (but larger than VR) sub-market exists within the mobile market.

3.  **AI, Really...? Fundamentally the Weakest Area, Though We're Working Hard...**

This market also has high synergy with AI, and can bring about good results through the combination of object recognition and image recognition fields. But!! Can this alone, based on market size, become Korea's beacon?

AI and AR technologies are ultimately packaged and supplied by global platform companies. What Korea can gain from AI and AR is ultimately the service market where these technologies are applied, and it's difficult to see AI and AR creating a new market, rather than just being part of the mobile market. The paradigm shift and next growth engine that the government envisioned while championing the 4th Industrial Revolution surely didn't mean just this.

Furthermore, the mobile service sector is still experiencing rapid growth worldwide, so private investment is also active. It would be truly fortunate if the world's best software solution company emerged in AI and AR, but it won't be an easy story given that mobile platforms have all been taken over.

AI is still valid, but I believe AI technology development will be difficult for us to lead or overturn the game. We might do well just by not falling behind. Fundamentally, we are weak in long-term technology research in the software sector, and AI technology development itself is difficult in a structure that constantly talks about performance and quantitative evaluations in the first and second years.

4.  **VR Will Happen, But Not Now. Now is the Opportunity for Government Policy.**

In such a situation... I believe that VR currently presents a quite good opportunity for Korea. This is because we have a past experience of significant success through high-speed internet. 5G will also be meaningful, but it cannot be an alternative like high-speed internet was back then. The core of high-speed internet at that time was intertwined with the popularization of new devices, namely PCs. Furthermore, 'O-yang video' (a reference to early online video content) and StarCraft fueled it, and smartphones themselves had clear reasons to be purchased. The significance of PC and mobile proliferation was the expansion of a new software market.

1) **If 5G is deployed... telecom companies and fast-follower manufacturers will benefit, but SW services will be late.**

So, can 5G do that? 5G alone cannot expand a new software market. Even if PCs and mobile devices become faster, new markets and innovations won't necessarily emerge. Ultimately, appropriate consumer devices suitable for 5G are needed, and VR could be that. So, should we wait a bit, like in the iPhone era? Did Naver's position really improve with the advent of the iPhone and Android era? If you ask, honestly, no, except for the huge success with Line. Even Kakao + Naver combined would struggle to reclaim Naver's past glory from the PC era, and the reason is Google and Apple; it's no lie to say that Google and Apple have dominated the world. You might refute this by citing Samsung Electronics, but I'm talking about the software service market, not the hardware market.

To describe the characteristics of this software service market, the first mover tends to take all. I believe that now, when the whole world is skeptical about VR, might be the most opportune time for the government to step in. When things are going well, the government isn't really needed. Even now, many VR companies are crossing the 'death valley' with government funds, but I think this is the most suitable time for the government to properly fulfill its role of 'promotion'. If we become a winner when everyone else dismisses it as premature, we could become the Google, Apple, or Facebook of this market when it grows later.

5.  **While Awaiting Price Drops, Now is the Time for the Government to Proactively Create the Market.**

This isn't to say that the government should pour more money into VR companies. Precisely, the problem with the current VR market is relatively simple: it's the absence and immaturity of the market. The expectations of teenagers and young people for VR far exceed what older generations imagine. Those kids simply don't have money. This is what I observed and felt on-site: kids genuinely excited and enthusiastic about VR webtoons, and repeatedly visiting the ComicsV booth because they wanted a 5,000 won VR-box given as a prize. These are, in fact, the main players of the 4th Industrial Revolution era. There is sufficient motivation for demand. And fortunately, the price of Oculus Go, developed by Facebook and manufactured by Xiaomi, has dropped to 240,000 won. While it's not much money for adults, children lack a clear justification for purchasing it. Parents will surely think it's for gaming, and in fact, there's a lack of appropriate content for children to enjoy. (If you remove 'appropriate,' there's already an abundance of content that kids would love.) In our time, we bought computers saying it was for studying, and parents bought them for us to study. The reality, of course, was the exact opposite.... But in hindsight, most of the friends who played games on computers back then are doing well in this industry.

It's the same for adults; it's fun, but not enough to justify spending that much money...

6.  **What would happen if subsidies were provided to VR purchasers?**

Now, we've reached a price threshold rather than an experience threshold. So, at this stage, what if the government forcibly accelerates the market by a few months, or about a year? What if about 100,000 won is provided to individual purchasers? The adoption rate of VR could accelerate by several months to about a year compared to other countries.

If 100 billion won out of the 400 billion won the government plans to invest in the VR/AR industry is used for VR device distribution, 1 million units could be supplied, a scale that would allow Korea to capture a significant portion of VR devices installed worldwide. Then what would happen?

*   Oculus Go 32G could be purchased for 140,000 won, meaning it would be bought at 60% of the price compared to overseas.

Spending 100 billion won this way would create a B2C market of 1 million standalone VR devices, which is satisfying just to imagine. I predict that stories will begin to circulate that Korea has conquered the VR market, not just StarCraft. And 1 million users is a scale that would be considered a huge success for a typical vertical platform in Korea. In other words, Korea would have the only self-sustaining independent market in the VR sector. Oculus has no general distributor in Korea, and Korea was excluded from its B2B model, but with such a policy, there would be no reason for them not to enter. Facebook invested 2 trillion won in the future of VR. Currently, the Korean game market exceeds 20 trillion won. Even if 100 billion won goes to foreign companies like Xiaomi, wouldn't it be meaningful enough if we could capture a future VR software and service market worth tens of trillions of won? Samsung and LG might also lower their prices to similar levels and rush into production, or frankly, from Samsung and LG's perspective, receiving about 100 billion won from the government might not significantly boost their competitiveness, so they might not be very interested.

7.  **VR is the only area where private demand can be directly expanded.**

In the current situation where technology promotion policies are always driven from the supply side, if we think centered on SW and content as final consumer goods, couldn't we instead implement demand expansion policies? In this case, to maximize policy efficiency, it must be directly delivered to purchasing customers without intermediate steps. Moreover, since the benefits of the policy directly reach consumers, i.e., the public, opposition would be relatively low, and as it's an entirely new technology area, there are no conflicting industries. It's a complete blue ocean, just like high-speed internet was.

8.  **There's already a success story with electric vehicles.**

Do you think there's no precedent for such a policy? No. Electric vehicles have already done it. As a result, many BMWs were sold, but Ioniq, Kona, and Niro were aggressively developed and are now selling out. This can achieve a much broader and more direct effect than providing millions of won in subsidies for cars worth tens of millions of won.

This was initially a simple idea I jotted down on my timeline, but since many people offered enthusiastic feedback, I've organized it a bit more and posted it on my blog.

titleEn: Why Did I Start a Business?
contentEn:
Random Thoughts on IT

Why Did I Start a Business?

Luke ・ 2018. 5. 8. 10:50

Copy URL Add Neighbor

Other functions of the main text

When working on government support projects, I'm often asked about my motivation for starting a business. There might be a thousand and one reasons, but the thought that comes to mind here is, "Why am I doing this?" When I transitioned from development to planning, I used to say, "I love making things." As a child, I enjoyed LEGOs and plastic models, and then I chose to be a developer as my calling, and then a planner...

This time, I chose to start a business to create something I dreamed of a little more. It would be great if what I created brought wonderful wealth and honor, but just the fact that what I dream of is being made is overwhelming, and it's an overwhelming feeling when someone uses it.

When I was young, I created a very simple program at someone's request, and I was incredibly happy to see it work and to see someone using it. Perhaps this small catharsis made me want to try something a little bigger and more wonderful.

And the fundamental experience behind this was my admiration for the software and machines that moved me after I used them. Who could have made something so wonderful? It deeply impressed me, and some even changed the world.

Of course, everyone assumes changing the world and making a lot of money. If that's not guaranteed, you won't get fuel for your rocket, and it's hard to find colleagues.

However, my most fundamental motivation isn't something grand like that, but rather the great feeling of a child using what I made and being happy about it. I hope that what I've created brings joy to someone and becomes a new dream for someone else. But perhaps because it's too idealistic, this kind of answer isn't found in the government's startup motivation questions. ^^ However, since the process itself is the goal, I can say that I won't give up easily.

And that's why I love Elon Musk more than Zuckerberg.

titleEn: [VR Webtoon Review] Walking the Alley (Choi Ho-cheol)
contentEn:
Anime/Manga

[VR Webtoon Review] Walking the Alley (Choi Ho-cheol)

Luke ・ 2017. 10. 19. 23:57

Copy URL Add Neighbor

Body Other Functions

Honestly, not many people are watching it yet, and as someone involved in VR webtoons, which are a very unfamiliar format, I felt I needed to share more about it, so I'm writing this review. And, in fact, the bigger reason is that it's a work worth writing about.

This work is one that can answer the most direct questions about what VR webtoons are and what value they hold. This work, in fact, has already been published as an offline book... and is now being presented online for the first time by artist Choi Ho-cheol.

Walking the Alley::ComixV

It captures the urban landscapes and daily life observed while walking around. My wish is to be able to depict not just what is seen, but also the relationships between people and spaces.

comixv.com

First, two episodes of this work are currently available.

1. Gwanghwamun in Winter 2016

Episode 1 captures the scene of Gwanghwamun in the winter of 2016.

Looking at the square surrounded by barricades, what could that police officer be thinking? The sky is very gloomy.

Turning the screen or my head downwards, I see people tying their shoelaces and conversing.

And looking up, I see the water cannon that took the life of elder Baek Nam-gi.

And the next scene... it's actually a scene that surprised me when I received the storyboard.

The space of Gwanghwamun changes to night

I just received this storyboard and for a long time... I was like, 'Whoa...'

Gathering everyone's wishes, the Sewol Ferry rises.

As of October 2017, that winter's wish ultimately led to the Sewol Ferry being raised, and 4 out of 9 missing victims have returned home.

This work breaks our prejudice that webtoons are digital comics with vertically arranged panels. The essence of comics lies in pictures and stories, and stories don't necessarily need to be conveyed only through text. While speech bubbles are a very effective means of communication, I believe the origin of comics lies in the pictures and stories themselves. Just two images can deliver as much emotion and exhilaration as a short webtoon enjoyed for tens of minutes.

Every single person caught in the gaze tells a story, achieving empathy, one of the biggest characteristics of webtoons. And it's a work that successfully combines VR's most powerful immersion and spatial reproduction.

2. Episode 2: Euljiro Loop Line

Walking the Alley Episode 2, 'Euljiro Loop Line,' boasts overwhelming density.

Seoul in 1995, Sindorim before development. The scenery from my high school days is palpable. A landscape that still feels more human. An airplane flying precariously close to the cloudy sky. I won't explain it further.

This drawing is an adaptation of a 2-meter painting housed at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art into a VR version.

Euljiro Loop Line

Author Choi Ho-cheol

Publisher Geobukibooks

Release 2008.02.26.

View Details

Our team members worked on the sound, and I was satisfied because I felt they captured the atmosphere of that time very well.

To those who ask, 'What kind of art is a comic?' I believe this is a work that can be proudly presented. Such works don't come out often. We fly all the way to distant France to see the masterpiece Mona Lisa.

I am ready to pay for such a work anytime. Is it just my thought? It's a work too good to be seen for free, though it doesn't have a paid feature yet.

It's a must-see for those who love comics, and a work I'd intentionally show to those who disparage comics.

3. Where can you watch it?

You can watch it right now at the link below. If you install a separate Android or iOS app, you can also continue to receive updates for VR webtoons.

Walking the Alley::ComixV

It captures the urban landscapes and daily life observed while walking around. My wish is to be able to depict not just what is seen, but also the relationships between people and spaces.

comixv.com

If you have a smartphone and a simple VR device like Cardboard or a VR box, I highly recommend watching it with that. If you have a Gear VR, please install the app below to enjoy it.

ComixV - VR Comic / VR Webtoon

Webtoons come to life, VR webtoons are ComixV

www.oculus.com

If it were me, I wouldn't regret buying a Gear VR just to see this one work.
