For those curious about ComicsV, the meaning of virtual reality and comics, and how the future comic profession environment will change? A conference will be held where you can learn about these topics. Oh... and I'll be there too.

{{IMG:1}}

What will comics look like when they meet virtual reality (VR) and artificial intelligence (AI), the hot topics of this year? We introduce comic and animation content applying new technologies. Top experts in related fields, VR YouTubers, and comic artists will participate, covering topics such as virtual reality comics, webtoon platform development, comics and animation in virtual reality, and AI technology that can replace or assist creators.

**• Date & Time :****2017. 7. 23.(Sun) 13:00 ~ 15:30**
**• Venue :****Korea Manhwa Contents Agency, 5th Floor Seminar Room**
• Target Audience : Industry professionals interested in VR/AI, comic artists, general attendees, etc.

**13:00~13:20 Section1.** **Virtual Reality Comic Platform Development Story** : Yang Byeong-seok, CEO of ComicsV (20 min)
- You can hear about ComicsV's founding background and development strategy.
**13:20~13:40 ****Section2.** **Virtual Reality Comic Content** : Professor Park In-ha, Chungkang College of Cultural Industries (20 min)
- The meaning and current status of VR technology in comics
**13:50~14:10 ****Section3. ****AI and Artists** : Professor Jeong Ji-hoon, Kyung Hee Cyber University (20 min)
- Will AI threaten the jobs of comic artists too?
**14:10~14:30 ******** ****Virtual Reality Character Animation** : Lee Bae-sil, CEO of Panda8 Studio (20 min)
- Let's hear the story from CEO Lee Bae-sil, the only full-fledged VR animation producer in Korea.

** * Panel Discussion**
- In addition to the presenters: VR expert YouTuber Meolmiwang, and 'Wara! Convenience Store VR' artist Ji Kang-min.

### [ComicsV] Talking about Virtual Reality Webtoons (VR Webtoons)

https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
[Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
* ・ *
2017. 5. 25. 11:24

I apologize for the recent lack of posts. Since diving into the startup world, I seem to have even more work, making it difficult to write. Still, I felt bad leaving it as is for those who have been following my blog and waiting for my articles, so I pondered a way to achieve both. Many startups publish articles in the media to promote their companies, but I have the advantage of being able to tell my story more comfortably on my blog, and I intend to leverage that.
First, this is my first post on the topic, where I will write about what I consider "Virtual Reality Webtoons."

##### 1. What is a Virtual Reality Webtoon?

###### 1) Comics viewed on VR/AR platforms, considered future platforms

First, regarding "what is virtual reality?", you can refer to my blog or my report.

SPRi - Software Policy Research Institute: Issue Report A Study on VR / AR Growth Direction and Korea Industry Activation Plan Abstract 2016 was the year when commercial VR/AR devices began to be distributed worldwide. Unlike Korea, expectations for VR/AR have been steadily increasing overseas since 2014, and it has now reached a stage of contemplating monetization and hype. Optimism and concern about the VR/AR market coexist, and this can be traced back to the failure of VR popularization in the 1990s. The second VR diffusion period 2 spri.kr

https://spri.kr/posts/view/21749?code=issue_reports

I will initially define it as the narrow scope of viewing through an HMD, as everyone knows. This corresponds to the technical definition mentioned in my report. Think of devices like Oculus and Gear VR.

###### 2) 360-degree comics, not 3D

Second, the question that always arises with virtual reality, "Is 360-degree video also virtual reality?", applies equally to comics. Here, I have adopted 360 degrees.
There is no disagreement that the most important experience of virtual reality is 3D, or the experience provided by a three-dimensional space. However, 3D space requires users to be more active. That's why AR games like Pokémon GO are called exercise games.
In the case of games, this choice and feedback itself is the content and fun, so it fits very well. Educational content is also considered suitable for 3D environments because the effect of experience is high, not just knowledge transfer.
However, for content where the author's story is important, user movement exponentially increases the number of possibilities. And viewers or readers who consume that content approach media to enjoy it comfortably. When smart TVs were first introduced, there was a debate about "lean back" versus "lean forward," and the conclusion for video content was "lean back," and Netflix still makes videos. Of course, video games have continued to exist and grow as a separate market. These two are different genres, even if they share the same platform. It's similar to how reports and novels have different writing styles and consumption channels. Strictly speaking, 360 degrees is difficult to call a virtual reality experience, but the characteristic of VR HMDs is that they can bring a 360-degree screen cheaply to your eyes.
And the value of a 360-degree screen differs significantly from video and 2D comics like ours, and this market can greatly help grow the virtual reality market.

###### 3) It's not animation.

This is the third question, often asked by those who have briefly experienced it: "Why doesn't it move?" Yes, webtoons don't move. Of course, there have been attempts at interactive webtoons, like Horang's "Bongcheon-dong Ghost," but webtoons, or comics, do not move.
  A good animation director cannot necessarily be a good webtoon artist. Even with the advent of animation, the comic market still exists. The grammar of the two is distinctly different. Animation is something you passively sit and comfortably watch, offering more experiences, whereas comics are positioned somewhere between novels and animation.
  The charm of text is immense, and comics heavily rely on omission and exaggeration, showing only the best compositions and allowing readers to imagine the intermediate processes. 2D paintings are drawn differently from how humans see. This is because humans are animals that easily make mistakes, or rather, imagine more richly than what they actually see.
  And if all information is provided, this mechanism of imagination is difficult to operate, and the charm derived from the imagination of those empty spaces diminishes. This is why, when you see a photorealistic drawing, you might admire the skill, but it's often difficult to convey emotion.
  Comics are closer to novels and paintings. And I pondered how to transfer that grammar to a new medium called VR. The most interesting question was, "Will panels have meaning in a 360-degree space?" I believe artists will conduct many interesting experiments with this.

##### 2. The Greater Value of VR Webtoons Compared to VR Videos

{{IMG:1}}

 If I've explained what we mean by virtual reality comics earlier, now I'd like to discuss their value.
 When it comes to VR, 360-degree video is the most frequently attempted format. This is because it can already be uploaded to major platforms like YouTube, and anyone can easily produce it.
 I believe the value of 360-degree comics is much greater than that of video. The reason is that it's easier to express the artist's imagination than with video. In 360-degree video, existing film sets must not be visible, and the things that need to be controlled increase exponentially. Even with 360 degrees, you cannot express everything you imagine.
 However, comics are ultimately resolved through the artist's drawings. It's a screen where everything is controlled by the artist anyway, and any space can be drawn through imagination.
 Furthermore, for video, the need for larger screens has largely been met as TVs have continuously grown. However, comics have transformed into snack culture, shrinking in size to be viewed on smartphones, and vertical-scrolling webtoons even halve their resolution. It has become a very difficult and small space for directing.
 But finally, in virtual reality, that space expands explosively. While webtoons viewed on the bus always had their sound off, sound is standard with HMDs.
 The low resolution of VR HMDs is also not a big problem for comics. The reason low resolution is an issue in video is because small, distant objects that cannot be expressed by pixels are visible, but in comics, you can simply not draw such things or omit them, and imagination or optical illusion will fill that area.

 That's why we started this and aim to build an ecosystem. **We hope that those interested in this technology and virtual reality webtoons, especially not just comic artists but also illustrators and painters, will show interest.** We plan to distribute educational materials and are also planning academic conferences. This article was contributed as a column for the 'Software-Centered Society' in March.

Recently, an image of an academy curriculum for 1st graders was posted on a public community called 'Life Coding'. The curriculum, which starts from Scratch and extends to Linux and web servers, was surprisingly broad, to the extent that one might believe it was a first-year computer science course. I felt a bitter disappointment that what I had worried about since the launch of software education seemed to be happening. Although I gave quite a few special lectures on software education last year, I already dislike software education. I hear complaints that there's more to learn. At this juncture, I have once again organized my thoughts on what I believe software education should be.

{{IMG:1}}
							
								
									Intimidating Software Education

**First**, **software education is an experience of process, not knowledge acquisition**. A few days ago, I stopped my daughter, who is about to enter elementary school, from studying because of her poor learning habits. When checking her workbook, she would mark answers as correct without verifying them, even if she knew them, or mark wrong answers as correct, calling them mistakes. While I understood her desire to get good scores, it was no longer learning but a bad habit, so I immediately stopped her studies and explained the importance of making mistakes. I realized that not only teachers and parents but also our children can easily fall into score-first, knowledge-first, and progress-first mentalities, forgetting their purpose and direction, much like the excessive curriculum at the computer academy mentioned earlier.
In traditional education, which aimed to cultivate industrial workers, the important thing was to measure how much one knew about the many problems and solutions accumulated by ancestors. This allowed for the creation of personnel with specific job skills, and thus there was clear progress, scores, and a way to evaluate children. Therefore, scores were important, and their importance cannot be denied even now.
However, the education for our children who will live in the future society must be different. When discussing software education, two terms that invariably appear are the Fourth Industrial Revolution and artificial intelligence; simple software development has already reached a level where it is possible by AI.
Furthermore, the characteristic of software, its replicability, means there is no need to solve the same problem again. Through the open-source movement, necessary software can be easily obtained for free. Software education places less importance on knowledge than other types of education. Therefore, if software education ends with knowledge transfer, it could be a waste of time that only burdens children.
To give another example from my own experience recently, I explained the waterfall model and spiral model of software engineering to my daughter, who has weak self-control. Although these are concepts taught in university, their content is very simple: a sequence of analysis, design, development, and evaluation, and the concept of repeating this to improve. Applying this, I instructed her to design her day's schedule for 5 minutes after waking up, act based on it throughout the day, and then write a diary in the evening for evaluation and analysis. In fact, coding in software education is part of this problem-solving process and a condensed version of it.
Many people misunderstand software education as merely memorizing program functions and knowing features, like a math formula. However, much more important is the experience and acquisition of the process. Moreover, the process is not absolute. It must be applied differently depending on the nature of the problem, and if the premise changes, the problem also changes frequently. Software education should be about learning and experiencing the process, not just knowledge.

**Second**, **software education is education that redeems mathematics**. There are many arguments that "Korean language education is better" or "math education is better" than software education. Among them, let's talk about math education, which led the Third Industrial Revolution and whose importance is already recognized.
Indeed, software originated from mathematics. It is also clear that it utilizes many mathematical elements. However, today's mathematics has long been detached from real life, and now software education is the only subject that can connect mathematics to real life.
Some people ask what use mathematics has beyond the four basic operations. Most adults would agree that interest rates are probably the most complex calculation in real life. However, those who have processed data with computers, created 3D graphics, or had even a little experience with artificial intelligence program structures would not agree with this idea. While there's no need to solve difficult math problems like those on a math test, it's difficult to understand and use such software without understanding the content of each math unit. Rather, by operating software and wanting to do more, one is prompted to relearn insufficient math. This is why I've seen people in the math field who are negative about software education, but not people in the software field who are negative about math.
Software deals with real-world data and can even change the real world with physical computing learning tools like Arduino. And one directly experiences the numerous problems that arise when mathematical theories are actualized into code. Theory is just theory, and mathematics is theoretical education.
This experience does not diminish the importance of mathematics, but it makes us recognize the limitations of mathematics and the importance of software education. It's not that mathematics can teach software education, but rather that software education is the only education that can bring mathematics out of the world of concepts and back into our lives.

**Third**, **software education needs time for play and thought**.
Finally, many people worry about children playing games during software education time, so I've organized my thoughts on games and play. While I won't deny that there are cases where games have a negative impact on learning, when information devices are used for learning, the negative aspects of games are reduced, and games with educational elements help improve children's intellectual abilities. Therefore, software education is being developed with an unclear distinction between learning and play. Rather, it is more likely to have a negative effect if children perceive smartphones and computers simply as game consoles. As children grow, their ability to handle information devices becomes important. In such a situation, it is greedy to block information devices from an early age and then suddenly expect them to handle them well in college. It is inevitable that children's generation will experience both learning and play through information devices; instead, we need to consider how they can play in a better way, and parents also need to participate in play.
There is also a misunderstanding about information devices, which is that they eliminate time for thinking. However, many software education activities and certain game genres require a great deal of thinking time. While a parent might find it somewhat frustrating to see a child sitting in front of a computer for a long time, it is more important to understand what the child is doing during this time. In reality, some tasks require a long time, and others do not, so fostering the ability to plan and control oneself is more important than ever. Now, **the importance of teaching that control ability can be said to be equivalent to teaching how to use chopsticks.**
Furthermore, what's important is to look at *what* one is addicted to, rather than *how much* one is addicted to smartphones or computers. This applies to both play and learning. While it might feel urgent, if you rush and try to extract something within a time limit, problems are bound to arise. Software education absolutely needs time for play and thought. To achieve this, both children and parents need both play and learning in software education, and it requires time and empathy.
Software education will become full-fledged starting in 2018. As the biggest characteristic of software is rapid change, it may be virtually impossible to provide a precise answer for software education itself. However, software education, which allows learning from mistakes, has nothing to discard in its trial-and-error process. It needs to be flexible to evolve into better education, becoming better tomorrow than it is today. That is what I believe software education should aim for.

titleEn: Please let me quit...
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

I should hate you,
It's enough to hate you,
Why do I still like you?
I should hate you.
If I can't erase you,
I should at least hate you,
But why...
Why do I, who am struggling, worry about others
And miss the one who left?
That's why it hurts so much.
That's why I'm dying like this.
Calling and calling,
Are you trying to turn into a stone?
Or become light ash
And fly to their side?
Who would remember you for doing that?
Who would shed a single tear for you for doing that?
You'll just become a laughingstock for passersby.
You'll just become entertainment for the crowd.
The only ones who understand you are the sad clowns who put on makeup every day,
And the fairy tale protagonists who are already dead.
Stop it.
Stop it, I tell you.
This bleeding foolishness.
Please make it stop...
2003. 11. 26

Entering it seemed to be by will,
But leaving it was not by choice – that was love.
At least, according to my experience...
2017. 02. 21

titleEn: Act Now
The Dog and Her
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

Whenever I see a dog, that person who especially loved dogs comes to mind. What does that person see that makes them think of me? Paintings..? I'd rather it be something like that. Because then it would be something that's everywhere, like dogs... That person might have forgotten me, but I somewhat resent dogs for constantly bringing them to mind.
2003. 10. 26

Now that I'm married, I can't raise a dog because of the child. But back then, the dog was also a being that connected the two of us. And when we met again, the dog she raised had grown old and passed away to heaven. A dog that only looks at one person might be foolish, but isn't that why they are loved?
2017. 01. 31

contentEn:
[Musings on IT](https://blog.naver.com/PostList.naver?blogId=fstory97&categoryNo=41&from=postList)

### The Path VR Experience Centers Should Take

https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
[Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
* ・ *
2016. 12. 19. 10:04

[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220889342077&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220889342077&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
[Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220889342077&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

##### 1. Let's increase offline distribution channels to revitalize the VR market.

There are many opinions that we should increase offline distribution channels to revitalize the domestic VR market. Arcade game centers, or what are commonly called "game rooms," are often discussed as being at the center of this. I agree with the overall context of this discussion.
While having facilities where one can experience VR is certainly important for the VR industry, I question whether VR experience rooms or game rooms should be the successor to arcade game centers or PC bangs.

##### 2. Are PC bangs and arcade game centers the answer?

First, VR still cannot be played for as long as PC games. Eye fatigue is an issue, and single-player games, not network games, are difficult to play for extended periods due to content supply problems. Most importantly, playing active games for a long time is physically tiring. Therefore, the PC bang model, which profits from selling ramen to long-term users, would not be suitable for VR.
What about arcade game centers? First, there are adult arcades like "Sea Story" that ruined the game industry, and the arcades remaining in movie theaters. It feels like an extreme polarization: one went towards the shadows, and the other is struggling towards the light. My personal opinion is that these two should be separated. And I strongly agree with applying VR to the arcades remaining in movie theaters. However, I feel that such spaces are too limited to kickstart the VR industry, making me wonder if they would be sufficient.

##### 3. Hints for VR Experience Rooms from Claw Machine Arcades

Recently, some noticeable stores have emerged. For a while now, when I go to the main shopping district in Sanbon, I've seen a significant increase in claw machine arcades. Perhaps because they are registered as game facilities, minors are prohibited from entering after 10 PM. These claw machine arcades have a few characteristics: standardization, something provided offline, and user targeting.

{{IMG:1}}

###### 1) Standardization

First, standardization facilitates the spread of chain networks. Claw machine games, densely packed into small spaces, are easy to install and maintain. The biggest problem with today's VR rooms is the cumbersome headsets and controllers that might get lost. To be applied to actual offline chains, they need to be sturdy, resistant to loss, hygienic, and easy to put on and take off. Performance is a secondary concern. If there's still a market for hardware, couldn't Korea aim for this kind of area?

###### 2) Special Rewards Provided Offline

Second, something provided offline: claw machine arcades give out dolls as prizes. If this goes wrong, it can lead to currency exchange issues or turn into a gambling den, increasing speculation. However, doing something in an offline experience center and getting something offline provides a sense of acquisition. Currently, collecting cards in mobile games through gacha items is a similar element, but VR rooms lack the means to introduce such elements. So, what if we use games based on IPs to give out IP-related items? For example, by earning coins only available in VR rooms, one could get character prizes from a coin box... My kids go crazy for this. Actually, I used to love collecting 2,000-won characters (I stopped after marriage, and my wife threw them all away). Kakao Games, for instance, might find this a worthwhile business.

###### 3) Let's make it a date course

Third, the target users are couples. The reason it's located on the first floor is precisely this: the items obtained are actually for gifting. Currently, there are no VR contents that couples can enjoy together. If VR content is approached with this concept, it should include content that increases affection between couples and is fun. Think about why people specifically go to watch horror movies. If a VR experience room establishes itself as an essential date course for couples in this way, then it's game over. All offline content must become a culture. Otherwise, it's difficult for it to last long.
I'm writing this hoping it might be helpful to those considering an offline chain store. (Because I won't be doing it...)

ps. Currently, for the best VR experience in Seoul, I recommend VR-plus in Gangnam.
However, there isn't much reason to go a second time as there's no specialized content yet.
But, there's a world of difference between having experienced something and not, so I frequently use it to spread the word about VR.

                        Today was Suneung day.
And, JTBC's closing music was Lucid Fall's "Still There."

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
	        
	            
	            
	                
							

https://www.youtube.com/embed/V5CuFqQZiwk?wmode=transparent

	                
	                
	                    	Still There Music Video (2nd Anniversary Memorial Video for the Sewol Ferry Disaster)
	                
	            
	        
	    
    
	

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        While there are some who say money is skill and went to university by riding horses,
there were also some children who waited for the Suneung that many students took today, but ultimately couldn't take it.
This is why we, who are still here, must set things right.

I send a round of applause to everyone who took the Suneung today.
Whether you did well or not, today was the day someone had been waiting for so eagerly. Cheer up.
Instead, please just say "thank you" to your parents who silently stood by you, even if they couldn't give you money or buy you a horse.

### Is Choi Soon-sil worse than North Korea? Yes, she is!

	                
	            
	        
        
        
        
        

    
        https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
        [Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
        
            * ・ *
            2016. 11. 3. 19:56
        
    

	[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220852769160&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

            [** Add Neighbor**](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220852769160&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
	
        [Other Post Functions](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220852769160&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
               [Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220852769160&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

                        I no longer want to know or see anything about Choi Soon-sil, but even based on the facts that have already been revealed,** I believe Choi Soon-sil is in violation of the National Security Act.** Even if I don't want to see it, my Facebook timeline is in chaos, and news continues to pour out.
 At this point, **Choi Soon-sil's crime is not just corruption, but that she cut off loyal subjects (public officials) who were diligently working in their positions, and tried to devour the entire country**. **If a king is misled and surrounded by treacherous officials, the nation will soon fall and invite foreign enemies. Is she worse than North Korea? Of course, she is.**

North Korea is threatening, but it has not yet waged an all-out war. Choi Soon-sil has already violated the South Korean government, and it will likely take several years or more just to find and remove Choi Soon-sil's remnants and recover. In fact, it's questionable whether everything can even be removed. The economic damage is also far greater than when shells fell on Yeonpyeong Island. 
Simply put, it's become a situation similar to a North Korean spy infiltrating the Blue House and assassinating the president.
The president and the government seem to be in a near-vegetative state.

Stock prices have plummeted, and foreigners are reportedly pulling out because they expect the situation to be prolonged. The damage alone amounts to tens of trillions of won. I don't know where all the people who used to calculate the economic damage of the Sewol ferry incident have gone. Try calculating this.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                Choi Soon-sil Gate Rattles Stock Market, Foreigners Net Sell 18,000 Contracts in Three Days... Signs of Departure? However, 12... news.mtn.co.kr

http://news.mtn.co.kr/newscenter/news_viewer.mtn?gidx=2016110317144141237

                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        
Foreign media are also churning out articles like those in Sunday Seoul, and the national prestige has nowhere further to fall.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                [Facebook www.facebook.com](https://www.facebook.com/plugins/video.php?href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Fallyeozum%2Fvideos%2F1803530326531394%2F&show_text=0&width=560)
                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        
**The key treacherous officials who invited such foreign enemies must, of course, be severely punished. Perhaps the sin of those who installed the president, knowing these facts, is even greater. **

 Above all, the worst threat Choi Soon-sil brought about was the collapse of "liberal democracy," which promises rewards for effort, a government formed through democracy, and its members having a vocational calling. She clearly showed that no one needs to make an effort, and that power and money are everything. This is truly the worst. It's no wonder that "Gongsin" (a term for a study expert/master) said, "There's no need to study hard"...

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                Video This is a country where you don't need to study, Republic of Korea. ★ Gongsin Kang Sung-tae Our old man who changed his stance after the Choi Soon-sil, Chung Yoo-ra incident. titleEn: What Samsung Electronics Loses with the Galaxy Note 7 Withdrawal
contentEn:
[Musings on IT](https://blog.naver.com/PostList.naver?blogId=fstory97&categoryNo=41&from=postList)

### What Samsung Electronics Loses by Withdrawing the Galaxy Note 7

https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
[Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
* ・ *
2016. 10. 12. 10:10

[Copy URL](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220834136857&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[** Add Neighbor**](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220834136857&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[Other Body Functions](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220834136857&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

[Share](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220834136857&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
[Report](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220834136857&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

The recent Note 7 ignition incident has unexpectedly escalated, ultimately leading to the worst-case scenario of the Note 7 withdrawal. While people say that worrying about Samsung is the most useless worry in the world, I feel that Samsung Electronics' smartphone business is facing its worst crisis ever.

##### 1. Expected Decline in Android Flagship Market Share

This Note 7 incident will likely result in a crushing defeat in a battle that should not have been lost. It's already well-known that the Note 7's launch schedule was moved up to gain an advantage in the fight against the iPhone. iPhone and Samsung Electronics are companies that manufacture representative flagship devices for iOS and Android, respectively. Although they are often compared, in reality, not many users switch between Android and iOS. Getting used to one platform is a powerful thing.
However, Google recently released the Pixel phone, pricing it the same as the iPhone, no longer a low-cost phone, and touting it as the best in all specifications. In other words, they are advertising that "we are now the Android flagship." And, in fact, even Chinese phones, which used to be bought for their cheap price, have seen Huawei shed its cheap brand image some time ago and are now threatening Samsung Electronics' Android flagship market.
As a result, the exit of the Galaxy Note 7 has put many users looking for a flagship device in a situation where they have no choice but to consider other devices. Coincidentally, Google stepped up saying "we are the original!" - the timing couldn't be worse. I wondered if Google could secure even a few percent of the market, but given the current situation, I think they will settle in very easily. Google's establishment in the hardware market is not just a single battle but very bad news in the long run.

##### 2. Decline in Reliability of Korean (SDI) Lithium-Ion Batteries

Furthermore, this might not just be a problem for Samsung Electronics. Samsung SDI is pushing lithium-ion batteries as its next growth engine and is a beneficiary of electric vehicles. And, in fact, Tesla Motors also uses lithium-ion batteries, and one of Tesla Motors' biggest technological claims is that it has enhanced battery stability with 44 patents.
While cars and mobile phones clearly have different technologies and environments, Samsung SDI's lithium-ion battery technology is clearly set to lose significant credibility, and this may affect the battery market related to electric vehicles.
The Galaxy S8 series is likely to revert to lithium polymer batteries, potentially leading to increased costs and additional pressure on Samsung Electronics' profit margins.
It seems that the Note 7's downfall might have been trying to catch three rabbits at once: lowering prices, increasing performance, and shortening the schedule with Samsung's technology.
Honestly, the Note 7 was a very well-made phone, and it's a great pity. I even wonder if it would be possible to replace all batteries with lithium polymer ones... (but I don't know for sure, but it probably wouldn't be easy technically.)

##### 3. Decline in Samsung Brand Trust and the Burden of S8's Facelift

Friends who are interested in phones might care whether it's a Note 7 or just an S7, but many people overseas simply see it as a Samsung phone. Samsung phones have established a sophisticated design. Personally, I think the design has been superior to Apple's since the S6. However, now this design is likely to evoke memories of the Note 7. Samsung Electronics' brand has declined, and the S8 faces the burden of needing a complete facelift.

##### 4. Samsung Electronics' Future: Solving Three Challenges

Samsung Electronics seemed to be planning a strategy focused on IoT and services, acquiring the AI company Viv. However, it seems that the burden has increased as solving the current problems will require considerable time and effort. Of course, it is a company with that much manpower and money. Samsung Electronics now faces three challenges simultaneously: transforming into a service company, fending off attacks from competitors, and restoring trust.
However, a company is not run by one person. These three challenges can be tackled by three different organizations. But as the number of challenges increases, so do issues of prioritization and organizational coordination. They'll do well, though. Worrying about Samsung is useless, after all...

Additionally, I wonder if there will be changes in Samsung Electronics' management line. First, I expect many executives and employees will be held responsible and laid off ㅜㅜ How long will a global company like Samsung Electronics be run as a family business? I also wonder if it wouldn't be wise to shed the burden and step back as a major shareholder, operating primarily with professional managers... (The truth is, the CEO gets criticized whether they do well or poorly.) Well, this is just my personal opinion.

titleEn: The Core of the Progressive Tax Controversy Isn't Expensive or Cheap Electricity
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}
			
	    	
	    
    
         

	[IT 잡설 (IT 잡설)](https://blog.naver.com/PostList.naver?blogId=fstory97&categoryNo=41&from=postList)

 

        
     	
        
        	
	            
	                
                        

### The core of the progressive tax controversy is not expensive electricity, cheap electricity.

	                
	            
	        
        
        
        
        

    
        https://blog.naver.com/fstory97
        [Luke](https://blog.naver.com/fstory97)
        
            * ・ *
            2016. 8. 10. 10:20
        
    

	[URL 복사 (Copy URL)](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220784077066&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)

            [** 이웃추가 (Add Neighbor)**](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220784077066&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
	
        [본문 기타 기능 (Other functions for this post)](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220784077066&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
               [공유하기 (Share)](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220784077066&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
                [신고하기 (Report)](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=220784077066&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)
		
	
    

        
        
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        I'd like to share my personal opinion on the abolition of the progressive tax system. KEPCO is claiming that Korea's electricity rates are below cost, and I want to talk about that.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        

##### 1. Are Korea's electricity rates cheap or expensive?

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                         As I mentioned in the title that it's not the core issue, to give you the answer upfront, household electricity is cheap. KEPCO made a somewhat exaggerated claim of 50,000 won for 300-400kw usage with air conditioning, but it actually falls between 59,000 and 63,000 won. This is roughly the feeling of my own home, probably referring to an expanded 24-pyeong to under 30-pyeong apartment. Of course, if you use an old air conditioner and a 2-in-1 unit, it will be more. In my house, it's impossible to install a 2-in-1, so I use one air conditioner, one fan, and one circulator simultaneously. Measuring with EnerTalk, I think the 400kw line at the 4th stage of the progressive tax is the most standard level.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                [[스마트 전력계 에너톡] 우리집 에어콘 전기 얼마나 먹나? 궁금할때 에너톡 요즘 인공지능이다 VR/AR이다 시끄럽지만, 작년과 재작년즈음에는 IoT, 빅데이터가 한참 시끄러웠죠.... blog.naver.com](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220774524801)
                    
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                         Another point of contention is that industrial electricity is not cheap, but this is a bit of a misstatement. The fact that industrial electricity is particularly cheap has been a claim made by KEPCO all along. If you search online a little, you can find KEPCO's past claims. However, if KEPCO suddenly changes its tune and says that high-voltage electricity costs less to produce, then one answer can be found in the difference between the two rate systems, and eliminating that difference is actually the core of this controversy. And, above all, this is a demand of the times driven by technological development and a paradigm shift in energy.
 It's not simply a debate about whether household electricity with a progressive tax is cheap or not.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        

##### 2. Why is industrial electricity more rational than household electricity?

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                         I don't know if industrial electricity is cheap or not. Only KEPCO, which knows the production cost, would know.
 However, what is certain is that industrial electricity allows for price reductions through its own facilities, and even uses variable rates that charge different prices depending on the time of day. This has demand and price elasticity, allowing for more rational choices compared to household rates, which are simply calculated by total monthly usage and lumped together with a progressive tax.
 To put it simply with communication fees, if households pay a monthly communication fee with a progressive tax applied, businesses use a communication plan with price elasticity based on demand, meaning they can formulate a strategy for communication fees. The problem is that households do not have the choice mentioned above. This is because households have historically existed only as unilateral consumers of electricity.

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        

##### 3. Why are households now talking about price elasticity, not progressive tax?

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                         But why has the progressive tax issue suddenly come up now? I see two main reasons for this. First,

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                        

##### 1) Increased demand, global warming, urban heat island effect, and polarization

                    
                
            
        
    

    

    
        
            
                
                    
                         The first is a societal demand: it has simply gotten too hot, and the polarization among households has worsened. My mother-in-law is very reluctant to turn on the air conditioner and endures without it. It's very regrettable. Although they say they give more benefits to low-income individuals, the psychological pressure of the progressive tax is naturally felt more by low-income individuals. This is because they don't even have the means to measure their usage. I earnestly ask KEPCO to tell them it's okay to turn on the air conditioner, or at least send them real-time electricity usage information.
 I believe the reason is that many people, already annoyed by the heat, think of KEPCO even more every time they turn on the air conditioner.

##### 2) Emergence of Energy-based IoT Services

The second is technological advancement. I purchased an IoT device called EnerTalk and am currently measuring real-time electricity usage. However, in the current situation in Korea, looking at that data only allows for the option of simply saving. But what if it were a market with demand-based price elasticity, like industrial use? Below is Tesla's home battery, which I mentioned yesterday. It stores 10Kwh of electricity, and the average monthly electricity consumption in the US is said to be 900Kwh. (3 times that of Korea!!)

{{IMG:2}}

As I mentioned earlier, 10kW per day is the daily electricity consumption of an average household. What if price elasticity were applied and IoT-based devices were activated? Wouldn't it be possible to receive KEPCO's price API, charge during cheap hours, and use the battery during expensive hours?
Currently, KEPCO's concern due to the abolition of the progressive tax system is the power supply and demand issue during peak hours. The simple abolition of the progressive tax is not the problem. The next step after the progressive tax is demand-based rate rationalization, not simply making it unconditionally cheap. Perhaps the name "progressive tax" merely refers to the current uniform rate system, rather than a systemic problem with the progressive tax itself, and I hope the public accepts it that way.
What about electric vehicles? If you own an electric car at home, you could optimize your household energy plan by using the electric car's battery instead of a separate battery pack.

##### 4. Rational Electricity Market: Key Infrastructure for the Renewable Energy Industry

For detached houses, it seems that about 300kW can be covered by a residential solar power system.

{{IMG:3}}

In fact, in autumn and spring, there would likely be surplus electricity, and if that electricity could be sold back to KEPCO, investment in the facility costs would become easier.
For apartment buildings, if models were created to aggregate the aforementioned home batteries in large quantities underground, or link them with electric vehicles in the parking lot, the efficiency of electricity use would be maximized.
The path forward is not simply "don't waste electricity," but "use it efficiently," and I believe that such market changes in electricity infrastructure will have an enormous impact on the entire industry.

**I hope KEPCO also views this issue regarding the progressive tax not merely as a demand for electricity bill reduction, but as a demand for future electricity industry infrastructure.**

titleEn: [Smart Power Meter EnerTalk] How much electricity does our air conditioner use? When you're curious, EnerTalk
contentEn:
These days, AI and VR/AR are making a lot of noise, but last year and the year before, it was all about IoT and Big Data. It's true that despite these technologies, there haven't been many standout products. Was it all just hype? I don't think so. When things get noisy, it means investors are flocking in, and planning and development take time. It can take as little as 6 months, and if hardware is involved, that period can be even longer. Among them, I'd like to introduce you to EnerTalk, a domestic smart power meter. This post was written after being selected as an EnerTalk experience group member. I originally planned to write it sooner, but I wanted to check the electricity bill after a full month of usage post-installation, so it took a little longer.

1. What is the smart power meter EnerTalk?

It's a smart device that connects to your home's wireless LAN to provide real-time electricity usage, predict electricity bills based on usage, and allow comparison with other households.

{{IMG:1}}

**EnerTalk (Our Home's Electricity Usage Guide) Electricity bill measurement, power consumption measurement, standby power, progressive tariff management, electricity bill shock management, electricity bill saving, patented product, energy saving meter, electricity saving, electricity bill reduction device**

Seller
EnerTalk
*npay_available*

Price
65,000 won

http://storefarm.naver.com/enertalk/products/414863942

EnerTalk is the same product as LG Uplus's IoT Energy Meter.

{{IMG:2}}

However, if you install it through LG Uplus, it's difficult to get proper service unless you subscribe to LG Uplus's wired internet network. In short, you're tied to the Uplus communication network. I initially considered this product, but I didn't want to change my home's IPTV from KT, so I eventually gave up.

2. Installation

First, the installation. I installed it on May 20, 2016. A technician visited. Of course, the technician visit is separate from the device cost. However, if you're not afraid of handling electricity, installation is not too difficult. Since I was part of the experience group, I received a visit to hear the explanation.

1) Open the distribution board (fuse box)

First, the distribution board. My house is an e-Pyeonhan Sesang apartment built in June 2007, so I assume similar brands would be similar.

{{IMG:3}}
Apartment Distribution Board

When you open it, it looks like this. I'll connect it to the circuit breaker on the far right.

{{IMG:4}}

2) Check the product

The components are simple: an electric wire, the EnerTalk main unit. That wire will supply electricity from the circuit breaker to the EnerTalk main unit. The hook-like thing on top of EnerTalk is actually the power measurement sensor. I'll open the hook and clamp it onto the main power line.

{{IMG:5}}

3) Power supply

Loosen the screws on the distribution board and EnerTalk, connect them with the enclosed wire, tighten them, and then turn on the power. A light will come on, indicating that EnerTalk is receiving electricity normally. When connecting, always turn off the switch of the circuit breaker you are connecting to.

{{IMG:6}}

4) Sensor installation

The sensor opens like this.

{{IMG:7}}
EnerTalk Power Measurement Sensor

I guess it measures the strength of the magnetic field when electricity flows. Clamp it firmly onto the main power line's insulation. Then, organize the equipment. My house's distribution board didn't have much extra space, but it fit somehow. Then, close it. If you search other blogs for EnerTalk installation, you'll find more detailed photos, so you can refer to those.

{{IMG:8}}

3. App connection

Naturally, you need a Wifi router at home; 2.4Ghz connection is supported. Install the EnerTalk app.

[**EnerTalk HOME - 에너톡 - Android app on Google Play** play.google.com](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ionicframework.enertalkhome874425)

After signing up, it connects with EnerTalk for the first time and searches for your router. You select your home's router and enter the password, which tells EnerTalk about your home's router and connects it. I considered taking screenshots of each step, but I don't think it's necessary, so I'll just explain this much.

4. Let's see how much electricity our house uses in a month.

For detailed settings, you can call the apartment management office to find out when the electricity bill is tallied. My apartment said it was the 10th of every month. However, when I checked this month's bill, it was different.

{{IMG:9}}

{{IMG:10}}

I called the management office, and it turns out the June bill was from May 10th to June 9th.

{{IMG:11}}

9 days of usage weren't measured. ㅜㅜ It seems I'll have to wait another month for accurate figures. Since the moving date was included, there will probably be a significant error. This way, you can directly see how many Kwh you used each month. Seeing it with my own eyes, the difference between August and June is huge.

5. Realizing the power of the electricity-guzzling air conditioner.

I recently received an unfamiliar alarm.

{{IMG:12}}

Huh... what's this? I didn't have this last month. So I checked... Wow. It's going up like this because I've been running the air conditioner due to the heat. The difference between the 19th and the 24th is enormous.

{{IMG:13}}

Comparing the two days by hour, on the 19th, I only ran the air conditioner briefly around 6 PM, while on Sunday, July 24th, I ran it all day while playing with the kids at home. Playing at home isn't free either. It seems I spent about 1500 won on the air conditioner that day.

{{IMG:14}}

6. Am I using too much?

It's hard to confirm with absolute figures since it's grouped by apartment size and the range of family members is wide, but fortunately, I'm not using too much. ^^

{{IMG:15}}

7. Other features

EnerTalk provides an Open API, allowing you to create your own services. A hackathon related to this was held recently. And I know they are planning to offer an "Energy Fingerprint" feature. If enough of this data accumulates, we can identify the characteristics of how different appliances consume electricity, which I expect will lead to more efficient electricity usage habits. We might even be able to tell if an air conditioner is on or if it's a hairdryer based on electricity usage patterns, especially if we utilize the Big Data and AI technologies mentioned earlier. Google acquired the IoT company Nest for 3.2 trillion won. Even in Korea, despite the smaller market, good companies like these are actively working, and the world seems to be gradually becoming smarter. I used to think that by the 21st century, all homes would be smart, but arriving in the 21st century, it's fun to gradually transform them into smart devices one by one.

8. Reasonable electricity bill is needed.

Recently, lawyer Kwak Sang-eon, who is also the son-in-law of former President Roh Moo-hyun, has been leading a movement and lawsuit against KEPCO's progressive electricity tariff system.

http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=052&aid=0000880333&sid1=001
**[Live Economy] Lawless progressive electricity tariff, only households bear the burden** [Live Interview] ■ Broadcast: YTN Radio FM 94.5 (15:10~16:00) ■ Host: Kim Woo-sung PD ■ Interviewee: Kwak Sang-eon, Lawyer at Law Firm Ingang ◇ Kim Woo-sung PD (hereinafter Kim Woo-sung)> For several days... news.naver.com

http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=052&aid=0000880333&sid1=001

I agree with this stance. The progressive tariff for household electricity seems to have been a policy for Korea's export-oriented economy. It was probably an expression of the will to prioritize exports even if domestic demand had to sacrifice. However, with unstable international affairs and diminishing trickle-down effects these days, the argument that domestic demand and consumption have a significant impact on the national economy and happiness is gaining traction. And I believe this progressive tariff is one of the things holding back domestic demand and consumption. Furthermore, with the advent of electric vehicles, our energy policy needs a paradigm shift. It's time for a reasonable electricity pricing system with price elasticity, where you pay for what you use. Looking at the progressive tariff graph makes it even more real. To achieve that, it's time for us to look into how much we actually use. And I believe IoT devices like this are one way to do that.

### [Forest Story Coming Out] I support Megal.

Through this discussion, I've learned something new.
It seems that just writing "I support Megal" in the title immediately invites disparagement and criticism.
Is it really about opposing hate? Does this mean Megal and Ilbe can be included as objects of hate?

In my post, I have never criticized anyone, whether they support Megal or not.
In my post, I have never criticized specific individuals or specific groups. Criticism from supporters and opponents is different. While I may have responded in a similar tone when feeling upset by sarcastic or unconditionally critical comments, the original post was humble. However, the comments ultimately throw stones at individual "Megal supporters."

I was so dumbfounded that I considered speaking more strongly, but fearing the discussion would escalate further, I revised the main text to use polite language.

Justice cannot be achieved by abandoning reason and sanity. No matter how well it's dressed up, it's simply violence.

The current flow of events no longer prioritizes the issue or the truth. Megal has already become a corpse, and the violent comments accumulating to criticize Megal are increasing more than the trashy posts made by the Megal camp.
The internet is search-based, so only pages are visible. It's practically difficult to grasp the truth and context without considerable effort.
In other words, the public will ultimately be more exposed to the violent comments from the anti-Megal camp, and will inevitably focus on that violence rather than understanding the angry anti-Megal camp. It's natural that declarations of support for Megal from progressive figures are increasing.

I hope the anti-Megal camp stops justifying violence. Currently, the actions of the anti-Megal camp even look like mirroring. Megal's mirroring. Megal copied Ilbe, and the anti-Megal camp copied Megal... There's no point in claiming to be different from Ilbe while acting that way.

If you wish to debate, please be courteous. If you cannot acknowledge differences, it ultimately leads to fascism.

titleEn: [Son of a Bitch Lawsuit] The Youth Protection Act is not a Child Protection Act.
contentEn:
1. Child protection cannot be a reason in the 'Bastard' controversy.

It seems many people are most confused about this in the 'Bastard' controversy, but the Juvenile Protection Act aims to protect adolescents, not children. Children must fundamentally be subjects assumed to be under parental supervision. Even in the case of daycare centers, it's assumed they are always under the supervision of teachers. Parents who simply hand a computer or smartphone to a child and then tell them not to watch 'Bastard' are actually infringing upon the rights of adolescents. I hope this point is not confused. Intermediate age ratings like 12 and 15 are recommendations, not 12-rated or 15-rated restrictions. For children, this means parents should manage their viewing based on these recommendations. Even if we concede a hundred times that Naver has a problem, it would only be for not indicating the recommended age. (However, this webtoon is not popular with children anyway, and children would show strong aversion to it. Children do not like strong stimuli. Don't mistakenly think children will like it. Forcing them to watch it would be child abuse.) If all content rated 'G' (General Audience) had to protect children, then all of it would need 12-rated or 15-rated restrictions. Especially news and social affairs sections. Then, ultimately, the worst situation in the world would occur, where all internet content would require real-name verification, something even communist parties don't do for all content. (It seems there are people who want that. You're not from Namsan, are you?)

2. Youth protection should not infringe upon the freedom of artistic consumption.

The Juvenile Protection Act should also be approached from the perspective of laws concerning the exploitation of adolescents. That's why the Cinderella Law, having nothing else to attach, ended up with something strange like 'the right to sleep'. If the Cinderella Law's intent is to be followed, then late-night self-study should also be abolished. While some argue for blocking various things due to adolescents' immature values, explicit sexual content or violent content should indeed be blocked. (In fact, gore, which is violent content, is not preferred by adults in Korea either. It can be considered almost non-existent here.) I agree with blocking content depicting sexual fantasies because adolescents are in the midst of secondary sexual characteristics. However, I believe it is better to grant adolescents the right to view serious, especially good, content that deals with other social issues, even if it might be somewhat uncomfortable. This is because it infringes upon adolescents' freedom of artistic consumption, rather than protecting them.

3. Distinguish the controversy and separate the frames. Understand why people are angry and calling others 'kkondae'. Children vs. Adolescents, Pornography vs. Cultural Content.

This controversy is structured as a 2x2 matrix. One axis is **Children and Adolescents**, and the other is **Pornography and Cultural Content**. This is because content like 'Bastard' is not gore or pornography. And the reason many creators and fans are angry and calling others 'kkondae' is precisely because their beloved cultural content was treated in the same way as gore and pornography. In comics, this kind of controversy is, in fact, nothing new.

http://blog.naver.com/enterani/220753694367
[**Burn the Harmful Comics!** German-American psychiatrist Fredric Wertham, in 1954, published 'Seduction of the Innocent' &... blog.naver.com](http://blog.naver.com/enterani/220753694367)

One of the things I often argued with my mother about when I was young was, **"It's much better than watching those trashy morning dramas full of obvious plots!"** Here, the aforementioned framing problem arises: the target age group of the content and the nature of the content itself. My mother prevented me from watching those comics because she demoted that cultural content to pornography, and I, in turn, demoted the morning dramas my mother watched to pornography. Perhaps, this kind of conflict hasn't changed, whether in the past or now. This conflict seems to have given me a clearer view of the issues at hand. This controversy is structured as a 2x2 matrix. titleEn: Gapyeong Onar Pool Villa: Close, Relaxing Modernity
contentEn:
The weather is gloomy this weekend. On Friday, I got drenched on my way home from work due to a massive downpour. It seems like the monsoon season has officially begun. Once the monsoon ends, the scorching heat will return, and it will be time to plan your summer vacation. I went on a trip to nearby Gapyeong last week, on June 26th.

{{IMG:1}}{{IMG:2}}{{IMG:3}}{{IMG:4}}{{IMG:5}}{{IMG:6}}{{IMG:7}}{{IMG:8}}{{IMG:9}}{{IMG:10}}{{IMG:11}}{{IMG:12}}{{IMG:13}}{{IMG:14}}{{IMG:15}}{{IMG:16}}{{IMG:17}}50m{{IMG:18}}{{IMG:19}}{{IMG:20}}© NAVER Corp.[More](https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=223834004873&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#)[/OpenStreetMap](http://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright)
