titleEn: Google Has Arrived as the Ultimate Photo Organizer
contentEn:
There was talk that Google I/O was unremarkable, but I recently heard amazing news from Google. The fact that Google's photo storage service has become free. In fact, I recently compared cloud storage capacities, and at the time, I chose Microsoft's OneDrive, which offers 1 terabyte of space along with Office 365. Besides that, Amazon was already offering near-free cloud space, but I didn't choose it because Amazon boasted terrible speeds in Korea.

**1. Why I chose Google Photos instead of OneDrive: Free and Fast!**
However, OneDrive has been uploading 450GB for two weeks now. The speed is truly terrible. But recently, Google introduced free photo storage. I tested it, and it boasts a much more comfortable speed than OneDrive. Of course, there's one limitation: it's restricted to 16-megapixel photos and Full HD videos. First, for Full HD, most smartphones and cameras have a maximum resolution around that level, so it won't be a big problem. However, a 16-megapixel camera is a resolution that applies to the latest smartphones, but it's a bit lacking for DSLR users or Galaxy Zoom 2 users like me. Still, if you think about it, once you reach around 16 megapixels, other factors become more important than pixels, so I think it's pretty decent.

**2. Smartphone Settings: Photos taken go straight to the cloud.**
You can download the app below.

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.photos
                                [**Photos - Android Apps on Google Play** play.google.com](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.photos)

If your family wants to use the same photo space, you can create a separate Google ID. On my wife's smartphone, only the Google Photos app is logged in with my ID. However, you need to be careful here: if two accounts are set up on an Android smartphone, a disaster can occur where all schedules and phone numbers download and get mixed up, so please turn off all synchronization when initially setting up the secondary account. Synchronization is set by default to only occur when using Wi-Fi, and if you set it to high quality, it seems to automatically resize and upload based on 16 megapixels.

**3. Let's upload photos from PC too.**
I uploaded the entire photo folder that was being synced to OneDrive.
Download the desktop uploader from the link below.

https://photos.google.com/apps
                                [**Sign in - Google Accounts** photos.google.com](https://photos.google.com/apps)

When you log in with your Google account, a pop-up like the one below appears.

{{IMG:1}}

By default, all images and videos from 'My Pictures', 'Desktop', and 'Memory' are uploaded. If you're sharing with family, make sure there's no adult content. Select the photo drive to back up on your PC via 'Add'. The quality is high quality. (This will be based on 16 megapixels.) Let's turn off statistics... though Google might not like it.. Then, if you start backup, it will automatically... upload continuously.

**4. Web and App Freedom, and Automatic Photo and Video Editing.**
As expected from a web company, it's also available via the web.

https://photos.google.com/
                                [**Sign in - Google Accounts** photos.google.com](https://photos.google.com/)

As you upload, you'll encounter amazing features. While typical photo apps offer powerful photo editing tools and filters, Google's features actually edit them and present them to the user, asking 'How about this?' With Google Stories and Google Assistant, you can freely access them across web and app, PC and mobile.

**1) Google Stories: Automatically creates travel stories as pages**
Google Stories automatically creates stories based on the location information in your photos. And you can share them on social networks. I just uploaded photos, and this appeared.

https://photos.google.com/share/AF1QipOEEoYv-g-5gxwpEe4tcvKW0e-QLvzbH-7n4l9a04sthvgM8PH198Hc28MuduZbeA/story/AF1QipMedRUwqoGUpNRGMaJlGXrii7ovEkJ4rt6lEiA6DziTmk5EvZB-7Wz72Sr5ZObR5Q?key=NkdWdU55UXdDVzd3X1B2OUZhQnRKLW1UZ2o3U3FR
                                [**Sunday in Yongin-si** July 13, 2014 (Sun) • 10 activities photos.google.com](https://photos.google.com/share/AF1QipOEEoYv-g-5gxwpEe4tcvKW0e-QLvzbH-7n4l9a04sthvgM8PH198Hc28MuduZbeA/story/AF1QipMedRUwqoGUpNRGMaJlGXrii7ovEkJ4rt6lEiA6DziTmk5EvZB-7Wz72Sr5ZObR5Q?key=NkdWdU55UXdDVzd3X1B2OUZhQnRKLW1UZ2o3U3FR)

They say if you turn on location tags when traveling, these will automatically be created one by one.

{{IMG:2}}
                                

https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=223833996641&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

You can directly upload these to KakaoStory or Facebook.

2) Assistant: Automatically edits and presents photos and videos
The Assistant automatically edits uploaded photos and videos, re-editing them into cool videos or other photos. Again, I didn't do anything for the video below. Google edited it on its own.

https://photos.google.com/share/AF1QipP3SDGWz9Tybmip_-j5wM2vSJap6CFsx71rMOpXXG0g1uWobT4tGFv4wycwZa_Gyg?key=UjR0LU1OdHVieU04N2d4NXQwdFdfTmFHTXBfczRn
                                [**Photos by Byoung Seok Yang** photos.google.com](https://photos.google.com/share/AF1QipP3SDGWz9Tybmip_-j5wM2vSJap6CFsx71rMOpXXG0g1uWobT4tGFv4wycwZa_Gyg?key=UjR0LU1OdHVieU04N2d4NXQwdFdfTmFHTXBfczRn)

Even animated GIFs (짤방) like this are automatic... OMG

https://photos.google.com/share/AF1QipOB6h3Cu3zIKuK04v2mQ4hy2DJ_ocrRxAkLNecv6Y572Xj17j4bXTnla4ZHtbBG5g?key=djhramN6WnB0NlRkclU4VEdBVUFldElkZ2FZUnhR
                                [**Photos by Byoung Seok Yang** photos.google.com](https://photos.google.com/share/AF1QipOB6h3Cu3zIKuK04v2mQ4hy2DJ_ocrRxAkLNecv6Y572Xj17j4bXTnla4ZHtbBG5g?key=djhramN6WnB0NlRkclU4VEdBVUFldElkZ2FZUnhR)

3) Automatic Photo Classification

{{IMG:3}}

It automatically classifies photos. Deep learning technology for photo classification seems to already be integrated (which is why some misidentifications are visible). While previous services that offered cloud and free photo storage merely emphasized cloud space, Google seems to have created the ultimate solution in the photo field, offering seamless integration between mobile and PC, easy photo management, and even automation technology for photo sharing. Actually, the Google Stories feature is said to have been around for quite some time, but as word-of-mouth about the free photo space spreads, this excellent technology seems to be gaining attention once again.

**4. Crisis for Domestic Photo Services**
N Drive began charging for storage, while Daum Cloud shut down its cloud business. The situation is evolving into a battle that demands powerful infrastructure and high technological expertise. Personal photo services are very important. Images contain more information than text, and by interpreting them, much more can be done. I believe Google's attack on the Korean home market has begun. First, the most nervous will likely be direct competitors like N Drive and indirect competitors like KakaoStory. After shutting down Daum Cloud, how will Kakao defend KakaoStory? Kakao Album seems to be already in a somewhat bad state, so it would be difficult to compete with that. I have a slight feeling that it's highly likely to go towards an integrated service of KakaoStory and Kakao Album, and in Naver's case, while they are aggressively starting with Pola, it won't be easy given the sluggish social graph. So, will they adopt an unlimited photo policy like Google? I think we'll have to wait and see. Anyway... I think this is a moment when Google, having laid the groundwork with Android, is trying to reap the harvest. I plan to write an additional post on this separately.

titleEn: [GoGoGo] Webtoon President Ha Il-kwon Returns with New Effects
contentEn:
**1. Webtoon President Ha Il-kwon is Back**
Today, a new work by author Ha Il-kwon was released.

[**Go Go Go** Worries of living with a grandfather with dementia and a game-addict father<br comic.naver.com](http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/list.nhn?titleId=655277)

Author Ha Il-kwon, whom you can always trust to deliver, is perhaps best described as the "Webtoon President," as expressed in the top comments. Author Ha Il-kwon not only best understands and utilizes the characteristics of webtoons but is also one of the best authors already recognized for his artistic merit.

**2. A Webtoon with GIFs? No. An Advanced Smarttoon**

[**GIF - Enha Wiki Mirror** mirror.enha.kr](https://mirror.enha.kr/wiki/%EC%9B%80%EC%A7%A4)

I scrolled down a bit, noticed something unusual, and scrolled back up. It was an effect that moved dynamically with the scroll. As you scroll, new layers appear, layers move at different speeds based on perspective, and on mobile, certain actions trigger vibrations. Comments were calling it a webtoon with GIFs. However, as someone with a developer background, I quickly realized these technologies were based on web technologies. The appropriate meeting of technology and content is probably what this is all about. In fact, previous Smarttoons had a few issues. The user experience was too different from scroll-based PC webtoons, requiring two rounds of editing, and the effects were limited, leading to requests for more features. Also, users felt the panels were excessively narrow. In Rangtto's "SM Player," characters even complained about the narrow panels because it was a Smarttoon. This "GIF webtoon"? Smarttoon 2? Or just Webtoon 2? I'm not sure what to call it, but the information released to the press only mentions "Webtoon Effect Editor" provision, so there doesn't seem to be a separate brand. For convenience, I'll call it Smarttoon 2. The advantage of Smarttoon 2 is that it's a scroll-based webtoon where PC and mobile environments are not separately divided. Therefore, it has the advantage of maximizing effects with just a slight addition of effects to existing scroll webtoons. Technically, it involves separating the movement speed or effects of multiple layers based on scroll position, a technology previously seen on web event pages.

**3. A Typical Platform Evolving with Third Parties: Naver Webtoon**
According to the article, this feature was created in consultation with the authors.

[**Sports Chosun :: Naver Provides 'Webtoon Effect Editor' to Help Webtoon Authors with Direction** sports.chosun.com](http://sports.chosun.com/news/utype.htm?id=201505270100308860022006&ServiceDate=20150527)

This means content was considered from the planning stage. A significant number of ideas from author H, famous for surprising people every summer, are said to be included in this work. Author H actually has experience at a game development company and is capable of coding himself, making him knowledgeable in technology. When I think of a popular role model for why one should receive software education, I think of author H. In any case, the development of a platform and its competitiveness are determined by how closely it collaborates with the third parties operating on it to create rules (policies) and forms (platforms/services). The fact that this close collaboration model is working well suggests that Naver Webtoon's competitiveness will be sustained.

**4. Is This the Mobile Content Pikicast and Naver Post Were Looking For?**
In fact, Naver seems to have been deeply contemplating the answer to mobile content for a long time. Naver Post was one attempt, but what I've felt recently is that Pikicast offered the closest solution: flipping content suitable for mobile, pages with simple repetitive animations, and a social-based dissemination model. It was content typically optimized for mobile, and indeed, it's the most widely distributed content on Facebook. However, recently, changes are visible in Naver Webtoon. The sharing of content to social networks, previously restricted due to copyright issues, has been eased, allowing active sharing of panels to social networks. And this webtoon with applied effects has provided an appropriate and powerful solution for scrolling and mobile. It even made me wonder if this wasn't the answer Naver Post was looking for, rather than just a webtoon. Naver Webtoon is said to be operating independently as a CIC (Company-in-Company). I understand they are currently striving for global reach alongside Lezhin Comics, and I wish for the day Naver Webtoon's status catches up with Marvel worldwide.

titleEn: Buy 1TB Cloud, Get Office & Tablet Free
contentEn:
My wife and I use the Galaxy Zoom 2. While it's ridiculously thick compared to a regular smartphone, its photo quality is excellent, and since it's lighter than a mirrorless camera, we hardly use our Nex-5. As recent phones like the Galaxy S6 and G4 also highlight photography as a strength, the desire for high-quality photos taken with smartphones is increasing. And as we take more photos, photo storage has also become a very big issue. If you have a child like me, the value of photos is immense. Hard drives can fail at any time. Some people store them on portable external hard drives, but for children's photos, I strongly advise against it due to stability issues. For this reason, I was using a NAS with two hard drives that supported dual backup. However, it was an old NAS, so the speed was frustrating, and since I used it at home, I couldn't always leave it on. To view old photos again, I had to turn on the NAS. Also, viewing them on a smartphone wasn't very smooth. So, while considering cloud services as the best alternative, I'd like to share the know-how behind my choice.

**1. Cloud Comparison**
First, let me tell you my choice: I chose OneDrive. Previously, I was using NDrive for automatic smartphone backups. When considering moving my NAS to the cloud, the first thing that caught my eye was NDrive, which offered 1TB for 100,000 won, the lowest price. NDrive offers 1TB at the lowest price, and its mobile app is also very well-made. It even shows subtitles for videos uploaded to the cloud, making it optimal for the Korean market.

| NDrive | Dropbox | Google Drive | OneDrive | iCloud | col6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free Storage | 30GB | 15GB | 15GB | 15GB | 5GB |
| 100GB/year | 50,000 won | - | 27,000 won | 33,000 won | - |
| 1TB/year | 100,000 won | 120$ (approx. 130,000 won) | 120$ (approx. 130,000 won) | 108,000 won (Office 365 included) | 240$ (264,000 won) |
| Special Features | **Good speed/app, default online mode, convenient for devices with low storage** | 50GB free for Galaxy users | Unlimited photos up to 2048x2048 | 1TB free for Office 365 users | Long live iPhone |

However, the decisive reason I chose OneDrive was the 1TB free for Office 365 users. Upon checking, it turned out I was already an Office 365 user. I had written a post about it before, but the x98 3g air Windows tablet includes a 1-year Office 365 subscription.

**2. Should I buy a tablet just for 1TB of cloud storage?**
If you need 1TB of cloud storage, I highly recommend buying a Windows tablet. Really cheap tablets are under 100,000 won, so instead of buying 1TB of OneDrive, you can just buy a tablet. Based on Danawa, you can purchase Windows tablets at the following price points:

| Price | Display | Memory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Under 100,000 won | 8-inch (1280x800) | 16G |
| Under 200,000 won | 9-inch (1920x1200) | 32G |
| Under 300,000 won | 10-inch (2045x1536) | 64G |

If you subtract the price of OneDrive, the 8-inch model can be considered free, essentially making it a Windows tablet subsidy. It's clear that MS is very aggressive with tablets.
[윈도우OS 가격비교리스트 :: 행복쇼핑의 시작 ! 다나와 (가격비교) - Danawa.comgoo.gl](http://goo.gl/XEPK3d){{IMG:1}}

**3. OneDrive Tips and Disappointments**
**1) Convenient to manage on a PC with equivalent storage to OneDrive**
For usability, it's convenient to have a hard drive with the same capacity. If you set it up on that disk for Windows and edit files, they will automatically sync to OneDrive. I also first moved my NAS data to my PC. This way, you can manage it quickly from your local PC. If your laptop has insufficient storage, you'll have to use it as online-only. This is a bit inconvenient, more than you'd think.

**2) Disappointing Mobile App**
The OneDrive mobile app has the disadvantage that viewing photos is not as convenient compared to Dropbox or NDrive. It was a bit inconvenient that it doesn't automatically group and display photos by date. Moreover, after uploading 450GB from my NAS all at once, viewing by chronological order became meaningless. At least the NAS was managed by folders, so that was okay. MS has become very progressive since the CEO change, and I hope the Android app will be further improved.

**3) Disappointing Speed**
Until MS builds a cloud center in Korea, it will likely be slower than NDrive.

**4. Conclusion: MS seems to be a price bully.**
If you purchase 1TB of OneDrive for a year, you get an 8-inch tablet for free. It seems impossible to escape MS.

**P.S. Adding one more important piece of information that I missed.**
**In Amazon's case, they offer unlimited storage.** Unlimited photos and 5GB of video for 12$ (13,000 won) per year, **unlimited storage is offered for 60$ (approx. 66,000 won).** The app is decent, but there seem to be some speed issues, perhaps due to the physical location of the cloud center. Now that gigabit internet is being installed here... I understand why MS and Amazon want to build cloud centers in Korea... I'll have to do a speed comparison when I have time.

titleEn: A Deeper Look at Naver'
contentEn:
전문가들은 검색시 네이버를 잘 안씁니다. 그도 그럴것이 고급 지식을 요구하는 검색어는 정답이 최 상위로 노출되기보다는 사용자들이 생산하는 수많은 콘텐츠에 묻혀서 잘 노출되지 않았기 때문이죠. 이에반해 구글은 딱 원하는 것을 바로바로 잘 찾아주어 선호되었습니다. 해당 부분은 어쩔수 없는 기술력의 차이로 지적 받곤 했죠.
 
그런데, 금일 검색을 하다가... 간만에 네이버의 검색 기술에 대한 칭찬을 한번 해볼까 합니다. 제가 검색을 주제로 네이버를 칭찬하기는 처음인것 같아요. 기술이 없는건 아니었고, 사실 국내 최고의 기술을 가졌던 것은 분명하지만, 구글 대비... 라고 하면 꼬리를 내릴 수 밖에 없었거든요.

**1. 제가 놀란건 "더 알아보는... " 영역입니다.**
{{IMG:1}}사실 네이버는 검색결과를 편집합니다. 특히 중요하다고 생각하거나 자주 사용자들이 찾는 검색 결과는 더 예쁘고, 필요한 지식들을 찾아서 편집하죠. '핀테크'에 대한 정답형 지식 뿐만 아니라, '핀테크'와 연관된 지식 정보들이나 CP들이 공급하는 고급 콘텐츠인 메거진이 같이 노출되고 있습니다. 이 점은 '핀테크'에 기대했던 정답형 검색 결과와 흡사할 뿐 만 아니라 더 깊이있는 내용을 전달하고 있습니다.

자주 비교되는 구글 결과입니다.{{IMG:2}}많이 차이나네요. 이미지가 상위로 올라온 건 아무래도, 핀테크관련된 ppt를 만들때 구글 이미지 검색을 통해 자료를 찾는 사용자가 많지 않기 때문일까? 하는 생각이 살짝 듭니다. 모든 검색결과의 순서에는 이유가 있습니다.

모든 검색어에 "더 알아보는..." 이 있는건 아닌것 같습니다.
{{IMG:3}}

{{IMG:4}}

더 알아보는 지식백과와 더 알아보는 매거진에 대해 부정적으로 생각하시는 분들도 있을 수 있습니다.
**지식백과와 매거진은 네이버에서 직접 확보한 고급 콘텐츠, 곧 콘테츠팜임은 분명합니다.**하지만, 검색어를 입력시, 검색어가 포함되지 않은 연관된 지식 결과까지 함께 보여주고 있습니다.이는 지식을 태그등을 기반으로 연관도에 대한 높은 학습 결과가 아닐까 하는 생각이 듭니다.{{IMG:5}}
 외부의 개방된 웹환경을 검색하는 능력을 고도화 하기 보다는 내부의 콘텐츠를 고도화했다는 비난을 들을 수 있는 부분도 있으나, 네이버가 가지고 있는 막강한 콘텐츠들이 지식을 기반으로 유기적인 검색을 하고 있음에 대해서는 높이 평가할 부분이라고 봅니다.
 또한 최근 네이버 포스트나 폴라등을 보면, 정제된 고급 사용자 콘텐츠의 확보에 열을 올리고 있음에는 분명합니다. **더 알아보는 매거진 역시, 네이버와 계약된 CP들의 콘텐츠로 검색결과가 임의로 편집되는 것은 아닌것 같습니다. 국내의 좁은 콘텐츠 풀의 특성이 이러한 형태로 네이버의 진화를 이끌어내고 있지 않은가 하는 생각이 듭니다.**
그리고, 추가적으로 우측 상단에는 **"원본반영"이라는 버튼이 추가 되었는데, 네이버 내부에서는 원래 "저품질 신고"라는 버튼이 있었습니다. **직원들이 보기에 검색결과가 안좋으면 이를 검토해서 서비스를 더 좋은 방향으로 바꿀수 있도록 하기 위함이었죠. 이를 전 사용자에게 확대함으로서 검색품질을 높이기 위한 욕구의 표출로 보입니다.
 최근 모바일의 환경을 보면, 콘텐츠 팜의 효과가 더더욱 두드러지고 있는 상황이기에 네이버의 전략은 어느정도 유효한 것 같습니다. 언젠가는 해외에서도 당당히 겨룰 수 있는 구글 수준의 검색을 만들어냈으면 합니다.

Experts don't often use Naver for search. That's because search queries requiring advanced knowledge often didn't show the correct answer at the top, but rather got buried among the vast amount of user-generated content. In contrast, Google was preferred because it quickly and accurately found exactly what users wanted. This aspect was often pointed out as an unavoidable difference in technological capability.

However, while searching today... I'd like to praise Naver's search technology for the first time in a while. I think this is the first time I've praised Naver on the topic of search. It's not that they lacked technology; in fact, they clearly had the best technology in Korea, but when compared to Google... they had no choice but to back down.

**1. What surprised me was the "Learn More..." section.**
{{IMG:1}}In fact, Naver edits search results. Especially for results deemed important or frequently sought by users, they are presented more attractively, with necessary knowledge curated and edited. Not only answer-type knowledge about 'fintech,' but also related knowledge information and high-quality content like magazines supplied by CPs are being displayed together. This aspect is not only similar to the answer-type search results expected for 'fintech' but also delivers more in-depth content.

Here are the frequently compared Google results.{{IMG:2}}There's a big difference. I have a slight thought that perhaps images appear higher because not many users search for materials via Google Image Search when creating fintech-related PPTs. There's a reason behind the order of all search results.

It seems that "Learn More..." isn't available for all search queries.
{{IMG:3}}

{{IMG:4}}

There might be people who have negative thoughts about "Learn More Encyclopedia" and "Learn More Magazine."
**The Encyclopedia and Magazine sections are clearly high-quality content directly secured by Naver, essentially content farms.** However, when a search term is entered, it also displays related knowledge results that do not contain the exact search term. I suspect this is the result of advanced learning regarding relevance based on tags and other factors.{{IMG:5}}
While there might be criticism that Naver has prioritized enhancing its internal content rather than refining its ability to search the external open web, I believe it's highly commendable that Naver's powerful content is enabling organic search based on knowledge.
Furthermore, looking at recent Naver Post and Pholar, it's clear that they are actively working to secure refined, high-quality user content. **The "Learn More Magazine" also seems to consist of content from CPs contracted with Naver, and the search results do not appear to be arbitrarily edited. I suspect that the characteristics of Korea's relatively narrow content pool are driving Naver's evolution in this direction.**
Additionally, a "**Reflect Original**" button has been added to the top right. Internally at Naver, there was originally a "**Report Low Quality**" button. This was to allow employees to review poor search results and change the service for the better. Extending this to all users appears to be an expression of the desire to improve search quality.
Considering the recent mobile environment, where the effect of content farms is becoming even more prominent, Naver's strategy seems somewhat effective. I hope that someday, Naver will create a Google-level search engine that can confidently compete internationally.

titleEn: Remembering the Sewol Ferry Disaster, One Year On
contentEn:
Lest we forget, I felt I had to leave something behind...
I am sorry, and I am grateful. I am sorry for the many unfinished tasks due to foolish adults, and I am grateful to the children who, through their great sacrifice, helped us discover this challenge before an even greater disaster befell us.

Over the past year, adults seem to have been foolish. It seems we wasted time only on finding who was at fault and defending ourselves.

This is my personal opinion, but I don't trust people. A man-made disaster caused by a person is not the fault of that person, but rather a systemic disaster. I was taught that errors caused by entering special characters into an input box should be filtered out at the input stage.

However, in many parts of Korea, it's still common to simply write "Entering special characters here will result in a fine" in a corner, and then try to punish those who don't comply.

I wish we would change our perspective a little. If a problem isn't being solved, or if it's being hidden, we should first examine the system to understand how it's possible to hide it.

There was an announcement about a big data society. In a society like this, the term 'big data society' is still far off. We need to re-evaluate what data we need and whether we can accumulate reliable data without embellishment. A society overflowing with noisy data is not a big data society. As of April 16, 2015, one year later, I wonder what has been accumulated over the past year. We can only make judgments after removing and replacing someone from their position and then creating reliable data. We are a democratic society. We must act according to procedures, and it only functions when we build social trust capital. We need to re-examine whether we are accumulating the basic data necessary to build that trust capital.

If not, the feeling of sorrow for those precious children will likely never fade.

titleEn: Why Gear VR Is Worse Than Oculus
contentEn:
Searching for Gear VR, I found a truly absurd article and would like to share it. It's an article comparing Gear VR and Oculus. Since the content is very wrong, I'd like to first meticulously debunk those parts, and then explain the relationship between Gear VR and Oculus.
http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=092&aid=0002070154&sid1=001[[Five Reasons Why Gear VR is Better Than Oculus RiftQHD-class ultra-high resolution screen… providing better realism (ZDNet Korea = Reporter Bong Seong-chang) For those whose job is to experience new IT devices every day, IT devices alone...news.naver.com](http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&oid=092&aid=0002070154&sid1=001)
{{IMG:1}}
The gist of it is the nonsense claim that Gear VR is hardware-superior to Oculus. I will explain it properly.
■ **QHD-class ultra-high resolution screen… providing better realism**
"The display resolution used in DK2 is 1920×1080 pixels, which is Full HD. On the other hand, the resolution of the Galaxy Note 4, which acts as the display for Gear VR, is QHD-class at 2560×1440 pixels, making it more detailed. In other words, Gear VR is much more advantageous in terms of realism."
However, **DK2's display is 960x1080 per eye**. Where did they get 1920x1080 from? The Galaxy Note 4's **resolution is halved when it goes into Gear VR, making it 1280x1440**. Of course, that's slightly higher than DK2. Are they saying they used a Note 3 display in terms of specs? 960x1080?? **(Further correction: I've confirmed that the entire panel is used. Not the whole device, but just the panel. Since it's half of 1920x1080, 960x1080 is correct. I miscalculated. The reason for using the same panel is presumed to be due to the cost of AMOLED panels. I thought using individual displays would be cheaper and more efficient, but it seems they used the Note 4 as is due to mass production and HDMI. In the end, Cardboard, VR, and DK2 all use the same single panel with just a divider.)**
■ **20ms lower latency… no motion sickness felt**
???? I was breathless the moment I saw this. **DK2's latency is 2ms, 3ms**. It supports 60, 72, 75 Hz. At 20ms, you can't even see properly. "Experts believe that if screen latency drops below 20ms, most people will not experience motion sickness." Which experts did you ask? **LCD response time is not that slow. It's around 2ms, similar to AMOLED.**
**Addition (2015.04.06): It has been confirmed as a fact that Gear VR is faster with a latency of 20ms.** What confused me in the article was that it stated "minimum latency due to AMOLED," making me think the latency referred to display latency. However, the latency mentioned here refers to the total latency from when motion occurs until it is reflected on the screen, which has nothing to do with the screen itself. Therefore, **while DK2 is superior in rendering speed, it has been confirmed that the total time, including the time for the screen to be transmitted via HDMI to the head-mounted display (Screen Latency = Motion Input Time + Rendering Time + HDMI Transmission Time + VSync Wait Time), results in a time of 20ms or more.** However, the claim that AMOLED provides an advantage, as stated in the article, is false. **Among the tens of milliseconds of latency, the effect of AMOLED, even at best, shows a difference of less than 1ms in screen display time.**
■ **Wireless freedom… enjoy VR anytime, anywhere**
This part is correct. This technology, called Gear VR or mobile VR, allows you to freely view 360 degrees, and its advantage is being wireless. However, Oculus has a reason for giving up 360 degrees. It's motion recognition. **They said you don't get closer when you move your body, but Oculus does.** That's why a camera is attached to the PC, Oculus requires more performance, and the viewing angle is limited compared to VR. **It performs motion sensing like Kinect with the PC's camera. I can't understand how they wrote such an article without even trying it once.**

■ **Reasonable price for enjoying virtual reality**
They calculated DK2 at 388,000 won and VR at 220,000 won... but they missed the Note 4 price for VR. ㅡㅡ; If you're going by that, comparing it to a 20,000 won Cardboard would be more appropriate.

■ **The relationship between Oculus and Gear VR… Gear is actually not Samsung technology.**
And finally, it seems they think Gear VR and Oculus are made by different companies... Gear VR is more of an Oculus product than a Samsung one. The SDK is also distributed by Oculus.
https://developer.oculus.com/downloads/#sdk=mobile

{{IMG:2}}

http://ebay.auction.co.kr/promotion/naver/detail/301501582420

[[Overseas] NEW Samsung Gear VR Oculus Rift SM-R320 Innovator Edition Note 4 Headset...](http://ebay.auction.co.kr/promotion/naver/detail/301501582420)

Shopping Mall
eBay Shopping

[View Review](http://ebay.auction.co.kr/promotion/naver/detail/301501582420)

The relationship between Oculus and GearVR is similar to the relationship between Google, who made Android, and Samsung. They were never in competition to begin with, and most of the technology belongs to Oculus. If we're making such comparisons, we might as well try to make Note pen technology compete with Wacom. ㅡㅡ; (In the case of Note, it's Wacom technology.)
■ **Oculus vs GearVR Performance: PC vs Smartphone**
And, in terms of hardware performance, the Note 4 is a drop in the bucket. That's because DK2 uses a PC's graphics card for rendering. Comparing PC gaming graphics cards with smartphone graphics performance is an excessive joke.
Even if you want to write an advertisement article for Samsung... I hope you write it with proper knowledge. I recently bought a Cardboard and have been enjoying it; it's quite good. I recommend trying Cardboard rather than GearVR. In fact, there isn't a huge difference between Cardboard and VR. Also, it seems there isn't enough content yet to warrant buying and enjoying GearVR.
**ps. Comments are taking up time without much constructive progress, so I'm closing them. Let me say a few things I want to convey.**
**1. This blog also aims to learn through communication.**
 - Therefore, providing data or new facts is very welcome.
 - I do not delete my mistakes; I add to them and correct them. The reason for writing this blog was to criticize an article written by a reporter in a very confusing manner. Thanks to that, I also experienced confusion and misunderstanding, but a well-known developer corrected me. It was a good learning experience.
**2. This is not a consumer-oriented blog.**
 - This blog is for developers or IT professionals.
 - 'Wow, it's really good. It was an exciting experience.' For such emotional opinions, you might want to look for other review blogs. I am not a professional review blogger. That's why I don't take many photos. The income I earn from this blog comes from manuscript requests and consulting as an expert for IT professional organizations, not product reviews.
 - As a consumer who likes specific products, there are sometimes parts that might be annoying, leading to occasional unproductive debates, but I haven't particularly changed my mind, and my predictions have often turned out to be correct.
 ex) I wrote about the limitations of the Vega Iron strategy and was heavily criticized by Vega fans, but Pantech eventually went under. When the iPhone 3GS came out, I argued that Android would rise during the Cupcake era and was criticized by colleagues at work, but my prediction turned out to be correct. I predicted that Windows would become free and was heavily criticized, but it eventually became free. Consumer perspectives and market situations are different, and it's necessary to view them broadly. Currently, VR is at this point. Samsung isn't unaware of this. I believe there are many smart people there working hard. If you're curious about my predictions for Samsung Electronics' future, please check the link below. My prediction is that the Galaxy S6 will not be Samsung's savior, regardless of sales volume.
http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220288518629[Will the Galaxy S6 Edge be Samsung's Savior?Since Samsung's Galaxy S3, no major model has captured my interest. I didn't feel much difference between the S4 and S5. Rather, abnormal models like the Zoom 2...blog.naver.com](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220288518629)
Of course, I have been wrong before. I predicted the domestic failure of the iPhone 3GS, but KT was an unexpected variable... Predictions are made based on past experience and data, with added intuition. Therefore, if facts deviate from that, I can be wrong.
**3. As a consumer, I strictly maintain the characteristic of being a consumer from a developer's perspective.**
 - While the purpose is learning, there are also evaluations based on personal opinions.
 - Therefore, the aspects I value are different. My perspective is more supplier- and developer-centric than consumer-centric. Or, I maintain the perspective of a consumer as a developer (technician). If my perspective were the same as the general public, I believe there would be no reason to maintain my blog amidst the countless others. I have no desire to earn money from blogging, nor do I have the time for it.
ps. If you have any additional opinions, need to correct a fact, or have more news to share, please send an email or a direct message. I have separate plans to write a post about VR strategy later. Thank you.
**ps2. 2015-06-24 Today, I finally got to experience GearVR and am leaving an additional note. I tried to find places to experience it, but it wasn't available at supermarkets, so I tried it at Gangnam d'light. (The Samsung section staff at supermarkets didn't even know it existed.)**** The conclusion is the same as Cardboard. The only good thing was the ability to manually adjust focus. I expected the resolution to be better, but I was quite disappointed. It didn't have the same impact as when I used Oculus. ****If you want the convenience of GearVR, I recommend purchasing FENGJING.**

titleEn: Little Person: Owner's Dot Doodle / Original Creation
contentEn:
**
****A Small Person****
**{{IMG:1}}
2002. 05. 15
There once lived a very small person. He had been small since childhood. He looked at tall people and wished he could grow as tall as them.**
**by Forest Child

**2015. 03. 27**
The theme of 'a small child' is something I've often used in my writing and drawings since I was young.
Perhaps because I was on the shorter side, I often envied the world of tall people and felt insignificant.
Whether it was about my heart or my height. Because of this, I often felt very impatient or had an inferiority complex. Even now, I don't consider myself tall. I'm already past my mid-thirties, I know more, and I've become a little more composed about many things in the world, but I still don't feel like I've grown much from my middle and high school days, when I used to commute on tiptoes among tall people on the bus. I still envy people with big hearts that aren't swayed by the wind.
However, while reading a children's storybook to my child, an ant said to a mouse who envied larger animals, "I'm so jealous of how big you are!" It's a simple lesson even children learn, but it seems our hearts don't quite grasp it. That's probably why everyone constantly harbors desires.
But, perhaps because they resemble my wife and me, our children are also on the smaller side, and I hope they don't inherit our height. Is this also a desire?

titleEn: Legendary Pink Elephant
contentEn:
**The Legendary Pink Elephant**

{{IMG:1}}

2002. 05. 03
During WWII, the US requested India to dispatch troops.
So, India dispatched the legendary pink elephant.
Just imagine it.
An elephant wearing a turban, gracefully evading anti-aircraft fire, showering Hitler's head with watermelon seeds.
However, unfortunately, that elephant didn't last long.
Every time it achieved a feat, it was awarded a medal, and on the day it received its 1000th medal, it was hit by German anti-aircraft guns due to the heavy weight of the medals.
Nevertheless, that elephant had historical value.
It's just that it wasn't human, so it wasn't recorded.

by Forest Child

**2015. 03. 25**

Today, my wife went out in the evening, so I had to put the children to bed.

My second son looked for his mom while falling asleep, so I spontaneously made up a story for him.
It was a story about Cocomong from the Refrigerator Kingdom crash-landing in Broom's Town on Robocong, and how the rescue team, including Poli, together defeated Virus King's giant robot.
Since it was a story I made up on the spot for my child, I guess the advantage is that I don't have to worry about copyright.

However, far from falling asleep, my son kept making "whoosh, bang" sounds, so I had to hold him to sleep.

contentEn:
**1. Remember Lineable, the $5 Innovation?** I once introduced Lineable, a $5 anti-missing child bracelet. It was a wearable device that used beacons to track children's locations together. What made it particularly innovative was the idea of protecting children collectively. At the time, it was crowdfunding on Indiegogo, far surpassing its initial goal of $30,000, reaching $40,000, spreading through social networks over 3,500 times, being featured on TechCrunch on September 24th, and winning first place at D.camp's D.day on September 26th. Many people left comments on my blog, and many were curious about where and when to buy it. It seems all parents share the same sentiment.

**2. Finally, Concrete News About Lineable Has Arrived.** So, here's an update. Detailed purchase information for Lineable has been released. **1) Sizes and Colors** Sizes are available in S, M, and L for ages 3 to 12, and a variety of color options are now available. {{IMG:1}} **2) One Heart Package with Customizable Logos and Text** The One Heart Package (250,000 KRW) for 50 units, likely for use in daycare centers or schools, allows for customizable text and logos. {{IMG:2}}

**3) Schedule** The app is scheduled for release in February, and products will be shipped sequentially starting March 15th.
**4) Price** The Korean price is 5,000 KRW, with a separate shipping fee of 3,000 KRW.

**3. Where Can You Buy It? Pre-order Now for a Heartwarming 1+1 Deal** Protect your child, and give one more to a child in need. {{IMG:3}} And there's more. Following its Indiegogo campaign abroad, Lineable is now crowdfunding in Korea through Wadiz. Crowdfunding might sound complicated, but you can simply think of it as similar to a pre-order. A slight difference is that if the goal is not met, the project is canceled and refunds are issued; if it is met, the product is manufactured and delivered to customers. The target amount is 20 million KRW, with a deadline of January 31st, and 20% has already been achieved. At this rate, it seems likely to reach 20 million KRW without difficulty by January 31st. The reason for this crowdfunding isn't solely to raise funds for product manufacturing. For every one purchased, one will be donated to children at a special education school for the disabled. If you're planning to buy anyway, why not participate in this project a little earlier? Not only can you get Lineable the fastest, but you can also help children with disabilities. This project began because of an email from a female student majoring in special education in Chungnam. Children with disabilities are more likely to go missing during outdoor events, and the risks are greater. Earlier this year in Changwon, a child with disabilities was found dead 15 days after going missing, and it was pointed out that the accident was due to inadequate initial response. What if a product like this had existed then? This project started before the product was even released, thanks to the beautiful letter from the student expressing this wish. Heo5pa6, the author of Naver Webtoon's "What If?", also showed this wish in a short webtoon. {{IMG:4}} [http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/detail.nhn?titleId=631780&no=38](http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/detail.nhn?titleId=631780&no=38) In Hwang Jun-ho's original work, the child does not have a location tracker and suffers a terrible death. In reality, from the disappearance of the Frog Boys to countless large and small missing person cases around us, I myself experienced being lost as a child when I visited my maternal grandparents' house. Fortunately, I was found within 3 hours. My five-year-old daughter still cries loudly in shock if Mom or Dad disappears from her sight for a moment, and I rush to hug her when I hear her.

**4. Participate or Purchase Now.** Don't you want to make a world where we protect our children together a reality? So, [click the image below!](http://www.wadiz.kr/Campaign/Details/552) [http://www.wadiz.kr/Campaign/Details/552](http://www.wadiz.kr/Campaign/Details/552) {{IMG:5}}

titleEn: [iPhone 6 vs Galaxy Note
contentEn:
**1. Is this news of Apple's new product launch? Or Samsung's advertisement?**
As always, whenever Apple releases a new product, the media eagerly compares it to Samsung's new products. But what's interesting is that Apple's domestic market share is already below 10%. Did the media cover LG's new product launch, which has a higher market share, as much as this? Seeing this, it makes me wonder if the media is using Apple's new product launch as an excuse to advertise for Samsung. That's because, in fact, I understand that Samsung hasn't seen much success since the Galaxy S3 and Note 2. Recently, an earnings shock has even led to rumors of a crisis for Samsung. In contrast, Apple's stock price remains strong. All in all, this means Samsung's situation is not good. Nevertheless, reading articles claiming that Apple abandoned Jobs and followed Samsung with the iPhone 6 Plus makes me feel quite pathetic in many ways. In fact, Jobs himself would overturn past judgments if he thought it was right depending on the situation, and under Tim Cook's leadership, many of Jobs' stubborn preferences have already been abandoned. Therefore, this controversy is now an old story. Instead, I suspect that even with a low domestic market share, they are trying to advertise the Galaxy Note 4 by borrowing the reputation of the iPhone, a symbol of innovation.

**2. Stop singing the praises of hardware innovation, and turn your attention to software where innovation is happening.**
​{{IMG:1}}​
[ Image Source: Lee Mal-nyeon's Journey to the West ]
[http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/list.nhn?titleId=602921&week=thu](http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/list.nhn?titleId=602921&week=thu)​​​
Xiaomi is often mentioned when discussing Samsung's earnings shock. The comparison between Apple and Samsung was similar, but software was always cited as Samsung's weakness. While this was well covered through cooperation with Google, as mobile competition shifts from OS to services, the importance of software in smartphones has grown even more. News from Silicon Valley is mostly filled with stories about software innovation. Of course, many companies in Korea are also making efforts, and sometimes they produce truly excellent results. In fact, Naver Line's success story is more noteworthy overseas than the Galaxy Note 4. Google isn't just updating Android. Instead, it's making many innovative attempts by updating many other software and services. Nevertheless, if you click on the IT section of Korean media, most of it is about smartphones, which are now a stale topic, and mobile carriers' LTE broadband. I haven't seen a single person around me say their phone is better because of broadband after LTE. The innovation consumers perceive has ended in telecommunications and hardware. What remains seems to be smartwatches, as part of IoT, but software will also determine that market. However, it seems both Apple and Samsung still need to be observed further. But the media is still only talking about hardware. I'm not interested. And if you try it yourself, you'll realize it's not important. Pebble didn't sell that much because its hardware was outstanding.

**3. The IT section should focus on reader value rather than advertiser value.**
I suspect this attitude is due to just one reason. That is, because mobile carriers and Samsung Electronics are advertisers. Isn't it time to stop dedicating the entire IT section as advertising space for advertisers? Even with the president talking about a software-centric society, reading articles that are essentially ad pages feels like a waste of time. Will we ever see articles that we can truly value? That value comes from expertise, not advertising.

titleEn: [Academic Discussion for the Electronic Document Industry] Current
contentEn:
Recently, the film "The Admiral: Roaring Currents" has brought renewed attention to our ancestors. (I haven't seen it yet, though.) Admiral Yi Sun-sin's leadership and our ancestors' remarkable scientific technologies led to victory in the Imjin War. I once watched the movie "Masquerade," which was said to be based on the lost 15 days of Gwanghae in the Joseon Dynasty Annals. In an era where everything is recorded, from the daily historical records of Joseon to the internet age, our ancestors left behind such a great legacy hundreds of years ago. From Jikji, the world's first movable metal type, to the Tripitaka Koreana and King Sejong's Hangeul, our ancestors' outstanding scientific technology for knowledge transfer might even be connected to South Korea's current status as a high-speed internet nation. Furthermore, an academic forum on the electronic document industry was held on July 24th to continue this legacy of our ancestors. You might feel it's an anticlimax to introduce a small event with such a grand explanation, but documents are the means by which we transmit all the knowledge we enjoy to future generations. It's just that this has now transitioned to the internet and computers. In that sense, the value of "electronic documents" can be discussed as having "historical" value beyond industrial value. Perhaps people living at the time Hangeul was created might have felt that this new technology called Hangeul was nothing special. However, the cultural benefits that "Hangeul" has brought us today are so immense that they are difficult to evaluate in monetary terms.

First, I was a bit late for the event. I don't know where my head is every day, but I misunderstood the venue and went to the wrong place. Thanks to that, I missed some of the initial parts of the event. Representatives from major companies such as Unidocs, Infraware, Handysoft, Hancom, and Microsoft gave presentations. Since you might not be familiar with the company names other than Hancom and Microsoft, I'll explain.

**1. Participating Company Introductions**

**1) Hancom - Korea's Original Word Processor**
First, Hancom was founded by CEO Lee Chan-jin, a first-generation venture entrepreneur. Although he is no longer the CEO, it is the company that established word processor independence in Korea, and it can be considered the standard word processor for government and schools today.

**2) Infraware - Global Mobile Word Processor Powerhouse, also supports Hangeul**
Second, Infraware is a powerhouse in Android-based mobile word processors with its Polaris product. It is installed on most smartphones and supports even Hancom's HWP format, as well as MS Office files, with excellent compatibility. The number of Polaris word processors installed worldwide is said to reach 600 million copies. Of course, 600 million copies include pre-loads on smartphones, not just active users.

**3) Handysoft - Groupware and Public SW Powerhouse**
Third, Handysoft, though not well-known to general users now, previously created a word processor called Arirang and, as a groupware powerhouse, developed groupware for many public projects. I remember the Ministry of National Defense's groupware being Handysoft's when I was in the military. Although it's a company that's somewhat struggling now due to the de facto standard of Hancom's HWP format and the free distribution of the Onnara System by the Ministry of Interior and Safety, it has traditionally been the strongest company in public software, and it excels at embedding Hangeul to create groupware and various public SW.

**4) Unidocs - Adobe should be grateful for PDF**
Fourth, Unidocs is a company that develops software using PDF. They developed PDF readers for old feature phones, which even Adobe hadn't attempted, as well as extended PDF formats and SW developed using PDF, possessing top-tier technical capabilities.

**5) Microsoft - Too famous to omit..**
With these five companies participating, it could be said that virtually all representative companies in the domestic electronic document market were present.

**2. Key Issues by Company**

**1) Leading Companies: Hancom / Microsoft - We are not exclusive.**
Hancom and Microsoft seemed to have similar positions. Hancom asserted that the HWP format has already been opened, and Microsoft stated that they are already doing well in openness by leading OXML. In fact, Microsoft's reason for openness was a passive response to criticism about its closed nature and to counter ODF, so the motivation might not seem entirely pure, but it is certainly much more open in XML format than Hancom.

**2) Infraware - Please open it properly.**
Infraware complained that the open specifications of Hancom's binary format do not keep up with the latest versions, making it difficult to utilize. Simply put, they acknowledged Hancom's efforts to open, but asked them to do it properly. And fundamentally, they advocated for complete disclosure of specifications, XML over binary, and international standard formats.
{{IMG:1}}
This point perfectly aligned with my thoughts and seemed to be aimed at Hancom.

**3) Handysoft - The reason for using ActiveX is Hancom.**
They talked a lot about public SW development, but the issue of format openness not being well-achieved overlapped somewhat with Infraware's point. A unique point was that when creating web-based groupware, there is a strong need for the Hangeul format, and because copy-and-paste is required, they are forced to maintain ActiveX technology. It seemed that Hancom needed to consider this more deeply.

**4) Unidocs: PDF is not just for reading.**
Unidocs explained that PDF is expanding into various forms of documents. And fundamentally, they emphasized its excellent rendering capability on any platform. Indeed, in the era of N-screens, PDF might be the document format that has grown the most. This is because the need for distribution has grown much larger than the need for production, and electronic documents are no longer viewed only on computers.

**3. What I Hope for from Domestic Electronic Document Companies**

First, I won't discuss Microsoft separately. MS Office is excellent. However, since most public documents are currently in HWP, let's focus on Hancom.

**1) Don't just think about selling products; create a document platform ecosystem through openness.**
As Infraware pointed out earlier, proper openness is a very natural thing. In the past, openness was viewed as a form of social contribution, but now the goal is to create and lead an ecosystem through openness. Therefore, in the past, even when opening, it was common to create slight differences to keep latecomers in check. However, currently, efforts are made to build an ecosystem around a technology platform by allowing anyone to become a new 3rd Party through open APIs or formats. This distributes the risk of the technology platform's collapse among other 3rd Party companies.

Now, openness is a competitive advantage, so companies strive for the latest features and try to involve as many companies as possible. Microsoft and Google are already moving in that direction. Furthermore, after expanding their scale and influence, they strive for international standardization, which is also part of expanding the technology platform's ecosystem. Therefore, efforts in OASIS activities and significant support for opening the HWP format must be increased. Technology openness is not just about uploading a specification. The easiest misunderstanding about open source is thinking it's a favor, but open source is an internet platform service. To encourage more participation, the quality of documentation must be maintained, and participants must be encouraged. The reason why large sums of money are invested in seemingly unprofitable open-source projects, leading to fierce competition, is precisely this.

Please remember that what made Hancom what it is today was not expensive packages. Hancom's success came from dominating the ecosystem through low-priced mass distribution in the early stages. Today's ecosystem war is not just about product performance. Please remember that it is made up of ecosystem members.

**2) Let's create an open-source renderer for documents that leads the standard for Korean standard electronic documents.**
I believe we should not stop at opening file formats but also consider open-sourcing the render engine. The reason why public certificates and ActiveX were cornered in Korea was primarily due to the onslaught of mobile devices. If it had only been the desktop market, this situation would not have occurred. The iPhone played a decisive role in this, and the reason why Safari on iPhone and mobile web on Android look identical is because they used the same render engine called WebKit. (Render: software that determines how a document will be displayed after reading it.) Even if web standards are open and adhered to perfectly, maintaining perfect visual consistency for complex documents is actually difficult. To solve this, PDF uses an image-based technology. This is why PDF shows excellent rendering performance on mobile devices.

I believe WebKit's unified rendering played the biggest role in bringing down Microsoft's dominance. Of course, Google, now considering itself large enough, has proposed separating render engines, and Microsoft, feeling threatened, is trying to shift towards Mozilla Firefox's open-source render engine. The reason why Infraware, a strong player in mobile browsers, easily entered the document market is that the technical stacks of document technology and web technology are almost identical. Therefore, in the document market, unifying the render engine is the only way to achieve practical compatibility that users can feel, not just spec openness in words.

When I talked about open source, Hancom said they were cautious due to their business model, but I reiterate that a technology platform is for dissemination, not a competitive asset to be tightly guarded. This trend will become even stronger if the shift is made to web-based word processors dominated by open technologies. Furthermore, if we create and lead an open-source render engine that drives ODF, we can lead the international trend of ODF. Apple influenced web standards with WebKit.

just as it gives us light.
**3) Instead of expanding into the web's domain, it's correct to integrate into the web.** There was talk about scripts and various forms of active documents, but personally, I don't see this as being in the domain of documents. This is because document reproduction can be difficult depending on the engine, and it's a functional issue. Furthermore, such transformed documents are virtually no different from the web. In fact, it's true that documents themselves are already threatened by web technology. If we're talking about the highest volume of document production worldwide, it would undoubtedly be web documents. I'm currently creating another such document through this blog. Ultimately, it's not about document formats expanding into the web, but rather when the web enters the domain of documents, including print, that we can ask for web standards to be recognized as the standard format for documents. Trying to make documents dynamically like the web unnecessarily will only lead to being outcompeted in a game of scale against the countless web platform players worldwide.
**4. More attention and investment in electronic documents.** One topic that came up during the forum was that many electronic documents are stored, but it's very often impossible to perfectly retrieve them as they were used in the past. This means either replacing them with the latest version of the file, emulating the program needed to open older versions, or keeping all the old hardware, software, and even printers. What do you think is the answer? In terms of cost, option 3, maintaining the old environment, is the cheapest. However, in the long run, these things are highly likely to be lost someday. Emulation has difficulties in terms of the quality of its reproduction. The best answer is continuous updates and migration. However, it's regrettable that this has not been the way things have been operated so far. How regrettable would it be if the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty were preserved but no one could ever read them? It would be like losing the precious knowledge of our ancestors. More attention and investment from a long-term perspective seem necessary.

titleEn: What Happens When True AI Arrives?
contentEn:
**1. Passing the Turing Test in 2014.**
What exactly is "true artificial intelligence"? First, a software program that recently passed the Turing Test has finally emerged. It's a simple test where if one-third of randomly selected people cannot distinguish whether their interlocutor is software or a human, it is recognized as artificial intelligence. There's a criticism that people were further deceived in this test due to the setup of the AI being an elementary school student from Ukraine who wasn't fluent in English, leading to the question, "Is it really true AI?" To address this, more sophisticated tests are currently being discussed, but the very act of passing the Turing Test is undeniably a monumental achievement.
{{IMG:1}}
**2. The Development of Artificial Intelligence**
The artificial intelligence we often imagine is like Atom or similar robots, but in academia, "intelligence" is actually developing by modeling and approaching the various ways our brains think, each with its own method. "Distinction," "reasoning," "learning," "grouping," "memory," "computation," "language," "speech/vision recognition," and "emotion" are all developing in their own ways. And some artificial intelligences are far ahead of humans. Representative examples are memory and computation. While some might argue that memory and computation are not artificial intelligence, they are nonetheless part of the brain's functions, and a "thinking machine" that models these is the computer, which is both the first and the last, and there is progress in other areas as well.
**3. Artificial Intelligence Adds Flexibility to Rigid Machines.**
Artificial intelligence is replacing simple human brain tasks. Memory is already a given, and recently, software that automatically writes newspaper articles has appeared, writing more articles than humans. Pepper, a robot created by SoftBank, is a cloud-based emotion-recognition AI robot. In many areas, machines are already ahead of humans and are taking over human jobs. Amidst this, AI will evolve from rigid, task-efficient machines to machines that communicate with people.

{{IMG:2}}

[ Vulcans, who suppress emotions to the maximum, are less human than Pepper ]
**4. What Can We Create with Artificial Intelligence?**
If you look at the setting of Tayo the Little Bus, which children love, Tayo is a bus that operates with an AI chip. What's interesting is that, like the elementary school AI Eugene, Tayo is an AI implemented as a young child. And it drives without a bus driver. In fact, driverless cars that run without a bus driver have been fully developed by Google. When Google's driverless car, Pepper's emotion recognition, and Eugene's intelligence are combined, the era has arrived where Tayo the Little Bus can literally become a reality. Even if the bus's AI is that of a young child, the driving itself is handled by Google's engine, so the driving is not unskilled.

[ Little Bus Gani was newly created by inheriting the memory chip of veteran bus 'One'. ]
The Turing Test is conducted without seeing faces. Also, when a specific field is narrowed down, artificial intelligence becomes very natural (as do humans, in fact), which is why software that writes articles in specific fields has been put into practical use. What about telemarketers who constantly converse with people on specific topics? Recently, there was a report that numerous telemarketers were about to lose their jobs due to a card security breach. What about artificial intelligence? AI that doesn't get tired and isn't subjected to emotional labor. It's clearly already right around the corner.
**5. Can Machines Replace or Dominate Humanity?**
Those who dream of dystopia imagine AI dominating humanity or an era where everyone loses their jobs. First, regarding the issue of dominating humanity, the inherent nature of artificial intelligence is still far from allowing us to speak of "self-realization" or "self" for AI. If complexity continues to increase, it's not impossible that we might someday see the first such software in our lifetime, but thinking about such an era is still too premature. Before that, the shock of the changes in the world created by software that humans perceive as human-like will be considerable. As I mentioned, countless simple jobs will disappear. And in fact, these things have continuously happened throughout the development of technology. While it might be frightening for those who cling to existing jobs or paradigms, I am confident that it will be a positive development for human society, and given the frequent news of M&A of AI companies by global corporations, it is already an unstoppable trend.
There is also a theory that by cooking food, humanity reduced the energy needed to digest nutrients, which increased the energy capacity available to the brain, thereby making humanity more intelligent.
I firmly believe that by entrusting these simple tasks to software, humanity will be able to do more productive and intelligent work. **I hope that humanity and society will be reborn to be more relaxed, allowing us to look around and reflect more on ourselves. While this might be an overly vague utopian ideal, I believe we can also devote more thought to those who are left behind with the remaining resources and surplus, and I think we must do so.**
**"The 21st Century Age of Artificial Intelligence" is truly coming.**

titleEn: Reasons to Pay Attention to the Underval
contentEn:
저는 초등학교 때 MSX(8bit PC)를 만나, 중학교 2학년 시절, 컴퓨터로 진로를 정해 컴퓨터 학과를 전공하고 개발자로 사회 초년 생활을 시작한 골수 컴퓨터 맨입니다. 제 인생에 컴퓨터를 빼 놓으면 할 얘기가 별로 없을 정도죠. 기획을 거쳐 지금은 소프트웨어 산업에 대해 고민해보는 곳에 도달했습니다. 제가 속한 조직에서 여러가지 이야기를 듣고, 얼마전 있었던 소프트웨어 산업 살리기 끝장 토론에서도 많은 이야기를 듣습니다. 제가 막말로 이찬진과 안철수 선배님들을 보고 자라 이 자리에 까지 왔지만, '속았다'라는 생각을 할 정도로 기대했던 것과 많이 다르다는 생각을 하곤 합니다. 그도 그럴 것이 현재 한국 사회에서는 소프트웨어에 대한 인식이 의외로 아직도 낮다는 사실에 깜짝 깜짝 놀라곤 했습니다. 그래서 이번에는 소프트웨어에 대한 이야기를 해볼까 합니다.
I am a hardcore computer person who first encountered an MSX (8-bit PC) in elementary school, decided on a career in computers in my second year of middle school, majored in computer science, and started my professional life as a developer. There's not much to talk about in my life if you take computers out of it. After working in planning, I've now reached a point where I'm contemplating the software industry. I hear various discussions within my organization, and I also heard a lot during the recent "Software Industry Revival Marathon Debate." Frankly, I grew up looking up to seniors like Lee Chan-jin and Ahn Cheol-soo, and that's how I got to where I am today, but I often feel like I've been "fooled" because things are so different from what I expected. This is especially true because I'm constantly surprised by how low the perception of software still is in Korean society. So, this time, I'd like to talk about software.

**1. Aren't Naver and Nexon software companies?** {{IMG:1}}

http://m.gfmarket.naver.com/sticker/detail/code/moon_and_james

**I thought the company I worked for was a software company. But it turns out it's not a software company. Naver is classified as an internet service company, an IT service. And the gaming industry, which I once aspired to join, is categorized as cultural content, meaning it's also not a software industry. I thought, "What kind of nonsense is this?" but if we go by this standard, today's venture boom also strangely isn't considered a software industry. And what's even funnier is that computer science students, the better their school and skills, are working in industries other than the software industry. Leading IT companies like Google, Facebook, and Amazon also wouldn't be considered software companies. The reason Microsoft is classified as a software company is because it sells Windows as packaged software. If it transitions to internet-based cloud services like Office 365, then even this company would strangely no longer be a software company. So, what I'm trying to say is that one of the reasons the software industry is undervalued is that even companies the public perceives as software companies are not classified as such.**

**- 1.1. Why are internet services a software industry? -**
Before discussing point 2, let's talk more about why IT services are a software industry. Everything in the world is made up of hardware and software. What we generally call a program, or code, is not actually software in itself. You might think this is nonsense, but code, or a program, is like letters in literature. Just as a sentence doesn't mean a novel, software doesn't mean the code itself. Software refers to the logic of a program, that intangible something. Of course, just as there are writers who write more beautifully, those who code more wonderfully and efficiently are also excellent developers. Simply put, if the bat we use to play baseball is hardware, then the rules of baseball are software. Therefore, the essence of 'service' in the IT service industry is software, and if it utilizes internet technology, the proportion of coding, or development technology, as mentioned earlier, is very high, and the product comes out as a program, or software, making it clearly a software industry. To give another example, in the webtoon industry, where books used to be the hardware, computers or smartphones now serve as the hardware, and the publishing industry has transitioned to the software industry. The comic book publishing market has transformed into a comic software market. Online shopping is also similar; traditional offline stores have transitioned to internet software. Internet services are also one of the most extreme (and extreme in development methods) industries within the software sector.

**2. Samsung Electronics is also a software company, it turns out** {{IMG:2}}

http://m.gfmarket.naver.com/sticker/detail/code/brown_and_cony

**Now, let me tell you another fact that the public often doesn't know: the proportion of software personnel among Samsung Electronics' workforce is much higher than you might think. At my alma mater, getting a job at Samsung Electronics was very easy compared to other departments, as Samsung Electronics and LG Electronics had been sweeping up excellent software talent early on through programs like software memberships. (My wife doesn't believe me when I say I could have easily gone to Samsung Electronics if I had put my mind to it ㅡㅡ;)**
**And as you know, Google, which exerts the greatest influence in the global mobile phone market, is a pure software company, and Apple is a company that operates across both hardware and software.**
**Although the title says Samsung Electronics is a software company, that doesn't mean Samsung Electronics is not a hardware company. Samsung Electronics is still a hardware company, but a very large portion of its operations relies heavily on software, and that proportion is increasing. There's even a saying that advanced cars run on software, not gasoline.**
**This means that the nature of the software industry is not exclusive to other industries in a vertical sense, but rather a horizontal industry that is embedded in all industries, with its proportion steadily increasing and becoming a competitive advantage for each industry.**
**This leads to the argument that everyone needs to understand software, a topic I will discuss separately later. (It's not about coding.)**

**3. All industries are shifting towards software**
As I mentioned earlier, Samsung Electronics has a very high and increasing proportion of software, but there are cases where, on the surface, companies appear to sell hardware, but in reality, they are selling software. Simply put, hardware is developed to be optimized for software and given as a bonus, all to sell the software. Amazon's Kindle strategy is a prime example of this. Amazon's Kindle is sold at or below cost to create a foundation for Amazon's e-commerce profits. The news that SoftBank's recently demonstrated Pepper robot costs less than 2 million won is also a price that would be unthinkable for a company that primarily makes profit from hardware. SoftBank, which originally started with software distribution and whose main business was internet ventures like Yahoo, likely believes it can generate sufficient profit through other software ecosystems. That's why they announced the release of an SDK for developers simultaneously with the product launch. This is one of the reasons why major Korean conglomerates, which primarily focus on hardware, cannot easily approach machines like Pepper. Even if they manage to keep up with the hardware, they lack experience in the crucial software areas of artificial intelligence and internet business models.

**4. Undervalued Software, Let's Re-focus.**
It's no exaggeration to say that the world's center is moving towards software, yet the perception of software in Korea is severely undervalued. Low developer treatment, a narrow domestic market, and the public's perception that software and services are free—that's simply not true. Software is not free. Naver and Google, which you use, don't operate for free. They earn appropriate advertising revenue to sustain their businesses and make a profit, and they offer various paid services.
Due to its inherently disruptive and innovative nature, software can feel like it's providing groundbreaking services for free, but it's using software as a tool to tap into existing user needs in the market, not doing business out of thin air.
Therefore, paid software is sold because it has value and scarcity. Compared to hardware, where satisfaction tends to decrease immediately after purchase, software satisfaction lasts much longer, and its pricing is also more granular.
Furthermore, as software boasts flexibility as its advantage, it enhances satisfaction through continuous upgrades and services rather than just the initial purchase cost, and this requires appropriate financial compensation. This is because the lifecycles of software and hardware are very different. Unlike hardware, which has a high initial purchase cost but rapidly declining satisfaction, software has a relatively low initial purchase cost, but satisfaction is maintained, and it requires continuous investment and upgrades.
This shift in perception will be a touchstone for where we place more value in the future. We always tell children to cultivate their inner selves rather than their appearance. That is the value of software. It doesn't wear out, but through continuous investment, it can provide higher added value and sometimes be a means of innovation—that is software.
