titleEn: I Need to Focus on Myself
contentEn:
Saturday morning. I often drive grandfathers from Anyang to Yangji Church for worship. The road from North Suwon to the Yangji Interchange, which is often congested, is a section that allows for a lot of thought. Lately, I've been thinking about the wrong paths I've been on and the opportunities I've consistently missed. I've pondered these negative thoughts. I also think that life seems to have its ups and downs, but when I consider the biggest difference between myself during the downhill sections and myself during the uphill sections, it wasn't just about doing what I loved and what suited me. I realized it was when I was diligently refining myself and faithfully dedicating myself to the time and tasks given to me. By refining myself and thinking, I was able to make plans, and by putting them into practice, I was able to generate passion.

Perhaps the opportunities I've consistently missed are also due to this attitude of mine. The One I believe in often tells me to wait. And often, the reason for that was that I wasn't ready. Things undertaken with only eagerness and no preparation are bound to go wrong.

I said I didn't have time, but looking back, my biggest regret was being chased by things I didn't want to do, rather than doing my best to seize opportunities. I realized that to get the time and opportunities to do what I want, I need to do my best at the things I don't want to do. And since opportunities and situations won't change immediately starting today, I thought it was right to start by thinking about what I *can* do.

Lately, I often find myself caught up in feelings of immaturity, inadequacy, and inferiority. When things are going well, I feel like I'm leading the world, but then I easily get frustrated and complain like this.

What I need now seems to be more thought. And then, putting that thought into action. The saying, "If you don't pray, how will it be answered?" is like saying, "If you don't act, how will it be achieved?"

First, I think my life needs to be organized. Rather than being chased by life, I need to regain control. The same goes for this blog. As more people visit, the original purpose seems to have changed a lot. I want to refrain from posting as if I'm being chased, without even organizing myself and my surroundings. I need more time to think. As a developer, and as a planner whom I aspire to be in the future, it seems nothing will come of it if I'm not prepared myself.

I'm rambling like this in a post because I hope these resolutions, made by my insufficient and weak self, don't just end with a single thought.

titleEn: [Yeonpyeongdo Shell
contentEn:
**1. North Korea Becomes a Supernova**
Looking at the recent Yeonpyeong Island incident, my heart feels heavy. What's clear now is that North Korea is truly hurtling towards its end. Stars are said to disappear after a powerful supernova explosion when they reach the end of their lives. While some stars slowly shrink depending on their size, North Korea ultimately seems to have chosen the path of a supernova among the two options.
North Korea's succession issue with Kim Jong-un, severe food and energy shortages, and its method to resolve these were not through self-improvement via socialist changes like China, but solely through international aid. This international aid came with restructuring conditions, similar to South Korea's IMF crisis. But North Korea rejected this. Instead, North Korea used its usual method of instigating crises, but it seems to have crossed a line that shouldn't have been crossed.
In the case of the Cheonan incident, it couldn't be officially attributed to the North, regardless of the circumstances. From an international diplomatic perspective, no country other than South Korea specifically demanded compensation from North Korea for the Cheonan. However, this time is different. North Korean ground forces directly attacked a civilian village and our troops with artillery. In fact, what South Korea considers the biggest military problem is not nuclear weapons, but this artillery. It's essentially an official air raid.

**2. Increased Sanctions Against North Korea, and Greater Threats**
Neither the US nor South Korea will propose negotiations here. That's an obvious fact. If North Korea played this card to solidify Kim Jong-un's hereditary succession internally, then it implies they have now rejected US-South Korea dialogue.
The scenario now expected is stronger pressure on North Korea. Even China, which had been helping, is now in an awkward position. Moreover, it's during the Guangzhou Asian Games. For China, it must be a frustrating situation. And now, that strong pressure on North Korea leads to only one conclusion: the acceleration of North Korea's collapse. **If North Korean oil tankers are seized and financial sanctions are imposed, North Korea will not be able to survive this winter and will face a severe crisis.**
Then North Korea will soon fall into chaos, and the remaining option will be to plan an even stronger event to resolve it. They know this won't solve it, but they have no choice. Or, some military factions might even carry out a full-scale invasion of the South. If fuel is cut off, there are no options. They can't just sit and die, so they'll lash out.
The reason Japan, which started WWII and absolutely wanted to avoid fighting the US, ended up fighting the US was precisely this oil issue, and it's not much different now. Just a few days ago, while playing Civilization V, I attacked the non-violent Gandhi to secure oil and captured his capital.
Even if people talk about anti-communism or whatever, the truth is that Juche ideology doesn't spread easily in our society like Christianity, and what's important is the current situation; the drivers of war are not ideology but North Korea's political and economic problems. It's clear that North Korea is currently in a very dangerous state. The impact on our economy now that North Korean risk is at its peak is also frightening to imagine. Predictions of an imminent nuclear test were rampant, but North Korea instead carried out an even more provocative act. It wouldn't be strange if a nuclear test happened any day now.

**3. Lee Myung-bak Administration's North Korea Policy, The End of the Chicken Game**
It cannot be said that the Lee Myung-bak administration bears no responsibility for this situation. Aid to the North was reduced, and the North drove the Kaesong Industrial Complex to ruin. Instead of negotiations like 'what will we give each other' or 'I'll give you this if you give me that,' from the moment negotiations began with 'I've given a lot so far, now I demand,' it seems like an unreasonable demand was made to North Korea, which has nothing. We would certainly be the winner of this chicken game. Ultimately, at the end of the chicken game, North Korea's collapse is the final goal, and we have enough stamina. However, such a unification process would be dozens of times more painful than Germany's absorption unification.
After the Cheonan incident, the North Korea issue effectively left our hands and was passed to the US; I had hoped President Lee Myung-bak would resolve it wisely, but he failed to offer any sharp solutions.
Strong expressions of regret to North Korea. When has North Korea ever batted an eye at such things? And I don't even know when it wasn't regrettable. The world was not convinced that the Cheonan incident was definitively North Korea's doing, and only verbal cooperation was obtained from China.

****
**4. Now, We Await the Actions of the US and China, While South Korea Suffers Damage and is Marginalized**
Now, all that's left is to await America's choice. What will they do? "Don't escalate the conflict." That simply sounds like 'maintain defensive posture until the US military comes and decides'. That's just how it sounds. And that's the reality. Clearly, the repercussions of this situation will not end simply. The US going to the negotiating table would be an action that would undermine the already struggling Obama administration, so they will absolutely not do it. Rather, moving the fleet to exert pressure would be more characteristic of Obama. And the reason this couldn't be done in the past was because it involved the main US fleet entering right in front of China's nose. However, given the seriousness of the situation, we don't know what conclusion the US and China will reach. **It's possible they might hold secret talks, decide to divide North Korea's interests between the US and China, and encourage North Korea's collapse.**
**The only possibility for a peaceful end is for the US to outwardly exert pressure on North Korea, but to continue indirectly negotiated support through China to maintain the North Korean regime.** If this is judged to be advantageous to the two great powers, they might take this approach, contrary to what they announce publicly.
**However, if North Korea suddenly collapses, the South Korean government will be powerless. Instead, it will have to worry about guerrilla warfare and localized conflicts, defend a fluctuating exchange rate, and manage incoming refugees, which alone would drive it crazy. It might even need international aid at that point.**
Of course, this doesn't mean it will become a reality immediately. It just means there's a considerable possibility. Historically, wars happen where they seem unlikely, and don't happen where they seem likely; they are not caused by some old, stale emotions. Rather, those emotions are often created through propaganda and used to decide on war. So, will we just stand by?

**5. What's Needed Now is Anti-Communism? Drop Such Political Terms, and Worry About Security.**
Many people still use the term 'anti-communism,' but I believe 'security' is the more appropriate term. If it's anti-communism, then China should also be included as an enemy. And such a war would be a US vs. China war, meaning World War III. Many socialist countries are already in cooperative relationships with us. Therefore, the term 'anti-communism' is not only inappropriate, but communism itself is not inherently bad. It's just that North Korea is dangerous. That is precisely security. Thinking extremely, even democratic Taiwan could attack South Korea along with China. Excessively emotional responses and a North Korea policy used solely for political gain ultimately led to this worsening situation, and I believe North Korea also carried out this act for political exploitation.
I feel bitter and scared. Because for politicians, both in the South and the North, war and human lives are ultimately just tools for seizing power.

**However, in the current situation, what we must choose and cannot abandon is a sense of security.** And such a comprehensive sense of security can empower the government or allow for criticism of the government's initial response. Furthermore, a state of readiness to respond to potential localized conflicts and guerrilla warfare is also necessary. Fear and anger are inappropriate. In fact, anger is just another expression of fear.
I even wonder what if we had paid as much attention to North Korea relations as to the Four Major Rivers project. If we had fully opened the Kaesong Industrial Complex and transformed it like China, the stock market would have easily surpassed 2000 points.

**Finally, I express my condolences to the fallen soldiers and victims. I am sorry for creating a lacking and weak nation that could not protect them.**
****
**ps. I wonder if the counterattack should have been with MLRS instead of K9 (Are MLRS deployed on Yeonpyeong Island?). How much damage could have been inflicted on North Korean artillery in tunnels?**
****

titleEn: Korean News Sites Are Distributing Malicious Scripts
contentEn:
A while ago, I received an email from Naver like the one below.
 

 
 
 
The content stated that suspicious malicious script was found on the page of an article linked to my OpenCast. Not only that, but there are often news outlets that cannot be accessed when using the Firefox browser.
 
{{IMG:1}}

At that time, the warning message also indicated that the site was suspected of being a distributor of malicious scripts.

What does it mean for the media, which has a responsibility to report facts neutrally and objectively, to embed malicious scripts? Generally, malicious scripts are somewhat different from viruses. While malicious scripts can certainly be used as a method to attempt hacking, they are more often used to extract information from a user's PC or to secretly make the browser perform actions unintended by the user. What on earth were news organizations thinking when they embedded code suspected of being malicious scripts on their pages? To steal customer information? Or was it code embedded by a third-party advertiser to whom an ad script was assigned?

Regardless of whether it's the former or the latter, the news organization operating the site cannot be said to be free of responsibility. Are they so irresponsible that they don't even know about malicious scripts embedded in their ads, or are they trying to increase effectiveness by displaying infinite pop-up windows to users, like an adult site? It all leads to the same conclusion: they are not fulfilling their responsibilities, and a news organization that doesn't fulfill its responsibilities cannot be trusted.
It seems to be the destiny of such news organizations to ultimately churn out only articles that cater to the tastes of their advertisers.

In a situation where news organizations, which claim to provide relatively high-quality information outside of portals, operate in this manner, I don't know how much we can trust the current media. Perhaps they bear far greater responsibility than portals, so I don't understand why they operate this way. Do they even know that they are branded as distributors of malicious scripts?

titleEn: [Share] 20 - If I Go
Foreign Software is Sweeping Korea, Riding the Smartphone
contentEn:
**1. The Hardware Market in the Platform War, What About Software?
**It seems the IT industry's buzz around smartphones like the iPhone and Android, though somewhat subdued now, shows no signs of cooling down. Personally, I feel that the discussion about foreign platforms, which started in the smartphone hardware market, is gradually spreading to the software market.
Certainly, recent articles show that domestic portal services still wield significant influence on the web. However, what about the increasing number of Twitter and Facebook subscribers? If domestic portal operators have been in "defense mode" for most of their services, then perhaps these microblogging and new SNS markets are in "attack mode."
In fact, Twitter, Facebook, and Google, much like mobile platforms, are integrating their services and establishing themselves as single platforms on the web. Smartphone usage is high, and user dependency on these services is even higher than app usage.

**2. Highly Competitive Foreign Services Are Preloaded on Devices, and in Our Minds.
**These foreign services clearly possess more competitiveness and a larger scale than domestic services. The fact that Google's search bar is being recognized as the standard search bar for smartphones is also a cause for concern. Of course, in the case of Android, it might be understood as Google supplying a high-quality smartphone OS under certain conditions.
However, considering that Naver's strong position in the Korean internet market is now based on its search bar, not banner ads, it feels like we are essentially giving up the domestic search ad market's home turf due to the allure of smartphone OS.
Even on my Optimus Q, which at least has Naver's search bar inserted and various domestic apps preloaded, Google's search bar is standard, and Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, etc., are pre-installed with prioritized icon placement. Furthermore, smartphone advertisements, excluding ScanSearch, seem to emphasize the availability of foreign solutions rather than domestic software services. This atmosphere is also reflected in the media, creating the impression that Twitter is the only microblogging service.

**3. Is This Really Okay? Reverse Discrimination Against Domestic Services? **
In reality, from the very beginning, domestic software services have been at a disadvantage in the battle against leading global services, not just in terms of service quality but also in their position on smartphones. An old comment from an iPhone user stated that the advantage of Apple's products is that everything works without installing anything else. This is a result of Apple not giving external services a chance to intervene, or preloading its own equivalent services, not just on the hardware platform but also for software services. A similar example is the market share gained by Microsoft's Internet Explorer.
Furthermore, smartphone users will increasingly be much lighter users than PC users. In other words, there will be more users who won't bother to delete Google's pre-installed apps and install domestic ones. Also, for those who feel behind the times because they don't know much about smartphones, if the perception spreads that using Twitter, Facebook, and Google is how you stay ahead, and these are naturally pre-installed on their newly purchased phones, usage rates will only increase.

**4. Will Korean Software Have a Place in the Future Market?
**The recent complaints from portal companies about reverse discrimination on smartphones are not to be dismissed lightly. Most of the money earned from the global internet flows into a few corporations. In Korea, domestic portals similarly earn a significant amount. The problem isn't just that this money flows to foreign companies, but whether there's a real possibility of it being reinvested into the domestic software industry.
Perhaps, if we erase national borders, this discussion might be meaningless. If one argues that Korea's software industry has already become a "Galapagos" and thus lacks competitiveness and should perish, then further discussion would be pointless. The issue is that if Korea intends to view the IT industry as a future growth engine, then more discussion is needed.
I believe both domestic companies, Naver and Daum, are good companies. If these two companies were not Korean but American companies founded in the US, couldn't they truly stand shoulder-to-shoulder with Google? Success domestically is very difficult, but success in overseas expansion is even harder. However, what about the opposite case? Imagine a service with over 100 million users versus a fringe service with barely 10 million users; a large droplet easily absorbing a small one to become one.

**5. The Vulnerable Korean Software Industry
**Korean software does not have as robust a content industry foundation as Japan. The frustrating reality is that the path for the existing content business is blocked by government ministries imposing various regulations and censorship, while only researching ways to collect taxes.
Furthermore, the platform industry is just beginning, and the Ministry of Information and Communication, which once exercised coercive power to create standards, no longer exists. (Even when it did exist, it was swayed by large corporations, resulting in different keypad designs for the three mobile carriers, and it's amusing how they're now startled by China creating its own standards...)
Everyone acknowledges that the iPhone's power was actually in its software, but how far has the Korean software industry's strength truly come? And I can't shake the uncomfortable feeling I get when I see preloaded foreign apps that I don't use and can't delete. It's also a reality that the e-commerce market, with Auction and Gmarket moving to eBay, means eBay now holds most of the domestic market. In this game of capital and scale, even seemingly giant domestic companies are often like candles in the wind. It seems that Korean laws, perhaps designed to favor large corporations, result in domestic companies being similarly disadvantaged when large foreign companies enter. If you feel wronged, you should learn English... (I don't know why I'm writing so darkly, perhaps because I'm squeezing in this post after enjoying Civilization V for a while.)

**6. Request for Minimal Preloads and Deletion Capability
**To hand over such concerns and decisions to the user as much as possible, shouldn't preloaded apps be minimized? If preloading is unavoidable for business reasons, I hope they would at least allow us to delete them. Whether they are foreign or domestic apps.

titleEn: The Presumption of Recommending a Tweet from
contentEn:
A link to the post above was uploaded on Me2day. Reading the content, it explains why Twitter or Facebook is recommended for teenagers and people in their twenties. Is that really the case? Let's talk about that briefly this time.

**1. Is Twitter easier for communicating with other generations?**
- Me2day definitely has a higher influx of light users due to its easier interface compared to Twitter and domestic advertising. Also, news outlets and media companies tend to consider Twitter as the representative SNS and report on it, which is why they only cited Twitter during the recent heavy rainfall. Although many real-time posts about the heavy rain were flooded on Me2day, it seemed to be outside the media's interest. Anyway, let's check one fact: Is Twitter really easier for communicating with other generations? Below is data from Ranky.com as of October 19, 2010.

{{IMG:1}}

{{IMG:2}}

Looking at the Ranky.com data above, we can see the age-group distribution of Me2day and Twitter users. Summarized, it is as follows:

| Category | Me2day | Twitter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Teens | 6 | 2 |
| 20s | 32 | 28 |
| 30s | 42 | 49 |
| 40s | 15 | 15 |
| 50s and older | 5 | 6 |

Based on this data, one assumption is necessary: for there to be a lot of inter-generational communication, the number of users across generations must be evenly distributed. So, what if we calculate the mean and variance?

| Category | Me2day | Twitter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean | 28.1 years old | 29.5 years old |
| Variance/Standard Deviation | 8442 / 91.88 | 7475 / 86.45 |

- **Surprisingly, the average age for Me2day is 28.1, which is not significantly lower than Twitter's 29.5.** Twitter users often assume Me2day users are mostly teenagers, but these figures prove that's not the case at all.

- A larger variance and standard deviation indicate a lower concentration in specific age groups. **The biggest difference between Me2day and Twitter is actually that Me2day has a larger variance and standard deviation. In other words, if you want inter-generational communication, Me2day is a better service than Twitter.** The 7% gap in the 30s actually went directly to the teens and 20s, and furthermore, the 40s and 50s are distributed similarly to Twitter.

- What's unique is that the difference between UV (Unique Visitors) and PV (Page Views) is not significant, which is similar to the Cyworld pattern. While Twitter tends to attract users through search, Me2day indicates that users spend a longer time on the service. Compared to Facebook, it would probably show similar results.

**- Is the situation better for Facebook currently? I also have dozens of friends on Facebook, but none are in their early 20s or younger. Given the recent significant increase in Facebook subscribers, it seems that internet-friendly, IT-related acquaintances are flocking to Facebook. Therefore, as of now, it doesn't seem to help with inter-generational communication.**

**2. Does using Twitter or Facebook lead to communication with people overseas?**
**1) What about the language barrier... Should one study even on Twitter?**
Certainly, using Twitter and Facebook often leads to interactions with international users. However... English is a barrier for me too. If you want to communicate with people overseas, I think English proficiency comes first. That said, we can't force Facebook or Twitter for English education. Isn't this perception that children should only study even on the internet no different from the current government viewing children merely as studying machines?

**2) Minimal Effectiveness**
And more than that, using Facebook actually increases gaming. ㅡㅡ; The same would probably apply to Me2day or blogs now. To communicate with people overseas, there's no way to prove that Twitter is overwhelmingly more effective than learning English, making foreign friends, having pen pals, or chatting via messenger.

**3. Encounter different issues**
**1) No way to prevent information bias and social bias**
Furthermore, the problem with social networks is the tendency to focus on social information. While domestic information can be acquired from both official sources like newspapers and broadcasts, and social information, allowing for comparison and reflection, social information encountered through Twitter is often uncritically accepted by children, even if its authenticity hasn't been verified. I recall seeing the original author suffer because false information was spread via Twitter. Seeing the personal information of a female teacher involved in compensated dating being exposed by the DC Investigation Team recently even makes me feel scared. While Twitter does convey other news, it ultimately tends to lean towards information that aligns with the preferences of the people one follows.

**4. What's important is not the system, but rather who you communicate with**
Fundamentally, that's what's important. Who you communicate with is what matters. What the system provides is minimal. Social systems, in particular, are heavily influenced by friends. **Can we really say that children who engage in heated debates on Twitter are better than children who share photos with family and relatives on Cyworld and build affection?** Blind faith in a system... this is the most frightening thing. It's the fundamental reason why information delivered by that system is accepted uncritically. If blind faith in Twitter goes too far, how is it different from blind faith in state-run broadcasting that branded the Gwangju Uprising participants as rioters? Is collective intelligence always wise? No, it's not. Sometimes, it can be like hamsters running towards a cliff.

What I want to teach children is not to **'do something,' but rather to 'do something together.'** Instead of writing reasons why I recommend Twitter or Facebook over Cyworld or Me2day to teens and 20s, I would say, 'Let's do Twitter or Facebook together.' The reasons are for the children to create and choose. Are we just sitting back and saying, 'This service has many users in their 30s, so if teens want to communicate, they should come on their own'? Do the uncles in their 30s have no intention of listening to what teens have to say? Following yesterday's post about announcer Kim Ju-ha ([http://fstory97.blog.me/70095739780](http://fstory97.blog.me/70095739780)), I've been writing only negative things about Twitter recently. I believe this isn't because Twitter is bad, but rather a problem with certain statements made on Twitter. By the way... how about an interactive comment feedback system between Me2day, Twitter, and Facebook? Blogs have trackbacks, which at least allow for some loose coupling... but these operate like entirely different continents. (Or am I unaware? If anyone knows, please reply.) Has the blog comment standardization movement ultimately failed?

titleEn: Internet Violence: A Problem for All of Us
contentEn:
Internet messages are light, and it's difficult to know their source and authenticity. The content of individual messages is often a one-sided conversation, blurted out without context. And sometimes their purpose is malicious, leading to innocent people being harmed. Recently, many one-sided comments were posted on my blog, telling me to listen to sermons from a specific religious cafe.

{{IMG:1}}
 
At first, I replied to those comments, telling them not to evangelize in inappropriate places. Although I am also a Christian, I believe that evangelism without regard for time and place only creates antipathy and is a sign of bad manners. However, they posted on other posts without replying to my comment. I was dumbfounded and tried to send a private message, but it was set to refuse messages. When I visited their blog, all spaces where others could write were blocked. So, I just sent one email.

That person didn't stop there and posted the same comment again. So this time, I decided to really find out what kind of cafe it was. But it wasn't on Naver, and the place I found through Googling was a Daum cafe. When I checked the cafe, an unexpected announcement was prominently displayed at the top.
It stated that **people doing such random promotions on Naver blogs have nothing to do with them, and although they requested action from Naver, there was no solution.**
{{IMG:2}}
 
 

Reading this phrase, "there is no solution," made me realize once again the fatal weakness of our internet today. Although the internet and social media are gaining popularity and the era of Web 2.0 democracy has arrived, a small number of unethical users cause significant harm, and there are no proper methods or systems to prevent this.

This diminishes the meaning of the internet's existence. While some people find justice through the internet, individuals and organizations can also suffer irreparable harm through it.
Moreover, the majority of the public, who become perpetrators due to inaccurate information, are unaware of this. This responsibility, once held by the media, has now spread to all internet users, but there's no proper way to enforce it. Are there no measures to block and prevent this? 
 
What if there were specific countermeasures for each stage: the stage of intentionally producing false information, the stage of disseminating it, the stage where this inaccurate information spreads through systems and the public, the stage where a third party accepts this distorted information, and the actions taken as a perpetrator? What if there were specific countermeasures for each of these stages? The important thing is that the structure should not harm the positive functions of the internet. **A government or portal that simply proposes "unconditionally filter and imprison" as a solution would be wasting their salaries.**

Perhaps the solution to internet violence should start with culture and education? I believe this issue is not just a problem for the government or portals, but for all of us.

titleEn: [Idea] Product Matching Information Sharing System
contentEn:
**1. Title: Product Matching Information Sharing System**

**2. First Draft Date: January 26, 2010**

**3. Background:** When users buy a single product, they have a desire to purchase products that match it. A prime example is clothing coordination, and such information is produced and distributed by user knowledge-sharing sites or professional CPs (shopping malls). Portals and open markets handle a variety of products, and this is to consider a system that can share and distribute matching information for each product.

**4. Details**
**4.1. Matching Resource Collection (Target: CP, Advertiser)**
l Matching Resources: Standardized data for matching original or advertised products
Resources such as images registered by advertisers or CPs providing original content, with standardized sizes for matching.
- Product Matching Resource Registration Tool

Above shows the registration of matching resources corresponding to the original
[http://shopping.naver.com/detail/detail.nhn?cat_id=00030005&nv_mid=4140712333]
Product matching resources include resource attributes like front, back, left, right, top, bottom, and matching resources like 2D or 3D images.

Matching resources are collected by CPs and advertisers, and can provide guides such as direction. The important thing is that it means collecting resources that match with the Legacy System.

**4.2 Authoring Matching Information by Collecting Matching Resources (Target: CP, Advertiser, Administrator, User)**

Click '+' to select matching resources. Collect these images to create matching information.

**4.3 User Inquiry of Matching Information (Target: All Naver Shopping Users)**

These matching information items are serviced as shown above and can be used by general users.
**4.4. Matching information as described above has a higher-level category. (PC parts, coordination – can be provided with shopping category services)**
**4.5. Matching information can be shared among users or ranked higher through a recommendation system. (Recommendation-based service)**
**4.6. Issued in a cast format, recommended coordinations from large malls can be viewed. (Expert Recommendation Service)**
**4.7. Seasonal themed coordinations, such as celebrity styles, are also possible. (Theme Service)**
**4.8. Matching resources can include not only images but also sound or video. Clicking could produce sound, or videos could be uploaded as supplementary information. (UX Aspect)**
**4.9. At the top of portals displaying matching information, specific mall matching information can be prioritized and displayed, allowing for sales as advertisements. (Advertising Model)**
**4.10. Users can be informed through images that related matching information exists for a matching resource, and clicking it can display the related matching resource information. (e.g., Naver Checkout)**

**5. Key Features**
- Method for collecting matching images for advertisements and original content information
- Method for adding recommendation and comment supplementary information to matching information storage content for products
- Method for user subscription to matching information

titleEn: [Cheongdam Piacere]
contentEn:
** 1. Going for a Maternity Photoshoot.**
 September 15, 2010, was the day my wife had an appointment for a free maternity photoshoot. My wife said she had applied for a free maternity photoshoot at Cheongdam Piace Studio ([http://cafe.naver.com/piacestudio](http://cafe.naver.com/piacestudio)) and won. They were offering free photoshoots on a first-come, first-served basis at specific times each week.
 Anyway, thanks to that, I even took a day off work, and we planned to go for a maternity photoshoot in the afternoon after a hospital visit in the morning. It had been a long time since we visited Seoul, especially Cheongdam-dong. (Cheongdam-dong reminds me of the ladies of Cheongdam-dong.)
 The day was bright and clear, and the optimized route searched on Naver Maps showed a path passing in front of COEX.

 And the Mappy navigation system showed a route through the Umyeonsan toll tunnel. The reservation was for 3 PM, but I left at 1 PM, planning to arrive by 2:30 PM. I thought it would be faster since the navigation was directing me through a toll road. But what happened... this navigation system told me to go through the middle of Gangnam during lunchtime. I regretted not checking the entire route. (It seems I should use portal or mobile carrier apps for real-time routes.)
 I called Piace, apologizing repeatedly, and eventually, the navigation system dropped me off at 3:10 PM in an alley in Cheongdam-dong. Ah... but this wasn't the place. It dropped me in front of the old office, Namugeuneul, before Piace moved.

**[ *Caution: If your navigation system guides you next to Gangnam-gu Office Station, that is a different studio. ] **
 
 Listening to my wife's nagging, we quickly crossed a narrow alley and arrived at 3:30 PM. 

**** 
** 3. Schedule getting tangled due to late shooting time**
 Normally, if you arrive early, you get to enjoy a cup of coffee with cookies at the pretty cafe downstairs, but we didn't even have time to look around the cafe. My wife's hair was roughly styled, and we had to proceed with the shoot. They usually style the hair beautifully, almost like a bride's, and seeing my wife envy other expectant mothers made me feel so sorry. {{IMG:2}}
 On top of that, the beautiful red-strapped hanbok dress my wife had her eye on was already worn by someone who arrived earlier. At this point, I definitely thought we should have come earlier. When we were about to start shooting, the photographer's flash trigger broke. The photographer ran from the basement studio to the top floor... The shoot finally started at 4 PM.
 
 
** **
 **4. Photoshoot Begins**
** **
{{IMG:3}}
[ Ah... my face is being revealed. ]

 
{{IMG:4}}
**[ Beautiful maternity photos sent by Piace - Frame requested! ]**
******** 
****  

**[ Photos taken by the helper ]**
 
 I also brought my DSLR, so I could take pictures too. I highly recommend bringing a camera when your wife has her maternity photoshoot. I wore a suit, which I never usually wear, and during the shoot, the helper even took pictures with our camera. My wife, of course, scolded me, saying they took better pictures than I did.
 
 
The second studio was on the 2nd floor, I think... (Is that right?) The atmosphere there was completely different. This place had a sweeter feel? My wife also changed into a different dress this time. By the time we finished all the shots, it was almost 5:30 PM. While other studios quickly do free photoshoots in 30 minutes, this place felt almost like a wedding photoshoot.
 
 
{{IMG:5}}
**[ With the photographer, the helper, and my wife..]**
**** 
 
**5. After the Photoshoot...**
 Afterward, they showed us various baby growth albums on the table above the dressing room. The baby photos they showed were so pretty. 

**{{IMG:6}}
  [ The dressing room is downstairs, and you can have a consultation at the table upstairs. ]**
 

However, because I had another appointment, I had to leave the studio in a hurry after only a brief explanation. It felt rude to the person explaining, as it was a free service, and I should have at least listened carefully. I also regretted not having more time to look around other studios. According to other people's reviews, the other studios were also pretty. Anyway, I thought it would have been a wonderful experience with more leisure if I had moved faster, but I was happy with the photos they sent.

 
 **They said if I posted a review, they would give me a beautiful crystal frame and the rest of the original photos. I found out that other free photoshoots usually don't provide the originals. If you're planning a maternity photoshoot, it might be a good idea to try Piace Studio. (Be sure to go early and have a relaxed day~.)**
** **
 With our baby due on October 9th, I really feel how little time is left these days. My heart yearns to create good memories for our baby, but I also feel sorry that it's always just a wish. Later, when our baby is born, I will tell them how much Mom and Dad were waiting for them.

titleEn: [Air Doll] Many Air Dolls Live in This
contentEn:
{{IMG:1}}

http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/basic.nhn?code=52075

[Air Doll](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/basic.nhn?code=52075)

Director
Hirokazu Kore-eda
Cast
Bae Doona, Arata, Joe Odagiri, Itao Itsuji
Release
2009 Japan
Rating

[View Review](http://movie.naver.com/movie/bi/mi/review.nhn?code=52075)   

 
**1. Is the world beautiful?**
This weekend, feeling a bit down for various reasons, I watched the movie Air Doll at home via VOD with my pregnant wife. It's the film for which Bae Doona received the Best Actress award in Japan. The protagonist is an air doll created to satisfy sexual desires. When the air doll suddenly gained a heart, the first thing she said was, "It's beautiful." What she said was perhaps directed at the most common things in the world. Afterward, the things she saw while wandering the world were, like a camera's gaze, common but beautiful. In contrast, only the hearts of the busy people within that backdrop stood out.
 
**2. There are no villains. Only clumsy people.**
In this film, many marginalized people appear, but there are no real villains. Perhaps only the video store owner who threatened the air doll and took advantage of her... Even the male owner, whom the air doll didn't love, was in fact just someone clumsy at communicating with people. Many "air dolls" appear in this movie. Junichi, who tells the air doll, "Me too," or the various marginalized human figures who pass by. They are all clumsy and insignificant. Those who receive no attention from anyone, or are even ignored. The story of this film is actually centered on them. The somewhat fantastical story of the air doll is a bait to draw out the theme, or a symbol of these people.
 
**3. Are you a substitute?**
Nozomi continuously talks about being a "substitute" in the film. Simply a substitute for sexual desire, and indeed, the male owner brings in another new air doll and puts the original air doll in storage. However, the male protagonist himself often hears at his job that there are plenty of people who can replace him. This is the irony, and this frightening truth is today's reality. There are many people. And for any position, if you look closely, there's always someone who can take your place. It's a simple fact. A very dry fact, except for the detail that each one of those people has a heart.

 
**4. The difference between heart and air**
In the very end, the film culminates in tragedy due to Junichi's ambiguous lie and the air doll's ignorance. And the air doll dies by letting out her own air, which was made of Junichi's breath. Air can be refilled, but once his breath is let out, it cannot be refilled with anything else. Something irreplaceable is someone's breath. Are we not living by someone's breath, and losing it is tantamount to death?
 
This review has become a bit scattered, but seeing the common, lonely human figures in the film made me feel sad, as if I was seeing my own clumsy self. Would it have been more comfortable without a heart? But it is precisely because we have a heart that we can understand the pain of others and say that the world is beautiful. We are all, in fact, as light as air. Though sometimes we act foolishly, as if we are the best in the world or as if we have no heart.

titleEn: No Room for Apple TV in Korea's
contentEn:
**1. Apple TV? Google TV? In fact, they are all IPTV**
As Apple launched a new TV and Google entered the smart TV market, the war between the two camps, which began with mobile phones, is expanding. In fact, the concepts introduced by both companies are not new at all. These concepts have already been present in existing IPTV. However, realistically, the network and IPTV performance couldn't support them, and they lacked completeness.

**2. Apple TV will not have a significant impact in Korea.**
The question is whether this TV market will also undergo a major transformation, just as feature phones quickly turned into smartphones. First of all, I believe Apple's strategy in Korea is very pessimistic. I don't know much about the broadcasting market overseas, so I won't discuss that.

**1) Apple TV cannot relay terrestrial broadcasts**
IPTV began to establish itself in Korea when terrestrial broadcasts started being transmitted live. Considering viewership ratings in Korea, terrestrial broadcasts are almost absolute, and if Apple TV cannot broadcast them, it is highly likely to struggle, just like early IPTV. It will merely be an additional device like a video game console and cannot replace IPTV or cable TV.

**2) Apple TV will suffer from a lack of domestic content**
This is also a domestic issue; unless Korean subtitles are embedded, it will inevitably suffer from a lack of content. Of course, Apple is not going to make such a concession for Korea, nor is there any operator to do so on its behalf. In the case of Korean dramas, broadcasters will certainly not provide content. The probability of broadcasters, who are in a superior position even to current IPTV operators, bending to Apple, which doesn't even have a sales presence, is zero.

**3) Apple TV lacks storage, making media bay utilization difficult**
It's obvious, but since it uses the iTunes purchase method, Apple, which doesn't yet offer cloud storage services, doesn't provide space for users to store videos and photos. Therefore, its utility as a personal multimedia NAS, which is currently sold in Korea, is low. Furthermore, since most distributed video formats are PC-based DivX, using Apple TV, like iTunes, requires a conversion process. And it must be stored on a Mac or iPad.
However, if you store wedding videos or similar content here, you will eventually face trouble. HDDs and SSDs are not permanent storage devices. CD-ROMs and DVDs are also much longer-lasting and safer than these, but their accessibility is low, and depending on how they are stored, they are not permanent media. That's why people use cloud services or NAS supporting RAID. It's unclear why Apple TV omitted storage and opted only for streaming.

**4) Apple TV lacks partners among Korean TV operators**
Apple's current power is largely due to KT's efforts, more so than Apple Korea's. However, KT is highly unlikely to do the same for Apple TV. Because they have QOOK TV. The QOOK Pad, which was released first this time, is also Android-based. If KT were to choose a next-generation IPTV set-top box, which would it choose between Apple and Google? It's actually not hard to figure out. One of the main revenue sources for IPTV is not subscriber acquisition, but rather value-added services like VOD and home shopping. Only Google TV can freely control these. I've heard that current IPTV providers are developing set-top boxes using Android. These Google IPTV set-top boxes might not be able to use the Google Market. Because they will be machines tailored to the tastes of broadcasters rather than adhering to Google CTS standards. They might not even have a browser.
And considering that IPTV already holds a significant market share by offering bundled discounts for subscriptions, there doesn't seem to be much room for Apple TV to enter.

**5) Apple TV without an LCD screen**
As you know, Apple TV is a set-top box. It's different from the TV we usually know. You can only watch Apple TV by connecting it to a Samsung or LG TV. Therefore, the consumption pattern is to first purchase a Samsung or LG device, and then buy an Apple TV. The problem is that bundling Google TV into Samsung and LG TVs will become prevalent. While this might be seen as bundling in a negative light, if you say that TVs also need an OS, there's nothing to argue against. Features that control something, like Time Machine or 3D functions, fundamentally imply a computing environment. And to make it more splendid and beautiful, and to sell content from Samsung, LG, or broadcasters, a platform will be installed. This could be Google or Samsung's Bada.

**6) Can it avoid the blade of domestic law?**
At one time, cyber asylum was popular. And Apple primarily offers overseas services. However, in the broadcasting industry, there is a sharp blade called the Broadcast Review Act. This law is very complex, starting from advertising conditions. It's very complicated with conditions regarding scenes of drinking or smoking, or those involving children or animals. I don't know if Apple TV can officially launch in Korea while avoiding this blade. I think it might need to be registered as an internet device rather than a broadcasting device.

**3. The essence of Google TV is that Android is an embedded OS.**
I read an article titled 'Apple and Google's Different Perspectives' which suggested that Google's platform would approach from a PC perspective, but this is incorrect.

Android embedded in a washing machine doesn't need to resemble a PC. That is the essence of an embedded OS, which supports various devices, not just a single one. Manufacturers choose this OS not so much to increase Google's market share or to check Apple, but rather because they can get powerful desired features and power at a low cost. If a manufacturer develops it from scratch, it incurs very high costs.

**4. Keep a close eye on Apple TV as the paradigm shifts.**
However, this doesn't mean you can ignore Apple TV. In fact, the future TV environment will shift from a broadcaster-led environment to one centered around diverse internet content. A model where individuals create content and share it with Apple in a 7:3 ratio will also emerge.
Perhaps that 3% will be in the form of review costs. In fact, broadcast content cannot be easily modified like software, so being denied registration would be a huge risk, but in Korea, broadcast reviews are already conducted by broadcasters and government agencies. Ultimately, this means that government-led surveillance and control will shift to private companies. And it could lead to protection for creators and ease of content distribution.
Such a paradigm shift can become a competitive advantage. This is why we must keep a close eye on Apple TV and ensure it can lead to cultural competitiveness.

titleEn: [Idea] Computer Power Consumption Reduction Module
contentEn:
**1. Title:** Computer Power Consumption Reduction Module Using UPS in a Smart Grid Environment

**2. First Draft Date:** August 19, 2009

**3. Background:** In a smart grid environment where electricity rates fluctuate in real-time, efforts are being made to minimize the cost of electricity used by systems.

**4. Concept:**
The concept involves using a UPS as a power buffer without additional equipment, charging it during off-peak hours when electricity is cheap, and using a portion of the UPS's power when electricity is expensive to save on electricity bills.

**5. Configuration**
It consists of three modules:
- A module that checks the UPS's power charging status
- A module that retrieves rate information from the smart grid
- A module that can control the system's power

**6.** Typically, a UPS is unused power except during emergencies, and while it's 100% available, using it as a buffer can save power consumption.
- The method used here is identical to stock trading.
e.g., It's possible to predict daily power usage graphs, and by directly applying strategies like dollar-cost averaging (split buying) and trading, it's possible to lower the unit cost of electricity.

titleEn: iPhone 4: Destined to Fail Despite
contentEn:
Pre-orders for the iPhone 4 in Korea, which began yesterday, are quickly approaching 150,000 units. (Has it surpassed that already?) This explosive success, unprecedented in Korea, once again demonstrates the iPhone's brand power. The reason I haven't attributed this success to the iPhone 4's inherent advantages is that pre-orders are for a device not yet in consumers' hands. Currently, the success of the iPhone 4 is entirely due to the trust in the Apple brand built by the iPhone 3GS.
Of course, I'm not saying the device won't sell after it's released. I think surpassing 1 million units will be easy. The iPhone 4 will certainly achieve success like this.
However, in the battle against Android, it will lose, both domestically and globally. You might find this puzzling, but I'd like to explain why.

**1. The iPhone's competitor is not Samsung, but Google.**
Will the iPhone 4 beat the Galaxy S? I can't say that rashly. But I can say one thing: in Korea, the Galaxy series (excluding the Galaxy S) will sell much more than the iPhone 4. And if you combine it with Android devices from Pantech, LG, HTC, Sony, etc., the gap will widen even further.
While Samsung and Pantech, who released the Galaxy S and Izar, appear to be intensely competing, what they've actually brought to the table is the Google platform. Pantech's direct anti-Apple advertisements also used the advantages of Google smartphones, not Pantech smartphones, as their weapon.

This Google platform directly impacts the iPhone's App Store ecosystem.
In fact, the current situation should be understood as Apple vs. Google, not Apple vs. Samsung. The success of the Google platform means a blow to the Apple ecosystem and the birth of an App Store even larger than Apple's.
Recently, Strabase announced mobile OS rankings, and Apple, which received good scores in UX and market, took first place.

However, the market data was from 2009, and the size of the Google Market has dramatically increased during the first half of 2010, narrowing the gap, and it's still ongoing.

**2. Apple will fail to keep up with market development**
In the case of the iPhone 3GS, device developers were helpless for several years, unable to create smartphone solutions to catch up, due to the lack of software platform technology.
However, a means to replace this has emerged, and that is Google, the latecomer.
And when the iPhone 4 was announced, people cheered again. This is because truly amazing technologies were implemented. However, the problem is that the situation is now different from the 3GS.
Software optimization has greatly improved since Froyo 2.2, and 3D performance is essentially a hardware battle dependent on accelerator chip performance. There's no guarantee that LG won't put a Retina Display, which they manufactured, on an Optimus phone.
What's clear now is that the iPhone 4's identity isn't in the software that device developers couldn't keep up with before, but rather in its hardware performance as its weapon.
And Apple's biggest dilemma is that it has to rely on the iPhone 4 for at least a year, or even more than two years. During that time, there might be at least 10 types of Android devices in Korea alone, and over 100 types worldwide.
In a year, the hardware cycle typically changes 2 to 3 times. Therefore, the period during which Apple maintains competitiveness with hardware performance is at best 6 months, and at best 8 months with brand power.
This is precisely why the mobile phone market became a low-margin red ocean as it rushed into hardware competition. Samsung was creating great phones, but the technological gap with Chinese phones wasn't that large, and there were difficulties with volume and unit costs.
If software differentiation disappears, the characteristics of this market will once again resurface.
The Tegra platform and 1.5GHz dual-core are also expected to come to Android. The iPhone 4's performance is currently slightly superior to Snapdragon, so by then, there will likely be a difference.

**3. Feature phone users will also be forced to choose between Apple and Google. Furthermore, many feature phones could unknowingly switch to Android for users.**
Smartphones, unlike feature phones, inherently make it difficult to churn out phones. This is because the cost of software, due to issues like updates, has become very high.
Therefore, device developers find it difficult to produce as many devices as before. If they focus on smartphones, they will certainly draw resources away from feature phones, including development personnel and even marketing costs.
Ultimately, broadcasts will be dominated by smartphones, and users will reluctantly buy smartphones because feature phones are unavailable. Then they will face the choice between Android and Apple.
At this point, what's important for such users is consistency with existing feature phones. This refers to the possibility of an Android phone appearing with a slide keypad instead of QWERTY or touch. Of course, it's highly likely that this device won't be able to access the Google Market, as it would deviate from Google's certified specifications. However, if Google's certification isn't required, device manufacturers can customize more aspects. If they wish, they could remove the browser, install only a few desired apps, or only allow access to the manufacturer's or carrier's special market. It could look 100% identical to a feature phone but be an Android phone internally.
In fact, even existing feature phones didn't have just one mobile OS. Multiple embedded OSs were being sold with the same UI. And now, they can discard those multiple embedded OSs and focus solely on Android.
This also allows for interchangeable developers for smartphones and feature phones, improving smartphone quality, and if they build their own platform well, it will be possible to churn out Android phones like in the past.
Although the current smartphone market is talked about like a huge craze, Apple's market share is in the single digits when considering the entire market, including feature phones.

**4. Traditional mobile powerhouses, led by gaming, are set to catch up.**
Now, another threat is set to emerge from the second half of this year: Microsoft, which has suffered humiliation with Windows Mobile, and mobile gaming giants Sony and Nintendo.
Microsoft's integrated solutions for Outlook and Office are still powerful. Both Android and iPhone have apps that correspond to Microsoft's solutions.
Everyone knows how enormous the sales of the NDSL were, and how much better the games on the much older PSP are compared to the iPhone.
They are launching a counterattack with games. iPhone users claim that apps are the iPhone's strength, but more than half of those killer apps were games.
Microsoft is releasing Windows 7 with Xbox development compatibility (XNA), and Sony, with a seemingly similar concept, is said to be launching a PSP phone. There's no news from Nintendo yet, but I doubt they'll just sit idly by with this news.
{{IMG:1}}
**[Rumored PSP phone based on Android 3.0]******

Furthermore, a large amount of Google's funds was poured into the developer of We Rule, which was considered an exclusive iPhone game. What does Google want in return for this money? Although it was under the guise of investing in social games, I suspect it implicitly urged development for Android.
Apple is a platform developer, not a game developer or publisher. While it has a talent for creating a good ecosystem, given the friction it creates when clashing with other companies, it's questionable whether it can manage large game-related third parties as well as Microsoft or Sony.
When the Xbox was launched, many were surprised by its flashy specs, but there were also many predictions that it would fail due to the lack of third-party support. However, Microsoft continuously invested a lot of money and established itself. This is an experience Apple does not have.
Currently, traditional gaming powerhouses occupy the top ranks on Apple's platform, and these are all entities that have maintained strong relationships with Microsoft.

**5. Conclusion**
**Although I've written at length, this doesn't mean you shouldn't buy an iPhone 4.** It's merely a prediction of market trends. And that prediction isn't for now. For the next few months, the iPhone 4 will probably be a satisfying phone.
And if my prediction is correct, a year from now, things will have changed a lot. In fact, you'll experience the same thing even if you buy a Galaxy S.
Why? Because smartphones are already becoming like PCs. The belief that your smartphone will be the latest model a year from now is something you should abandon. The problem is that contracts are for two years... OTL.

titleEn: [U+BOX] The Cloud Service Show
contentEn:
**1. Why Cloud Service?**
If I had to pick the service Naver is pushing the most, I'd have to talk about the N Drive service, which even has TV commercials.
[재생하기 바로보기가 지원되지 않는 파일입니다. 클릭하여 팝업창으로 플레이 해보세요.](http://blog.naver.com/EmbedHttpView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=70090487144&hashKey=03722c7eaf9c8460a0d94ce22148edda)
This is a service based on the concept of cloud services, which is one of the storage virtualization technologies. It's about lending storage to users and earning money or advertising revenue. A key characteristic of cloud services is the concept of utilizing any resource available on the internet, even within virtualization. This can expand beyond just storage to include processes and various computing resources.
Recently, two of the three major mobile carriers, SKT, KTF, and U+, have already jumped into this market.

| Provider | NHN | KT | U+ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Service Name | N Drive | Ucloud | Uplus Box |
| URL | [ndrive.naver.com/](http://ndrive.naver.com/) | [www.ucloud.com](http://www.ucloud.com/) | [www.uplusbox.co.kr](http://www.uplusbox.co.kr/) |
| Provided Capacity | 5G basic (no additional) | **20G basic** | 10G basic |
| Benefits | ** No restrictions** | Some KT users free | ** No restrictions** |
| Supported Platforms | ** PC, iPhone, Android** | PC, iPhone | ** PC, iPhone, Android** |

Currently, SKT has not yet launched a competing service, but as SKT is pushing the Galaxy S, it is expected to quickly release a corresponding service.
Why is that? It's because this cloud service is based on the internet and can be an alternative for mobile devices that lack sufficient processing power or storage. A long time ago, I mentioned that the day would soon come when mobile devices could use unlimited storage through storage virtualization, and the market is already moving in that direction.

[재생하기 바로보기가 지원되지 않는 파일입니다. 클릭하여 팝업창으로 플레이 해보세요.](http://blog.naver.com/EmbedHttpView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=70090487144&hashKey=b2f1c106091ade6d314e05a8456cb388)

**2. Prerequisites for Cloud Service Competitiveness**
What are the conditions for such cloud services?

**1) Heterogeneous Compatibility**
The advantage of the web and the internet is that they are platform-agnostic. It doesn't matter if it's a PC, iPhone, or Android. The cloud service must provide the same appropriate service regardless of which device requests which service. If iPhones and Androids use different video formats and resolutions, the service must encode the content to fit the device and then deliver it. Furthermore, if a web service is provided, mobile services must also be smoothly delivered. Web standards and cross-browser technologies are also used here.

**2) Smooth Network and Sufficient Available Capacity**
Since it uses the internet, it would be annoying if it's slow. Especially for wireless, reception and transmission speed become very important. This will be the driving force and need for mobile carriers to move to 4G. Particularly in such cloud services, streaming services that allow real-time viewing of multimedia files are primarily used, requiring an environment where HD-quality videos can be played in real-time. This requires a 100Mbps network, which is currently not covered by 3G.
Also, sufficient available capacity must be provided. Currently, Naver offers 5GB, and mobile carriers offer around 10GB, which doesn't seem like a very large capacity compared to the price of an SD card. Photos are increasingly uploaded in RAW format, and quality is improving. If you upload a Full HD video, it will fill up quickly. At this point, companies also need virtualization technology to secure such cheap, large-capacity storage. In fact, personal storage almost demands unlimited capacity.

**3) Openness**
Among current domestic cloud services, this might be the most lacking aspect. Images or files uploaded to N Drive or mobile carriers' clouds should be easily shareable on other SNS platforms like Twitter or Facebook. Furthermore, APIs should be opened to developers, providing open APIs that allow other applications or apps to access that storage. Through this, users will be able to read and edit files from domestic cloud services, just as they can read Google Docs documents in ThinkFree. This is probably the most lacking aspect compared to overseas cloud services like Google. However, the openness of virtualized storage alone becomes a useful feature and a competitive advantage for users. If a company's service only runs within its own ecosystem to push its own service, it will only be a sub-service and cannot become a cloud platform that transcends it.

**4) Security**
This was the first topic that came to mind when I saw the promotion to save resumes on N Drive. Cloud services ultimately involve entrusting one's important data to others. Just as banks always maintain ironclad security and compensate for security issues, security measures must be prioritized. Security must be strengthened without compromising availability, such as the heterogeneous compatibility mentioned first, and measures for damage compensation must be put in place.

**3. Changes Brought by Cloud Services**
These cloud services will actually be the biggest challenge to Apple's device-centric platform policy. The cloud doesn't just mean storage; the App Store itself can be interpreted as a type of cloud service, excluding only the download aspect, as it's a service downloaded from the internet. This is not platform-dependent, and various cloud platforms compete. One of the biggest competitive advantages of cloud services, as I mentioned earlier, is openness. This is because the web itself is a product of openness, and the term "cloud" is simply the web combined with services and a paid model. The accelerating decline in network costs and increase in speed are making this a reality, and a new war is beginning.

#### [[Seoul] On a Wonderful Day in July](http://shopping.naver.com/blog/go.nhn?cat_id=12090002&nv_mid=5602797414)

Category Hobbies, Ticketing, Travel/Reservation/Performance, Event/Classical, Opera
Mapo Art Center Art Hall Mac, 2010/07/08 ~ 2010/07/08
**Rating**

{{IMG:2}}
It was a wonderful performance held at Mapo Cultural Center on July 8, 2010, at 8 PM. My wife is a fan of Baritone Kim Dong-gyu, who hosts the CBS program "To You, My Beautiful," so I got tickets. Since it was a concert, we sat in the second row from the front, on the right side, in A-section seats. Thanks to that, my neck hurt a bit, and with one speaker so close, the sound tended to be unbalanced. It seems even for a concert, you shouldn't disregard the seating.
I left work a little earlier than usual, and it took a little over an hour to get from Bundang to Mapo. Fortunately, my pregnant wife drove directly from Anyang to my office, so we were able to arrive a bit earlier.

That day, I was a bit tired because my nose was bothering me due to the air conditioning. It was especially bad until the first intermission.
Kim Dong-gyu appeared from the second half and sang really well. Soprano Yoo Hye-na, who sang with Kim Dong-gyu, was also truly wonderful. Among the congratulatory wreaths, there was also a large one sent by Andre Kim. Seeing many people congratulating him after the show, it seemed he was one of the main stars of the day. Though I don't know much about music, so I didn't know the details.

This performance had many familiar songs, making it easy to listen to, and Kim Dong-gyu was almost like an MC. He could easily be called an entertainer. However, because he is a musician, he shone even brighter. I also wondered how such a voice could come out.
It was a nearly two-hour performance, but time flew by quickly. I wondered why "On a Wonderful Day in October," the motif for the concert's title "On a Wonderful Day in July," wasn't in the program, but it was sung as an encore.

titleEn: Comparison of the Top 3 Portal Mobile Pages
contentEn:
Recently, as mobile has become an issue, I came across an article suggesting that portals are becoming increasingly similar. Is that really the case? So, I decided to compare them. The comparison results showed that each portal exhibits quite different characteristics, which means that portals have different definitions of user convenience for mobile and also different strategies.

1. Main Page
First, let's look at the main page, the first face of a portal.
1) Naver - Icon Type

| Naver's main page is characterized by an arrangement of icons, similar to an iPhone. Above all, it is very concise compared to other portals. Another characteristic is the absence of content pushed to the user. At one point, Daum and Nate also seemed to briefly adopt this design, but currently, they are not prominently featuring such a design. KT offers a personalized main service where these service icons can be arranged. Naver might soon follow suit, but currently, with a small number of services provided, there seems to be no strong reason to do so. Behind the adoption of this concise appearance, as revealed in Naver SHIFT, it seems to reflect the need for a personalized web platform. The mobile page itself aims to extend into an OS. Naver App Store also seems to have recently launched, which appears to be in the same context. |
| --- |

Behind the adoption of this concise appearance, as revealed in Naver SHIFT, it seems to reflect the need for a personalized web platform. The mobile page itself aims to extend into an OS. Naver App Store also seems to have recently launched, which appears to be in the same context. |

2) Daum - Portal Type

| It has the longest size. It's really long. It requires the use of a scrollbar, and it also pushes the most information. The advantage is that web users can use it without a sense of disconnect, but for a mobile first page, it feels excessively heavy. Furthermore, I am negative about whether using a scroll is necessarily good. From the perspective that scrolling should only be used for essential content, I'm not particularly fond of this design. Icons of major services are exposed at the top. Through 'View All', you can access an icon menu, similar to Naver. However, since it's not prominently featured, it seems they are not actively pushing it. This first page shows that broadcasting, or rather, media elements, strongly influence Daum in terms of pushing content to users. |

3) Nate - List Type

| In Nate's case, it is in a list format. This seems advantageous as it allows for displaying more information, or representative information, compared to icons, and it's also highly commendable for being as easy to click as icons. Nate's main page seems noteworthy for attempting to differentiate itself from Naver and Daum. If it's a list format, it might be possible to add or remove services through future personalization. 2. Services
Let's discuss the portals' mobile services based on the number of services they provide.
**1) Naver**
- N Drive can be considered the most representative service. **It provides virtual storage,** allowing users to briefly view the contents of Word or HWP files, and is expected to become the foundation of future mobile platforms. Apart from news, there are no social issues or common communities. Issues can be accessed through cafes, and since comments cannot yet be made on news, it seems difficult to create major issues.
 Instead, it is expected to evolve into a form where users primarily collect and receive feedback on desired content through a list of neighbor blogs set up on PC.
 - The map service is only provided as an app and not on the web.

**\* Summary: Aims for the web as a platform.**

**2) Daum**
- Compared to other portals, it provides several **non-login-based blog services** (View, Agora, Tistory, Blog, Miznet). These meta-blog services emphasize media elements, and by offering services like Agora, the channels for direct participation in issues are strengthened. It seems to focus on providing a space where Daum users can gather and discuss. However, within Daum, these meta-blog services appear to have high similarity and low differentiation.
** - Map service** is also provided on the mobile web, offering the most advanced level of local services. However, map services provided via mobile web have the disadvantage of being less comfortable than apps. Most users are likely to use the app.
 - Microblogs like Me2day or Connecting are not prominently featured. (Does Daum's 'Yozm' not have a mobile version?)
** - MyPeople:** Allows for effective address book management by updating profiles online. It is designed to be very similar to a phone's address book, making it seem possible to replace the phone's address book. If provided as an app, the possibility of replacement would be even higher.

**\* Summary: Many redundant meta-blog services, easy for users to view issues, MyPeople's address book function is excellent.**

**3) Nate**
- As a latecomer, **content seems insufficient**; for comics, there are few new webtoons.
**- Memo:** It's notable that it provides a memo function, unlike other portals.
- **Services that leverage Cyworld's social networking features seem lacking.**

**\* Summary: Content seems insufficient, it's a pity that Cyworld is not being fully utilized.**

3. Search Results
1) Naver
** - Fusion Web:** When searching on mobile, it provides a Fusion Web service optimized for mobile, in addition to the existing category-based integrated search service.

2) Daum
 - A form where only the layout has been changed for mobile; there's no particular effort made for search. (I'm disappointed...)

3) Nate
** - Differentiation of Semantic Search:** Unlike other portals, it shows different classifications based on search terms through semantic search, which seems to increase search accessibility. Surprisingly good Nate search.

4. Different Aspects of Portals Revealed in Subtle Differences
These differences in mobile tendencies are likely due to the different directions each portal aims for, aren't they? When the iPhone first arrived in Korea, there was news that Daum was ahead in terms of the mobile page's first screen, but it was soon overtaken by Naver. While the reason that familiarity played a role certainly exists, it seems like we are just now reaching a point where each is developing features better suited for mobile.
 Mobile has various characteristics. It requires personalization, deals with low performance, small screens, and the need for real-time feedback, etc. I look forward to seeing how mobile web will develop in the future.

titleEn: Nintendo 3DS: Ushering in the Mobile 3D Era
contentEn:
News about the Nintendo 3DS has arrived. Contrary to [my expectation of a head-tracking display](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70083225106), it will feature a 3D display that uses binocular parallax. For now, due to issues like manufacturing costs, the parallax barrier method is the most widely speculated. First, to help understand this method, I'll show you a YouTube video.

[This file does not support direct playback. Click to play in a pop-up window.](http://blog.naver.com/EmbedHttpView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=70088364531&hashKey=aa8b2ee10bb1025933a98df20f480f1c)

You can think of this method like the hologram stickers on cards. It's a method that shows two images depending on the viewing angle. The biggest challenge with this method is that the display must always be positioned directly in front. This is because if your eyes are at the same angle relative to the display, you can only see one image. (For detailed technical information, please see the attached file.)
**{{IMG:1}}**
** [ Parallax Barrier 3D Method  : Source [http://www.kbench.com/digital/?no=85778](http://www.kbench.com/digital/?no=85778) ]**
**** 
**1. Glasses-free 3D Method Suitable for Mobile Devices**
However, this method is more advantageous for small displays than for large displays like TVs. This is because if you imagine a mobile display as a 50-inch large display, your two eyes would be in a position like a couple who have significantly broken up. On the other hand, for a person sitting in front of a large display, the distance between their eyes becomes almost a single point, making it very difficult to show different images to each eye.
Therefore, glasses-free displays are quite advantageous for mobile devices. While I expect the Nintendo 3DS to increase the demand for glasses-free 3D on TVs, it won't be easy. Furthermore, this method has severe viewing angle limitations for the viewer, making it unsuitable for living room TVs.

**2. Glasses-free 3D Method is Difficult in Shaky Environments**
However, mobile devices have one drawback: they are often viewed while moving, leading to significant shaking. If not handled correctly, both eyes might shift to the left or right, showing only one image, and suddenly the sense of depth can disappear. I also wonder if the feeling of suddenly turning 3D on and off would tire the eyes.

**3. A New Competitor in the Mobile Display Market**
From the highly readable Retina display of the recent iPhone 4G, to AMOLED which is relatively visible even in bright daylight, and LCDs that have been greatly improved without much fanfare, it seems a new method will be added to the battleground of mobile displays. If the Nintendo 3DS receives a good response, then a glasses-free 3D method will certainly be added.
For Samsung, this means one more competitor.

**4. Proliferation of Stereo Cameras**
The Nintendo 3DS, equipped with a stereo camera that was once considered a specialized camera, is expected to bring changes to the camera market. Initially, under the influence of the Nintendo 3DS, stereo cameras might start appearing in the closest smartphones, but their scope will gradually expand to general digital cameras. Advertisements like "10 million pixels plus 10 million pixels equals 20 million pixels" might also emerge. If 3D cameras appear, 3D digital photo frames will also emerge to match them.
 
{{IMG:2}}  

** [ The 3D Camera I envisioned in 2003 : **[**http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70078026282**](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/70078026282)** ] **

**5. Evolution of 3D Cameras**
In the future, this 3D technology will feature high-speed multi-focus, allowing it to focus on distance just like the human eye. And ultimately, I wonder if 3D cameras will evolve into devices like 3D scanners. Sounds like something out of a sci-fi movie, doesn't it?

**6. What kind of experience can two cameras and a 3D display provide?**
The most anticipated aspect of the Nintendo 3DS isn't simply that it shows 3D. Nintendo is a game console, and whenever it has added new sensors or output devices, new game software enabling new experiences has accompanied them. The most exciting part is what new titles will be created using the two cameras and 3D display. A new hardware environment requires new software. I believe that "real 3D" doesn't just mean the display; it means the user experience. I look forward to Nintendo's new challenge, as it feels threatened in the mobile game market by smartphones, including the recent iPhone.
